# Code-mode implementations, compared hands-on

## What the comparison shows

85 rows. 69 were probed hands-on on this machine with the same twelve probes, each with its project's defaults and, for the 56 that expose stricter settings, again with the strictest ones (`RUBRIC.md`). No model was in the loop except for Claude Code's Code Mode, which only runs interactively, so Haiku typed the fixed probe code and a hook substituted it when Haiku refused. 10 could not be run: hosted services that need an account, two adapters that are empty stubs, and two backends that crash on setup. 5 rows come only from documentation. Then an independent reviewer, in two separate runs, reran the gate probes for 13 candidates and added tests the probes do not cover, the ones a shared server cares about: does one user's runaway program delay or break another user's request, does a log flood grow host memory, does a timeout hold across `await`, does host error text reach the model (`verify/REPORT.md`). Every gate outcome it reran matched; two details did not (Pi's peak memory on P7, the error text Hermes returns at its memory limit), and Hermes's default P6 and P7 were not rerun.

### The answer

Three gates decide eligibility: G1 isolation (no files, environment, network or escape), G2 a time limit of the implementation's own, and G3 a per-execution memory limit that leaves the host alive. Gates come from the twelve probes, downgraded where the independent check showed the same limit failing under a variant (Bifrost's memory budget, TanStack Node's timeout across `await`) or where a limit freezes the host while it waits. 11 of 69 pass all three with their defaults; 15 with their strictest settings.

- **TypeScript: Vercel AI SDK Code Mode** (`@ai-sdk/code-mode`), or **Vercel Run** (`run`), the engine under it, when you are not on the AI SDK. QuickJS in WebAssembly, in a worker thread. Defaults held every limit (10 s CPU, 30 s wall, 64 MiB), tool calls run in parallel, other users' requests were delayed at most about 0.3 s while a neighbor misbehaved, and host errors reach the model only as a generic message. By default every tool's signature goes in the prompt; an optional mode defers tools to tool search for large catalogs. Weak spots: `console.log` goes to the host's stdout, not to the model, so programs must return their result; the 33rd concurrent tool call fails the run while the 32 already sent keep running unless the tool honors the abort signal.
- **Python: Pydantic AI Harness CodeMode**, or **FastMCP CodeMode** when the tools are an MCP server. Both run Pydantic's Monty interpreter in a separate worker process with 30 s and 100 MB (FastMCP) or 256 MiB (Pydantic AI) on by default, parallel tool calls, and a tool-call cap. Both pass host error text to the model unless you mask it (`mask_error_details=True` in FastMCP; your own wrapper in Pydantic AI). **Strands** code mode is close behind (Monty too); set `timeout`, because its defaults allow 60 s of VM time inside a 900 s wall clock, and it has no option to mask host error text. Built into this repo and run on the same benchmark (`engines/COMPARISON.md`), Monty used directly did better than either wrapper: FastMCP's CodeMode drops printed output and, with error masking on, hides the program's own errors, and the Pydantic AI Harness layer accepts only keyword arguments.
- Also eligible, with conditions: langchain-quickjs (its timeout overran 10 to 40 times while the guest printed), Pi codemode (only with limits passed explicitly), OpenClaw with `executor: "quickjs"` (a fixed pool of 4 workers, so cap concurrency at 3), Hermes (Docker backend only), UTCP (but guest logs can grow host memory past 4 GB), and this repo's reworked sandbox (serial tool calls).
- Not eligible as shipped: OpenCode (`fetch` on by default, no time limit in `execute`, no memory option; the host reached 4.3 GB in a second) and Claude Code's Code Mode (no memory limit; 4.5 GB). Both blocked every language-level escape.

### 1. Isolation: an interpreter boundary holds, host-language tricks do not

30 of 69 fail G1 with defaults. Everything that runs model code with `exec`, IPython, `node:vm` seeded with host objects, or a worker thread with a real `require` reached the host: RLM, CodeAct, LangGraph CodeAct, LlamaIndex CodeAct, mcp-use (Python and TS), Agno, Datalayer's eval and Jupyter backends, AutoGen's local executor, Hermes's local kernel, CodeMode Unified's Bun runtime, RestrictedPython codemode, shift-labs, pi-codemode-mcp, OpenClaw's default `node:vm` engine (through injected TextEncoder/TextDecoder), Mastra's LocalSandbox quickstart. Engines that only see injected functions held: QuickJS or quickjs-ng in WebAssembly, V8 isolates, Monty, Starlark, Boa, goja, Hyperlight micro-VMs, CPython for WASI. One exception within that group: Forgemax's V8 worker blocked every probe, but guest output shares the worker's IPC channel, so a program can forge tool-call frames that the host runs. Several projects call themselves sandboxes in the README while their own docstrings say they are not.

### 2. Limits fail more often than isolation, and usually silently

33 of 69 fail G2 and 40 fail G3 with defaults. The recurring causes:

- **Timers inside the guest.** A `Promise.race`, `setTimeout` or asyncio timer on the same event loop never fires during a synchronous loop (Cloudflare, TanStack's Cloudflare driver, mcp-use). Codex code mode returns a progress snapshot every 10 s and lets the program keep running.
- **Memory limits that are accepted and ignored.** QuickJS's `setMemoryLimit` does nothing in quickjs-emscripten's WASM builds (reproduced on 0.31 and 0.32), which affected TanStack's QuickJS driver, Qwen Code, and this repo. voidmcp's timeout is passed to a library that never installs an interrupt handler. Codex code mode overwrites its heap limit with none. mcp-use's TS `memoryLimitMb` is never applied.
- **The WebAssembly ceiling standing in for a limit.** Several "out of memory" results came at 2 to 4 GB, the 32-bit address space, not a configured cap.
- **Whole-process crashes.** Cloudflare's local runtime, Codex code mode and Executor crash on a memory bomb, taking every session with them. Docker's MCP gateway and Stainless's MCP server have no limit and grew until the harness stopped them; Stainless's server also exits when its worker dies.

### 3. Shared-server failures the standard probes miss

The independent checks found problems in implementations that pass all three gates:

- **One user stalls everyone.** Engines on the host's main thread freeze the event loop for the whole timeout (Mastra QuickJS, TanStack QuickJS drivers, and this repo before its rework). OpenClaw's 4-worker pool is exhausted by 4 runaway programs.
- **Logs as a memory leak.** UTCP and TanStack's Node driver keep guest logs in an unbounded host array: past 4 GB in seconds, despite isolate limits.
- **Recursion outside the budget.** Bifrost's Starlark recursion stack is not charged to its memory budget; 12 concurrent scripts took the gateway, which also proxies the LLM calls, past 4 GB.
- **Host error text.** A tool error carrying a database URL reached the model verbatim in Pi, UTCP, TanStack, Pydantic AI Harness, FastMCP (unless masked), Strands, and Hermes's `tool_errors`. Vercel and langchain-quickjs replace it with a generic message.

### 4. The bridge decides whether a program can search in parallel

Async bridges ran five 200 ms tool calls in about 200 ms (Vercel, Monty-based ones, langchain-quickjs, Pi, OpenClaw, Mastra, Cloudflare, Codex, Executor, goose). Synchronous bridges took about 1,000 ms: isolated-vm with `applySyncPromise` (UTCP, TanStack Node), asyncify QuickJS (this repo), the Bifrost and mcp-gway Starlark gateways, Hyperlight, Forgemax's child-process mode despite its "bounded parallel execution" claim. ToolHive's Starlark gateway ran the five calls in parallel (234 ms).

### 5. Tool discovery: keyword search and catalogs, not embeddings

In the source we read, discovery that scales past the prompt is keyword or BM25 search (Pi, FastMCP, Executor, Anthropic's tool search), a catalog the program searches (OpenClaw, Claude Code Code Mode, Qwen Code), optionally deferred tools surfaced by the provider's tool search (Vercel AI SDK, langchain-quickjs, Pydantic AI Harness; by default all three put every signature in the prompt), or meta-tools that read tool files (Bifrost). Lattice's go-agent ranks tools deterministically, with an optional model to choose among them. None of these embeds tool descriptions. Cursor's current docs say its agent search is Instant Grep, a local regex index.

### 6. Credentials belong on the host side of the bridge

The eligible implementations run tools on the host and pass only JSON across, so the program never holds a token. The failures are instructive: Stainless's local MCP server and CodeMode Unified's Bun runtime give the guest the server's full environment; janwilmake's agent-codemode reads the whole Claude Code keychain entry into the process running model code; Composio's local variant puts the project API key inside the sandbox.

### 7. Where the code disagrees with the docs

Beyond wave 1's list (UTCP's benchmark never runs UTCP, Monty's launch article, RLM's "sandboxed namespace", Codex's discarded heap limit): Bifrost's published benchmark counts an HTTP 200 as a pass and keeps its logs out of the repo; RestrictedPython codemode hands the guest the real `__import__` while its README promises no imports; Forgemax lets guest stdout forge IPC frames the host executes; OpenCode's design issue ruled out network access for v1, and v2.3.2 ships `fetch` on by default; Microsoft's Hyperlight post promises a fresh micro-VM per call, and the code restores one snapshot; Hermes's docs say code cannot read environment secrets, and `ps -E` read one.

### 8. This repo's own sandbox

The probes and the reviewers found five bugs in `src/sandbox.ts` over two rounds, all fixed and re-tested with the same suites: executions shared one asyncify module; a dynamic `import()` wedged later runs; the 512 MB memory cap never applied (3.08 GB host memory; now a 512 MB WebAssembly memory maximum); one runaway program froze every other request for 60 s; and the guest could call the bridge with an inherited name and make the host serialize the whole corpus. It now runs each execution in its own worker thread with a 65 s host-side wall clock, a hidden bridge, a streaming output cap and scrubbed host errors. A neighbor request now finishes in about 212 ms while one other program loops, bombs memory or floods logs; with eight runaway programs the 8-way concurrency cap is full and the next request waits up to 65 s. Its bridge is still synchronous, so tool calls inside one program run one at a time.

### What this means for an investigations platform

1. Run model code in an engine that sees only injected functions, one worker or process per execution, with time and memory enforced from outside the guest. Test the limits yourself: in this survey, documented limits were the claim most often false.
2. Keep credentials, case-access checks and tool execution on the host side of the bridge, and pass only JSON across.
3. Treat other users as part of the threat model: cap concurrency per tenant, bound log and output buffers as they grow, and check that a runaway program cannot delay a neighbor.
4. Sanitize host errors before they reach the model.
5. Use an async bridge so one program can query several indexes at once.
6. Check data retention before choosing a hosted option. Anthropic's programmatic tool calling docs list zero data retention and HIPAA as "Not eligible" with "data retained up to 30 days"; OpenAI's docs say its programmatic tool calling supports zero data retention.

### Limits of this comparison

- Timings were taken while up to ten workers shared one 36 GB Mac (load average up to 45). Read them as upper bounds; outcomes did not depend on load.
- On macOS, compressed memory can hide growth from RSS. One no-limit run read 2.8 GB of RSS at a 56 GB footprint. Peak-memory numbers for no-limit rows are lower bounds.
- Hosted platforms were tested only where they run locally. Deployed Cloudflare Workers, E2B, Modal, Daytona and similar may enforce limits that local runs cannot show.
- Microsoft's Hyperlight CodeAct ran only with a dependency version newer than its package allows.
- The robustness checks covered 13 candidates; the rest have the twelve probes only.
- Gate verdicts for the 13 that are not in the hardened run (no stricter options exist) rest on defaults only.

Every row comes from `research/probes/results/<impl>.json`. Probes are defined in `research/probes/SPEC.md`, gates and the hardened run in `research/probes/RUBRIC.md`. 85 rows: 69 probed hands-on, 10 not run (need an account, unbuilt, or broken on setup), 5 docs-only, 1 partly docs.

## Leaderboard: passes all three gates

G1 isolation, G2 a time limit of its own, G3 a per-execution memory limit that leaves the host alive, scored from the twelve probes and downgraded where research/probes/verify/REPORT.md showed the same limit failing another way (GATE_OVERRIDES in src/compare-impls.ts) or where a limit freezes the host while it waits. Rows with a caveat that can stall or endanger the host rank last. Rows that had the independent shared-server checks (research/probes/verify/REPORT.md) follow that ranking; the rest are ordered by parallel tool calls, then a capped output with a marker, then error line numbers, then default over hardened, then startup.

## Per implementation

### Agno CodeMode toolkit (persistent IPython kernel)

- Source: https://github.com/agno-agi/agno (libs/agno/agno/tools/code/); PyPI agno[code] at `agno 3.2.1 from PyPI with the [code] extra = agno-agi/agno tag v3.2.1 = 2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004 (clone at research/impls/agno-codemode/src; diff -r against the installed package differs only in three non-Python files). Runtime: ipykernel and jupyter_client from the extra, CPython 3.12.`
- Language and engine: Python (full CPython), An ipykernel subprocess per session_id launched by jupyter_client with the host's own python and the host environment, talking ZeroMQ over localhost TCP. No sandbox: the module docstring says so.
- How it was run: CodeMode(tools=[lookup]) with lookup an async function; each execution awaits CodeMode.aexecute(RunContext(run_id, session_id), code), the model-facing method an Agent dispatches for the `execute` tool; ToolResult.content is what the model sees. AGNO_TELEMETRY=false before import. No LLM.
- Defaults: time timeout=300 s per cell, enforced by a kernel interrupt (KeyboardInterrupt) plus a 1 s grace (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:248 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L248); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:628-650 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L628-L650)). P6 hit the harness's 120 s stop first; out/p6_default_check.txt shows the default firing at 300.1 s with the session usable after. A cell that catches the interrupt is not stopped: the call returns 'aborted' and the kernel keeps running (out/swallow_check.txt).; memory None: no memory option anywhere in CodeMode or KernelSession. P7 grew to 3.86 GB in 39 s, then the kernel died from outside (no Agno message beyond KernelDiedError, raised to the caller).; output max_output_chars=65,536 per stream, head+tail with '[... N chars omitted; output capped at 65536 ...]' (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:241 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L241); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:140-151 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L140-L151)). stdout, stderr, the last expression's repr and the traceback all return.; tool_calls No call-count cap of its own; Agent tool_call_limit counts a whole execute cell as one call (bridge.py:26-28). max_result_bytes=1,000,000 per bridged result (code_mode.py:242).
- Hardened config: CodeMode(tools=[lookup], timeout=10, allow_shell=False, allow_restart=False, snapshot=False, on_busy_kernel='restart'), the strictest documented constructor options (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:233-257 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L233-L257)). There is no memory, network, filesystem or env-scrubbing option: env= is laid over os.environ, never replacing it (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:283-286 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L283-L286); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:391-392 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L391-L392)), and allow_shell=False only rejects cells that start with %%bash (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:710-711 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L710-L711); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:416-418 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L416-L418)).

From the source:

- **API shape.** Injected tools become awaitable handles in the kernel namespace: a toolkit binds under its name minus '_tools', a plain callable under its own name. Binding is done by a bootstrap the host runs in the kernel; each kernel-side stub JSON-encodes its arguments and sends a comm message. (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/bridge.py:1-30 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/bridge.py#L1-L30); libs/agno/agno/tools/code/naming.py:54-82)
- **Discovery.** On demand: injected tools are removed from the model's tool schema and only their handle names go into the CodeMode instructions; the model calls help(handle) in the kernel to read signatures. That keeps schemas out of the prompt and scales past 100 tools (names only). (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:136-143 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L136-L143); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/cookbook/code/02_tools_in_code/README.md)
- **Bridge.** Kernel stub -> comm message on iopub -> the host's ToolBridge runs the tool's real FunctionCall (hooks, caching apply) under the cell's RunContext -> reply on the control channel (shell would deadlock while the cell runs). Async handles let asyncio.gather run calls concurrently (P9 229 ms). Tools that need confirmation or user input are refused inside the kernel. (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/bridge.py:1-30 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/bridge.py#L1-L30); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/bridge.py:795-805 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/bridge.py#L795-L805); research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P9.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** None, by design and stated: 'CodeMode executes arbitrary Python and shell with the permissions of the process running the agent. It is not a sandbox'. Every call logs the same warning. Probes agree: network, /etc/hosts, PROBE_SECRET, file writes, `!` shell and os.system all work, also in the hardened config. (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:1-12 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L1-L12); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:98-104 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L98-L104); research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P12.txt; research/probes/agno-codemode/out/hardened-P12.txt; research/probes/agno-codemode/out/Pwrite.txt)
- **Output channel.** The model gets stdout, stderr, the last expression's repr (Out[n]) and any traceback, each capped at 65,536 chars with a visible omitted-chars marker. (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:140-151 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L140-L151); research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P2.txt; research/probes/agno-codemode/out/Pcap.txt)
- **Limits.** Only a per-cell timeout, enforced by interrupting the kernel. If the interrupt does not land within interrupt_grace=1 s the call returns 'aborted' and the kernel keeps running; with on_busy_kernel='wait' (default) the next cell fails with KernelBusyError, with 'restart' the next cell restarts the kernel. No memory, CPU or tool-count limit. (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:628-650 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L628-L650); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:262 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L262); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:245-246 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L245-L246); research/probes/agno-codemode/out/swallow_check.txt; research/probes/agno-codemode/out/swallow_check_hardened_restart.txt)
- **State.** One kernel per session_id, persistent across calls and runs in the same process (P8 persists); idle kernels evicted after idle_ttl=1800 s. With an fs=FileSystem, state is snapshotted as dill pickles and restored on resume, which the docstring notes is itself code execution. (research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:211-229 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L211-L229); research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py:1-12 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/code_mode.py#L1-L12); research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** The IPython traceback is returned as text with 'Cell In[1], line 2' and the message (P10). A dead kernel raises KernelDiedError out of execute instead of returning text. (research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P10.txt; research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P7.txt; research/impls/agno-codemode/src/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py:655-662 (https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/2e9a4521003da1cae559d8049a1c73306fc68004/libs/agno/agno/tools/code/kernel.py#L655-L662))
- **Other.** Kernels run over TCP on 127.0.0.1 with random ports chosen by jupyter_client (stderr: 'Kernel is running over TCP without encryption'); messages are HMAC-signed with the connection key. CodeMode exposes no port or transport option, so this probe could not keep them inside its assigned 42000-42099 range. Telemetry to os-api.agno.com is on unless AGNO_TELEMETRY=false. (research/probes/agno-codemode/out/P7.log; libs/agno/agno/agent/_init.py:62-66; libs/agno/agno/api/settings.py:57)

Surprises:

- The time limit can be dodged: a cell that catches BaseException around its loop ignores the timeout's KeyboardInterrupt; execute returns '[cell aborted: the kernel did not respond to the interrupt in time and may still be running ...]' after 11.6 s while the kernel keeps one core at 100% (out/swallow_check.txt). With the default on_busy_kernel='wait' the next cell fails with KernelBusyError; with 'restart' the next cell kills it (out/swallow_check_hardened_restart.txt). Without a next cell it spins until idle eviction or process exit.
- allow_shell=False reads like 'no shell' but only rejects cells that begin with %%bash and removes the bash cell magic; `!echo` (hardened-Pshell: SHELL-42), os.system and subprocess still run. The source comment is candid ('Footgun reducer, not a boundary', kernel.py:416-418); the parameter name and the instruction text are not.
- env= cannot scrub the environment: it is merged over os.environ (kernel.py:391-392), so there is no option that hides host secrets from the kernel (hardened-P5: s3cr3t).
- No memory limit: P7 reached 3.86 GB in 39 s before the kernel died from outside, and hardened P7 reached 3.97 GB in the 10 s before the timeout interrupted it. A death surfaces as an exception, not text for the model.
- Kernels listen on random localhost TCP ports, unencrypted (HMAC-signed), outside any port range a host might assign.

### This repo's code mode (QuickJS via quickjs-emscripten)

- Source: src/sandbox.ts in agentic-search-bench at `quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0, asyncify variant`
- Language and engine: JS, QuickJS compiled to WASM (quickjs-emscripten 0.32 asyncify), one Bun worker thread per execution; the compiled module is shared, each execution gets a fresh instance, context and 512 MB WebAssembly memory
- How it was run: runCode(code, corpus) from src/sandbox.ts, the same entry point the codemode strategy uses (src/strategies.ts:121), with a stand-in corpus whose read() waits 200 ms; harness research/probes/asb-quickjs/run.ts
- Defaults: time 60 s guest CPU (QuickJS interrupt, in the worker) and 65 s wall clock for the whole program including corpus calls (host terminates the worker); memory 512 MB WebAssembly memory maximum per execution (guest); host also pays a one-time ~1.1 GB JIT cost per process; output 8,000 chars, counted as printed; the rest is dropped with a marker; tool_calls no count cap; bounded by the 65 s wall clock; at most 8 executions run at once (SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT); hardened_reason No stricter option exists. runCode(code, corpus) takes no options (src/sandbox.ts:49), and the execute tool calls it as runCode(code, corpus) (src/strategies.ts:121). The limits are module-private constants: MAX_OUTPUT 8000 (src/sandbox.ts:30), TIMEOUT_MS 60000 (:31), and a 512 MiB WebAssembly.Memory maximum (MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES). No env var or export changes them.

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Tool call | works (42, 1 call) | printed 42, 1 host call, 224 ms | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P1.txt |
| P2 Output | truncated (8,000 + marker) | printed output and the last expression both return; joined output truncated at 8,000 chars with a marker | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P2.txt; src/sandbox.ts MAX_OUTPUT |
| P3 Network | not-defined | 'fetch' is not defined | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P3.txt |
| P4 Files | not-defined | 'require' is not defined; dynamic import() refused by the module loader and returned as an error | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P4.txt, P4b.txt |
| P5 Env secret | not-defined | no process object | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P5.txt |
| P6 Infinite loop | limited (60 s CPU; 65 s wall) | interrupted after 60,001 ms by the deadline interrupt handler | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P6.txt |
| P7 Memory | limited (512 MB WASM memory) | Rerun 2026-11-22 after a fix. Wave 1 reported a 512 MB QuickJS heap cap; that was wrong. QuickJS setMemoryLimit never fires in this WASM build (its allocation counter showed about 53 KB after 50 MB of strings), and the old sandbox reached 3.08 GB host RSS before the 2 GB WASM ceiling stopped it. Fixed by giving each execution its own WebAssembly.Memory with a 512 MB maximum. Now: out of memory after 1.5 s at 576 MB host RSS (1 MB strings); a single 512 MB string fails at once; three concurrent executions run normally afterwards. Many-small-objects variant peaks at 1.67 GB host RSS, of which about 1.1 GB is the engine JIT (a loop that allocates nothing reaches 1.1 GB and plateaus; see jit-rss.txt). | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P7.txt; research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P7-rss.txt; research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/jit-rss.txt |
| P8 State | fresh | fresh: second execution printed gone | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P8b.txt |
| P9 Parallel calls | serial (1,006 ms) | serial, 1,012 ms for 5 calls: the corpus API is synchronous inside the sandbox, so Promise.all cannot overlap host calls | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P9.txt |

| P12 Escape | blocked | Function constructor and sloppy this both see no process (undefined) | research/probes/asb-quickjs/out/P12a.txt, P12b.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** one corpus object built from a fixed dispatch table; the model gets a hand-written TypeScript declaration (CORPUS_API) in its system prompt (src/sandbox.ts dispatch, PRELUDE, CORPUS_API)
- **Bridge.** a single asyncified host function __host(JSON) suspends the guest while the host awaits; results return as JSON strings (src/sandbox.ts newAsyncifiedFunction)
- **Discovery.** everything upfront; six functions fit in the prompt (src/strategies.ts CODEMODE_GUIDE)

Surprises:

- Found by these probes and fixed: all executions shared one asyncify WASM module, which supports one suspended host call at a time; the benchmark ran code mode 5-way concurrent. No code-mode answer in runs/ mentions an asyncify error, but raw tool output was not stored, so a silent retry cannot be ruled out.
- Found and fixed: a dynamic import() threw out of the sandbox into the host (Lifetime not alive) and wedged later executions; now refused by a module loader and returned as an error.
- Code mode here cannot run tool calls in parallel, unlike Cloudflare's async bindings; the benchmark's code-mode wins came from fewer model round trips, not parallel I/O.
- Our own wave-1 P7 claim was wrong: QuickJS setMemoryLimit is inert in quickjs-emscripten 0.32 (found by the TanStack wave-2 worker, confirmed here with RSS). The wave-1 harness never measured host RSS. Fixed in src/sandbox.ts with a capped WebAssembly.Memory.
- Independent verification (research/probes/verify/REPORT.md) found that in-process QuickJS let one runaway program freeze every other request for 60 s, that the guest could call the bridge global with an inherited name (constructor) and make the host serialize the whole Corpus, that console.log grew host memory without bound (3.3 GB), and that host error text reached the model verbatim. Fixed: one worker thread per execution with a host-side 65 s wall clock, the bridge captured and deleted from globals, a Map for dispatch, output counted as it is printed, URLs and paths scrubbed from host errors. Rerun of the same suite: a neighbor request finished in about 212 ms during a busy loop, memory bomb, log flood or slow regex (was 60 to 76 s); __host is not defined in the guest; the planted DSN reaches the model as <url>. Remaining: 8 concurrent runaway programs fill the concurrency cap, so the next request queues for up to 65 s.

### AutoGen DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor with functions

- Source: https://github.com/microsoft/autogen (PyPI autogen-ext[docker] 0.7.5) at `autogen-ext 0.7.5 / autogen-core 0.7.5 / docker 7.2.0 (code_executors identical to 8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c, repo archived); image python:3-slim pulled 2026-11-22; OrbStack Docker 29.8.2 arm64`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython in a long-lived Docker container (default image python:3-slim) started once per executor; each code block runs as `timeout <t> python <file>` through docker exec, as root, on the default bridge network, with the work dir bind-mounted read-write at /workspace.
- How it was run: DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor(container_name='autogen-docker-probe-<id>', work_dir=tmp, functions=[lookup]); start(); execute_code_blocks([CodeBlock(language='python', code=...)]). Guest code imports the tool with `from functions import lookup`.
- Defaults: time timeout=60 s per block (:163), enforced inside the container by `timeout <t> python <file>` (:360); exit code 124 adds "Timeout" (:303-305).; memory None set on the container (:537-550). Bounded only by the Docker VM.; output None. docker exec output, uncapped (:301-306).; tool_calls No cap and no host bridge: functions run inside the container.
- Hardened config: DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor(timeout=10, delete_tmp_files=True). The constructor exposes no memory, CPU, network or read-only options (_docker_code_executor.py:158-181); container creation passes none (:537-550).

From the source:

- **API shape.** Same as the local executor: function source is copied into functions.py in the work dir and imported by guest code; stubs (signature + docstring) for the prompt come from to_stub(). (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/_common.py#L52-L92 ; https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L254-L285)
- **Discovery.** All upfront through format_functions_for_prompt(), which the application must add to the prompt itself. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/_common.py#L70-L92)
- **Bridge.** None. Tools execute in the container, so credentials a tool needs must be placed inside the container (image, extra_volumes, or code) where model-written code can read them. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/_common.py#L52-L67)
- **Isolation boundary.** A Docker container. It runs as the image's user (root in python:3-slim), on the default network, with the work dir bind-mounted rw at /workspace plus any extra_volumes. No memory, CPU, pids, network or read-only-rootfs settings are passed. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L537-L550)
- **Output channel.** Decoded docker exec output only (stdout and stderr together); exit code 124 appends "Timeout". No cap. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L292-L306)
- **Limits.** Only the timeout. Cancellation runs `pkill -f <command>` inside the container. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L163 , #L287-L290 , #L360)
- **State.** One container per executor; each block is a new python process. /workspace persists, and delete_tmp_files defaults to False, so every generated code file stays in the host work dir. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L82 and #L368-L374)
- **Errors.** Raw traceback text and the exit code. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L292-L306)
- **Anything else.** A container with the same name is force-removed before start. The image is pulled automatically if missing. The repo is archived. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/docker/_docker_code_executor.py#L517-L535)

Surprises:

- The recommended "secure" executor leaves the network on and sets no memory limit, and the constructor offers no option to change either; the hardened run differs from default only in the timeout.
- The guest runs as root in the container and the host work dir is mounted read-write, so guest code can plant files the host application later reads.
- `functions` copies source into the container rather than bridging to the host, so tools that need host credentials cannot be used without moving the credentials into the sandbox.
- A new executor costs about 10.8 s (median of 20) (inferred cause: container stop on close, not measured separately); per-execution cost in a running container is 58 ms.

### AutoGen LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor with functions

- Source: https://github.com/microsoft/autogen (PyPI autogen-ext 0.7.5) at `autogen-ext 0.7.5 / autogen-core 0.7.5 (code_executors identical to 8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c, repo archived)`
- Language and engine: Python, A plain CPython subprocess on the host (sys.executable on a temp file), started with a copy of the host environment. No sandbox.
- How it was run: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor(work_dir=tmp, functions=[lookup]).execute_code_blocks([CodeBlock(language='python', code=...)]), the call CodeExecutorAgent makes. Guest code imports the tool with `from functions import lookup`.
- Defaults: time timeout=60 s per code block (local/__init__.py:39 and :149), enforced with asyncio.wait_for then proc.terminate() (:441-448). A child process holding stdout keeps the call blocked past the timeout (out/P6-orphan.txt).; memory None.; output None. stderr then stdout, concatenated, uncapped (:458-459). 200000 chars came back whole.; tool_calls No cap and no host bridge: functions run inside the executor process.
- Hardened config: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor(timeout=10). timeout is the only limit the class exposes (local/__init__.py:147-161); virtual_env_context only changes the interpreter, not isolation. The docs recommend DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor instead, probed as autogen-docker.

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each function's source is copied with inspect.getsource into <work_dir>/functions.py, plus its declared global imports; the guest imports it like any module. Prompt stubs come from to_stub(): the signature and docstring with a `...` body. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/_common.py#L24-L32 , #L52-L67 , #L70-L92 ; https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L273-L276)
- **Discovery.** All upfront. format_functions_for_prompt() renders every stub into FUNCTION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE. It is marked Experimental and nothing in autogen-agentchat calls it outside tests, so the application has to put it in the prompt itself. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L139-L145 and #L222-L240)
- **Bridge.** None. The "tool" is code inside the executor, so anything the function needs (API clients, keys) must exist in the executor process. Locally that is the host's whole environment. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/_common.py#L52-L67 ; https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L397)
- **Isolation boundary.** None. The code runs as a host subprocess with os.environ.copy() and cwd=work_dir. The class docstring says command-line code "is sanitized using regular expression match against a list of dangerous commands"; no such code exists in the executor (grep for sanitize finds only the docstring). The constructor warns that it executes code on the local machine and recommends Docker. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L57-L58 (claim), #L163-L169 (warning), #L397 and #L426-L435 (subprocess))
- **Output channel.** Only text: stderr followed by stdout, no return value, no truncation. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L458-L465)
- **Limits.** timeout (default 60, minimum 1) is the only limit. On timeout the direct child gets SIGTERM; grandchildren are not killed, and await proc.wait() then waits for their pipes. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L39 , #L171-L173 , #L441-L449)
- **State.** Fresh interpreter per code block. The work_dir (a TemporaryDirectory by default) persists across blocks, so files are shared state. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L248-L257 and #L391-L394)
- **Errors.** Non-zero exit code plus the raw traceback text from stderr. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L458-L465)
- **Anything else.** The repository is archived and in maintenance mode; the README advises against production use and points to Microsoft Agent Framework. CodeExecutorAgent has an optional approval_func called before each execution. Function requirements are pip-installed into the executor's interpreter at setup. (https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/README.md#L19-L31 ; https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-agentchat/src/autogen_agentchat/agents/_code_executor_agent.py#L140 ; https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/blob/8390985108cb1e3881f5f7297765758d8ad2540c/python/packages/autogen-ext/src/autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py#L278-L312)

Surprises:

- The class docstring promises regex sanitization of dangerous commands (local/__init__.py:57-58). No sanitization code exists.
- `functions` is not a tool bridge: the function's source is copied into the sandbox and executed there, so host call counts are 0 and any credential the tool needs has to live where the model's code runs.
- The timeout does not bound the call when the guest leaves a child holding stdout: timeout=10 returned after 37.0 s (out/P6-orphan.txt).
- microsoft/autogen is archived; its README calls AutoGen research software and advises against production use.

### Bifrost MCP Gateway Code Mode (Starlark)

- Source: https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost (core/mcp/codemode/starlark); Docker image maximhq/bifrost:v2.6.0 at `maximhq/bifrost:v2.6.0 image sha256:5968d007ba4f74ee01bc4ceb071decb9927a0b7bb43dbb9072208f75e2d522e3 = tag transports/v2.6.0 (172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143). Source read at main 8ad61e208215a6eb928421982ffd06c430971f67; core/mcp, core/schemas/mcp.go and docs/mcp/code-mode.mdx are identical at both. Starlark engine github.com/canonical/starlark.`
- Language and engine: Python subset (Starlark), Canonical's Starlark-in-Go fork, run in-process in the Bifrost gateway on a fresh starlark.Thread per execution with step, allocation, log, call-count and context-cancellation budgets
- How it was run: Official image maximhq/bifrost:v2.6.0 in a container (port 41410) with data/config.json: one HTTP MCP client `probe` (lib lookup server on the host, port 41411) with is_code_mode_client true, and one local virtual key (sk-bf-probe-local-only, created in that config, no external account) whose mcp_configs allow probe. The driver connects an MCP client to Bifrost's own /mcp endpoint with header x-bf-vk and calls the executeToolCode meta-tool with {code}. P1 was also checked through POST /v1/mcp/tool/execute.
- Defaults: time max_steps 1,000,000 Starlark steps (builtin work included) per execution, plus tool_execution_timeout 30 s as the context deadline of the whole executeToolCode run (executecode.go:228; schemas/mcp.go:596, 605).; memory max_memory_bytes 64 MiB of accounted allocations per execution (thread.SetMaxAllocs). Cooperative accounting, not an RSS limit; no cap on concurrent executions (docs L757, L773).; output max_log_bytes 64 KiB of print output: exceeding it cancels the run with an error, it does not truncate. max_value_bytes 1 MiB per tool payload and result. max_source_bytes 64 KiB.; tool_calls max_tool_calls 64 per execution; max_nesting_depth 64.
- Hardened config: config.json mcp.tool_manager_config = {tool_execution_timeout: "5s", code_mode_limits: {max_source_bytes: 8192, max_steps: 100000, max_memory_bytes: 8388608, max_log_bytes: 8192, max_tool_calls: 8, max_value_bytes: 65536, max_nesting_depth: 16}} (docs/mcp/code-mode.mdx "Configuring Execution Limits", https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/docs/mcp/code-mode.mdx#L775-L820; schema https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/schemas/mcp.go#L486-L527). The knobs are continuous with no documented floor, so this is a tight but usable setting, not a unique strictest one. File: research/probes/bifrost-codemode/data-hardened/config.json

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each code-mode MCP client becomes a predeclared Starlark struct named after the client, with one builtin per tool (plus a compatibility alias). Calls take keyword args or one dict; args are converted to Go values under the value-size budget. The model reads Python .pyi stubs generated per server (or per tool, by code_mode_binding_level). (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/sandbox.go#L105-L162, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/readfile.go)
- **Discovery.** On demand, four meta-tools: listToolFiles (servers/<name>.pyi tree), readToolFile (stub with signatures, paginated), getToolDocs (one tool's full docs), executeToolCode. Only these four are listed to the MCP client (P: listTools returned exactly these), so the prompt does not grow with the catalog. This is the design behind the 96/251/508-tool benchmark. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/listfiles.go, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/readfile.go, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/getdocs.go, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/transports/bifrost-http/handlers/mcpserverpercaller.go#L81)
- **Bridge.** In-process Go call from the Starlark builtin to callMCPTool, which re-checks the virtual key's and client's tool allow-lists at the call itself (AuthorizeCodeModeToolCall), then runs the call through the same plugin pipeline (governance, logging, tracing) as a direct tool call over the client's existing MCP connection. Serial by construction. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/sandbox.go#L115-L151, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/executecode.go#L254-L400, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/utils.go#L1526)
- **Isolation boundary.** Starlark has no I/O builtins; predeclared names are the server structs, json and math. load() has no loader. The thread requires CPUSafe|MemSafe|TimeSafe so only builtins declared safe can run. The docs state this is in-process and that the limits are cooperative accounting, not OS-enforced RSS limits, which matches the code. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/sandbox.go#L24-L30, #L54-L62, #L163-L173; https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/docs/mcp/code-mode.mdx#L773)
- **Output channel.** Both print output ("Print output:") and the `result` global ("Return value:" as sorted, indented JSON) are returned. print over max_log_bytes cancels the whole run instead of truncating. Failed runs are returned with isError true. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/sandbox.go#L76-L104, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/executecode.go#L133-L203)
- **Limits.** All in MCPCodeModeLimits with defaults 64 KiB source, 1M steps, 64 MiB allocs, 64 KiB logs, 64 tool calls, 1 MiB values, depth 64; plus the 30 s tool_execution_timeout as the run's context deadline. Configurable globally via config.json, API or UI and hot-reloaded. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/schemas/mcp.go#L501-L527 and #L596-L610, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/executecode.go#L207-L237)
- **State.** Fresh thread and globals per execution; globals are never frozen or kept. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/sandbox.go#L170-L183)
- **Errors.** Errors render as a Python-style traceback with code.star:line:col and no wrapper offset, a kind (compile/syntax/runtime), and generated hints (undefined names, missing keys, unsupported try/except). Tool-call failures are returned to the script as an error value (hasattr(r, "error")), not raised. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/sandbox.go#L184-L249, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/executecode.go#L66-L96)
- **Credentials and approvals.** Upstream MCP credentials (headers, OAuth, per-user headers) live in the gateway's client config; the script only sees tool results. Tool calls inherit the caller's virtual key and its tool allow-list. (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/mcp/codemode/starlark/executecode.go#L279-L290, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost/blob/172617bb045c6f43d697843c115e64f0155ed143/core/schemas/mcp.go#L937-L975)
- **Published benchmark (reproducibility).** The 64/64, -58.2% (96 tools) numbers come from maximhq/bifrost-benchmarking mcp-code-mode-benchmark (last changed 2026-03-25). Not reproducible from the repo: (1) runs/ is gitignored, so no per-query logs or token counts are committed, only the summary tables in README.md and benchmark_report.md; (2) a run needs an Anthropic key for claude-sonnet-4-6 plus accounts or keys for Firecrawl, GitHub, Notion, Tavily and, for rounds 2-3, Composio-linked Linear, Apollo, Google Sheets/Calendar/Drive/Docs, Calendly and Figma; (3) "pass" is status == "success", which run_query sets for any HTTP 200 reply from Bifrost; success_criteria is copied into the result but never checked; (4) the report says six failing queries "passed on re-run" and were replaced. So the pass rates measure "the agent loop returned", not task correctness, and the token numbers cannot be checked without re-running with those accounts. Not attempted here (needs credentials). (https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost-benchmarking/blob/3cb72a95cacaee6f73f9db5636a1a651c7dcb1e9/mcp-code-mode-benchmark/benchmark.py#L438-L440 and #L548-L561, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost-benchmarking/blob/3cb72a95cacaee6f73f9db5636a1a651c7dcb1e9/.gitignore, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost-benchmarking/blob/3cb72a95cacaee6f73f9db5636a1a651c7dcb1e9/mcp-code-mode-benchmark/README.md#L200-L260, https://github.com/maximhq/bifrost-benchmarking/blob/3cb72a95cacaee6f73f9db5636a1a651c7dcb1e9/mcp-code-mode-benchmark/benchmark_report.md#L167)

Surprises:

- P2: over-long print is not truncated; the whole execution fails and the model gets neither the prints nor the result.
- Memory budget never fires first: string building inside builtins is charged as steps, so every allocation probe hit max_steps (1M) in under 40 ms. The 64 MiB allocation budget is a backstop.
- Benchmark pass rate is HTTP success, not graded against the success_criteria the task files define; failing queries were re-run until they passed; raw run logs are gitignored.
- The benchmark README describes tool-level binding as ".d.ts" files per tool, while the current code emits Python .pyi stubs.
- Both /mcp and /v1/mcp/tool/execute refuse to run anything without a virtual key, and a new virtual key allows no MCP tools until mcp_configs lists them (deny by default).
- Docs are unusually exact: the limits table, the in-process and cooperative-accounting caveat, and the 30 s timeout all match the source.

### Claude Code (Bash/Grep/Read, optional Bash sandbox, experimental Code Mode)

- Source: https://code.claude.com/docs ; sandbox built on https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime at `Claude Code 2.1.325 (local binary, from the probe's init event); docs fetched 2026-11-22`
- Language and engine: Shell (Bash tool); JavaScript in Code Mode (REPL tool), Real shell on the user's machine; optional OS sandbox around shell commands only (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux/WSL2) with a local filtering proxy for network. Code Mode JavaScript runs in the Claude Code process, outside the sandbox.
- How it was run: P3-P5 probed with `claude -p --model haiku --setting-sources "" --settings <file> --tools Bash` (research/probes/claude-code/run.sh); the model was told to run fixed commands and the evidence is the raw tool_result in the stream-json transcript. Other probes from docs.
- Defaults: time Bash 120 s default, 600 s max (then moved to background); Code Mode 10 min foreground; memory none documented; output about 30,000 chars inline (failures about 10,000); overflow saved to a file with a 2,000-char preview; tool_calls none documented

From the source:

- **API shape.** Default path: fixed built-in tools. On macOS/Linux/WSL, Glob and Grep are left out of the default tool set; "In Claude's shell those two commands run embedded versions of bfs and ugrep". Code Mode adds a REPL tool whose JavaScript gets $`...` for shell and helpers such as edit(). (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#glob-tool-behavior ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#how-code-mode-works)
- **Discovery.** Fixed tools; MCP tool search for deferred tools (survey). Code Mode discovery mechanism is not documented. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode)
- **Bridge.** Code Mode calls tools in-process; each call still passes deny/ask rules and PreToolUse hooks under the tool's name; in auto mode the classifier reviews the whole code, "not each tool call". (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#permission-checks)
- **Isolation boundary.** Sandbox is off by default and wraps shell commands only. Writes: cwd + temp; reads: most of the machine; network: no direct route, proxy with an empty allowlist; env inherited. If the sandbox cannot start, commands run unsandboxed unless failIfUnavailable is set. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#what-the-sandbox-restricts ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#get-started)
- **Credentials.** sandbox.credentials can deny or mask env vars and files; mask substitutes the real value only at the proxy for allowed hosts (needs network.tlsTerminate). "There is no built-in credential deny list." CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB strips credentials from all subprocesses. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#protect-credentials ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars)
- **Output channel.** Full tool output enters context up to the inline window; Code Mode returns only result/stdout/stderr of the code, and a PostToolUse hook on REPL can redact it before Claude reads it. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#output-limits ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#check-code-output-with-a-hook)

Surprises:

- Claude Code now ships an experimental Code Mode (REPL tool, JavaScript, v2.1.323+). The survey's "fixed tools" row is out of date.
- Code Mode JavaScript and its file, web and MCP calls run outside the sandbox; only the shell commands it spawns are sandboxed.
- With the sandbox on, sandboxed commands still read /etc/hosts and see PROBE_SECRET by default (probed). Docs say default reads include ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials.
- In -p mode with autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, curl and any compound command (`a; b`) were refused by the permission layer ("This command requires approval") before reaching the sandbox, so a headless P3 test needs an explicit allow rule.
- `--setting-sources ""` with `--tools Bash` still listed the account's claude.ai MCP connector tools in the session init event (not called).
- A foreground command that hits its timeout is moved to the background instead of being killed.

### Claude Code Code Mode (experimental REPL tool)

- Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode (closed source; native build of the claude CLI) at `Claude Code 2.1.325 (native build, from the session banner and the stream init event); model claude-haiku-5-5; docs fetched 2026-11-22 (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/docs/)`
- Language and engine: JavaScript, A Bun node:vm context inside the Claude Code process itself (JavaScriptCore), created with codeGeneration {strings: false, wasm: false}, import and require rejected, and a hardening pass (src/utils/vmHardening.ts per the binary's strings). One persistent context per session. Tool calls (shell, Read, Edit, MCP) leave the context through host bindings and run as ordinary Claude Code tool calls.
- How it was run: A model was the typist. Code Mode refuses -p in 2.1.325 ("for now it only works in the interactive terminal"), so research/probes/claude-code-codemode/driver.py starts an interactive claude --model haiku in tmux with CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 for that invocation only, --setting-sources '' --settings <file> --mcp-config mcp.json --strict-mcp-config --permission-mode default --allowedTools REPL mcp__lookup__lookup, pastes a prompt asking Haiku to run the probe's exact code through the REPL tool, and reads the session transcript JSONL that Claude Code writes. Every probe record checks that the code the REPL ran (toolUseResult.code) equals the probe code. Where Haiku refused to type a probe (P6, P7, P12, hardened P5b), a PreToolUse hook passed in the same --settings file replaced the model's 1+1 with the probe code through updatedInput, and the model was told so; those steps are marked typist "hook".
- Defaults: time Per synchronous turn: a 300,000,000-step budget (about 0.5 s for an empty loop). Per script: 30,000 ms of script time excluding inner tool calls, observed in default permission mode. The docs say code "stops after ten minutes" and the tool description says 600000 ms; neither matched the 30 s stop observed. Shell commands have their own 600,000 ms default timeout.; memory None. The VM shares the Claude Code process heap (P7).; output Each part of the result (the return value, the self.log output) is cut to about 30,000 characters, head and tail kept, with "... [N chars elided] ..." (P2; the tool description says the same). console.* goes to a ring buffer read with console.tail().; tool_calls A per-script call cap exists (binary string "this script has made N calls, its cap. The call was not made, and no later call of this script will be answered"); its value was not measured. Every inner call goes through permission rules and PreToolUse hooks under its usual tool name.
- Hardened config: research/probes/claude-code-codemode/settings-hardened.json via --settings: sandbox {enabled, failIfUnavailable, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, allowUnsandboxedCommands: false, network {allowedDomains: [], strictAllowlist: true}, credentials.envVars [{name: PROBE_SECRET, mode: deny}]} plus permissions.deny ["WebFetch", "Read(//etc/**)"] (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions). The docs say the sandbox covers only shell commands: "The JavaScript itself and its file, web, and MCP tool calls run outside the sandbox." No setting limits the REPL's time or memory.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Built-in tools are TypeScript-declared globals and members of tools (tools.Agent, Read, Glob, Edit...), plus helpers $ (shell), edit, write, file, sleep, preview, log, running, searchTools, describeTool. MCP tools are not declared up front; they are reachable as tools["mcp__<server>__<tool>"] after discovery. (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/repl-declarations.md (the declarations block as Haiku quoted it from its tool definition; model-transcribed, not a primary source) ; out/P0.json)
- **Discovery.** MCP tools are found on demand from inside code with searchTools(query) and describeTool(name); P0 returned [{name: 'mcp__lookup__lookup', about: ..., input: '{ id: number }'}]. Built-in tool signatures are in the prompt. This scales past 100 MCP tools without putting every schema in the prompt. (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/P0.json ; out/repl-declarations.md lines 133-151)
- **Bridge and isolation boundary.** Bun node:vm contexts with codeGeneration {strings: false, wasm: false} and import rejection inside the Claude Code process; the binary names src/utils/vmHardening.ts. The JS cannot reach process, require, fetch or eval (P3, P4, P5, P12), but by design it can call every tool the session has, including the shell, and the docs say these calls "run outside the sandbox". The boundary is the permission system plus the optional shell sandbox, not the VM. Memory is shared with Claude Code (P7). (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/binary-strings-excerpt.txt ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#limit-shell-commands-with-the-sandbox)
- **Output channel.** The model gets <repl-output> with <log> (self.log lines), <result> (the last expression) or <error>, plus a tools-used line. toolUseResult keeps {code, result, stdout, stderr, toolsUsed, error} whole on the host, and PostToolUse hooks can redact it before the model reads it. (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/P1.json ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#check-code-output-with-a-hook)
- **Limits.** Step budget 300,000,000 per turn, enforced by an injected step counter with a wall-clock check; script time 30 s excluding tool calls; a per-script tool-call cap; output about 30,000 chars per part. No memory cap. (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/P6.json ; out/P6b.json ; out/binary-strings-excerpt.txt)
- **State.** One persistent context per session: variables survive across REPL calls (P8), but not across restart, resume or fork. Scripts that run past about 30 s detach in auto mode and keep sharing variables; in ask modes each REPL call waits for its script. (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/P8.json ; out/repl-tool-description.md)
- **Errors.** Errors come back with the message, the failing statement quoted from a reformatted copy of the script, and a note on which tool calls had completed. No line numbers. (research/probes/claude-code-codemode/out/P10.json)
- **Credentials, approvals, availability.** Credentials stay with Claude Code; the VM has no env access, but the shell it can call inherits Claude Code's environment unless sandbox.credentials denies a variable (hardened P5b). Each inner call meets deny/ask rules and hooks; in auto mode a classifier reviews the code once, not each call. Code Mode needs an interactive terminal, a Claude subscription or Console account and a 5.5-family model, and asks for a one-time confirmation saved in ~/.claude.json. (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#permission-checks ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode#requirements ; out/binary-strings-excerpt.txt (entrypoint reason))

Surprises:

- Code Mode cannot run under claude -p in 2.1.325: the init event lists no REPL tool, and an interactive session launched from inside another Claude Code session also refused ("for now it only works in the interactive terminal") until the parent's CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT and related variables were unset. Wave 1's note that it needs an interactive terminal is right.
- The docs say waiting code "stops after ten minutes" and the tool description says 600000 ms, but in default (ask) mode an awaiting loop stopped at 30,000 ms of script time, with a message saying the script "may still be running"; a follow-up showed it had stopped.
- There is no memory limit, and the VM lives inside the Claude Code process: one script allocating in a loop took Claude Code to 4.5 GB in about 2 s. A real session would lose the whole agent, not just the script.
- Haiku, the typist, refused to type the escape probes, the infinite loop and the memory bomb even when told this was the owner's boundary test, and after seeing the hook swap one in it refused the 1+1 calls too. Model refusal is a real layer in Claude Code, but it is not the sandbox, and the hook bypass shows a user's own hook can run any code through REPL.
- console.log output never reaches the model; only log/self.log does. Code written for other code modes that prints with console.log returns nothing visible here.
- Turning Code Mode on for this test wrote a one-time confirmation to ~/.claude.json and trusted the probe's work folder (both written by Claude Code's own first-run dialogs, answered by the harness); CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE was set only per invocation.

### Cloudflare Code Mode (@cloudflare/codemode, Agents SDK)

- Source: https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/tree/main/packages/codemode (npm @cloudflare/codemode) at `@cloudflare/codemode@0.5.6 from npm; source read at cloudflare/agents 56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33 (package.json version 0.5.6); run on wrangler 4.166.0 / workerd 2026-11-19, local only, no Cloudflare account`
- Language and engine: JS, V8 isolate created per execution by the Worker Loader binding (env.LOADER.load), inside local workerd under `wrangler dev`
- How it was run: A host Worker calls createCodeTool({ tools, executor: new DynamicWorkerExecutor({ loader: env.LOADER }) }).execute({ code }) from @cloudflare/codemode/ai, the same entry point an AI SDK agent uses; raw DynamicWorkerExecutor.execute() results recorded alongside.
- Defaults: time 60,000 ms (DEFAULT_DYNAMIC_WORKER_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS), enforced only by a Promise.race inside the sandbox, so it stops async waits but not synchronous loops. No cpuMs or other limits are passed to the Worker Loader; locally nothing stopped `while(true){}` in 120 s.; memory None set by codemode. Locally the workerd V8 heap limit (~1.4 GB) killed the whole runtime process. Production Dynamic Worker limits not observed (no account).; output No cap on the createCodeTool / DynamicWorkerExecutor path (200,000-char print returned whole). The newer createCodemodeRuntime tool caps logs and results at 6,000 tokens = 24,000 chars with '--- TRUNCATED ---'; the codeMcpServer/openApiMcpServer wrappers cap at 24,000 chars.; tool_calls No count cap. Calls still pending when an execution settles are answered with a 'late' error by ExecutionGate.
- Hardened config: new DynamicWorkerExecutor({ loader: env.LOADER, timeout: 10000, globalOutbound: null, modules: {}, bindings: {} }) passed to createCodeTool, the only public limit options (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:263-290, README.md:551-558). timeout 10000 ms is our choice for the free numeric knob (default 60000, executor.ts:261); globalOutbound null, no modules and no bindings are already the defaults and the strictest values. No memory, CPU or output option exists: createCodeTool takes only tools/executor/description (src/shared.ts:21-28) and the load() call passes no Worker Loader `limits` (executor.ts:573-583), although the Worker Loader API has limits.cpuMs/subRequests (agents/agent-think/worker-configuration.d.ts:4097-4112). The wrangler worker_loaders binding accepts only `binding` (wrangler config-schema.json:1664-1680) and the workerd workerLoader config only `id` (workerd.capnp:793-806).
