From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools become methods on a namespace object (`codemode` by default, one per ToolProvider). generateTypes converts each tool's Zod / Standard / JSON Schema input (and optional output schema) to JSON Schema and then to TypeScript `type XInput`, `type XOutput`, plus `declare const codemode: { x: (input: XInput) => Promise<XOutput> }` with JSDoc from descriptions. It is pasted into the tool description through the {{types}} placeholder. Without an output schema the output type is `unknown` (see out/tool-description.txt). (packages/codemode/src/tool-types.ts:221-285 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/tool-types.ts#L221-L285); packages/codemode/src/tool.ts:98-121 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/tool.ts#L98-L121); packages/codemode/src/shared.ts:10-19 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/shared.ts#L10-L19))
- **Discovery.** Legacy createCodeTool puts every tool's types in the one tool description upfront. The newer createCodemodeRuntime path exposes `codemode.search(query)` / `codemode.describe(path)` inside the sandbox; search is weighted keyword token matching over connector method paths and descriptions (path 12, method 10, connector 8, description 5), top 50, with no embeddings. (packages/codemode/src/tool.ts:94-114 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/tool.ts#L94-L114); packages/codemode/src/connectors/search.ts:11-18 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/connectors/search.ts#L11-L18); packages/codemode/src/connectors/search.ts:163-206 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/connectors/search.ts#L163-L206); packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts:1-20 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts#L1-L20))
- **Bridge.** Workers RPC. The host builds one ToolDispatcher (an RpcTarget) per namespace and passes them as arguments to the sandbox entrypoint's evaluate(__dispatchers, __connectors). Inside the sandbox a Proxy per namespace turns `ns.tool(args)` into `__dispatchers.ns.call(name, JSON)`; results come back as JSON with a base64 tag for binary. Connectors use direct RPC callTool instead. (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:235-257 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L235-L257); packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:434-450 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L434-L450); packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:601-604 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L601-L604))
- **Isolation boundary.** Each execute() calls env.LOADER.load() for a new Worker with compatibilityDate '2025-06-01', nodejs_compat, globalOutbound null by default, and env only when bindings are passed. README claims network is blocked at the runtime level; probes P3, P4, P5, P12 match. The model's code is spliced into the WorkerEntrypoint's evaluate() method body, so `this`, `__dispatchers`, `__logs` and the console override are in its scope (probe P12x). (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:573-583 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L573-L583); packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:484-516 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L484-L516); packages/codemode/README.md:481-493 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/README.md#L481-L493))
- **Output channel.** console.log/warn/error are replaced to push into __logs; evaluate returns {result, logs}. runCode returns {result, logs} on success and on error throws 'Code execution failed: <msg>' followed by '\n\nConsole output:\n' and the logs. No truncation on this path; the runtime path's toModelOutput truncates logs with truncateResult (6,000 tokens x 4 chars). (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:489-512 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L489-L512); packages/codemode/src/run-code.ts:16-31 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/run-code.ts#L16-L31); packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts:789-801 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts#L789-L801); packages/codemode/src/truncate.ts:19-21 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/truncate.ts#L19-L21))
- **Limits.** Only the 60 s Promise.race timeout. load() gets no CPU, memory or subrequest limits. No tool-call cap. (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:261 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L261); packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:498-508 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L498-L508); packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:573-583 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L573-L583))
- **State.** Fresh Worker per execution (load(), not get(id)), so no state between runs. The runtime path adds durability through a Durable Object facet: a tool-call log replayed after approvals, at most 50 executions kept, 1,000,000-byte cap per logged value, saved 'snippets' the model can rerun. (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:569-583 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L569-L583); packages/codemode/src/runtime.ts:144-156 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/runtime.ts#L144-L156); packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts:1-20 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/proxy-tool.ts#L1-L20))
- **Errors.** The sandbox catch returns err.message only (stack and line dropped). A tool throwing on the host is returned as {error: message} and re-thrown in the sandbox as new Error(message). runCode prefixes 'Code execution failed: '. (packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:509-512 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L509-L512); packages/codemode/src/executor.ts:242-256 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/executor.ts#L242-L256); packages/codemode/src/run-code.ts:22-27 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/run-code.ts#L22-L27))
- **Approvals, credentials, async.** createCodeTool silently drops tools with needsApproval (documented limitation); the runtime path pauses instead for requiresApproval connector methods and resumes by replay. Credentials stay host-side because tools execute on the host. Code is normalized with acorn (fences stripped, last expression returned), and async/Promise.all work. (packages/codemode/src/resolve.ts:16-31 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/resolve.ts#L16-L31); packages/codemode/README.md:718-723 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/README.md#L718-L723); packages/codemode/src/normalize.ts:14-81 (https://github.com/cloudflare/agents/blob/56f5d5cc635df14d36a6a08b8e5a56113f08fb33/packages/codemode/src/normalize.ts#L14-L81))

Surprises:

- DynamicWorkerExecutor's documented 60 s timeout is a Promise.race inside the sandbox. The README warns that sync loops cannot be preempted only for the browser iframe executor (README.md:567, 721), but the Worker executor has the same limitation and passes no CPU limit to the Worker Loader (executor.ts:498-508, 573-583). Locally `while(true){}` ran past 120 s and froze the whole dev runtime.
- A memory blow-up in the sandbox killed the entire local workerd process, host Worker included. The caller got HTTP 500 'Network connection lost' rather than an execution error. Production isolation may differ; not verified without an account.
- createCodeTool returns console logs uncapped (all 200,000 chars), while the newer runtime tool and the MCP wrappers in the same package cap at 24,000 chars.
- The sandbox compatibility date is hard-coded to 2025-06-01 (executor.ts:574), whatever the host Worker's date is.
- Model code runs as the body of the sandbox WorkerEntrypoint method. `this` is the CodeExecutor instance with ctx.waitUntil, and harness internals (__dispatchers, __logs) are reachable. This grants no extra capability beyond the tools.
- Tool discovery in the newer runtime is plain weighted keyword matching (connectors/search.ts), not embeddings.

### Cloudflare API MCP server (server-side Code Mode: search + execute)

- Source: https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp at `b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa (2026-11-19); deps from its package-lock via npm ci; runs on its own local vitest + @cloudflare/vitest-plugin workerd pool, no Cloudflare account`
- Language and engine: JS, V8 isolate per tool call from the Worker Loader binding (env.LOADER.get with a random id); `search` isolates are loaded by the forge-tools service Worker, `execute` isolates by the main Worker
- How it was run: The repo's own test harness (npm test style: vitest with @cloudflare/vitest-plugin) drives the real Worker through MCP tools/call with a dummy bearer token; MSW mocks only the Cloudflare API, including a GET /lookup/:id route that stands in for the host tool.
- Defaults: time None in code. search has no timeout at all; execute stops early only when the rate-limit wait budget (30 s) or the 1,000 unsent-requests cap trips. Sync loops ran past 120 s locally.; memory None set. Locally the workerd V8 heap limit crashed the whole runtime. Production Worker limits not observed (no account).; output Return value only, capped at ~6,000 tokens = 24,000 chars with a '--- TRUNCATED ---' marker. Each call can pass truncate:false, and the connection can turn it off with ?truncateToolResult=false. console output is not returned.; tool_calls No count cap; at most 20 cloudflare.request calls in flight per run; 1,000 'not sent' rate-limit answers stop the run.; hardened_reason No stricter public option exists at commit b8602d6. No timeout, CPU or memory knob: both Worker Loader calls hard-code their config with no `limits` (src/tools/execute.ts:150-154, src/forge-tools/search.ts:29-53) and wrangler.jsonc sets no `limits`. The only public config is the query params codemode, experimentalOutputSchema, truncateToolResult and scopeChallenge (src/mcp-handler.ts:49-63) and the vars CLOUDFLARE_API_BASE, CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_DOMAIN, MCP_RESOURCE and RESPONSE_VALIDATION_SAMPLE_RATE (wrangler.jsonc vars; worker-configuration.d.ts:66). Truncation is already on by default in code mode (src/server.ts:72, cap 6,000 tokens at src/truncate.ts:19-21) and the model can still pass truncate:false per call. execute's network allowlist is already the single API host (src/tools/execute.ts:78-119). Rate-limit pacing constants are hard-coded (src/rate-limit.ts:45-100). ?codemode=false removes code execution entirely rather than hardening it. So the default run is also the hardened run.

From the source:

- **API shape.** No per-tool code generation in Code Mode. The model gets two hand-written TypeScript declarations: SPEC_TYPES for the `spec` object (OpenAPI 3 shape) in `search`, and CLOUDFLARE_TYPES for `cloudflare.request({method, path, query, headers, body})` plus `accountId` in `execute`. The 2,500+ operations stay data. With ?codemode=false the server instead registers ~3,000 forge-generated direct tools. (src/tools/search.ts:25-58 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/search.ts#L25-L58); src/constants.ts:27-39 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/constants.ts#L27-L39); src/tools/execute.ts:613-619 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L613-L619); src/server.ts:84-99 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/server.ts#L84-L99))
- **Discovery.** On demand. The model writes JS that walks the pre-resolved OpenAPI spec (`spec.paths`) in the `search` tool; the description lists only the first 30 products and some example queries. A `docs` tool is registered alongside. (src/tools/search.ts:15-28 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/search.ts#L15-L28); src/forge-tools/search.ts:29-56 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/forge-tools/search.ts#L29-L56); src/server.ts:95-99 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/server.ts#L95-L99))
- **Bridge.** No RPC tool dispatch. execute's sandbox calls its own fetch(); the Worker Loader routes all outbound traffic to the GlobalOutbound WorkerEntrypoint (globalOutbound: exports.GlobalOutbound({props})), which rejects hosts other than the API base with a 403, applies policy guards, injects the bearer token, and retries. search has no bridge at all: the spec is a text module inside its isolate. (src/tools/execute.ts:78-119 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L78-L119); src/tools/execute.ts:150-154 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L150-L154); src/tools/execute.ts:295-296 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L295-L296))
- **Isolation boundary.** Worker Loader V8 isolate per call, compat date 2026-01-12, no nodejs_compat, globalOutbound null for search and the GlobalOutbound proxy for execute. The blog claims 'no file system, no environment variables to leak through prompt injection and external fetches disabled by default'; probes P3-P5 and P12 match. Code is spliced verbatim into the module source as `(${code})()`. (src/forge-tools/search.ts:29-53 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/forge-tools/search.ts#L29-L53); src/tools/execute.ts:150-154 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L150-L154); src/tools/execute.ts:531 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L531))
- **Output channel.** Only the returned value. Neither harness overrides console, so logs go to Workers Logs, not the model. Results go through truncateResponse (structural JSON truncation, 6,000 tokens x 4 chars) unless truncate is false. (src/tools/execute.ts:527-543 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L527-L543); src/forge-tools/search.ts:42-49 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/forge-tools/search.ts#L42-L49); src/truncate.ts:19-22 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/truncate.ts#L19-L22); src/truncate.ts:41-50 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/truncate.ts#L41-L50))
- **Limits.** No timeout or CPU/memory limit in code. execute has rate-limit pacing: 30 s wait budget, 5 s longest single hold, 20 in flight, stop after 1,000 unsent requests. The comments rely on the MCP client's 60 s timeout. (src/rate-limit.ts:41-91 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/rate-limit.ts#L41-L91); src/tools/execute.ts:230-259 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L230-L259))
- **State.** Fresh isolate per call with a random id. The code comments say dynamic-worker isolates disallow eval, so code cannot be passed into a warm isolate. No snapshots. (src/forge-tools/search.ts:19-30 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/forge-tools/search.ts#L19-L30); src/tools/execute.ts:122-149 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L122-L149))
- **Errors.** The sandbox returns err.message only, and the tool returns 'Error: <message>' with isError true. Hints are appended for unknown accounts, GraphQL permission refusals, and missing OAuth scopes (step-up challenge, only when replaySafe). (src/tools/execute.ts:532-542 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L532-L542); src/utils/errors.ts:9-18 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/utils/errors.ts#L9-L18); src/tools/execute.ts:700-727 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L700-L727))
- **Credentials, approvals, async.** The API token lives only in GlobalOutbound props and never enters the isolate. OAuth 2.1 with downscoped tokens through workers-oauth-provider. The sandbox records each request so a failed run can be marked replay-safe for step-up. execute is annotated destructiveHint true; there is no human approval gate in the server. Async and Promise.all work. (src/tools/execute.ts:66-100 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L66-L100); src/tools/execute.ts:668-679 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/tools/execute.ts#L668-L679); src/index.ts:33-62 (https://github.com/cloudflare/mcp/blob/b8602d6d5ce543ef5933ea3d98f06be8e20759fa/src/index.ts#L33-L62))

Surprises:

- The blog says the server exports just two tools. At this commit Code Mode registers five: docs, search, execute, whoami and submit_feedback (server.ts:95-99), plus MCP skills.
- cloudflare/mcp does not use @cloudflare/codemode at all (package.json dependencies). It has its own harness, which differs from the SDK's openApiMcpServer: a `spec` global instead of codemode.spec(), no normalizeCode, no 60 s timeout.
- No execution timeout in either tool. A sync loop ran past 120 s locally, so the code relies on the platform CPU limit and the client's timeout.
- console.log output never reaches the model. A probe that prints its answer returns 'undefined'.
- Code is not normalized. Anything but a function expression fails with a SyntaxError at a line in the generated worker.js.
- In execute, fetch to a non-API host does not throw. It returns a synthetic 403 Response that code can read.
- Each search call re-parses the 27 MB spec in a new isolate: about 120 ms per call locally against about 3 ms for execute.
- A sandbox OOM crashed the whole local runtime, MCP Worker included, so the client got no error result.

### cmcp (Code Mode MCP proxy, Rust)

- Source: https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp at `2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426 (crate code-mode-mcp 0.1.0; no GitHub releases exist). Cargo.lock: rquickjs 0.11.0, oxc 0.114.0, rmcp 0.16.`
- Language and engine: TS (types stripped by oxc, run as JS), QuickJS via rquickjs 0.11 (AsyncRuntime + AsyncContext::full), in-process in the Rust proxy. One runtime and one context per proxy state, reused for every search and execute call; 64 MB runtime memory limit.
- How it was run: Built with `cargo build --release --locked` in rust:1-bookworm (container cmcp-build), then run inside Docker: `docker run -i --rm --name cmcp-probe-* -e PROBE_SECRET=s3cr3t node:24-bookworm-slim /opt/cmcp --config /work/state/config.toml serve` (linux/arm64 in Docker Desktop's VM, not the macOS host), with the lookup MCP server (lookup-server.mjs, registered twice as lookup and lookup2 via `cmcp add --transport stdio`) in the same container. P4 /etc/hosts and P5 env therefore refer to the container. run-probes.mjs drives the execute and search tools over MCP stdio, no LLM.
- Defaults: time None. No timeout or interrupt handler anywhere in src/ (grep for timeout/interrupt finds nothing). P6 ran past 120 s and wedged execute. No option exists to add one.; memory 64 MB per proxy runtime, hard-coded (src/sandbox.rs:52), shared by all executions in that proxy process. No option to change it.; output Return value only, pretty-printed JSON truncated to 40,000 bytes with a marker (src/lib.rs:23, 150-160; src/server.rs:18). The per-call max_length argument is model-controlled; 0 disables truncation. console.* goes to proxy stderr only.; tool_calls No cap found.; hardened null: the CLI and config expose no time, memory, network or tool-call options (only --config, server definitions, and the per-call max_length, which the model controls). Checked src/main.rs Cli/Commands and src/config.rs.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each upstream server becomes a global Proxy object (hyphens to underscores) whose properties are async functions calling __call_tool(server, tool, JSON). The full catalog is also injected as `tools`. TypeScript declarations are generated from each tool's JSON Schema, but they are only prepended to the agent's code before oxc strips them: they are never shown to the model and never type-checked (a string assigned to a number variable and a wrong parameter name both ran, out/setup-typecheck.txt). (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L163-L187 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/catalog.rs#L58-L97 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L361-L389 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/transpile.rs#L11-L46)
- **Discovery.** On demand: the search tool runs model-written code over the catalog array (server, name, description, input_schema) inside the same QuickJS context, and returns its result truncated at 40k. Only two tools are in the prompt, so it scales past 100 tools. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L82-L111 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/server.rs#L132-L153 ; out/setup.txt)
- **Bridge.** rquickjs Async native function: the JS promise awaits a Rust future that calls rmcp call_tool. The future first locks a per-upstream tokio Mutex and holds it for the whole call, so calls to the same server serialize (P9) while calls to different servers overlap. Results are the raw MCP CallToolResult serialized to JSON, not unwrapped. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L122-L146 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/client.rs#L133-L147 (lock at L144))
- **Isolation boundary.** QuickJS in-process with only builtins plus two native functions; no module loader, no std/os modules. The README claims "Sandboxed: code runs in a QuickJS engine with a 64 MB memory limit"; the code matches for memory, files, env and network, but there is no time limit, and the single shared context means one execution can poison or starve later ones. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/README.md#L26 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L50-L80 ; out/P4.txt, P8.txt, P7-hog.txt)
- **Output channel.** Only the JSON-stringified return value goes back. console.* is a shim that calls __stderr, which eprintln!s to the proxy's stderr, so logs never reach the model. Truncation slices the string at a byte index, which panics on a UTF-8 boundary. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L32-L63 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/lib.rs#L150-L160 ; out/P2-utf8.txt)
- **Limits.** Memory: rt.set_memory_limit(64 MB) once per proxy state. Time: none. Output: 40,000 default, overridable per call. Tool calls: none. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L51-L52 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/server.rs#L17-L36)
- **State.** Persistent. ProxyState holds one Sandbox (one AsyncRuntime/AsyncContext) until a config reload, and every search/execute takes the engine mutex and evaluates in that context, so globals and prototype changes persist and executions are serialized. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/lib.rs#L42-L97 (mutex at L71, L84) ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/lib.rs#L135-L147)
- **Errors.** Errors become an isError text: "execute error: JS promise rejected: <message> + stack" with eval_script line numbers offset by the injected setup; transpile errors drop the position. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/sandbox.rs#L189-L196 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/server.rs#L173-L175 ; out/P10.txt)
- **Credentials.** Kept on the host side: `env:VAR` references in config are resolved by the proxy at connect time for HTTP auth headers and stdio child env, and the sandbox only gets server proxies. stdio upstreams inherit the proxy's whole environment (tokio Command default) plus configured vars. (https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/client.rs#L55-L75 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/client.rs#L108-L118 ; https://github.com/assimelha/cmcp/blob/2bf2e58460634c6c8ae8a50cc177719efed99426/src/client.rs#L201-L206)

Surprises:

- No execution time limit at all, and because executions share one context behind a mutex, one `while(true){}` wedges execute and search for the rest of the proxy's life (ping still answers).
- console.log output never reaches the model: it is written to the proxy's stderr. The spec P1 and P2 forms return null to the caller.
- Tool results are the raw MCP CallToolResult, so `(await server.tool()).field` is undefined for normal text-returning servers; the model must parse content[0].text itself. Nothing in the tool descriptions says so.
- README says "Type-safe: auto-generated TypeScript declarations" (line 25). The declarations are never shown to the model and oxc strips types without checking, so a wrong parameter name or type mismatch runs without complaint.
- State persists across executions in one shared QuickJS context. A prototype override in one execution changed [].map in a later one, and memory held in a global by one execution made a later 5 MB allocation fail.
- Response truncation slices at a byte index (lib.rs:154). A result whose byte 40,000 falls inside a multi-byte character panics the handler; the MCP request is never answered (client waits forever), though the proxy keeps serving other requests.
- Promise.all over one server is serial (1,036 ms for five 200 ms calls) because of a per-upstream mutex; the tool description is accurate that parallelism is across different servers.
- No releases on GitHub; README asks for `cargo install --path .` and Rust 1.91+, while CLAUDE.md says Rust 1.85+.

### CodeAct (Wang et al., ICML 2024): mint PythonREPL, the agent environment's executor

- Source: https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act (also ships a Jupyter-gateway chat engine under scripts/chat/code_execution/, not probed) at `commit d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8 (default branch HEAD; last push 2024-05-23); ipython 9.18.1 (resolved; repo leaves it unpinned)`
- Language and engine: Python, IPython InteractiveShell.run_cell() in the host process, with stdout captured through IPython.utils.io.capture_output. Not isolated.
- How it was run: PythonREPL(user_ns={'lookup': fn}) then repl(code) for each probe. This matches GeneralEnv.__init__ (general_env.py:66-70) and handle_tool_call (general_env.py:143). The default timeout is 30 s.
- Defaults: time 30 s, via SIGALRM (python_tool.py:21, 28-38). Observed P6: returned after 30.03 s with a TimeoutError traceback.; memory None found. P7 stopped by the harness at 4.14 GB peak RSS after 0.3 s, before the 30 s alarm.; output 2000 chars of captured stdout, then '...\n[Output Truncated]' (python_tool.py:72-73). The return value is not separate: it appears only as IPython's Out line in stdout, so the cut can remove it.; tool_calls None. lookup is an ordinary function in user_ns, and the executor counts nothing.
- Hardened config: The repo's containerized code execution engine: JupyterGatewayDocker(name=...) with RESOURCE_CONSTRAINTS {'mem_limit': '8g', 'nano_cpus': 2_000_000_000} (scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py:239-245) and JupyterKernel.execute(code, timeout=60) (scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py:136, 209-213), the same calls api.py:66-90 makes per conversation, documented in README.md:144-150 (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py#L239-L245). Image docker.io/xingyaoww/codeact-executor:latest (amd64 only, 7.45 GB compressed, run under emulation). No network option. Harness pins the host port to 41910 and names containers codeact-hardened-<probe>; research/probes/codeact/hardened.py. The in-process PythonREPL's only stricter knob is a lower timeout (python_tool.py:21), which does not change isolation.

From the source:

- **API shape.** GeneralEnv builds user_ns = {tool.name: tool.__call__} for every Tool in its tool set, then adds task.user_ns. Each tool is a plain Python callable in the IPython namespace. There is no generated stub and no schema-to-code step. (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/envs/general_env.py#L66-L70)
- **Discovery.** The model sees every tool up front. get_toolset_description() writes each tool's signature and description into the prompt as 'Tool function available (already imported in <execute> environment)'. The env passes it into the prompt templates. (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/__init__.py#L8-L18; https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/envs/general_env.py#L122, #L287)
- **Bridge.** No bridge. A tool call is a direct Python call in the same process, inside the IPython shell (P1, P9 with 5 host calls). (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/envs/general_env.py#L138-L152 (handle_tool_call calls self.python_repl(env_input)))
- **Isolation boundary.** None in the executor. PythonREPL is commented 'This PythonREPL is not used by the environment; It is THE ENVIRONMENT' and has no restriction on imports, builtins or files. The NOT_USED signature shows the class is not a tool. The repo's only sandbox language is in mint/utils/exec.py, which is the human-eval correctness harness, and it tells users to sandbox it. The containerized engine is in the chat demo, not the agent environment. (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/python_tool.py#L10-L16; https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/utils/exec.py#L52-L57; https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/README.md (containerized engine, chat UI); https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py#L239 (JupyterGatewayDocker))
- **Output channel.** __call__ returns only the captured stdout. An empty output becomes '[Executed Successfully with No Output]'. The traceback path is redacted by regex. The expression value of the last line appears only as an Out line in stdout, so the 2000-char cut can remove it (P2). (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/python_tool.py#L49-L75 (__call__), #L59-L60 (empty output), #L66-L71 (path redaction), #L72-L73 (truncation))
- **Limits.** Time: timeout=30 by default, enforced by SIGALRM inside time_limit. The shell turns the TimeoutError into text, so the caller gets a string back and no exception (P6). Memory: none. Tool calls: none. The SIGALRM handler needs the main thread (a signal.signal rule), which is inferred from the Python signal docs and not probed. (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/python_tool.py#L18-L38 (signature, default timeout 30, time_limit))
- **State.** Persistent for one PythonREPL. reset() calls InteractiveShell.clear_instance() and makes a new shell from a copy of user_ns. GeneralEnv creates one PythonREPL in __init__ (general_env.py:68). The reset() method I read (general_env.py:274-300) does not call python_repl.reset(), so a new episode on the same env object may keep variables. That is inferred from the lines read, not probed (P8 persists in one object). (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/python_tool.py#L40-L47 (reset); https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/envs/general_env.py#L68 (creation); #L274-L300 (reset, no python_repl call))
- **Errors.** Exceptions are not raised to the caller. IPython prints a traceback into captured stdout, and the path is redacted. The message and the 'Cell In[1], line N' line both survive (P10). The outer try in handle_tool_call only catches errors from parse_action and the call itself. (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/python_tool.py#L49-L75; https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/envs/general_env.py#L138-L152)
- **Approvals, credentials, PII.** None in the code. Anything in the host environment is readable (P5), and a shell command runs with the host's privileges (P12). The repo has no credential handling in this path. (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/mint/tools/python_tool.py (whole file))

Surprises:

- The 2000-char cut removes the last expression, which is where the return value shows up. A probe that relies on a final-expression result can lose it silently (P2).
- The README describes a containerized code execution engine, and that is true for the chat demo. The agent environment that the paper's evaluations use runs PythonREPL in the host process with no container (python_tool.py#L10-L16, general_env.py#L68).
- The 30 s limit does work as documented: P6 returned at 30.03 s. It is a SIGALRM inside the shell, so a blocking C call would not be interrupted (not probed).
- The memory allocation loop reached 4.14 GB in 0.3 s, which was faster than the 30 s alarm. No memory limit exists below the process's own limits.
- The repo's last push was 2024-05-23, so the executor is pinned to an older IPython-era design. The unpinned ipython resolved to 9.18.1.

- Source: https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified at `6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93 (2025-10-01)`

From the source:

- **Isolation boundary.** Writes the wrapped program to $TMPDIR/bun-exec-<id>.ts and spawns bun with no env option, so the child inherits the server's whole environment, and with no permission model. capabilities() still reports hasNativeIsolation: true. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/bun-runtime.ts#L68-L78; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/bun-runtime.ts#L292; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/bun-runtime.ts#L158)
- **Credentials (measured).** Program code read MCP_CONFIG_PATH from env and then the config file itself, which holds every downstream MCP server's command and env. (research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P14_credentials.txt)
- **Runtime path.** Uses $HOME/.bun/bin/bun whenever HOME is set, without checking that it exists; the 'bun' PATH fallback is unreachable. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/bun-runtime.ts#L38-L41)
- **Bridge.** Not a live bridge but a two-pass replay. Pass 1 runs the whole program with every mcp.* call returning a placeholder string and logging '__MCP_CALL__' JSON; the server then runs all logged calls with Promise.all, bakes the results into the source as literals, and runs the whole program a second time. Arguments that depend on an earlier tool result are computed from the placeholder, and every side effect happens twice (P13). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L903-L918; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L946-L1021; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L1111-L1134; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P13_twoPass.txt)
- **API shape.** A generated `const mcp = { <server>: { <tool>: async (args) => __mcpCall('<server>.<tool>', args) } }` proxy is prepended to the program. Results come back wrapped as {content, text, parsed, isError, helpers}, so `r.value` is undefined and the value sits at r.parsed.value (P1). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L403-L466; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L974-L1007)
- **Discovery.** On-demand mode (the default) tells the model to read the resource mcp://types/declarations, but reading it always fails: loadTypeScriptDeclarations calls require() inside an ES module. The model gets no tool names. auto-include mode (CODEMODE_TYPE_EXPOSURE) lists every tool in the description instead. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L35; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L327-L340; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L513-L529; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P15_discovery.txt)
- **Setup.** Tool access is off unless CODEMODE_ENABLE_MCP_INTEGRATION=true, which the README does not mention. execute_code defaults to runtime 'quickjs', although the README recommends Bun. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L1359; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879)
- **Credentials.** Tools run in the MCP server process, but on startup it prints the first 20 characters of every downstream MCP server env value with console.log, which goes to stdout, the MCP protocol channel. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L281; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/envlog-stdout.txt)
- **Limits.** execute_code takes a timeout (default 30 s) and nothing else; getRuntime builds every runtime with only {type}, so the memoryLimit, Deno permission and E2B apiKey fields in RuntimeConfig cannot be set through the MCP server. No output cap, no tool-call cap. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L502-L508; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L945)
- **HTTP mode.** The HTTP backend's /execute ignores the `runtime` field shown in the README curl example; its sandbox manager only wraps QuickJS. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/server.ts#L109-L128; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/index.ts#L9-L19)
- **Maintenance.** 27 commits, last on 2025-10-01, single author; package.json says MIT but the repo has no LICENSE file; not published to npm. The README badge says 'Production Ready'. (git log at 6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93; npm view @danieliser/codemode-unified -> 404)

Surprises:

- Tool calls are replayed, not bridged: the program runs twice, and a call whose arguments depend on an earlier result gets the placeholder's value (lookup(a.parsed.value) was called with id -1 and returned {id: -1, value: -2}).
- A file-append side effect in a program with one tool call happened twice.
- The model is told to read mcp://types/declarations, which always errors, so in the default mode it cannot learn the tool names.
- README says 'Sandboxed execution with memory/CPU limits' and 'Network access controls'; the Bun runtime has neither, and reads host files, env and runs shell commands.
- Default runtime is quickjs, not the recommended Bun.

From the source:

- **Isolation boundary.** Deno's permission flags are the boundary: --allow-net and --no-prompt always; read, write and env only when ExecutionOptions.permissions asks, which the MCP server never passes. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/deno-runtime.ts#L202-L222)
- **Runtime path.** Uses $HOME/.deno/bin/deno whenever HOME is set, without checking it exists; a deno installed elsewhere (Homebrew here) fails initialisation with 'Deno not found'. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/deno-runtime.ts#L38-L41; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/deno-runtime.ts#L44-L52)
- **Bridge.** Not a live bridge but a two-pass replay. Pass 1 runs the whole program with every mcp.* call returning a placeholder string and logging '__MCP_CALL__' JSON; the server then runs all logged calls with Promise.all, bakes the results into the source as literals, and runs the whole program a second time. Arguments that depend on an earlier tool result are computed from the placeholder, and every side effect happens twice (P13). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L903-L918; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L946-L1021; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L1111-L1134; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P13_twoPass.txt)
- **API shape.** A generated `const mcp = { <server>: { <tool>: async (args) => __mcpCall('<server>.<tool>', args) } }` proxy is prepended to the program. Results come back wrapped as {content, text, parsed, isError, helpers}, so `r.value` is undefined and the value sits at r.parsed.value (P1). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L403-L466; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L974-L1007)
- **Discovery.** On-demand mode (the default) tells the model to read the resource mcp://types/declarations, but reading it always fails: loadTypeScriptDeclarations calls require() inside an ES module. The model gets no tool names. auto-include mode (CODEMODE_TYPE_EXPOSURE) lists every tool in the description instead. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L35; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L327-L340; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L513-L529; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P15_discovery.txt)
- **Setup.** Tool access is off unless CODEMODE_ENABLE_MCP_INTEGRATION=true, which the README does not mention. execute_code defaults to runtime 'quickjs', although the README recommends Bun. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L1359; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879)
- **Credentials.** Tools run in the MCP server process, but on startup it prints the first 20 characters of every downstream MCP server env value with console.log, which goes to stdout, the MCP protocol channel. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L281; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/envlog-stdout.txt)
- **Limits.** execute_code takes a timeout (default 30 s) and nothing else; getRuntime builds every runtime with only {type}, so the memoryLimit, Deno permission and E2B apiKey fields in RuntimeConfig cannot be set through the MCP server. No output cap, no tool-call cap. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L502-L508; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L945)
- **HTTP mode.** The HTTP backend's /execute ignores the `runtime` field shown in the README curl example; its sandbox manager only wraps QuickJS. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/server.ts#L109-L128; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/index.ts#L9-L19)
- **Maintenance.** 27 commits, last on 2025-10-01, single author; package.json says MIT but the repo has no LICENSE file; not published to npm. The README badge says 'Production Ready'. (git log at 6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93; npm view @danieliser/codemode-unified -> 404)

Surprises:

- Network is always on (--allow-net with no host list), so code can reach any host, including services on localhost.
- Same two-pass replay as Bun: a dependent tool call got the placeholder's value (id -1).
- The runtime looks only at ~/.deno/bin/deno, so a Homebrew deno is not found.

### CodeMode Unified, QuickJS runtime (the default runtime)

- Source: https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified at `6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93 (2025-10-01)`
- Language and engine: JS/TS, QuickJS WASM (quickjs-emscripten 0.23) in the MCP server process; a pool of reused contexts with no memory or interrupt limits
- How it was run: MCP stdio server dist/mcp-server.js (CODEMODE_ENABLE_MCP_INTEGRATION=true, MCP_CONFIG_PATH naming a stdio MCP server that serves `lookup`), tool execute_code {code, runtime: 'quickjs'}. Probes run in the script form this runtime accepts (last expression is the result; no await, return or console), most on a new server each, because a reused context rejects every program after the first
- Defaults: time 30 s setTimeout that cannot interrupt synchronous evaluation; memory none configured; output no cap; tool_calls not possible (console missing, no async)
- Hardened config: execute_code argument timeout: 5000 (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879)

From the source:

- **Isolation boundary.** Contexts come from one shared WASM module, are pooled (max(2, cpus/2)) and reused for up to 100 executions; the security configuration methods are empty ('No configuration for now - minimal test'). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/quickjs-runtime.ts#L29-L35; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/quickjs-runtime.ts#L125-L143; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/quickjs-runtime.ts#L164-L189)
- **Limits.** evalCode runs synchronously inside a Promise whose timeout is a setTimeout; no interrupt handler or memory limit is set, so neither time nor memory is bounded by the implementation. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/quickjs-runtime.ts#L196-L223)
- **Language.** The adapter declares supportsAsync false, and the code is evaluated as a global script, so `await`, top-level `return` and console are unavailable; the MCP prelude that relies on console.log therefore fails. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/quickjs-runtime.ts#L61-L71; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/quickjs-runtime.ts#L223)

Surprises:

- The default runtime cannot call tools at all: the injected bridge needs console.log and await, which this runtime lacks.

### OpenAI Codex CLI code mode (codex-code-mode-host, V8)

- Source: https://github.com/openai/codex (installed @openai/codex via bun ships codex-code-mode-host) at `codex-cli 0.169.0; source tag rust-v0.169.0 = d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4`
- Language and engine: JS (ES module), V8 isolate (rusty v8 with v8_enable_sandbox) in a separate codex-code-mode-host process that is spawned without Seatbelt
- How it was run: Python client spawns the shipped codex-code-mode-host binary and speaks its default framed-JSON stdio protocol (same handshake and capabilities as codex-rs/code-mode remote_session), opens a session with server-side output truncation as Codex core does, executes cells with one function tool `lookup`, and answers tool/invoke delegate requests; no model.
- Defaults: time none; cells yield to the caller after 10 s (DEFAULT_EXEC_YIELD_TIME_MS) and keep running until terminated or interrupted; memory none enforced; V8 default heap (~1.4 GB observed) then fatal OOM of the host process; output 10,000 tokens per exec call by default (DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_PER_EXEC_CALL), truncated with a warning header; 1 MiB bounded-output cap on the wire; tool_calls no count limit observed; capability 'delegate-capacity-4096' advertises 4,096 concurrent delegate requests
- Hardened config: No Codex config key, host CLI flag or env var sets a time or heap limit: [features.code_mode] only has default_exec_yield_time_ms, experimental_show_cell_overhead, tool_input_schema_max_bytes, excluded_tool_namespaces, direct_only_tool_namespaces (features/src/feature_configs.rs:38-60); codex-code-mode-host takes only --listen and --otel-trace-listen/--otel-trace-exporter (code-mode-host/src/main.rs:20-43); Codex core always opens sessions with default (empty) limits (core/src/code_mode_host.rs:64-66, core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:257). So the strictest public knobs are the host's stdio protocol fields, sent directly: session/open cellExecutionLimits {maxHeapSizeBytes: 67108864 (64 MiB, chosen), maxYieldTimeMs: 1000 (chosen)} (code-mode-protocol/src/host/payload.rs:26-31, host/message.rs:186-194), outputTruncation server; session/execute yield_time_ms 1000, max_output_tokens 1000 (payload.rs:205-211). The host advertises session-cell-execution-resource-limits and replies session/ready, then drops the heap limit (code-mode-runtime/src/service.rs:59-71 sets max_heap_size_bytes: None; isolates use CreateParams::default, runtime/mod.rs:191), so it counts as absent. maxYieldTimeMs only caps when the caller gets a Yielded snapshot (service.rs:257-270). session/terminate is a real kill (out/codemode/hardened-P6-terminate.txt) but only on request: core sends it when the model calls wait with terminate:true (core/src/tools/code_mode/wait_handler.rs:129) or the user interrupts (core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs:171), so it is not a limit. A separate run that sent session/terminate after the first yield got Terminated at 1.06 s and the same session and a new session then ran a trivial cell, so terminate works but nothing sends it automatically. | research/probes/codex-sandbox/out/codemode/hardened-P6.txt and research/probes/codex-sandbox/out/codemode/hardened-P6-terminate.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** Generated: Codex renders a TypeScript declaration `declare const tools: { name(args: {...}): Promise<...> }` from each tool's JSON Schema into the exec tool description; in V8 each enabled tool becomes a function on the `tools` object, named by normalize_code_mode_identifier. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/description.rs#L465-L473, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/description.rs#L417, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/globals.rs#L65-L78)
- **Discovery.** Upfront by default (all enabled tools declared in the description, plus an ALL_TOOLS global); feature code_mode_tool_search adds ranked in-code search, and code_mode_only hides direct tools behind exec/wait. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/globals.rs#L80, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L150-L170, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs#L436)
- **Bridge.** Separate host process. Core and host exchange u32-length-prefixed JSON frames over stdio (or gRPC over stdio). A tools.x() call becomes a delegate/request tool/invoke frame to Codex core, which runs the tool through its normal router and answers with delegate/response. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/host/codec.rs#L11-L47, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/host/message.rs#L132-L240, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/callbacks.rs#L15)
- **Isolation boundary.** V8 isolate with the V8 sandbox build flag; console, Atomics, SharedArrayBuffer and WebAssembly are deleted; imports are rejected. The host process itself is spawned with plain Command (no Seatbelt), with Codex-internal tokens scrubbed from its env. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/Cargo.toml#L30, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/globals.rs#L16-L24, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/module_loader.rs#L192, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode/src/remote_session/connection.rs#L164-L176, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/core/src/code_mode_host.rs#L246-L256)
- **Output channel.** Only what the cell emits through text()/image()/content() returns as content_items, plus error_text. Server-side truncation to max_output_tokens (default 10,000) with a 'Warning: truncated output' header. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-protocol/src/runtime.rs#L15-L17, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/output/output_render.rs#L62, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/utils/output-truncation/src/lib.rs#L42)
- **Limits.** The protocol carries max_heap_size_bytes, but CodeModeService::with_options overwrites it with None and the runtime creates isolates with default CreateParams, so no heap cap is applied (only the UI engine gets 64 MB). No wall-clock limit; yield_time_ms only controls when the caller gets a Yielded snapshot. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/service.rs#L59-L71, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/mod.rs#L191, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/ui/engine.rs#L23-L25)
- **State.** Fresh V8 context per cell; a session-level key/value store (store/load) is snapshotted into each cell. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/session_runtime/mod.rs#L46-L48, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/callbacks.rs#L215)
- **Errors.** Uncaught errors return as content 'Script error:\n<message + stack>' and error_text, with exec_main.mjs line:col. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/code-mode-runtime/src/runtime/module_loader.rs#L16, research/probes/codex-sandbox/out/codemode/P10.txt)
- **Other.** Feature `code_mode` is stage UnderDevelopment and default off; sub-flags select the standalone host, gRPC transport, prewarm, interrupt handling and code-mode-only. Async: top-level await, Promise.all, setTimeout and notify() are available. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L1305-L1310, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L150-L170)

Surprises:

- Codex was briefed as having no code mode; codex-cli 0.169.0 ships one (codex-code-mode-host, 70 MB V8 binary) behind the `code_mode` feature flag.
- max_heap_size_bytes is part of the wire protocol and the host advertises 'session-cell-execution-resource-limits', yet service.rs forces the heap limit to None; an allocation loop crashes the entire host process (P7).
- No execution time limit: a busy loop keeps a cell alive indefinitely and only yields observations every 10 s (P6).
- The code-mode host runs outside Seatbelt; the only boundary for model-written JS is the V8 isolate, while shell commands get Seatbelt.
- A bare final expression is discarded; output must go through text() (console is deleted) (P2).

### OpenAI Codex CLI shell sandbox (macOS Seatbelt via `codex sandbox`)

- Source: https://github.com/openai/codex (installed @openai/codex via bun) at `codex-cli 0.169.0; source tag rust-v0.169.0 = d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4`
- Language and engine: shell / python3 (any process), /usr/bin/sandbox-exec with a generated Seatbelt (SBPL) profile; the command runs as a normal macOS process under it
- How it was run: `codex sandbox [-c sandbox_mode="workspace-write"] -- <argv>` from the native vendor binary, CODEX_HOME pointed at an empty folder so no user config applies; each probe ran in the default read-only mode and in workspace-write; no model call.
- Defaults: time none in Seatbelt or `codex sandbox`; the agent's one-shot exec defaults to 10 s (DEFAULT_EXEC_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS); memory none; output none in `codex sandbox` (inherited stdio); agent exec captures up to 1 MiB and returns 10,000 tokens by default to the model; tool_calls not applicable (no tool bridge)
- Hardened config: codex sandbox -c shell_environment_policy.inherit="core" -c shell_environment_policy.ignore_default_excludes=false -c 'permissions.hardened.filesystem={":minimal"="read",":workspace_roots"="read","/opt/homebrew/Cellar/python@3.15/3.15.0_1"="read","/etc/**"="deny","/private/etc/**"="deny"}' -c permissions.hardened.network.enabled=false -P hardened -C research/probes/codex-sandbox/work -- <argv>, with CODEX_HOME at the empty research/impls/codex-sandbox/codex-home-hardened. Sources (research/impls/codex-sandbox/src/codex-rs (tag rust-v0.169.0)): env inherit modes all/core/none (protocol/src/config_types.rs:207-218; core keeps PATH, SHELL, TMPDIR, HOME, LANG, LC_*, LOGNAME, USER, protocol/src/shell_environment.rs:178-181), applied by codex sandbox at cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs:257; ignore_default_excludes defaults true (config/src/shell_environment_policy.rs:136); permission profiles with filesystem read/write/deny entries, special paths and network.enabled (config/src/permissions_toml.rs:113-119, 224-231, 330-348; core/src/config/permissions.rs:834-848); -P/--permission-profile and -C (cli/src/lib.rs:59-79). The python keg read grant is needed because :minimal does not cover Homebrew. A plain "/etc"="deny" entry is silently overridden under :minimal (platform defaults allow /etc, sandboxing/src/seatbelt_read_only_platform_defaults.sbpl:94-95; path denies are only carved out of a matching readable root, sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs:957), so the glob form is used (out/hardened-P4-variants.txt). No time, CPU or memory option exists: codex sandbox waits on the child with no timeout (cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs:438) and Seatbelt profiles carry no resource rules.

From the source:

- **API shape.** No tool API. The sandbox wraps one argv: SandboxManager.transform builds `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec -p <policy> -D... -- <argv>`. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs#L405-L436, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L61, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L1048-L1057)
- **Discovery.** Not applicable to the sandbox. (Codex code mode has its own discovery; see the codex-codemode results.) (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L150-L153)
- **Bridge.** None. The child inherits stdin/stdout/stderr and `codex sandbox` waits for exit with no timeout. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs#L520-L534, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs#L438)
- **Isolation boundary.** Seatbelt profile starting with (deny default), then allow process-exec/fork so children inherit the policy, allow-listed sysctls and mach services. Read access is full-disk `(allow file-read*)` for the default profiles; writes only to writable roots (none in read-only, cwd + temp dirs in workspace-write); network rules are added only when network is enabled, so the default emits none. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt_base_policy.sbpl#L7-L13, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L926-L931, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L354-L366, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt.rs#L989-L1036)
- **Output channel.** `codex sandbox` passes stdio through. In the agent, one-shot exec caps raw output at DEFAULT_OUTPUT_BYTES_CAP (1 MiB) and unified exec returns at most 10,000 tokens by default. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/core/src/exec.rs#L80, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/mod.rs#L74-L76)
- **Limits.** No CPU, memory or process-count rules in the SBPL files or the generated sections. Time limits exist only in the agent: DEFAULT_EXEC_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS = 10,000. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/sandboxing/src/seatbelt_base_policy.sbpl#L1-L116, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/core/src/exec.rs#L62)
- **State.** Fresh process per command. `codex sandbox` with no flags uses legacy read-only mode unless the config uses permission profiles or the CLI passes sandbox_mode. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs#L585-L626)
- **Errors.** Whatever the process writes to stderr plus its exit code; Seatbelt denials surface as EPERM ('Operation not permitted') or, for network, as DNS resolution failures. --log-denials can print the denials. (research/probes/codex-sandbox/out/P3.txt, research/probes/codex-sandbox/out/P12.txt)
- **Other.** Environment: shell_environment_policy defaults to inherit=All and ignore_default_excludes=true, so host secrets pass to sandboxed commands unless configured; only a fixed list of Codex-internal tokens is always scrubbed. CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt and CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1 are injected. (https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/config/src/shell_environment_policy.rs#L135-L136, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/protocol/src/shell_environment.rs#L14-L21, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/protocol/src/shell_environment.rs#L139-L143, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs#L397-L404, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox.rs#L525-L527)

Surprises:

- Codex does have a code mode: codex-cli 0.169.0 ships codex-code-mode-host (V8) behind the `code_mode` feature flag (stage UnderDevelopment, off by default). Probed separately in research/probes/codex-sandbox/out/codemode/.
- Secrets in the host environment reach sandboxed commands by default: the *KEY*/*SECRET*/*TOKEN* exclude list exists but ignore_default_excludes defaults to true (P5).
- Read-only still means full-disk read: any file the user can read is readable inside the sandbox (P4).
- Blocked network surfaces as 'Could not resolve host' / 'nodename nor servname provided', not a permission error, which can mislead a model into retrying (P3).
- No time or memory limit at the sandbox layer; limits live in the agent's exec tool only (P6, P7).

### Datalayer Agent Codemode, eval sandbox (default variant)

- Source: https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode (installed from the clone); sandbox from PyPI code-sandboxes (repo https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes) at `agent-codemode 566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea (version 1.1.1), code-sandboxes 1.12.4 (tag v1.12.4 = d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5; installed files identical), mcp 2.3.0`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython exec() in the host process. Code that contains 'await ' is wrapped in an async function and run with asyncio.run() on the worker thread that CodeModeExecutor hands it to (asyncio.to_thread).
- How it was run: ToolRegistry with one stdio MCP server (lookup_server.py), CodeModeExecutor(registry, CodeModeConfig(sandbox_variant='eval')).setup(), then executor.execute(code, timeout=30), the call that the project's MCP server handler and pydantic-ai toolset make.
- Defaults: time None enforced. execute() takes a timeout and the MCP server passes 30 s, but EvalSandbox.run_code documents 'timeout: Timeout in seconds (not enforced in this simple implementation)' (eval.py:166). P6 ran 120 s until the harness stopped it.; memory None. P7 reached 4.4 GB host RSS in 2.3 s and was killed by the harness.; output stdout, stderr and the last expression's repr all come back, untruncated (P2: all 200,000 A's plus 'RETURNED').; tool_calls CodeModeConfig.max_tool_calls defaults to None (types.py:233); when set, executor.call_tool raises 'Tool call limit exceeded' (executor.py:1094-1096). Not reachable here because tool calls hang (P1).
- Hardened config: sandbox_client=CodeSandboxClient.create(variant='eval', config=SandboxConfig(timeout=30, network_policy='none', env_vars={}, memory_limit=256 MiB, cpu_limit=1.0)) passed to CodeModeExecutor, plus CodeModeConfig(max_tool_calls=50) and execute(timeout=30). SandboxConfig fields at code_sandboxes/models.py:576-618; network_policy is the only one EvalSandbox reads (eval.py:406-455).

From the source:

- **API shape.** Typed Python bindings are generated on disk from each MCP server's tool list: one async function per tool in generated/mcp/<server>/<tool>.py, all calling generated/client.py call_tool(), which awaits a host-registered __call_tool__. Code imports them: 'from generated.mcp.probe import lookup'. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/discovery/codegen.py#L21-L127; https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L224-L269)
- **Discovery.** On demand: list_tool_names (fast, deferred tools hidden), search_tools (keyword overlap count over name plus description, not BM25 or embeddings) and get_tool_details. Tools can be marked defer_loading. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/discovery/registry.py#L226-L318; https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/toolset.py#L320-L450)
- **Bridge.** For eval, executor.call_tool is injected into the exec namespace as __call_tool__ and calls the host ToolRegistry's MCP client directly. The MCP session is created on the main event loop during discover_all, but the user code runs in asyncio.run() on a worker thread, so the first tool call waits forever on a session bound to another loop. P1 and P9 hung with 0 host calls over both stdio and streamable HTTP; out/P1-stack.txt shows the worker thread parked in asyncio.run inside eval.py _run_coroutine_sync. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/eval/eval.py#L219-L263; https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L1222-L1336; https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/proxy/mcp_client.py#L97-L120; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-eval/out/P1-stack.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** None. The module and class docstrings say 'This sandbox does NOT provide security isolation. Do not use for executing untrusted code.' The namespace gets the real __builtins__. The project still makes eval the default sandbox_variant, and the docs call the sandbox 'isolated' ('Code executes in an isolated sandbox for safety'). (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/eval/eval.py#L5-L12; #L43-L55; #L90; https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/types.py#L229; https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/docs/docs/programmatic-tools/index.mdx#L231)
- **Network policy.** network_policy='none' monkeypatches socket.create_connection and socket.socket.connect for the duration of run_code. That stopped urllib (hardened P3) but not a connect on the C-level _socket.socket class, which reached example.com:443 in both configs (P3x). The patch is also process-wide, so it briefly blocks the host's own sockets while sandbox code runs. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/eval/eval.py#L406-L455; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-eval/out/hardened-P3x.txt)
- **Credentials.** CodeModeExecutor.setup() copies the whole host environment into SandboxConfig.env_vars (env_vars = dict(os.environ)) for every variant, and execute() can inject OAuth identity tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN and others) into os.environ inside the sandbox. For eval the code shares the host's os.environ anyway (P5 read s3cr3t in both configs). (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L243-L252; #L1157-L1182; #L1-L23 (module docstring))
- **Output channel.** ExecutionResult carries stdout and stderr lines plus result reprs; the MCP server handler returns stdout, stderr and error fields. No truncation in either path. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/server.py#L313-L352; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-eval/out/P2.txt)
- **State.** Persistent: one exec namespace per context for the executor's lifetime (P8 printed 7). Variables assigned in async code are copied back from locals() into the namespace. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/eval/eval.py#L250-L279)
- **Errors.** Exceptions become CodeError(name, value, traceback.format_exc()), so the message and '<sandbox>' line numbers survive (P10). (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/eval/eval.py#L342-L352)
- **Anything else.** MCPClient.call_tool catches every exception and returns {'error': str(e)} instead of raising, so a failed tool call looks like a normal return value to the code (seen as {'error': 'Connection closed'} in the jupyter variant, datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P9d.txt). BSD-3-Clause, pushed 2026-11-21. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/proxy/mcp_client.py#L221-L260)

Surprises:

- The default variant cannot call a tool: the first await on a generated binding hangs forever (P1, P9), over stdio and over HTTP. The README's Quick Start shows exactly this pattern.
- execute(timeout=30) is accepted but not enforced for eval, so a hung tool call or an infinite loop never returns (P1, P6).
- The docs page says code 'executes in an isolated sandbox for safety' while the default variant's own docstring says it provides no isolation (P4, P5, P12 all reach the host).
- network_policy='none' is a monkeypatch that a raw _socket connect bypasses (P3x).
- Every variant receives a copy of the full host environment through SandboxConfig.env_vars.

### Datalayer Agent Codemode, jupyter-server sandbox variant (local Jupyter Server it starts itself)

- Source: https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode; sandbox from PyPI code-sandboxes (repo https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes) at `agent-codemode 566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea (1.1.1), code-sandboxes 1.12.4 (tag v1.12.4 = d7030b0b), jupyter_server and ipykernel from the same venv`
- Language and engine: Python, An ipykernel process on the host, started by a Jupyter Server subprocess that the sandbox launches with the host interpreter, driven over HTTP and websockets by jupyter-kernel-client. Same user, same machine, same environment as the host.
- How it was run: Same harness as datalayer-codemode-eval with sandbox_variant='jupyter-server'. The client is built as CodeModeExecutor.setup() builds it (SandboxConfig(timeout=30, working_dir, env_vars=dict(os.environ))) plus port=41520 and python_executable=<venv python>, because the variant otherwise binds 8888 and runs `python` from PATH.
- Defaults: time SandboxConfig.timeout=30 is passed to execute_interactive (jupyter_server.py:779-782). At 30 s the caller gets an empty, successful-looking result, but the kernel is not interrupted: it stayed at 100% CPU and the next execution in the session hung until the harness stopped it (P6b).; memory None. P7 reached 4.0 GB in 9.3 s and was killed by the harness.; output stdout, stderr and the execute_result text all come back, untruncated (P2). Errors carry an ANSI-coloured IPython traceback.; tool_calls CodeModeConfig.max_tool_calls defaults to None (types.py:233). It is enforced only in the host's executor.call_tool, which this variant's in-kernel MCP clients never call.
- Hardened config: SandboxConfig(timeout=30, network_policy='none', env_vars={}, memory_limit=256 MiB, cpu_limit=1.0) with port=41520, passed as sandbox_client; CodeModeConfig(max_tool_calls=50). JupyterServerSandbox reads none of network_policy, env_vars, memory_limit or cpu_limit for a server it starts, so every hardened probe matched the default.
