From the source:

- **Bridge.** Not a host bridge. Without mcp_proxy_url, setup sends the host's MCP server configs (command, args, env) into the kernel and builds agent_codemode MCPClient objects there, so the kernel spawns its own copy of each MCP server and calls it directly (P1: 42, one call, logged by a server process the kernel started). Credentials that a server needs must therefore be readable by the kernel. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L536-L599; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P1.txt)
- **Parallel calls.** MCPClient creates its stdio session lazily with no lock, so five concurrent first calls race: four returned {'error': 'Connection closed'} as ordinary values and one succeeded (P9d). After one warm-up call the same gather ran in parallel, 202 ms host-side (P9w). (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/proxy/mcp_client.py#L97-L120; #L221-L260; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P9d.txt; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P9w.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** None beyond a separate process. The server is started with the caller's interpreter and inherits the host environment, so files, environment, network and os.system all work (P3, P4, P5, P12), with or without env_vars={}. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/jupyter_server/jupyter_server.py#L276-L283; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/hardened-P5.txt)
- **Limits.** The execute timeout only bounds how long the client waits. On timeout the result is execution_ok=True with no error and the kernel keeps running the loop; the sandbox has an interrupt endpoint (_do_interrupt) but run_code does not call it on timeout. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/jupyter_server/jupyter_server.py#L590-L607; #L779-L800; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P6b.txt)
- **State.** Persistent kernel namespace across executions (P8 printed 7). (research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** IPython tracebacks with cell line numbers and ANSI colour codes come back in the error text (P10). (research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P10.txt)
- **Startup.** One-time setup 2.6 s (Jupyter Server plus kernel start, plus binding generation run inside the kernel); median 8.8 ms per execution afterwards (P11). (research/probes/datalayer-codemode-jupyter/out/P11.txt)

Surprises:

- The only local Datalayer variant whose tool calls work is jupyter-server, and only because the kernel runs on the host and starts its own copies of the MCP servers.
- A timeout returns a blank success and leaves the kernel spinning; the next call in the same session hangs (P6b).
- Concurrent cold tool calls fail silently with {'error': 'Connection closed'} dicts rather than exceptions (P9d).
- The variant's default port 8888 and `python` from PATH had to be overridden through constructor arguments; CodeModeConfig has no field for either.

### Docker MCP Gateway code-mode (experimental)

- Source: https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway (pkg/codemode, pkg/gateway/codemode.go) at `4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16 (2026-11-19); pkg/codemode last changed d9058bf1 (2026-10-26); goja v0.0.0-20251008123653-cf18d89f3cf6`
- Language and engine: JS (ES5.1+/ES6 subset that goja supports), goja, a pure-Go JavaScript interpreter, run in-process inside the gateway (a new goja.Runtime per call, no interrupt, no memory cap)
- How it was run: Built docker-mcp from source in golang:1.26 (CGO_ENABLED=0, vendored), ran `docker-mcp gateway run --catalog <file> --enable-all-servers --static --transport streaming` in a node:22-slim container with HOME pointed at a probe-only folder, catalog = one remote MCP server (lib/lookup-server.mjs on the host) exposing lookup. The driver calls the gateway's own `code-mode` tool ({servers:[probe], name}) and then the generated `code-mode-<name>` tool with {script}. DOCKER_MCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_REMOTE_URLS=1 (docs/security.md dev/test opt-out) was set so the gateway accepts an http:// upstream; it only affects the gateway-to-upstream URL check. --static skips image pulls and the Docker-socket network probe. A second config (config-stdio.mjs) runs the same gateway on its default stdio transport.
- Defaults: time None. runJavascript calls vm.RunString with no vm.Interrupt and ignores ctx; no timeout anywhere in pkg/codemode (exec.go:13-48).; memory None. goja has no heap cap; the gateway's --memory/--cpus flags apply to MCP server containers, not to the gateway process that runs goja.; output No cap on the return value (exec.go:42-47). console output is not returned at all; it is written to the gateway's os.Stdout (console.go:19-41).; tool_calls No cap.; hardened_null_reason The gateway exposes no code-mode option: no timeout, memory, or output setting exists for code-mode (pkg/codemode has no configuration struct). --block-network, --block-secrets, --cpus and --memory apply to the tool servers' containers, not to the in-process goja runtime. Running the gateway itself in a memory-limited container is a deployment wrapper, so per RUBRIC it does not count.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each tool of the selected servers becomes a global JS function of the same name via vm.Set(tool.Name, callTool(...)). Docs for the model are generated from the MCP input schema by toolToJsDoc as `name(args: ArgsObject): string` plus a field list, and concatenated into the generated tool's description after a fixed prompt that says calls are synchronous and the script must return a string. (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L20-L29, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/functions.go#L11-L86, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/codemode.go#L12-L26 and #L47-L61)
- **Discovery.** Two steps. The model finds servers with mcp-find (catalog search) and enables them with mcp-add, then calls `code-mode` with {servers, name}. The gateway registers a new tool `code-mode-<name>` whose description holds every tool doc of those servers. So discovery is per-server, but all tools of a chosen server go into one description upfront. Servers must already be enabled for the session. (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/gateway/codemode.go#L48-L135, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/gateway/dynamic_mcps.go#L155-L184)
- **Bridge.** Direct in-process Go call: the JS function marshals its args, drops nil non-required keys, and invokes the registered MCP ToolHandler synchronously, returning only the first TextContent. The handler is the same one direct calls use, so the gateway's invoke policy and audit apply to code-mode calls (tool_policy.go comment). (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L50-L101, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/gateway/tool_policy.go#L36-L40)
- **Isolation boundary.** goja in the gateway process, not a separate sandbox process or container. The guest has no fs, net, process or require (P3-P5, P12), which matches the docs' claim that it "can only interact through MCP tools". But the docs' "isolated sandbox" has no resource boundary: no interrupt, no heap cap, and it shares the gateway's address space and stdout. (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L13-L48; docs https://docs.docker.com/ai/mcp-catalog-and-toolkit/dynamic-mcp/)
- **Output channel.** Only the return value goes back, formatted with fmt.Sprintf("%v"); undefined becomes "<no output>". console.* is fmt.Fprintln(os.Stdout). On the default stdio transport (gateway.go sets Transport: "stdio" in both in-container and on-host defaults) the gateway's stdout is the JSON-RPC channel, so guest prints become protocol messages. out/stdio-inject.txt: a script printed a forged tools/call response for the pending request id, and the MCP client returned "FORGED by guest console.log for id 2" instead of the real "REAL". (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/console.go#L19-L41, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L40-L47, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/cmd/docker-mcp/commands/gateway.go#L41 and #L55, research/probes/docker-mcp-gateway-codemode/out/stdio-inject.txt)
- **Limits.** None for time, memory, output, or call count. The infinite-loop goroutine outlives the client (P6) and memory growth is bounded only by the OS (P7). (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L13-L48)
- **State.** Fresh goja.Runtime per execution; nothing persists. The generated code-mode-<name> tool itself persists in the gateway for the session. (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L14, https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/gateway/codemode.go#L124-L135)
- **Errors.** Compile and runtime errors are returned as a successful tool result with text "Error running script: <goja error>", including <eval>:line:col; isError is never set. A tool handler error surfaces as a thrown Go error inside JS. (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L35-L38)
- **Credentials.** Tool servers run in their own containers (or as remotes) with secrets injected by the gateway; the JS never sees them. The goja runtime gets only console and the tool functions. (https://github.com/docker/mcp-gateway/blob/4b5180c5ba8e1b456c53b36b7f90f17964131a16/pkg/codemode/exec.go#L14-L29)

Surprises:

- Default stdio transport + console.log = JSON-RPC injection: model-written code can forge MCP responses to the client (out/stdio-inject.txt). The client accepted a forged result for the pending tool call and dropped the real one.
- The SPEC's await forms are all SyntaxErrors: the script is wrapped in a non-async IIFE and tools are synchronous, so Promise.all gives no parallelism (P9 1,018 ms for 5 x 200 ms).
- Docs say "isolated sandbox"; the code is an in-process goja runtime with no timeout, no memory cap, and no cancellation. One `while(true){}` pins a gateway core until restart; one allocation loop takes the whole gateway down.
- Errors come back as success (isError false) with text "Error running script: ...".
- console output is never returned to the model even though the prompt comment says console is there "to help the LLM debug its own code" (exec.go:16).
- The gateway refuses http:// remote MCP URLs unless DOCKER_MCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_REMOTE_URLS=1, and `--servers` silently disables dynamic tools (so code-mode only exists with --enable-all-servers or profiles).

### DSPy RLM with tools= (PythonInterpreter: Pyodide on Deno)

- Source: https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy (dspy/predict/rlm.py, dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py, dspy/primitives/runner.js); PyPI dspy at `dspy 3.5.0 from PyPI = stanfordnlp/dspy tag 3.5.0 = 4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404 (clone at research/impls/dspy-rlm/src; diff -r against the installed package differs only in __metadata__.py's version stamp and one .code-workspace file). Runtime: Pyodide 0.29.4 (npm, pinned in runner.js:3), Deno 2.9.8 (host install, found on PATH), CPython 3.12. DSPY_CACHEDIR and DENO_DIR pointed into research/impls/dspy-rlm/.`
- Language and engine: Python (full CPython compiled to WASM), Pyodide 0.29.4 (CPython in WebAssembly) inside a `deno run` subprocess with only --allow-read for the runner file and Deno's cache (cache read revoked after start-up); no --allow-net, --allow-env, --allow-write or --allow-run by default. JSON-RPC over the subprocess's stdin/stdout.
- How it was run: dspy.RLM('question -> answer', tools=[lookup]) with the default interpreter_factory=PythonInterpreter, driven by dspy.utils.DummyLM returning a scripted {plan, code} action per iteration (probe code, then SUBMIT). One probe execution = one rlm(question=...) forward. What the model sees is read from the next LM request (the chat message after the assistant turn that held the code). No LLM, no API key.
- Defaults: time None. PythonInterpreter has no timeout option and blocks on readline() until Deno answers (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:677-688 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L677-L688); execute loop research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:862-946 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L862-L946)). RLM's max_iters=20 bounds iterations, not time. Observed P6: no-limit-within-120s.; memory No DSPy option. The only ceiling is wasm32's 4 GiB address space (Pyodide's memory maximum is 65,536 pages, research/impls/dspy-rlm/deno-cache/npm/registry.npmjs.org/pyodide/0.29.4/pyodide.asm.js). Observed P7: MemoryError after 3.0 s at 2.5 GB peak host tree RSS; host alive, and the same interpreter ran the next iteration (out/P7next.txt).; output max_output_chars=10,000 per REPL entry, head 5,000 + tail 5,000 with '... (N characters omitted) ...' (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:327 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L327); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/repl_types.py:156-164 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/repl_types.py#L156-L164)). The sandbox returns the last expression's value if it is not None, else captured stdout, never both (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/runner.js:495-499 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/runner.js#L495-L499)).; tool_calls No cap on user tool calls. max_llm_calls=50 caps llm_query/llm_query_batched and sandbox sub-agent LM calls per forward (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:326 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L326)). Tool calls are serial: each blocks the guest in pyodide.ffi.run_sync and the host handles one at a time (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/runner.js:59-60 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/runner.js#L59-L60); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:612-616 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L612-L616)).; hardened hardened is null: the default PythonInterpreter already has every permission off (no read beyond its runtime files, no write, env, net or run), and neither PythonInterpreter nor RLM exposes a time or memory option (python_interpreter.py:233-246, rlm.py:322-333). The only interpreter with a timeout, LocalInterpreter(execution_timeout=...), is documented as not a sandbox (docs/docs/api/tools/LocalInterpreter.md:16-19), so it is looser, not stricter.

From the source:

- **API shape.** User tools are normalized to dspy.Tool; the action prompt lists each as `name(arg: type)` - description. Inside the sandbox each tool is a generated synchronous Python def with the tool's parameter names and types, whose body JSON-encodes the kwargs and calls the JS bridge through pyodide.ffi.run_sync. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:469-488 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L469-L488); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/runner.js:44-66 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/runner.js#L44-L66))
- **Discovery.** All tools upfront: every tool signature and description is formatted into the action instructions at construction. No search or lazy loading. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:469-488 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L469-L488))
- **Bridge.** Guest code -> run_sync(JS toolCallBridge) -> a JSON-RPC 'tool_call' line on Deno's stdout -> the host's execute() loop calls the Python tool in the host process and writes the result back on stdin -> the bridge returns it as JSON. One stdin reader and a synchronous host loop make tool calls strictly serial (P9 1,051 ms for five 200 ms calls). Tools, LM credentials and host files stay on the host: the in-sandbox dspy facade sends LM calls to a host SandboxLM that keeps credentials on the wrapped LM and refuses host-file media. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/runner.js:305-363 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/runner.js#L305-L363); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:583-616 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L583-L616); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/facade.py:187-201 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/facade.py#L187-L201); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/facade.py:717-731 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/facade.py#L717-L731); research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P9.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** Two layers: Pyodide's virtual filesystem (open('/etc/hosts') -> FileNotFoundError, os.environ empty) and Deno's permission system. Pyodide's `js` module reaches the Deno global, so Deno permissions are the real boundary: js.Deno.readTextFileSync, Deno.env.get, Deno.Command and fetch all raise NotCapable. The Deno process itself inherits the full host environment (deno_subprocess_env copies os.environ), so secrets are one --allow-env flag away. Docs claim 'no filesystem or network access'; probes agree. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:300-350 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L300-L350); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/deno_utils.py:6-10; research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/docs/docs/diving-deeper/rlm.md:37; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P12jsTry.txt; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P3try.txt)
- **Output channel.** The REPL entry the model sees holds the last expression's value when it is not None, otherwise captured stdout; printed text is discarded when the code ends in an expression (P2: only 'RETURNED', none of the 200,000 A's). Each entry is cut to max_output_chars=10,000 as head+tail with an '(N characters omitted)' marker (Pcap). (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/runner.js:495-499 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/runner.js#L495-L499); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/repl_types.py:156-164 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/repl_types.py#L156-L164); research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P2.txt; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P2both.txt; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/Pcap.txt)
- **Limits.** No time limit and no memory option anywhere in PythonInterpreter or RLM; the RLM knobs are max_iters, max_llm_calls and max_output_chars. LocalInterpreter has execution_timeout, but its docs say it is not a security sandbox, so it is not a hardened option. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:233-246 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L233-L246); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:322-333 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L322-L333); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/docs/docs/api/tools/LocalInterpreter.md:1-22)
- **State.** One interpreter per forward(): variables persist across REPL iterations of one RLM call and start fresh in the next call. Start-up restores a DSPy-built Pyodide memory snapshot from $DSPY_CACHEDIR/sandbox. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:883-898 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L883-L898); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/docs/docs/diving-deeper/rlm.md:37; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P8.txt; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P8within.txt)
- **Errors.** A Python exception reaches the model as '[Error] <Type>: <args list>' (P10: "[Error] ValueError: ['probe-boom']"): no traceback, no line number. A JS-side failure that ends the Deno process (uncaught network or Deno-permission errors, os.system) raises CodeInterpreterError out of rlm(); RLM only catches CodeExecutionError and SyntaxError, so the whole forward fails and the model never sees an error. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:939 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L939); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:1034-1046 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L1034-L1046); research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P10.txt; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P3.txt; research/probes/dspy-rlm/out/P12.txt)
- **Other.** llm_query / llm_query_batched and in-sandbox dspy sub-agents (Predict, ReAct, nested RLM) are bridged to the host LM. Deno is found on PATH unless the dspy[deno] extra is installed; versions 2.x only. The sandbox cache is written under $DSPY_CACHEDIR (default ~/.dspy_cache) unless DSPY_SANDBOX_CACHE=0. (research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/predict/rlm.py:490-556 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/predict/rlm.py#L490-L556); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py:88-140 (https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy/blob/4e9db7a83e71e4c36315a2402ae7ffd0c6493404/dspy/primitives/python_interpreter.py#L88-L140); research/impls/dspy-rlm/src/docs/docs/api/tools/PythonInterpreter.md:30-36)

Surprises:

- Printed output is silently dropped whenever the code's last statement is an expression with a non-None value: runner.js returns the value instead of stdout (runner.js:499). The RLM prompt tells the model to 'ALWAYS print to see results' (rlm.py:83), so a natural trailing expression hides everything it printed. Evidence out/P2.txt (0 of 200,000 A's returned) and out/P2both.txt.
- Several blocked operations kill the sandbox instead of raising inside it: an uncaught urllib error (P3), an uncaught js.Deno permission error (P12js), and os.system (P12b, 'Pyodide has suffered a fatal error ... NotCapable: Requires env access'). Deno exits, rlm() raises CodeInterpreterError to the caller, and the run is lost. The same calls inside try/except raise catchable errors (out/P3try.txt, out/P12jsTry.txt).
- No time limit at all: P6 ran past 120 s and there is no option for one in PythonInterpreter or RLM, so a single `while True: pass` hangs the forward indefinitely.
- Error text keeps the message but loses the traceback and line number, and shows exception args as a Python list ("ValueError: ['probe-boom']").
- The Deno subprocess receives the whole host environment; only the absence of --allow-env keeps it from guest code (P12jsTry A1: NotCapable for PROBE_SECRET). A user who passes enable_env_vars for one variable grants exactly that one, which is correct, but the secret values are present in the sandbox process's own memory.
- Pyodide's subclasses walk works (P12a: 1,122 classes, Popen and _wrap_close present), but they are the WASM interpreter's, not the host's: os.popen fails with 'emscripten does not support processes.'

### Executor (UsefulSoftwareCo / Rhys Sullivan)

- Source: https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor at `c381941128ad29263baa6906d3b082ad9327ce56 (CLI package 2.0.0-beta.66; interpreter @opencode-ai/codemode@0.0.0-dev-19272 with Executor's patch patches/@opencode-ai%2Fcodemode@0.0.0-dev-19272.patch; apps framework built locally as apps@0.0.1-beta.143)`
- Language and engine: JS (TypeScript accepted: transpiled with typescript 5.8.2 before interpreting), @opencode-ai/codemode: a tree-walking JavaScript interpreter written in JS (acorn parser, Effect fibers for async), running inside the Executor server's own Node.js process and heap. Not a V8 isolate, not workerd, not a subprocess. App tools themselves run in a separate workerd process.
- How it was run: Built the local server from source (bun install, apps:build) and ran it with node on 127.0.0.1:4399; deployed an app 'probe' with tool lookup via POST /v1/apps/deploy; each probe is one MCP tools/call 'execute' over streamable HTTP /mcp with the local bearer key (calls are tools.probe.lookup({id}) because Executor namespaces tools by app).
- Defaults: time 300,000 ms wall per execute, discovery plus program (packages/mcp/src/contracts/execute.ts:511); operator can change it with EXECUTOR_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS (apps/local/server/src/contracts/config.ts:61). Approval wait does not count (verified).; memory none. The interpreter shares the server's Node heap (about 4 GB default on this machine); exceeding it crashes the server.; output none. Executor passes no maxOutputBytes (packages/mcp/src/implementation/execute.ts:1784-1785); value and logs return whole (200,000-char log came back intact).; tool_calls 100 admitted calls per execute, tools.search included (packages/mcp/src/contracts/execute.ts:512; EXECUTOR_MCP_MAX_TOOL_CALLS). Also: 65,536-char source cap (contracts/execute.ts:32 and 243), 64 live programs per server (implementation/executions.ts:767), 2,000 nested async calls (codemode promises.js:19).
- Hardened config: Private server built from the pinned local source on 127.0.0.1:41840, fresh EXECUTOR_DATA_DIR and supplied keys (research/probes/executor/hardened-start-server.sh). EXECUTOR_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS=10000 (my choice; default 300000; apps/local/server/src/contracts/config.ts:61, default packages/mcp/src/contracts/execute.ts:511, documented apps/local/server/README.md:65). EXECUTOR_MCP_MAX_TOOL_CALLS=10 (my choice; default 100; config.ts:64, README.md:66; verified honored: the 11th call failed with 'Execution exceeded its tool-call limit of 10.', out/hardened-L-calls-11.txt). No other public limit exists: McpLimits has only these two fields (packages/mcp/src/contracts/execute.ts:504-507); no memory, output-size, network, filesystem or env option for programs; EXECUTOR_EVALUATION_MEMORY_MB bounds the declaration cache, not programs (packages/sdk/src/implementation/declaration-config.ts:22,45); the self-host Docker build reads only EXECUTOR_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS (apps/hosted/self-host/src/mcp.ts:49-54) and sets no container memory limit (apps/hosted/self-host/compose.yaml). The interpreter never has fetch, process or fs (apps/docs/content/mcp.md:120-122).

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each app tool becomes a CodeMode Tool.make with the app's input/output schemas (execute.ts:1001-1009); the program sees one global proxy, tools, a path-accumulating ToolReference (codemode interpreter/runtime.js:168). Signatures are rendered to TypeScript text only when search pages are read (codemode tool-schema.js:201, 248; patches/codemode-lazy-catalog.md). (https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor/blob/c381941128ad29263baa6906d3b082ad9327ce56/packages/mcp/src/implementation/execute.ts#L1001-L1009)
- **Discovery.** On demand. The MCP surface is fixed: skills, search, describe, call, execute, resume. Inside a program, tools.search, tools.search.describe and a global search() are served by Executor's backend BM25 search (execute.ts:1751-1782; patches/codemode-host-search.md). Apps not named statically are lazy namespaces loaded on first use (execute.ts:1415, 1771; patches/codemode-lazy-namespaces.md). (https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor/blob/c381941128ad29263baa6906d3b082ad9327ce56/packages/mcp/src/implementation/execute.ts#L1751-L1782)
- **Bridge.** No serialization boundary to the interpreter: a tools.* call is an Effect forked in the same process (codemode runtime.js:230), arguments copied as JSON data (tool-runtime.js:448-450), then backend.callTool sends it to the app runtime (execute.ts:973-981), which runs the app in a separate workerd process (packages/sdk/src/implementation/workerd-apps.ts:189-190, whose own comment says 'Agent execute(code) is unrelated'). Approval pause holds the program's fibers with a custom scheduler (implementation/program-scheduler.ts, executions.ts:777). (https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor/blob/c381941128ad29263baa6906d3b082ad9327ce56/packages/sdk/src/implementation/workerd-apps.ts#L189)
- **Isolation boundary.** The code is TypeScript-transpiled and parsed with acorn (codemode interpreter/execute.js:89-108), then walked by an interpreter whose global scope is an explicit allowlist: tools, search, Promise, Symbol, Object, Math, JSON, Number, String, Boolean, Array, console, Date, RegExp, Map, Set, URL, URLSearchParams, URI functions, Error constructors (runtime.js:168-197). No this, globalThis, Function, eval, timers. The boundary is the interpreter's object model, not a process or isolate: it runs in the Executor server's Node process. Docs say so: 'Limits are cooperative, not process isolation' (apps/docs/content/mcp.md:120-122). (research/impls/executor/src/node_modules/.bun/@opencode-ai+codemode@0.0.0-dev-19272/node_modules/@opencode-ai/codemode/dist/interpreter/runtime.js:160-197)
- **Output channel.** Both value (last expression or return) and console logs, plus toolCalls with per-call outcome and duration, wrapped in {status, execution, unavailableApps}. CodeMode can truncate (execute.js:86, 119-182) but Executor never sets maxOutputBytes. (https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor/blob/c381941128ad29263baa6906d3b082ad9327ce56/packages/mcp/src/implementation/execute.ts#L1784-L1785)
- **Limits.** Time: Effect.timeoutOrElse around the program (codemode execute.js:49-78), with Executor substituting a deadline clock so approval time is excluded (execute.ts:1651-1667). The loop is stoppable because Effect preempts a fiber every 2,048 ops; patched Turn keeps JS run-to-completion (promises.js:23-31). Tool calls: recordCall throws ToolCallLimitExceeded at calls.length >= max (tool-runtime.js:403-407), and it is a catchable program error. Source: schema maxLength on the MCP input (contracts/execute.ts:243). Memory: nothing. (https://github.com/UsefulSoftwareCo/executor/blob/c381941128ad29263baa6906d3b082ad9327ce56/packages/mcp/src/contracts/execute.ts#L504-L513)
- **State.** Fresh per execution: a new Interpreter and scope per call (codemode execute.js:19-32). No snapshots; a program paused for approval lives only in server memory, and a restart loses it (docs mcp.md 'What is coming later'; resumeUnavailableMessage 'lost' in contracts/execute.ts). (research/impls/executor/src/node_modules/.bun/@opencode-ai+codemode@0.0.0-dev-19272/node_modules/@opencode-ai/codemode/dist/interpreter/execute.js:19-32)
- **Errors.** normalizeError maps a program throw to {kind: ExecutionFailure, message: 'Uncaught: <message>'} with no stack and no location (codemode interpreter/errors.js:31-54). Interpreter-detected errors (unknown identifier, unsupported syntax, bad property) do carry {line, column}. A failing tool call becomes ToolFailure with a call_ reference (execute.ts:1884-1887). (research/impls/executor/src/node_modules/.bun/@opencode-ai+codemode@0.0.0-dev-19272/node_modules/@opencode-ai/codemode/dist/interpreter/errors.js:31-54)
- **Approvals and credentials.** Approval is declared per tool in app code (always()/never()); execute returns status approval-required with requestId and the exact invocation, and resume({requestId, response:{action}}) continues the same program. Verified: a 15 s approval wait under a 10 s timeout still completed. Credentials never enter the interpreter: accounts are resolved on the host and passed to the app in workerd (execute.ts:966-981). The local bearer key at plain /mcp gets model mode, because the URL parser defaults to model (packages/mcp-auth/src/contracts/grant.ts:143). (research/probes/executor/out/short-timeout/A-approval-resume.txt)

Surprises:

- The 'sandboxed interpreter' is a JS-in-JS tree-walker running in the Executor server's own Node process. A program's memory is the server's memory: P7 crashed the whole local server with a V8 heap OOM in about 62 s and dropped every session. Docs do hedge with 'cooperative, not process isolation', but name no memory limit, and there is none.
- A one-line synchronous infinite recursion, function f(n){return f(n+1)} f(0), crashed the whole server with a heap OOM in 31.5 s, twice (peak RSS 4.4 GB). Executor's own patch notes say 'Sync recursion is unchanged: it never overflows and runs until TimeoutExceeded' (patches/codemode-run-to-completion.md:85). The 5-minute timeout never gets a chance.
- After the server crash a workerd child process was left orphaned (PPID 1).
- The 100-call cap counts tools.search calls too: search plus 100 lookups failed. Hitting the cap is a catchable exception inside the program (a try/catch loop got 100 results and the error message), but uncaught it interrupts every in-flight call (101 parallel lookups: 100 interrupted, result failed in 30 ms).
- Thrown errors keep only the message: 'Uncaught: probe-boom', with no line number or stack, even though the interpreter reports line and column for its own errors.
- Common JS idioms do not exist: globalThis, this, setTimeout, Function, Object.getPrototypeOf. Docs mention no timers; the rest is undocumented and makes the P8 and P12 probe forms fail at parse or lookup time rather than at a security check.
- Docs match on the rest: 65,536 chars passes and 65,537 is rejected by the MCP schema (-32602); while(true) is stopped at 300,010 ms; results come back whole; approval wait is excluded from the time budget; other executions stay responsive (8 ms) while one program spins.

### FastMCP CodeMode transform (experimental)

- Source: PyPI fastmcp[code-mode]; repo https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp (fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py); docs https://gofastmcp.com/docs/servers/transforms/code-mode at `fastmcp 4.2.4 (tag v4.2.4 = 5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9; installed code_mode.py is byte-identical to the tag), pydantic-monty 1.6.0 (tag v1.6.0 = 3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829)`
- Language and engine: Python (Monty subset), Monty, a Rust Python-subset interpreter, run by pydantic-monty's AsyncMonty in a separate `monty subprocess` worker process. CodeMode opens a new worker pool per execute call (out/worker-processes.txt shows the worker as a child of the server process).
- How it was run: FastMCP('probe', transforms=[CodeMode()]) with a `lookup` tool, driven by an in-process fastmcp.Client calling the transformed server's `execute` tool (client.call_tool('execute', {'code': ...})); no model.
- Defaults: time max_feed_duration_secs=30 from MontySandboxProvider's baseline (code_mode.py:167-170). It counts sandbox time only; time spent awaiting call_tool is excluded. wall_clock_timeout_secs defaults to None (code_mode.py:636). P6 stopped at 30.2 s.; memory max_memory=100,000,000 bytes from the same baseline (code_mode.py:169). P7 stopped at 100,045,946 bytes, in 0.1 s.; output Only the value of the last expression (or `return`) comes back, as tool result text. print() output never reaches the caller: MontySandboxProvider passes no print_callback, and Monty then writes to the host process's stdout/stderr (P1, P2, out/P2-stdio.txt). No truncation of the returned value was observed or found in code_mode.py.; tool_calls max_tool_calls=50 per execute (code_mode.py:635, enforced at :730-736). Extra probe Pcap: 50 host calls ran, the 51st raised 'Tool call limit exceeded: at most 50 call_tool() invocations are allowed per execute().'
- Hardened config: MontySandboxProvider(limits={'max_feed_duration_secs': 10, 'max_memory': 50_000_000}) and CodeMode(sandbox_provider=..., wall_clock_timeout_secs=60), max_tool_calls left at 50. Values are the ones the docs show in the 'Resource limits' and 'Wall-clock limit' sections (https://gofastmcp.com/docs/servers/transforms/code-mode); options at code_mode.py:176-210 and :628-643.

From the source:

- **API shape.** No generated stubs. The sandbox gets exactly one host function, call_tool(tool_name, params), passed to Monty as an external function. The execute tool's description says so: 'Only `call_tool(tool_name: str, params: dict) -> Any` is available in scope.' Tool results come back as structured_content when the tool has an output schema, else as concatenated text. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L686-L694 (description); #L728-L758 (call_tool and run); #L116-L131 (_unwrap_tool_result))
- **Discovery.** The transform replaces the whole tool list with discovery tools plus execute. Defaults are Search (BM25 over the catalog, 'brief' names and descriptions) and GetSchemas ('detailed' parameter markdown); GetTags and ListTools are opt-in. So schemas load on demand, and the model never sees every schema up front unless ListTools(detail='full') is added. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L611-L612 (defaults); #L353-L435 (Search, BM25 at #L376-L381); #L438-L470 (GetSchemas); #L669-L670 (transform_tools))
- **Bridge.** call_tool is an async Python callback that Monty's worker invokes over its host channel. On the host it looks the tool up in the auth-filtered catalog and runs ctx.fastmcp.call_tool, so the real tool, and any credentials it holds, stay in the server process. Concurrent un-awaited calls work: asyncio.gather of 5 lookups took 215 ms host-side (P9). (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L738-L751; research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P9.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** Two layers. Language: Monty has no urllib/socket (P3 ModuleNotFoundError), refuses os.environ (P5), denies open('/etc/hosts') (P4 PermissionError), and has no __class__ on tuples or __import__ (P12). Process: each execute creates a new AsyncMonty pool whose worker is a separate `monty subprocess` process. The docs and the SandboxProvider docstring tell implementers never to use plain exec() for this untrusted code. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L139-L154 (SandboxProvider warning); #L305-L313 (AsyncMonty pool per run); pydantic_monty/_monty.pyi AsyncMonty docstring 'Async context manager owning a pool of `monty` subprocess workers' (v1.6.0); research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/worker-processes.txt)
- **Output channel.** The caller gets only the last expression's value or `return` (P2 returned 'RETURNED' and 0 of 200,000 A's). feed_run is called without print_callback, and pydantic-monty's documented default is the host process stdout/stderr, so sandbox prints land in the server's log. Over stdio transport they appeared on the server's stderr, not on the JSON-RPC channel, and the session kept working. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L309-L313; pydantic_monty/_monty.pyi AsyncMontySession.feed_run docstring 'Defaults to the host process stdout/stderr'; research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P2.txt; research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P2-stdio.txt)
- **Limits.** Monty limits that CodeMode sets by default: max_feed_duration_secs=30 and max_memory=100 MB. It sets no max_turn_duration_secs, no gc_interval, and leaves max_recursion_depth at Monty's standard 1,000. limits=None disables time, memory and GC limits. Unknown keys raise ValueError. CodeMode adds max_tool_calls=50 and an optional wall_clock_timeout_secs (default None), which is the only bound on time spent inside host tools. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L167-L173; #L176-L210; #L227-L236 (unknown keys); #L628-L643; #L753-L767 (wall clock))
- **State.** Fresh per execute: a new pool and a new checkout every call, so P8 printed 'gone'. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L305-L313; research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** Sandbox exceptions surface as a tool error 'Error calling tool 'execute': ValueError: probe-boom'. The type and message survive; no line number or traceback (P10). Failed call_tool calls raise with the tool's parameter list appended when the failure looks like a validation error. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L65-L95; research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P10.txt)
- **Startup cost.** Median 7.7 ms per execute through the in-process client in the final run_all.sh rerun (P11). An earlier run under heavier load from the other workers measured 51.1 ms, so the number is load-sensitive. A new AsyncMonty pool plus feed alone costs a median 6.0 ms versus 0.10 ms on a reused session (out/P11-breakdown.txt), so spawning the per-call `monty subprocess` worker is most of the cost. (research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P11.txt; research/probes/fastmcp-codemode/out/P11-breakdown.txt)
- **Anything else.** Apache-2.0, repo pushed 2026-11-22. The feature lives under fastmcp.experimental. Tools reach the sandbox through the same auth-filtered catalog the client would see (get_tool_catalog(ctx)), so visibility rules carry over. (https://github.com/PrefectHQ/fastmcp/blob/5ac27a2c6e0c31adf3bbc0ac46704ab0279902f9/fastmcp_slim/fastmcp/experimental/transforms/code_mode.py#L33-L34; #L738-L741)

Surprises:

- print() output is silently dropped from the result. The docs example only uses `return`, but SPEC-style print-based code returns an empty result while the text goes to the server's own stdout/stderr (P1 print, P2).
- Each execute spawns a fresh `monty subprocess` worker pool, so there is a process boundary as well as the interpreter boundary. Neither the FastMCP docs page nor code_mode.py says so; it comes from pydantic-monty 1.6.0's AsyncMonty.
- The default time limit does not bound host tool time: feed duration excludes time awaiting call_tool, and wall_clock_timeout_secs defaults to None. The docs say this plainly, so it is a design choice, not a mismatch.
- The tool-call cap error reaches the caller as 'Exception: Tool call limit exceeded...', losing the ToolError type (Pcap).

### Forgemax (postrv/forgemax)

- Source: https://github.com/postrv/forgemax at `v0.6.1 release binary forgemax-v0.6.1-macos-aarch64.tar.gz (SHA256SUMS verified), tag commit b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b (2026-10-09); main is one release-feed commit ahead (83878b19)`
- Language and engine: JS, V8 via deno_core 0.391 (bare JsRuntime, no Deno APIs), fresh runtime per execution inside a forgemax-worker child process with a cleared environment; code is first checked by an oxc AST validator and a regex ban list. The library default is in-process, but the CLI defaults to child_process.
- How it was run: Released `forgemax serve` over stdio driven by an MCP client (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.20.2); `lookup` is a local stdio MCP server (research/probes/forgemax/lookup-server.ts) configured as [servers.host]; each probe is an `execute` call with an `async () => {...}` body, calling forge.callTool("host", "lookup", {id}).
- Defaults: time 5 s CPU watchdog plus async timeout (SandboxConfig::default, crates/forge-sandbox/src/executor.rs:73; watchdog :857-897).; memory 64 MB V8 heap (executor.rs:76, applied at :794) with a near-heap-limit callback that terminates instead of aborting.; output 1 MB result cap (executor.rs:75, enforced :936); results over about 100,000 chars are truncated with a _truncated marker before reaching the model. console output is not a channel (it corrupts IPC).; tool_calls 50 per execution (executor.rs:78), counted inside the worker (ops.rs:85-102); max_parallel 8 for forge.parallel; 8 concurrent executions. In child-process mode tool calls are serialized by the host.
- Hardened config: [sandbox], [sandbox.pool] and [sandbox.stash] copied from forge.toml.example.production at v0.6.1, which SECURITY.md:102 calls 'a complete hardened config': timeout_secs=5, max_heap_mb=64, max_concurrent=8, max_tool_calls=50, execution_mode="child_process", max_ipc_message_size_mb=65, max_parallel=8, pool enabled (min 2, max 8 workers, max_uses 50), stash limits; plus circuit_breaker=true and timeout_secs=30 on the downstream server (SECURITY.md checklist). The limits equal the CLI defaults; the difference is the warm worker pool.

From the source:

- **API shape.** No per-tool stubs. One frozen `forge` object exposes callTool(server, tool, args), a two-level Proxy forge.server(name).category.tool(args), readResource, stash and parallel. TypeScript for this fixed API (forge.d.ts) is compiled into the binary and served in the MCP server instructions (5,594 chars here). (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/executor.rs#L603-L760 and https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-manifest/src/forge.d.ts)
- **Discovery.** A second MCP tool, `search`, runs model-written JS over the capability manifest (servers, categories, tools, schemas) in the same sandbox, so tool schemas never enter the prompt; the MCP surface stays at two tools however many downstream tools exist. (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/README.md#L5-L9; research/probes/forgemax/out/S1.txt, TOOLS.txt)
- **Bridge.** Sandbox calls a deno_core op; in child-process mode the worker writes a length-prefixed JSON ToolCallRequest to its stdout and the host's loop reads it, awaits dispatcher.call_tool(), and only then reads the next message. That inline await is why Promise.all and forge.parallel are serial in the production mode (P9) while in-process mode runs them in parallel. (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/host.rs#L190-L250)
- **Isolation boundary.** Defense in depth: oxc AST validation plus regex bans before execution, a bare deno_core runtime (no fetch/fs/process; Deno deleted, eval and Function constructors removed by the bootstrap), 64 MB heap, CPU watchdog, and a worker process started with env_clear() and kill_on_drop. SECURITY.md says process isolation 'is not an OS sandbox'. All SPEC isolation probes held. But the worker's stdout is both console output and the IPC channel, so guest code can write raw IPC frames: X1 printed forged ToolCallRequest frames and the host dispatched 2 lookups the guest never called through forge (bypassing the worker-side 50-call counter and known-tool check); X2 printed a forged ExecutionComplete and the host returned 'FORGED BY GUEST STDOUT' for a run that was still in while(true). Group policy and the dispatcher's own checks are host-side and still apply. (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/host.rs#L90-L99, https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox-worker/src/main.rs#L313-L342, https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/ops.rs#L85-L102; research/probes/forgemax/out/X1.txt, X2.txt, X2b.txt)
- **Output channel.** Only the JSON return value goes back, as MCP text; over 1 MB is an error, and large results are truncated with a _truncated/_original_chars/_shown_chars marker. forge.log goes to host tracing. console.log is defined (deno_core built-in) but any use in child-process mode corrupts the IPC stream and fails the execution with 'IPC message too large' (X3). (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/executor.rs#L936-L940 and https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/ops.rs#L56-L58; research/probes/forgemax/out/P2c.txt, X3.txt)
- **Limits.** Defaults timeout 5 s, heap 64 MB, output 1 MB, 50 tool calls, 8 concurrent executions, max_parallel 8; the CLI forces child_process unless configured otherwise. (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/executor.rs#L71-L84 and https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-cli/src/common.rs#L31-L62)
- **State.** Fresh JsRuntime per execution, including with the warm worker pool (hardened P8). Session-scoped forge.stash with TTL, size limits and group isolation is the explicit persistence path. (research/probes/forgemax/out/P8.txt, hardened-P8.txt, P8b.txt)
- **Errors.** Errors come back as {"error": message} text with MCP isError:false. Stack traces are dropped and URLs, IPs, paths and credentials are redacted (redact_error_message), so the model sees the message but no line number. (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/crates/forge-sandbox/src/redact.rs#L76-L94; research/probes/forgemax/out/P10b.txt)
- **Credentials and license.** Downstream credentials are expanded from the host env into forge.toml server entries and stay in the gateway; the sandbox sees only server/tool names. License is FSL-1.1-ALv2 (source-available, non-compete for two years per release), not OSI open source. (https://github.com/postrv/forgemax/blob/b042a44cee20afe18db905ee4282b3e3db52e88b/README.md#L15 and #L425-L428)

Surprises:

- console.log is defined but fatal: in the default child-process mode the worker's stdout carries IPC frames, so any print fails the execution with 'IPC message too large: <first 4 bytes of the print as a length>' (P2, X3). Models write console.log constantly.
- Because of the shared stdout, guest code can forge IPC frames: forged ToolCallRequest frames were dispatched by the host (X1, 2 host calls with no forge.callTool, bypassing the worker-side call counter), and a forged ExecutionComplete replaced the real result (X2). No SPEC isolation probe failed, but the IPC boundary the README lists ('protocol desync prevention') is writable from inside the sandbox.
- README advertises 'bounded parallel execution (forge.parallel())', but in the default and production child-process mode all tool calls are serial (1,014 ms for five 200 ms calls, with or without forge.parallel). Only in_process mode, documented as the test mode, ran them in parallel (205 ms).
- With serial calls, a 5 s timeout caps an execution at about 25 calls of 200 ms, below the 50-call limit; P9c hit the timeout after 26 calls and reported 'failed to send tool result: Broken pipe' instead of a timeout message.
- Sandbox failures are returned with MCP isError:false; the failure is only visible inside the text as {"error": ...}.
- The library's SandboxConfig default is InProcess (executor.rs:33-36, 'suitable for tests'); only the CLI switches the default to child_process. An embedder using forge-sandbox directly gets the weaker mode.

### goose Code Mode (code_execution platform extension)

- Source: https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose (github.com/block/goose redirects here) at `36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949 (main, 2026-11-20); boa_engine 0.22.0 per goose Cargo.lock`
- Language and engine: JS, Boa 0.22.0 (pure-Rust JS interpreter) on a dedicated OS thread inside the goose process; no OS sandbox
- How it was run: Rust harness compiles goose's javascript.rs verbatim (include!) and calls javascript::execute, the function CodeExecutionClient::handle_execute_javascript calls (code_execution.rs:123), with goose's 300 s default timeout and a lookup callback dispatched onto the host runtime like dispatch_tool; the MCP/agent layer above it was not built.
- Defaults: time 300 s wall deadline (goose DEFAULT_EXTENSION_TIMEOUT, overridable by GOOSE_DEFAULT_EXTENSION_TIMEOUT); plus Boa limits of 2,000,000 VM instructions, 100,000 loop iterations per frame, recursion 128. Native builtins (regex) are not counted, and the deadline cannot stop the worker thread.; memory none (P7b, P7c reached 4 GB in under 0.4 s); output 1,000,000 bytes for console output plus serialized return value combined; exceeding it is an error, not a truncation; tool_calls no count limit; at most 4 concurrent executions process-wide (WORKER_SLOTS)
- Hardened config: GOOSE_DEFAULT_EXTENSION_TIMEOUT=10 seconds (my choice; default 300, crates/goose/src/config/extensions.rs:10; read by execution_timeout() crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs:146-151; key declared crates/goose/src/config/base.rs:1459; the env var wins over config.yaml, base.rs:773-777). It is the only public knob: instruction limit 2,000,000, loop limit 100,000, recursion 128, output 1,000,000 bytes and 4 worker slots are constants (crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs:27-31, 226-232); a Platform extension config has no timeout field (crates/goose/src/agents/extension_config.rs:73-84); there is no memory option. Harness research/probes/goose-codemode/hardened-harness compiles javascript.rs verbatim and reads the env var as execution_timeout() does.

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|

From the source:

- **API shape.** No generated interface. One native object `tools` with a single method `call(name, args)`; args must be a JSON object. Model writes `async function run()`; goose appends `;run();`. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L237-L246 and https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L25)
- **Discovery.** On demand. The model sees three tools: list_functions (name + first line of description, 240 chars), get_function_details (original JSON input/output schemas), execute_javascript. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L247-L251 and https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L262-L275)
- **Bridge.** Boa NativeFunction::from_async_fn; the async job is polled by goose's own job loop on the worker thread; the callback spawns the MCP call onto goose's main tokio runtime. Tool results are flattened to assistant-visible text and JSON-parsed if possible. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L152-L187, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L271-L333, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L153-L233)
- **Isolation boundary.** Boa interpreter in-process, on a thread named goose-javascript. Claimed boundary (INSTRUCTIONS): 'isolated, with no filesystem, shell, network, packages, or environment access'. Code matches for capabilities (no host objects, IdleModuleLoader, timers rejected) but there is no memory cap and native builtins escape the CPU limits. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L25, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L222-L254, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L285)
- **Output channel.** Captured console lines plus 'Result: <JSON of run() return>' in one text block. 1,000,000-byte combined limit raises an error. Errors are prefixed 'Error: ' and capped by limit_error. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L31-L63, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L302-L321, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L282-L287)
- **Limits.** INSTRUCTION_LIMIT 2,000,000; loop limit 100,000; recursion 128; WORKER_SLOTS 4; timeout from goose config (default 300 s). Boa charges String.prototype.repeat per iteration against the loop limit, which is why the spec's repeat() probes fail. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L27-L31, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L222-L232, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L146-L151; boa_engine 0.22.0 (crates.io) src/builtins/string/mod.rs:736-740, src/vm/opcode/iteration/loop_ops.rs:13-23)
- **State.** Fresh Boa Context per execute_javascript call; no snapshot, no persistence API. (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L214-L228 and test https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L709-L717)
- **Errors.** Boa JsError to_string includes message, location and stack; syntax errors get a hint to define async function run(). (https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L257-L266, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L299-L301, test https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/javascript.rs#L979-L1001)
- **Other.** Code mode is behind cargo feature `code-mode` (on in goose-cli default features) and the extension is default_enabled: false. Tool calls from JS reuse goose's normal tool dispatch (CallRequest), so approvals and permissions of the underlying tools apply; summon's delegate and app-only/resource tools are excluded from the catalog. (crates/goose/Cargo.toml:23, crates/goose-cli/Cargo.toml:95, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/mod.rs#L158-L175, https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/blob/36b29113aff691e1a46a21a5c25900824caf9949/crates/goose/src/agents/platform_extensions/code_execution.rs#L57-L67)

Surprises:

- The Dec 2025 blog says goose 'generates a JavaScript interface representing the connected MCP tools'. At this commit there is no generated interface: one tools.call(name, args) proxy plus list_functions/get_function_details discovery (code_execution.rs:25).
- Boa's 100,000 loop limit is charged per String.prototype.repeat iteration, so ordinary code like "A".repeat(200000) fails with RuntimeLimitError (P2, P7).
- No memory limit: 4 GB in 0.3 s, inside the goose agent process itself (P7b, P7c).
- CPU limits count VM instructions only. A catastrophic regex ran past 120 s (P6b); after goose's 300 s deadline the thread keeps running and holds one of only 4 process-wide worker slots (javascript.rs:28,384-386,409-423).
- Error headline location points at goose's appended ';run();' line (code_mode.js:4:5), not the throw; the stack frame below it is correct (P10).
- The blog links block/goose; the repo now lives at aaif-goose/goose.

### Hermes Agent execute_code (Nous Research)

- Source: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent (tools/code_execution_tool.py, tools/code_kernel.py, tools/code_execution_env.py, tools/code_execution_rpc.py) at `hermes-agent tag v0.23.3 = caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029, editable install from the clone with `uv sync --frozen --python 3.14` (the project's documented dev path; setup.py refuses wheel builds). CPython 3.14. Hardened image nousresearch/hermes-sandbox:desktop (the default sandbox image, pulled 2026-11-22).`
- Language and engine: Python (full CPython), Default (local backend): a persistent CPython session kernel subprocess (hermes_kernel_runner.py) per conversation, in its own process group, with a scrubbed environment; tool calls over a Unix socket RPC. Hardened: the same kernel inside a Docker container (docker backend) with file-based RPC polled through docker exec.
- How it was run: tools.code_execution_tool.execute_code(code, task_id=<per session>, enabled_tools=[lookup, terminal, read_file, write_file]), the function the registered execute_code handler calls; its JSON string is what the model sees. HERMES_HOME pointed at research/impls/hermes-execute-code/home (or home-hardened) so ~/.hermes is never read. lookup needed an in-process patch (see source_notes 'API shape'); P1t/P9t use the built-in terminal tool unpatched. No LLM.
- Defaults: time code_execution.timeout=300 s per call (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:45 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L45); docs research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md:169-176 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md#L169-L176)); the kernel is killed and its state lost. P6 hit the harness's 120 s stop first; side check out/p6_default_check.txt: killed at 300.1 s, next call ran in a fresh kernel.; memory None on the local backend: no memory option for the local kernel. P7 grew to 3.3 GB in 32 s, then the kernel died from outside; the model saw 'The session kernel died while running the cell.' The Docker backend's container_memory (default 5,120 MB) is the only memory knob.; output stdout capped at 50,000 bytes, 40% head / 60% tail with '... [OUTPUT TRUNCATED - N bytes omitted out of T total] ...', the full text spilled to $HERMES_HOME/cache/exec and its path returned; stderr 10,000 bytes; output passes through secret redaction (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:47-79 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L47-L79); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:515-520 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L515-L520)). Ptoolcap: 50 of 55 lookups succeeded.
