From the source:

- **API shape.** The model's execute_code schema lists Python signatures for a hardcoded set of seven built-in tools (web_search, web_extract, read_file, write_file, search_files, patch, terminal), intersected with the session's enabled tools. A hermes_tools.py stub module is generated from the _TOOL_STUBS dict; each stub sends a JSON RPC. A user or plugin tool cannot be exposed through any option: this probe had to add `lookup` to SANDBOX_ALLOWED_TOOLS and _TOOL_STUBS in-process, after registering it with registry.register. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:40-42 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L40-L42); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:125-148 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L125-L148); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:199-206 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L199-L206); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:596-603 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L596-L603); research/probes/hermes-execute-code/adapter.py)
- **Discovery.** All upfront, and small by construction: the execute_code description carries the signatures of at most seven tools. No search; it does not reach MCP or plugin tools at all. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:848-862 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L848-L862); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:864-924 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L864-L924))
- **Bridge.** Local: the stub connects to a per-kernel Unix socket with a 32-byte token; the host's RPC loop checks the allowlist and the 50-call budget, then runs the tool through model_tools.handle_function_call under the current cell's authority (approvals, session). Tools and their credentials stay in the host process. The loop serves one request at a time, so calls are serial even from threads (P9threads 1,025 ms). Remote backends: request files polled through env.execute (hardened P9: 4,429 ms for five calls). (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_kernel.py:265-330 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_kernel.py#L265-L330); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_kernel.py:554-571 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_kernel.py#L554-L571); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_rpc.py:93-120 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_rpc.py#L93-L120); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_rpc.py:145-175 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_rpc.py#L145-L175); research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/P9threads.txt; research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/hardened-P9.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** The docstring is explicit: '"Sandbox" means the security envelope (env scrubbing, tool whitelist + call budget, output redaction), not an isolation jail'. Locally the kernel is plain CPython with the user's permissions: network, /etc/hosts, file writes and os.system all work. The env scrub is a name filter: names containing KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/... are dropped and anything starting with PATH, HOME, LC_, XDG_, CONDA... passes, so PATHFINDER_DB_URL reached the kernel; and the kernel read PROBE_SECRET from its parent's environment with `ps -E -p <ppid>`. The Docker backend is a real boundary: --network=none, cap-drop ALL, no host files, no forwarded env. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:722-735 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L722-L735); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_env.py:25-35 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_env.py#L25-L35); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_env.py:57-97 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_env.py#L57-L97); research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/P5scrub.txt; research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/hardened-P5scrub.txt; research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/hardened-docker-state-P3.txt)
- **Output channel.** Only stdout (plus a '--- stderr ---' block on errors) returns, inside a JSON envelope with status, tool_calls_made, duration and kernel state; the last expression's value is not returned. Output above 50,000 bytes is head/tail truncated with a marker and the full text is spilled to a file whose path is returned. Output is secret-redacted (P5scrub showed the URL password as ***), but the script itself holds the raw value. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:53-79 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L53-L79); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:515-520 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L515-L520); research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/P2.txt; research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/P5scrub.txt)
- **Limits.** Per call: timeout 300 s, 50 tool calls, 50 KB stdout, 10 KB stderr, all from config.yaml code_execution.*. No memory or CPU limit locally; the Docker backend adds container_memory/container_cpu (cgroup). (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:44-50 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L44-L50); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md:169-186 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md#L169-L186); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md:422-467 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/website/docs/user-guide/configuration.md#L422-L467))
- **State.** One persistent session kernel per conversation (P8 persists); a timeout, interrupt or kernel death drops it and the next call starts fresh. Kernels are reaped after kernel_idle_timeout=1800 s or beyond max_session_kernels=4. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md:188-200 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md#L188-L200); research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** The kernel's traceback goes back under '--- stderr ---' with 'File "<cell>", line 2' and the message (P10), plus a hint for missing hermes_tools imports. A kernel death or remote protocol failure returns status 'error' with a one-line note and no cause. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:183-197 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L183-L197); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_kernel.py:1010-1013 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_kernel.py#L1010-L1013); research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/P10.txt; research/probes/hermes-execute-code/out/hardened-P7.txt)
- **Other.** Approvals: check_execute_code_guard approves a script as a whole in gateway/ask contexts, but a local non-interactive session (the path probed here) is auto-approved; container backends skip the guard. A gateway-lifecycle guard rejects scripts that would stop the Hermes gateway. Telemetry (shared metrics) is consent-gated and was set off in config. (research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/approval.py:1480-1505; research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/tools/code_execution_tool.py:748-770 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/tools/code_execution_tool.py#L748-L770); research/impls/hermes-execute-code/src/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md:235-243 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/caafe5389ae585ef77387a962aee05b1bcf17029/website/docs/user-guide/features/code-execution.md#L235-L243))

Surprises:

- The docs' security box says the script 'cannot read secrets from environment variables unless explicitly allowed' (code-execution.md:237-239). On the local backend it can: the kernel's parent is the agent process, and `ps -E -ww -p <ppid>` printed its full environment, including PROBE_SECRET=s3cr3t (out/P5scrub.txt). Any credential whose name starts with a safe prefix (PATH..., HOME..., LC_..., XDG_..., CONDA...) also passes the scrub (PATHFINDER_DB_URL).
- A user or plugin tool cannot be called from execute_code: the in-sandbox tool set is a hardcoded frozenset of seven built-ins plus a hardcoded stub dict. The SPEC `lookup` tool needed an in-process monkeypatch.
- Tool calls are strictly serial: five 200 ms lookups took 1,026 ms in a loop and 1,025 ms from a ThreadPoolExecutor; through the Docker backend's file RPC they took 4,429 ms.
- Hardened (Docker, 512 MB): the memory probe was OOM-killed by the cgroup, but the model was told only 'Remote kernel protocol failure; kernel killed, state lost.' (hardened-P7) or, in a second run where only the kernel process died, a 10 s timeout message (hardened-P7next). Neither names memory.
- In a local session with no approval surface, execute_code auto-approves arbitrary code (approval.py:1486-1490 documents this as trusted-by-config).
- Hermes names its containers hermes-<hex> and keeps them running after the agent process exits (hardened-docker-state-P1.txt: still 'running' after the probe child exited); this probe removed them by label.

### agent-codemode (janwilmake)

- Source: https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode (npm agent-codemode 0.1.1) at `1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17 (package.json 0.1.1, same as npm latest); tsx 4.23.12 from the repo's devDependencies; Node 24.22.1`
- Language and engine: TS, None of its own. The agent writes a .ts script and runs it in the user's shell with tsx or node, as a normal OS process with the user's files, network, environment and credentials. The package is a client library and CLI for calling MCP servers.
- How it was run: Each probe is a .ts file run as a fresh `tsx <file>` process (the runner the README's example uses, README.md:173); the lookup tool is a local stdio MCP server reached through the package's exported StdioMcpClient. The documented mcp.<server> proxy was not used because its name resolution reads the macOS Keychain (see source_notes).
- Defaults: time None. The package sets no timeout on scripts or on tool calls (no timeout or AbortSignal in src/).; memory None from the project; Node's default heap only.; output None from the project. The script's stdout goes to whatever ran it.; tool_calls None.; hardened null: the project exposes no stricter option. It ships no runner, so there is nothing to configure; isolation would have to come from the user's agent or OS.

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Tool call | works (42, 1 call) | printed 42; the lookup MCP server counted 1 call. The script opens a StdioMcpClient to research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/lookup-server.mjs and calls callTool("lookup", {id: 21}). 975 ms including tsx startup and spawning the server. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P1.txt |
| P2 Output | untruncated (200,000 chars, no return) | All 200,000 chars reached the caller's stdout. A script has no return value, so "RETURNED" never appears. Nothing in the package caps output; whatever runs the shell command (the coding agent's Bash tool) decides what the model sees. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P2.txt |
| P3 Network | works (example.com 200) | Plain Node fetch returned status 200. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P3.txt |
| P4 Files | works (no boundary) | readFileSync("/etc/hosts") read 16 lines; await import("fs") also worked. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P4.txt |
| P5 Env secret | works (s3cr3t) | process.env.PROBE_SECRET printed s3cr3t: the script is an ordinary process with the shell's environment. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P5.txt |
| P6 Infinite loop | no-limit-within-120s | Spun until the harness killed it at 120 s. First run also left the real script process (tsx's grandchild) spinning after the tsx parent was killed; the harness now kills the whole tree it started. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P6.txt |
| P7 Memory | no-limit-within-120s (killed at 4.2 GB) | No limit from the project: the harness killed the process tree at 4,200 MB tree RSS after 5.8 s. Only Node's own default heap ceiling would stop it beyond that. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P7.txt |
| P8 State | fresh | Each script is a new process: the second printed "gone". State can still persist through files, since scripts have the whole filesystem. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P8.txt |
| P9 Parallel calls | parallel (252 ms) | Promise.all over five callTool calls on one StdioMcpClient printed 252; 5 server calls. Requests are matched by JSON-RPC id, so they overlap. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P9.txt |
| P10 Errors | works (Node stack, real line) | Exit code 1 and Node's stderr: "P10.ts:3 throw new Error(\"probe-boom\") ... Error: probe-boom at <anonymous> (.../P10.ts:3:7)". Message, source line and the real line number survive. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P10.txt |
| P11 Startup | works (173 ms, a new process) | 20 fresh `tsx P11.ts` processes: median 173 ms, p90 250 ms, under machine load average about 33. No one-time setup step beyond npm install. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P11.txt |
| P12 Escape | escaped (no boundary; PWNED) | There is no sandbox to escape. this.constructor.constructor("return process")() returned process (typeof object); the strict-mode sloppy-this form threw TypeError; execSync("echo PWNED") printed PWNED. | research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P12.txt |

From the source:

- **Isolation boundary.** There is none, by design. The README's own comparison table lists 'Where the code runs: your shell' and says 'No sandbox to deploy'. The package never executes model code; the coding agent writes a script and runs it with tsx in its Bash tool. Code mode here means 'no model between calls', not 'contained code'. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/README.md#L73 and #L180; research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P4.txt, P5.txt, P12.txt)
- **Credentials (the main finding).** The library's purpose is to hand scripts the user's MCP credentials: McpClient.fromClaudeCode reads the OAuth token from the macOS Keychain item 'Claude Code-credentials' with `security find-generic-password -s ... -w`, plus ~/.claude/.credentials.json. Even a stdio server lookup through mcp.<name> or openSession runs resolveName -> listServers -> listCredentials, which reads the whole Keychain blob. Credentials therefore live inside the process that runs model-written code. SECURITY.md says any process spawned from a Claude Code session can read every MCP token without a prompt. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/credentials.ts#L80-L92, https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/resolver.ts#L52-L54 and #L91-L93, https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/client.ts#L65-L69, https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/SECURITY.md#L19-L26)
- **Config discovery.** Reads MCP server definitions from ~/.claude.json, <cwd>/.mcp.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, Windsurf, VS Code settings and Gemini settings, expanding ${VAR} from the environment. HOME is honoured, so config can be redirected, but the Keychain read cannot. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/clients.ts#L17-L19 and #L80-L129; https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/config.ts#L40-L80)
- **API shape.** A runtime Proxy: mcp.<server>.<method>(args) opens a session lazily and maps camelCase back to the wire tool name against the live tools/list. `agent-codemode types` generates a TS module per server (one Args interface per tool, JSDoc clipped) that merges into the McpServers interface for compile-time checks. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/proxy.ts#L36-L90; https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/codegen.ts#L179)
- **Discovery.** No in-prompt catalog and no search tool: the agent runs `agent-codemode servers`, `tools <server>` or `types --all` in its shell and reads files. Scales with the agent's own file reading, not a schema dump. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/cli.ts; https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/.claude/skills/agent-codemode/SKILL.md#L49-L66)
- **Bridge.** Direct MCP from the script process: Streamable HTTP via fetch for remote servers, newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a spawned child's stdin/stdout for stdio servers. Stdio servers are spawned with {...process.env, ...cfg.env}, so they inherit the script's whole environment. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/client.ts#L130; https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/src/stdio-client.ts#L46-L51)
- **Output, limits, errors, state.** None of these are handled by the project: output is the script's stdout, errors are Node's uncaught-exception print and exit code, there are no time, memory, output or call limits, and each run is a new process. CLI exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 tool isError. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/README.md (CLI section); research/probes/janwilmake-agent-codemode/out/P2.txt, P6.txt, P7.txt, P10.txt)
- **Maintenance.** MIT; version 0.1.1; last commit 2026-08-19 (docs). Small (about 1,550 lines of TS), tests are one smoke script with an echo server. (https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/package.json; https://github.com/janwilmake/agent-codemode/blob/1d8b8735b9d085eeeca762edba8cda967b40df17/test/smoke.mjs)

Surprises:

- Not a sandboxed code mode at all: the shipped skill tells the agent to write scripts that run in the user's shell with the user's tokens. It meets the narrow definition (code calls tools, only output returns to the model) with no isolation, so it cannot pass G1, G2 or G3.
- Resolving any server name through mcp.<name>, openSession or the CLI reads the entire Claude Code Keychain blob (every MCP token), even when the target is a local stdio server that needs no token.
- tsx runs the script in a grandchild process. Killing the tsx process on a timeout left the spinning P6 script orphaned at 100% CPU until the harness killed it by PID; an agent's Bash timeout that kills only its direct child would leave the same orphan.
- The README's '290x less into context, 99.66% saved' figure is one prompt against the author's live Linear workspace; it is not reproducible from the repo (no benchmark script ships).

### LangChain deepagents CodeInterpreterMiddleware (langchain-quickjs)

- Source: https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/tree/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs (PyPI langchain-quickjs 0.4.0) at `langchain-quickjs 0.4.0 = deepagents tag langchain-quickjs==0.4.0, commit 3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a (installed wheel diffed identical to the tag); quickjs-rs 0.3.0; deepagents 0.7.41; langchain 1.5.2; langchain-core 1.8.4; langgraph 1.2.24 (research/impls/langchain-quickjs/requirements.lock.txt)`
- Language and engine: JS, quickjs-ng compiled to wasm32-wasip1 (rquickjs), run in-process by wasmtime through quickjs-rs 0.3.0, a pure-Python wheel. One wasm instance per Context, one Context per LangGraph thread, each on its own worker thread. The langchain-quickjs README says PyO3; quickjs-rs 0.3.0 is not PyO3.
- How it was run: langchain.agents.create_agent(model=<scripted stand-in that turns each human message into one eval tool call>, tools=[lookup], middleware=[CodeInterpreterMiddleware(ptc=["lookup"], ...)], checkpointer=InMemorySaver()).ainvoke(...); the probe output is the eval ToolMessage text. No LLM. research/probes/langchain-quickjs/run_all.py both.
- Defaults: time timeout=5.0 s per eval (middleware.py:71, 291), enforced by a deadline the QuickJS interrupt poll reads (quickjs_rs/runtime.py:65-73). It counts VM time only: the deadline is pushed back by every host wait (quickjs_rs/context.py:820-830). Measured: with timeout=1.0, eight serial 200 ms tool calls finished at 1,780 ms (out/extras.txt). Documented at README.md:115-126.; memory memory_limit=64 MiB (middleware.py:70, 290), applied as the QuickJS allocator limit inside each wasm instance (_repl.py:228-235; quickjs_rs/_engine.py:1248-1266). No wasmtime store limiter on linear memory was found.; output max_result_chars=4000 (middleware.py:73): <result>, <error>, and <stdout> are each cut to 4,000 chars with "… [truncated N chars]" (_format.py:16, 176-222). Console output is capped while collecting (_repl.py:132-156).; tool_calls max_ptc_calls=256 tools.* calls per eval (middleware.py:72, _ptc.py:216-230); over the cap the eval ends with PTCCallBudgetExceeded (measured at 8 in hardened, out/extras.txt). fs calls share the budget (_repl.py:519-522). task() dispatches have a concurrency cap of 32 but no count cap (_repl.py:69, 211).
- Hardened config: CodeInterpreterMiddleware(ptc=["lookup"], timeout=1.0, memory_limit=16*1024*1024, max_ptc_calls=8, mode="call", subagents=False), all public constructor options (middleware.py:287-303, documented at README.md:278-293 and middleware.py:143-269). fs stays None (the default, no fs). mode="call" gives a fresh Context per eval, so snapshots and snapshot_signing_key do not apply. The 1 s, 16 MiB and 8-call values were chosen by this run; no floor is documented. No network option exists because there is no network to turn on.

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Tool call | works (42, 1 host call) | tools.lookup({id: 21}) then console.log(r.value) printed 42, 1 host call. Tool output: "<stdout>\n42\n</stdout>\n<result>null</result>". The tool result reaches JS as a native object, not a string. | research/probes/langchain-quickjs/out/P1.txt |
| P2 Output | truncated (4,000 + marker) | Both came back. <result>RETURNED</result> plus a <stdout> block of 4,000 chars: 3,974 A's then the marker "… [truncated 196000 chars]". The real drop is 196,026 chars, so the marker undercounts by the 26 chars it replaced. | research/probes/langchain-quickjs/out/P2.txt |
| P3 Network | not-defined (no fetch) | ReferenceError: fetch is not defined. typeof XMLHttpRequest and WebSocket are "undefined". import("https://example.com") and import("os") -> ReferenceError: Error loading module. No request left the host. | research/probes/langchain-quickjs/out/P3.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** An explicit allowlist (ptc=[names or BaseTool]) picks tools (_ptc.py:66-134). In the guest, globalThis.tools is a Proxy that maps any allowlisted camelCase name to __tools_call(name, input) and lists names via __tools_names() (_ptc.py:434-457). The prompt gets TS-ish signatures rendered from each tool's args schema (_prompt.py:461-540). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/_ptc.py#L434-L457)
- **Discovery.** Every exposed tool's signature goes into the system prompt on each model call (middleware.py:654-705). The exception is tools flagged extras["defer_loading"]: they stay callable but are left out until provider tool search finds them (middleware.py:695-699, _prompt.py:472-480). That is the only path that scales past 100 tools, and it needs ProviderToolSearchMiddleware in front. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/middleware.py#L686-L705)
- **Bridge.** __tools_call is an async QuickJS host function. It debits the per-eval budget, injects ToolRuntime/state/store, and runs tool.arun on the agent's outer event loop via run_coroutine_threadsafe (_repl.py:159-171, 431-504). The guest gets a Promise, so Promise.all over tools runs in parallel (P9 206 ms). Command updates from tools are written to graph state (_ptc.py:398-416). Tools run on the host with host credentials; the guest sees only return values. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/_repl.py#L460-L504)
- **Isolation boundary.** The engine is quickjs-ng in a wasm32-wasip1 guest under wasmtime, in the host Python process. WASI gets only inherited stdout/stderr: no preopened dirs, no env, no args (quickjs_rs/_engine.py:357-360). No module loader is set, so every import fails. quickjs-rs names wasmtime as the residual escape path and recommends process isolation for hostile multi-tenant use (quickjs-rs README, Security). The capability surface is whatever the host registers: console, tools, task, and an __lc_fs function that refuses unless fs= is set (_repl.py:237-263, 506-518). With fs=True, code can read, write, and delete anything the backend reaches, bypassing permissions and HITL (middleware.py:133-141). (research/impls/langchain-quickjs/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/quickjs_rs/_engine.py:357-360 (quickjs-rs 0.3.0 wheel); https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/_repl.py#L237-L263)
- **Output channel.** The model gets one string: an optional <stdout> block, then <result> or <error type=...>, XML-escaped, each cut to max_result_chars with a marker (_format.py:176-222). The last expression's value is returned and a final Promise is awaited first (_repl.py:596-612). Unmarshalable values render as <result kind="handle">[Function] arity=N</result>. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/_format.py#L176-L222)
- **Limits.** Constructor knobs: memory_limit, timeout (None disables), max_ptc_calls (None disables), max_result_chars, max_subagent_concurrency, max_snapshot_bytes (middleware.py:287-346). The timeout bounds JS execution only, not wall time (quickjs_rs/context.py:820-830). Overlapping evals on one thread are refused, not queued (_repl.py:571-578). The process keeps at most 32 warm slots (_repl.py:75). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/middleware.py#L287-L346)
- **State.** mode="thread" (default) keeps one live Context per thread and, after each agent run, snapshots the whole wasm memory (1.3 MB here) into checkpointer state as a bsdiff4 patch chain (middleware.py:767-801, _snapshot.py:157-175). Restore is lazy on the next eval. Snapshots are unauthenticated unless snapshot_signing_key is set, and quickjs-rs calls snapshots trusted input (middleware.py:256-269). A snapshot over max_snapshot_bytes is dropped with a warning, which resets the thread's state (middleware.py:740-753). mode="turn" and "call" close the Context after the turn or each call (_repl.py:675-676). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/middleware.py#L736-L801)
- **Errors.** JS throws keep name, message and stack (_repl.py:680-683). Host-side failures map to Timeout, Deadlock, OutOfMemory, PTCCallBudgetExceeded, UnsupportedCommand, MarshalError, ConcurrentEval, or the Python exception name for task() (_repl.py:618-671). Cancellation re-raises as CancelledError. Errors never raise to the agent; they return as ToolMessage text. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/_repl.py#L618-L683)
- **Other: approvals.** PTC calls and task() dispatches skip ToolNode, so interrupt_on / HITL approval does not apply per call; the allowlist is the security boundary (middleware.py:216-220, README.md:206, 274). The eval tool itself can be gated. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/blob/3285b5cac24ea0d6375f256312267685d3dbcd5a/libs/partners/quickjs/langchain_quickjs/middleware.py#L201-L228)

Surprises:

- The README calls the engine "QuickJS embedded via PyO3 + rquickjs" and quickjs-rs "a PyO3 extension module" (README.md:3, 49). quickjs-rs 0.3.0, the version the pin allows (pyproject quickjs-rs>=0.3.0,<0.4.0), is a pure-Python wheel that runs quickjs-ng compiled to wasm under wasmtime (quickjs-rs 0.3.0 METADATA). That is a stronger boundary than the README describes.
- Date.now() is the real host clock: the guest value was 5 ms off host time.time() (out/extras.txt), and P9 measured 206 ms with it. The README (README.md:93), the system prompt (_prompt.py:330-333), and the eval tool schema ("No network/real-clock access", middleware.py:97) all say there is no real clock. The middleware builds Runtime without a clock callback (_repl.py:231-234), so quickjs-rs uses native WASI clocks (quickjs_rs/_engine.py:369-372).
- A host function __lc_fs is on globalThis in every Context even with fs=None (_repl.py:262, 506-512). Calling it fails with the misleading type ConcurrentEval: "fs called outside active eval" (_repl.py:514-518). It is not an escape, but guest code can see a filesystem hook that the docs say does not exist.
- A global task() exists by default (subagents=True) with no task tool configured; calling it returns <error type="RuntimeError">task tool not configured for this eval</error> (out/extras.txt).
- The README says the memory limit is "shared across every context" of the Runtime (README.md:128; middleware.py:144-145). In quickjs-rs 0.3.0 each Context is its own wasm instance with its own limit (quickjs_rs/_engine.py:1248-1266). The middleware uses one Context per thread, so the effective limit is per thread.
- The README and docstring type PTC tools as Promise<string> (README.md:213; middleware.py:202). They return native JS values (P1 read r.value directly), which the system prompt states correctly.
- The stdout truncation marker undercounts: 3,974 chars kept, and the marker says 196000 dropped when 196,026 were (_format.py:209-216, out/P2.txt).
- Documented but notable: timeout counts VM time only. With timeout=1.0, an eval awaiting eight 200 ms tool calls ran 1,780 ms and succeeded. G2 bounds CPU loops, not an eval's wall time; max_ptc_calls is the only bound on tool-wait time.
- In thread mode every turn after the first adds about 95 ms (turn 96-101 ms vs eval 1.4 ms, out/extras.txt), inferred to be the bsdiff4 diff of the 1.3 MB memory snapshot. After the P7 OOM the snapshot was 68 MB, over max_snapshot_bytes, and was dropped with only a log warning, so that thread's REPL state resets silently.
- Stack line numbers are exact for statement code (P10: 3:12 and 5:1) but shift by 1 to 2 lines when the code starts with "(" (P12 step 2 reports 3:1 for a 1-line program). The cause is a guess: the TOP_LEVEL_CONST_TO_VAR source transform (_repl.py:233).

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools are plain Python callables. create_codeact wraps each as a StructuredTool and puts tool.func into the sandbox context under the tool's name, so code calls lookup(21) directly. The eval_fn contract is (code, locals) -> (stdout, new_vars). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py#L12-L13; #L78-L84)
- **Discovery.** Upfront: create_default_prompt writes a Python signature and docstring for every tool into the system prompt. No search. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py#L29-L52)
- **Bridge.** None: the tool function runs in the same interpreter as the agent, called directly by exec'd code (P1: 1 host call). Credentials held by a tool are in the same process as the model's code. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py#L97-L121)
- **Isolation boundary.** None. The example passes builtins.__dict__ itself as the globals of exec, so any `global` assignment inside a function writes into the host's builtins module (P12d: a PROBE_LEAK name appeared in the harness's builtins). The README says to use a sandbox in production and points to the Pyodide example. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/math_example.py#L13-L29; https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/README.md#L101-L103; research/probes/langgraph-codeact/out/P12d.txt)
- **Output channel.** The sandbox node appends the eval_fn's stdout string as a user message for the model. Nothing else reaches the model, and nothing is truncated. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py#L112-L121)
- **Limits.** None anywhere in langgraph_codeact (128 lines) or the example eval. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py)
- **State.** Persistent through graph state: new top-level variables go into state['context'] and are merged back into the next exec's locals (P8 printed 7). With a checkpointer that state must be serializable. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py#L112-L121)
- **Errors.** The example returns 'Error during execution: ' + repr(e): type and message survive, no line number (P10). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/math_example.py#L22-L23; research/probes/langgraph-codeact/out/P10.txt)
- **Parallelism.** Tools are sync callables and there is no async path in the example eval, so a loop is serial (P9, 1,020 ms). Plain exec allows threads, and ThreadPoolExecutor.map ran the five lookups in 205 ms (P9b). (research/probes/langgraph-codeact/out/P9.txt; research/probes/langgraph-codeact/out/P9b.txt)
- **Maintenance.** Archived, MIT, last push 2025-05-16. (gh repo view langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact: isArchived true, pushedAt 2025-05-16T19:56:24Z)

Surprises:

- Compiled with MemorySaver, as both examples do, the agent raises TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable as soon as code creates a module, function or class at top level (import os, def f, a ThreadPoolExecutor), because those land in state['context'] and the checkpointer cannot store them. Seen with the uv.lock versions and with current langgraph 1.0.1 (out-memorysaver-lock/, out-latest/). The probes above therefore run without a checkpointer.
- Sandbox code can write into the host's builtins module through a function's `global` statement (P12d), because the example uses builtins.__dict__ as exec's globals.
- A function defined inside the exec'd code cannot call a tool: P8b's helper() raised NameError: name 'lookup' is not defined, because function globals are builtins.__dict__ while tools and top-level names live in the separate locals dict.

From the source:

- **API shape and bridge.** There is no host bridge. The example's eval_fn turns every callable in the context into source text with inspect.getsource() and pastes it in front of the code, and every other variable as name = repr(value). Tools therefore run inside Pyodide, not on the host, and only if their source is self-contained: a tool that uses a module-level import (as math_example.py's sin uses math) fails with NameError (P1, P9). A self-contained copy returned 42 with 0 host calls (P1s). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/pyodide_sandbox_example.py#L12-L75; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P1.txt; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P1s.txt)
- **Credentials.** Because tool source is copied into the sandbox, any secret a tool needs has to be inside the sandbox too (as a literal or via a permission the sandbox is given). Inferred from the eval_fn; nothing in the example keeps credentials on the host. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/pyodide_sandbox_example.py#L35-L43)
- **Discovery.** Upfront, the same create_default_prompt as the eval example: every tool's signature and docstring in the system prompt. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/langgraph_codeact/__init__.py#L29-L52)
- **Isolation boundary.** Deno's permission system around a Pyodide wasm runtime. Python's `js` module still reaches the Deno global (P12e printed Deno's version and pid), so the boundary that held was Deno's: file read, env and subprocess attempts all raised NotCapable (P12f, P5b, P12 os.system), and Pyodide's /etc/hosts is its own virtual file system (P4 Errno 44). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-sandbox/blob/65760b8430df99aa2e4c936310c392a07ff7b65c/libs/sandbox-py/langchain_sandbox/pyodide.py#L164-L198; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P12e.txt; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P12f.txt)
- **Network.** The example turns networking on (PyodideSandbox(allow_net=True), unrestricted). urllib cannot do https in Pyodide (P3), but js.fetch via pyodide.ffi.run_sync reached example.com with HTTP 200 (P3b). With allow_net=False the same call raised NotCapable (hardened-P3b). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/pyodide_sandbox_example.py#L111; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P3b.txt; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/hardened-P3b.txt)
- **Limits.** timeout_seconds wraps process.communicate() in asyncio.wait_for and kills the Deno process (hardened P6 stopped at 30.0 s). memory_limit_mb only adds --v8-flags=--max-old-space-size, which does not bound Pyodide's WebAssembly memory: hardened P7 with 256 MB passed 4.1 GB and was killed by the harness. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-sandbox/blob/65760b8430df99aa2e4c936310c392a07ff7b65c/libs/sandbox-py/langchain_sandbox/pyodide.py#L274-L276; #L304-L331; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/hardened-P7.txt)
- **State.** A new Deno process per execution; variables persist only because the eval_fn re-injects them as repr() literals, so P8 printed 7. Values whose repr is not valid Python cannot carry over. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/pyodide_sandbox_example.py#L35-L43)
- **Errors.** The generated wrapper catches every exception and returns {'error': str(e)}, so the model sees 'Error during execution: probe-boom' without the exception type or a line number (P10). (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph-codeact/blob/de14f16f5eb96351086c675c6a1bca238974b57d/examples/pyodide_sandbox_example.py#L16-L27; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P10.txt)
- **Startup.** Median 1,135 ms per execution (P11): every call starts Deno, loads Pyodide and runs once. The in-sandbox P9 loop took about 975 ms more than an empty run (2,110 ms), so the five 200 ms calls ran serially. (research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P11.txt; research/probes/langgraph-codeact-pyodide/out/P9s.txt)
- **Supply chain.** langchain-sandbox 0.0.5, the version in langgraph-codeact's uv.lock, fetches its Deno entry point from a personal JSR scope at run time: PKG_NAME = 'jsr:@eyurtsev/pyodide-sandbox@0.0.3' (0.0.6 moved to jsr:@langchain/pyodide-sandbox@0.0.4). With node_modules_dir='auto', Deno installs npm packages next to the nearest package.json. (https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-sandbox/blob/65760b8430df99aa2e4c936310c392a07ff7b65c/libs/sandbox-py/langchain_sandbox/pyodide.py#L40; #L198)

Surprises:

- The Pyodide example is presented as the secure option, but it does not bridge tools to the host at all: it pastes each tool's source into the sandbox, which breaks any tool that relies on its module's imports, including the example's own sin/cos helpers that use math.
- The example enables unrestricted network (allow_net=True) and sets no timeout, so the default run has network on and no time limit (P3b, P6).
- memory_limit_mb does not limit Pyodide memory (hardened P7 reached 4.1 GB).
- On first run Deno's node_modules_dir='auto' resolved to this repo's root package.json, installed every root dependency into the repo's node_modules/.deno, replaced six top-level node_modules entries and .bin with symlinks into it, and wrote deno.lock at the repo root. The versions match bun.lock and a bun import check still passed; deno.lock was removed, the node_modules layout was left as is. A deno.json in the probe folder now contains it.

### Protocol-Lattice go-agent CodeMode (go-utcp codemode, Expr runtime)

- Source: https://github.com/Protocol-Lattice/go-agent (runtime: github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp src/plugins/codemode) at `go-agent ebf73f2b10e26b41266d49535c95303821c2590d (2026-09-30); its go.mod pins go-utcp v1.12.3 (a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f); expr-lang/expr v1.17.8; built with go1.27.4 linux/arm64 in Docker`
- Language and engine: Expr (expr-lang/expr v1.17), expr-lang/expr, a Go expression language compiled and evaluated in the agent's own Go process (a goroutine per execution). No loops, no statements, no I/O; the only object in scope is `codemode` with CallTool / CallToolStream / Get.
- How it was run: Go harness run in Docker (Go is not on the host): codemode.NewCodeModeUTCP(fakeClient, nil).Execute(ctx, CodeModeArgs{Code, Timeout: 20000}), the call go-agent's CodeMode.CallTool makes after its LLM planning step (orchestrator.go:44). fakeClient implements UtcpClientInterface.CallTool for lookup.
- Defaults: time Execute defaults to 30000 ms (codemode.go:124); go-agent's CodeMode.CallTool passes 20000 (orchestrator.go:44); the generic tool handler defaults to 3000 (codemode.go:148). None stops the evaluating goroutine.; memory Expr DefaultMemoryBudget 1e6 allocation units (expr conf/config.go:15), not configurable through go-utcp or go-agent.; output Value only, uncapped. No print.; tool_calls None.; hardened null: go-agent hard-codes the 20 s timeout on its path and exposes no memory, budget or concurrency option, so no stricter configuration exists.

| P2 Output | no print; value 200,000 chars | Expr has no print: "unknown name print (1:1)". The value is the only output; `repeat("A", 200000)` came back as one 200000-char string, uncapped. CodeModeResult.Stdout exists but is never set. | research/probes/lattice-go-agent/out/fast.jsonl |

A runtime error returns "Expr runtime error: index out of range: 6 (array length is 2) (1:18)" plus the source line and a caret. go-agent's tool handler wraps it as "codemode expression produced an error: ...". | research/probes/lattice-go-agent/out/fast.jsonl |

From the source:

- **API shape.** No per-tool functions. One `codemode` object with CallTool(name, args), CallToolStream(name, args) and Get(value, key); the env passed to expr.Compile contains only that object. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L77-L96 and #L127-L130)
- **Discovery.** Host-side: go-agent ranks UTCP tool specs against the prompt (rankToolSpecs, candidate limit UTCP_CODEMODE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT, default 16) and gives only the candidates to a planner LLM, optionally behind the OpenRouter Jev decision layer that picks the exact tool. Generated code is validated to use only those tool names. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/orchestrator.go#L27-L49 , #L169 , #L208 , #L321 ; https://github.com/Protocol-Lattice/go-agent/blob/ebf73f2b10e26b41266d49535c95303821c2590d/README.md#L577-L627)
- **Bridge.** Direct in-process Go call into UtcpClient.CallTool with the execution context; results come back as Go values. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L79-L82)
- **Isolation boundary.** The boundary is the language: Expr cannot loop, import, or do I/O, and only `codemode` is in scope. There is no process or memory isolation. The README says to use CodeMode "only in trusted environments", and go-agent refuses codemode.run_code unless AllowUnsafeTools is set. (https://github.com/Protocol-Lattice/go-agent/blob/ebf73f2b10e26b41266d49535c95303821c2590d/README.md#L567-L575 ; https://github.com/Protocol-Lattice/go-agent/blob/ebf73f2b10e26b41266d49535c95303821c2590d/agent.go#L244-L248)
- **Output channel.** CodeModeResult{Value, Stdout, Stderr}: Value on success, Stderr holds the error; Stdout is never written. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L20 and #L122-L141)
- **Limits.** context.WithTimeout around a goroutine running expr.Run(program, env); on timeout Execute returns but the goroutine keeps evaluating because expr.Run never sees the context. Memory is only Expr's allocation budget. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L122-L141)
- **State.** Fresh: compile + run per call. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L130-L134)
- **Errors.** Expr compile and runtime errors carry (line:col) and a caret excerpt, wrapped as "Expr compilation failed" / "Expr runtime error". (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L130-L140)
- **Anything else.** Not general-purpose code: the planner prompt forbids loops and statements, so code mode here is a typed expression pipeline over tool calls. The LLM-planning path needs a model key; the harness skipped it and called Execute directly. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/go-utcp/blob/a0edb1984084857cb31f714009c4513451e9b07f/src/plugins/codemode/codemode.go#L31-L54)

Surprises:

- Code mode here is not a programming language: Expr has no loops, no print, no throw and no concurrency, so the SPEC's infinite loop, print and throw cannot be written as such.
- The timeout returns control but never stops the work: the Expr goroutine kept running and growing (491 MB RSS) after Execute returned at 20 s.
- Three different default timeouts on three paths: 30 s (Execute), 20 s (go-agent planner path), 3 s (generic tool handler).
- The only memory guard is Expr's allocation counter, which a nested reduce bypassed while RSS reached about 500 MB.
- Discovery is the most selective seen: deterministic ranking plus an optional external decision model choose candidate tools before the code-writing model sees any schemas.

### LlamaIndex CodeActAgent with the docs' SimpleCodeExecutor

- Source: PyPI llama-index-core (repo https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index); example https://developers.llamaindex.ai/python/examples/agent/code_act_agent/ (notebook docs/examples/agent/code_act_agent.ipynb) at `llama-index-core 0.14.26 (tag v0.14.26 = 3aaab93a2e823b9637ce3c6f0611e5e18a4a7a5b; installed codeact_agent.py identical), notebook at 847acaa6d4471ebb1b1ea6f7e7b94001ef787ef3, llama-index-workflows 2.26.1`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython exec(code, globals, locals) in the host process, on a thread-pool thread: CodeActAgent wraps the sync code_execute_fn in a FunctionTool, whose acall runs it with loop.run_in_executor.
- How it was run: Notebook cells 5, 6 and 8 as shipped (SimpleCodeExecutor copied verbatim; locals={'lookup': lookup}, globals with __builtins__ and numpy; CodeActAgent(code_execute_fn=code_executor.execute, llm=..., tools=[lookup]); Context(agent)), driven by agent.run(..., ctx=ctx) with a scripted CustomLLM that replies with <execute>code</execute> and then 'done'. What comes back is ToolCallResult.tool_output.content, which the agent hands the model.
- Defaults: time None: neither SimpleCodeExecutor nor CodeActAgent sets one, and BaseWorkflowAgent's workflow timeout defaults to None (base_agent.py:169). P6 ran 120 s until the harness stopped it; the loop runs on an executor thread that cannot be cancelled.; memory None (P7 reached 4.2 GB in 1.7 s; harness kill).; output Captured stdout, then stderr, then str(last expression) appended after a blank line, all as one string (P2: 200,000 A's plus RETURNED). No truncation in the executor or in handle_tool_call_results.; tool_calls No cap.; hardened No hardened run: SimpleCodeExecutor takes only locals and globals, and CodeActAgent.__init__ exposes no timeout or sandbox option (BaseWorkflowAgent's workflow timeout is not passed through, and would not stop the executor thread anyway). The docs only advise 'docker or external services'.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools reach the code only because the user puts the same functions into the executor's locals dict; CodeActAgent's tools list is used for the prompt only (_get_tool_fns returns real_fn callables to describe). Code calls lookup(21) as a plain function. (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/3aaab93a2e823b9637ce3c6f0611e5e18a4a7a5b/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/codeact_agent.py#L125-L149; https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/847acaa6d4471ebb1b1ea6f7e7b94001ef787ef3/docs/examples/agent/code_act_agent.ipynb (cell 6))
- **Discovery.** Upfront: every tool's signature and docstring goes into DEFAULT_CODE_ACT_PROMPT via {tool_descriptions}; a tool_retriever can pre-filter tools per step, but there is no search tool the model calls. (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/3aaab93a2e823b9637ce3c6f0611e5e18a4a7a5b/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/codeact_agent.py#L25-L58; #L171-L197; #L279-L283)
- **Bridge.** None: the tool is a host function called directly by exec'd code in the same process (P1, 1 host call). Credentials a tool holds share the process with model-written code. (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/3aaab93a2e823b9637ce3c6f0611e5e18a4a7a5b/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/codeact_agent.py#L98-L101; research/probes/llamaindex-codeact/out/P1.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** None, and the docs say so: 'This example includes code that will execute arbitrary code. This is dangerous, and proper sandboxing should be used in production environments', and the class docstring says 'not safe for production use'. globals gets the real __builtins__ (P3, P4, P5, P12 all reach the host). (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/847acaa6d4471ebb1b1ea6f7e7b94001ef787ef3/docs/examples/agent/code_act_agent.ipynb (cells 0, 4, 5))
- **Output channel.** handle_tool_call_results appends 'Result of executing the code given:' plus the full string as a user message; no limit anywhere. (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/3aaab93a2e823b9637ce3c6f0611e5e18a4a7a5b/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/agent/workflow/codeact_agent.py#L352-L382)
- **State.** Persistent: the executor's locals dict lives as long as the SimpleCodeExecutor (P8 printed 7). Because exec gets separate globals and locals dicts, top-level names land in locals and functions defined in the code cannot see them, tools included (P8b: NameError: name 'lookup' is not defined). (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/847acaa6d4471ebb1b1ea6f7e7b94001ef787ef3/docs/examples/agent/code_act_agent.ipynb (cell 5); research/probes/llamaindex-codeact/out/P8b.txt)
- **Errors.** The executor returns 'Error: <Type>: <msg>' plus traceback.format_exc(), so message and '<string>' line numbers survive (P10), along with host file paths. A bare `except:` around the first exec re-runs the whole code after any exception, so the traceback shows the error twice and every side effect before the error happens twice: one lookup call then a raise produced 2 host calls (P10b). (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/847acaa6d4471ebb1b1ea6f7e7b94001ef787ef3/docs/examples/agent/code_act_agent.ipynb (cell 5, the `except:` branch); research/probes/llamaindex-codeact/out/P10.txt; research/probes/llamaindex-codeact/out/P10b.txt)
- **Parallelism.** Tools are sync and the executor has no async path, so a loop is serial (P9, 1,019 ms). Threads are allowed: ThreadPoolExecutor.map ran five lookups in 213 ms (P9b). (research/probes/llamaindex-codeact/out/P9.txt; research/probes/llamaindex-codeact/out/P9b.txt)
- **Async and blocking.** A sync code_execute_fn runs via FunctionTool's sync_to_async, i.e. loop.run_in_executor, so the agent's event loop stays responsive while code runs, but a runaway loop keeps a thread pool worker forever. (https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/blob/3aaab93a2e823b9637ce3c6f0611e5e18a4a7a5b/llama-index-core/llama_index/core/tools/function_tool.py#L47-L55)
- **Maintenance.** MIT, repo pushed 2026-11-20. CodeActAgent is in llama-index-core; the executor exists only in the docs notebook. (gh api repos/run-llama/llama_index: pushed_at 2026-11-20, license MIT)

Surprises:

- The documented executor runs code twice whenever it raises: the bare `except:` meant for parse failures catches runtime errors too and calls exec(code) again (P10b: 2 host calls for 1 lookup).
- Functions written by the model cannot call the tools or each other's top-level names (P8b), because the executor passes separate globals and locals dicts to exec.
- The docs' install line installs llama-index-llms-ollama while the code imports llama_index.llms.openai.
- The executor's type hint says it returns Tuple[bool, str, Any] and its docstring says a dict; it returns a str.

### Lootbox (jx-codes/lootbox)

- Source: https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox at `587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a (deno.json version 0.0.54, last commit 2026-02-27); run from source on host Deno 2.9.8 with --no-lock (see surprises)`
- Language and engine: TS, A fresh `deno run --allow-net --allow-import=localhost:<port>` subprocess per script (V8 + Deno permissions; local script is type-checked). Tools are .ts files in .lootbox/tools, each run in a long-lived `deno run --allow-all` worker process; scripts reach them over a WebSocket to the lootbox server.
- How it was run: `deno run --allow-all --no-lock src/lootbox-cli.ts server` in research/probes/lootbox/work (lootbox.config.json: port 41310, root .lootbox, data ./data); `lookup` is .lootbox/tools/host.ts; each probe is sent as the same WebSocket message `lootbox exec` sends ({script, id}). Sandbox code calls tools.host.lookup(...).
- Defaults: time 10 s per script, hard-coded (src/lib/execute_llm_script.ts:26); not configurable. Tool calls time out at 30 s (src/lib/rpc/client.ts:26, rpc_worker.ts:69). The CLI waits 30 s for a response. No stricter option exists, so hardened is null.; memory None. P7 reached 4.3 GB before the harness stopped it.; output None. stdout returned whole on success; on failure only stderr (stdout dropped).; tool_calls No count cap. Network is always on (--allow-net with no host list) and there is no config key for it.

| P2 Output | print only, uncapped (200,000) | Only stdout returns, as `result`: 200,001 chars (all 200,000 A's), no truncation, no marker. The bare last expression "RETURNED" is not returned (module file, no return channel). | research/probes/lootbox/out/P2.txt |

No host object reached. | research/probes/lootbox/out/P12a.txt .. P12g.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each .ts file in .lootbox/tools is a namespace and its exported functions become tools. The server extracts their TypeScript types and generates a client module (`export const tools = { <ns>: { <fn>: createRpcCall("ns.fn") } }`) served at /client.ts; every script gets `import { tools } from "http://localhost:<port>/client.ts?v=<n>"` prepended. MCP servers appear as mcp_<name> namespaces. (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/execute_llm_script.ts#L13-L18 and https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/type_system/client_generator.ts#L508-L509)
- **Discovery.** On demand through the CLI: `lootbox tools` lists namespaces, `lootbox tools types <ns,...>` fetches TypeScript for chosen namespaces from /types/:namespaces. The agent pulls only what it needs, which scales past 100 tools. (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/lootbox-cli/tools.ts#L42 and https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/rpc/managers/route_handler.ts#L83)
- **Bridge.** The script opens a WebSocket to the lootbox server and sends {method: "ns.fn", args, id}; the server routes it to that namespace's worker process over /worker-ws. Tool workers run with --allow-all, so a tool has full host access by design. (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/rpc/client.ts#L87-L110, https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/rpc/managers/message_router.ts#L160-L180, https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/rpc/worker_manager.ts#L231-L244)
- **Isolation boundary.** Scripts run as `deno run --allow-net --allow-import=localhost:<port> --reload=... --no-check=remote <tmp>.ts`. Files, env and subprocesses are denied by Deno permissions; network is fully open. Help text says 'Sandboxed execution keeps your system safe' and 'Direct file system and environment access disabled', which matches; it also advertises fetch() as a feature. Open network means sandbox code can reach any LAN or localhost service, including the lootbox server itself (X1 fetched /client.ts, X2 started a nested script over /ws). (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/execute_llm_script.ts#L28-L40; help text https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/lootbox-cli/help.ts#L62-L83; research/probes/lootbox/out/X1.txt, X2.txt)
- **Output channel.** On success the response carries stdout as `result` (stderr warnings are dropped by the router). On failure it carries only stderr as `error`; stdout printed before the failure is discarded. No truncation anywhere. (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/execute_llm_script.ts#L52-L87 and https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/rpc/managers/message_router.ts#L108-L113; research/probes/lootbox/out/X3.txt)
- **Limits.** 10 s hard-coded wall clock via AbortController on Deno.Command; the timeout error branch is unreachable in practice (P6). No memory, output or call-count limits. (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/execute_llm_script.ts#L25-L26 and #L94-L111)
- **State.** Fresh process per script. Persistent state lives in tools (example kv, sqlite, memory tools write to disk). Every script, its output and error are also stored in a SQLite history (lootbox.db in the data dir, default ~/.local/share/lootbox). (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/script_history.ts#L29-L45 and https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/db.ts#L42-L43)
- **Errors.** No formatting: the model sees Deno's raw stderr, including Download/Check progress lines, ANSI codes and the temp path. The local script is type-checked in strict mode, so a type error blocks execution before any code runs (P8 and P12 spec forms). (research/probes/lootbox/out/P10b.txt, P8.txt, P12a.txt)
- **Network exposure.** The server uses Deno.serve with no hostname, which listens on all interfaces, and /ws has no authentication: anyone who can reach the port can run scripts, and those scripts have open network. (https://github.com/jx-codes/lootbox/blob/587a5a1b2694d0d00168665d8f1a536bc54e0f1a/src/lib/rpc/websocket_server.ts#L145)

Surprises:

- The documented install (`deno install` then `deno task compile`, per install.sh) fails on Deno 2.9.8: deno.lock pins npm tarballs from registry.npmmirror.com, which Deno rejects as not matching registry.npmjs.org. The harness ran from source with --no-lock.
- The timeout message 'Script execution timeout (10 seconds)' never reaches the caller: the aborted process resolves output() with success:false, so the caller gets only Deno's Download/Check stderr lines (P6).
- Printed output is lost whenever a script fails: the router returns only stderr as error (X3).
- Network is unrestricted by design (P3 works). The help text calls this 'Sandboxed execution keeps your system safe' while also allowing fetch to any host, including localhost services and the lootbox server itself (X1, X2).
- Each execution costs about 0.6 s because the script is type-checked and client.ts is re-downloaded with --reload every time.
- The spec's plain-JS probes fail TypeScript strict checking (TS7017, TS2532, TS2683), so model-written code that a JS sandbox would run can be rejected here before execution.
- Every script and its output are persisted to a SQLite history in the user's home data dir by default, which matters for code that handles sensitive data.

From the source:

- **Bridge.** Bootstrap passes two host References ($0 rpc, $1 log) into evalClosure; guest code only sees external_* closures over them. Arguments and results cross as JSON strings, and rpc uses apply with result.promise so calls overlap. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L208-L248)
- **Isolation boundary.** New ivm.Isolate with memoryLimit per run, disposed in finally. Two timeout layers: the eval timeout stops sync loops, a host timer disposes the isolate while it awaits. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L184-L194; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L275-L292)
- **Deployment.** The constructor throws unless Node runs with --no-node-snapshot, because isolate creation otherwise crashes the process. TypeScript is stripped on the host with esbuild, a native binary. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L48-L58; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L131)
- **API shape.** Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L164-L186)
- **Discovery.** Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L189-L213)
- **Credentials.** Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L102-L119)
- **Defaults.** Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L20-L21)
- **Errors.** The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/types.ts#L50-L54; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L153-L157; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L266-L270; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L425-L429)
- **Output channel.** Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/transport.ts#L76-L80; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L38-L40)

Surprises:

- One of ten default P7 runs ended with the host process segfaulting (exit 139) right after Mastra returned the memory-limit error; the other nine continued normally.
- error.line is in the result type but never filled.

### Mastra Code Mode, default stdio transport on LocalSandbox

- Source: npm @mastra/core 1.85.0 (createCodeMode from @mastra/core/tools); repo https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra at `@mastra/core 1.85.0; source read at aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00`
- Language and engine: TS (types stripped before running), A child `node --experimental-strip-types` process per run (host Node 24.22.1), spawned through LocalSandbox; no isolation unless `isolation` is set
- How it was run: createCodeMode({ tools: { lookup }, sandbox: new LocalSandbox() }).tool.execute({ code }, {}), the docs quickstart setup
- Defaults: time 30 s, then the process tree is killed; memory none from Mastra; the child node's own V8 heap limit (about 4.2 GB here); output no cap; tool_calls no cap

From the source:

- **Isolation boundary.** The stdio transport writes the program to a temp .ts file and spawns `node --experimental-strip-types` through the sandbox. With LocalSandbox the isolation default is 'none', and the docs say this runs 'as a host node process with host privileges'. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/transport.ts#L29-L55; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/local-sandbox.ts#L120-L129)
- **Env.** LocalSandbox passes only PATH plus explicitly configured env to commands, so host secrets in env do not reach the program by default. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/local-sandbox.ts#L92-L109; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/local-sandbox.ts#L682-L688)
- **Seatbelt profile.** The generated macOS profile allows all file reads, allows process-exec and fork, limits writes to the workspace and temp dirs, and denies network unless allowNetwork. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/native-sandbox/seatbelt.ts#L103-L108; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/native-sandbox/seatbelt.ts#L148-L150; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/workspace/sandbox/native-sandbox/seatbelt.ts#L186-L192)
- **Bridge.** Newline-delimited JSON frames on stdout with a NUL-delimited prefix; the host answers rpc frames on the child's stdin, matched by id so Promise.all works. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L98-L138)
- **API shape.** Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L164-L186)
- **Discovery.** Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L189-L213)
- **Credentials.** Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L102-L119)
- **Defaults.** Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L20-L21)
- **Errors.** The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/types.ts#L50-L54; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L153-L157; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L266-L270; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L425-L429)
- **Output channel.** Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/transport.ts#L76-L80; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L38-L40)

Surprises:

- The quickstart on the docs page uses `new LocalSandbox()`, which runs model code as a full host Node process: it read /etc/hosts, reached example.com and ran a shell command.
- Even with seatbelt isolation the program reads any file the user can read and can exec binaries; only network and writes are restricted.
- Env is scrubbed to PATH by default, which is stricter than most host-process runners.
