From the source:

- **Bridge.** Uses the synchronous QuickJS build on purpose: each external_* call hands the guest a deferred promise and returns at once, and the host pumps the guest job queue when the dispatch settles, so Promise.all overlaps calls. The authors note the asyncify build cannot suspend twice. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L29-L41; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L325-L347)
- **Isolation boundary.** New QuickJS runtime and context per run, memory and stack limits set, bridge functions deleted from globalThis after bootstrap, console frozen. The guest sees only external_* closures. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L229-L232; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L359-L401)
- **Limits.** Time is enforced by an interrupt handler comparing Date.now() to the deadline, plus a host timer for time spent awaiting. The interrupt only fires between guest operations on the host thread, so the host event loop is blocked until then (P6x). (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L289-L305)
- **API shape.** Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L164-L186)
- **Discovery.** Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L189-L213)
- **Credentials.** Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L102-L119)
- **Defaults.** Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L20-L21)
- **Errors.** The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/types.ts#L50-L54; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L153-L157; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L266-L270; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L425-L429)
- **Output channel.** Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/transport.ts#L76-L80; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L38-L40)

Surprises:

- A runaway loop blocks the whole host Node event loop until the timeout (0 of 50 timer ticks in 5 s): on a server, every other request stalls for up to 30 s. The docs describe QuickJS only as slower than the other transports.
- memoryLimitMb caps the QuickJS heap, but host RSS rose to 1.2 to 1.6 GB under the 128 MB default and to 785 MB under 32 MB, and stayed there: the shared WASM module's memory does not shrink.
- error.line is in the result type but never filled, so the model gets no line numbers.
- The docs page gives no default for config.timeout; the code default is 30 s (types.ts:32).

### mcp-gway (deuriib/mcp-gateway) Code Mode, executeTool (Starlark)

- Source: https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway (PyPI mcp-gway); docs/code-mode.md at `mcp-gway 6.9.2 from PyPI, byte-identical (diff -r) to src/mcp_gway at tag v6.9.2 = 93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71 (2026-11-10). Engine starlark-pyo3 2026.1.3 (PyO3 binding of starlark-rust), mcp 2.3.0 in the host venv. Container run: ghcr.io/deuriib/mcp-gway:6.9.2@sha256:3471b4784f3c3a882d9ea32d277ce499623b87421578cd4609cca99cf5955b18 (linux/amd64 only, emulated on arm64; ships mcp 2.0.0).`
- Language and engine: Python subset (Starlark, standard dialect: no while, no top-level for, no recursion), starlark-rust through starlark-pyo3, evaluated in-process in the gateway's Python process on a ThreadPoolExecutor worker, fresh starlark Module per execution, no step, memory or output limits in the interpreter. A regex validator rejects source containing import/class, the words open/os/sys/subprocess/socket, or any "__" before evaluation.
- How it was run: mcp-gway serve --transport http on 127.0.0.1 (ports 42160-42164) with HOME pointed at research/probes/mcp-gway-codemode/home; one local stdio upstream `Probe` (node lookup-server.mjs) registered with `mcp-gway add`. probe.py sends raw JSON-RPC tools/call executeTool {code} to POST /mcp (the endpoint an MCP client uses), saving the full JSON-RPC body because failures come back as JSON-RPC errors. Hardened run uses the project's published image with docker-compose.prod.yml's limits.
- Defaults: time 30 s wall per executeTool (DEFAULT_EXECUTE_TIMEOUT, code_mode.py:36), overridable by MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT and by a per-call `timeout` argument that the caller (the model) supplies with no ceiling (code_mode.py:83-87). Enforced only as future.result(timeout) on a worker thread (sandbox.py:285-297): it never stops CPU-bound Starlark (GIL held) and reports only after the script ends. Per upstream tool call: server config timeout 5,000 ms (server_factory.py:211-215).; memory None. Starlark runs in the gateway process with no heap or step budget. docker-compose.yml sets the whole container to 512m and docker-compose.prod.yml to 256m, which OOM-kills the gateway, not the execution.; output Envelope capped at MCP_GWAY_MAX_RESULT_BYTES (default 262,144, min 1,024, max 8,388,608); logs capped at 200 lines and 65,536 bytes, dropping whole lines from the front with a marker; result strings cut to 8,192 chars (2,048 on a second pass) with "…[truncated N bytes — ...]" (budget.py:19-31, 124-141, 176-248).; tool_calls No per-execution call-count limit. callManyTool (host-side only): at most 50 items, 8 concurrent, 120 s batch default (code_mode.py:37, 185, 615).
- Hardened config: Project's published image ghcr.io/deuriib/mcp-gway:6.9.2 (digest above) run with exactly the docker-compose.prod.yml limits and flags: --memory 256m --cpus 0.5 --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:size=64m --tmpfs /home/gateway/.cache:size=16m --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges:true (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/docker-compose.prod.yml#L27-L46), plus the documented knobs MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT=1 (docs/code-mode.md Execution Budgets) and MCP_GWAY_MAX_RESULT_BYTES=1024 (the documented minimum, docs/code-mode.md Result Budget; budget.py:19-21). Upstream lookup is research/probes/mcp-gway-codemode/container/lookup_server.py run inside the container (MCP_GWAY_ALLOW_LOCAL_COMMANDS=python). Script: research/probes/mcp-gway-codemode/start-container.sh. The same env knobs were also run on the host without the container (out/hardened-*.txt); results agree except P7, where the harness killed the host gateway at 4,144 MB phys_footprint after 7.2 s. No interpreter step or memory limit is exposed.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each registered server with is_code_mode_client becomes a Starlark struct named after the server (and its PascalCase alias) whose fields are Python callables, one per tools_to_execute-allowed tool, built by introspecting a ServerStruct object and emitting `Name = struct(tool = Name_tool)` preamble lines. The model reads .pyi stubs generated from each tool's JSON Schema (flat params, type mapping, first line of the description). (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/sandbox.py#L233-L251, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/server_factory.py#L370-L437, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/registry.py#L361-L392)
- **Discovery.** On demand. tools/list returns only five meta-tools (listToolFiles, readToolFile, getToolDocs, executeTool, callManyTool; out/tools-list.json); stubs are read per server or per tool (binding_level server|tool), so the prompt does not grow with the catalog. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/gateway.py#L207-L310, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/code_mode.py#L390-L480)
- **Bridge.** Synchronous Python callable inside the Starlark eval: tool_fn schedules _call_tool_async on the script's private event loop with run_coroutine_threadsafe and blocks on future.result. The call re-checks the tools_to_execute allow-list, opens (or reuses within this script) an MCP session to the upstream, and returns json.loads of the joined text content. Upstream isError is ignored, so a failed tool returns its error text as data. Serial by construction. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/server_factory.py#L408-L431, #L185-L299, #L525-L541)
- **Isolation boundary.** In-process starlark-rust (standard dialect, no I/O builtins, no load loader) plus a regex pre-filter on source text (import/class lines, the words open/os/sys/subprocess/socket outside string literals, any "__"). The executeTool description claims L2 "memory isolation" and L3 "bounded execution timeout"; the code has neither: no heap limit, and the timeout is a future.result on a thread whose `with ThreadPoolExecutor` exit waits for the runaway eval, which also holds the GIL and freezes the gateway. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/sandbox.py#L185-L299, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/code_mode.py#L90-L145, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/gateway.py#L255; research/probes/mcp-gway-codemode/out/gil-check.txt)
- **Output channel.** JSON envelope {result, logs, calls, usage}: `result` global (or an implicit last-expression rewrite), print() captured into logs, the per-call trace, and usage.truncated. Size budget trims logs, trace, then result, always with a marker and valid JSON. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/sandbox.py#L155-L179, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/budget.py#L124-L248)
- **State.** Fresh sl.Module per execution, but one StarlarkSandbox object per gateway whose _logs list is reset at the start of every execution and read at the end. Concurrent executions share it: in X1, request B's response contained "SECRET-FROM-A-2" printed by request A, and A lost its first line. The server_factory comment says ContextVars keep concurrent scripts from sharing caches and traces; logs were left out. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/sandbox.py#L196-L202 and #L224, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/code_mode.py#L269 and #L526, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/server_factory.py#L25-L27; research/probes/mcp-gway-codemode/out/X1.txt)
- **Errors.** Any exception from executeTool becomes a JSON-RPC error whose data carries only the exception type and an allow-listed [reason=...] token, to avoid leaking secrets in messages. A model never sees the Starlark message, line, logs or call trace of a failed script. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/gateway.py#L186-L202 and #L675-L708)
- **Limits.** Execution timeout resolves per-call `timeout` > MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT > 30 s; the per-call value comes from the tool arguments, so the caller can raise its own budget (600 s accepted under MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT=1). No step, memory or tool-call limits. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/code_mode.py#L35-L87 and #L482-L493; research/probes/mcp-gway-codemode/out/hardened-X2.txt)
- **Credentials and approvals.** Upstream secrets stay on the host side: per-server environment values may be {env:NAME} placeholders resolved only into the spawned child, OAuth tokens live under ~/.config/mcp-gway/tokens, and remote URLs pass an SSRF guard (https only, pinned DNS). Local commands must be on an allow-list (default npx, bunx, uvx, pipx). tools_to_auto_execute exists for an agent loop, but executeTool calls are not gated by approvals. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/core/client.py#L53-L80, https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/src/mcp_gway/domain/policy.py#L29-L46)
- **Maintenance.** MIT, single author, 0 GitHub stars, last push 2026-11-10 (v6.9.2). Heavy release cadence (tags through v6.9.2); container image is linux/amd64 only. (https://github.com/deuriib/mcp-gateway/blob/93d8f50ea4a5d16a8a7cfc5b7ad9056bd81e4b71/pyproject.toml#L1-L10, GitHub API repos/deuriib/mcp-gateway)

Surprises:

- docs/code-mode.md says "Every Code Mode execution is time-bounded" and the executeTool description promises "L3 bounded execution timeout", but a CPU-bound script is never stopped: starlark-pyo3 holds the GIL, so the 30 s (or 1 s) timeout never fires and the whole gateway, /health included, freezes (P6, gil-check.txt).
- When the timeout does fire (tool-bound code releases the GIL), the error arrives only after the script finishes and all its tool calls have run (X2: 0.5 s budget, 5 calls, 1.85 s).
- The executeTool description claims L2 "memory isolation"; there is no memory limit. On the host it grew to 56 GB phys_footprint; under the prod compose limit the kernel OOM-kills the entire gateway (P7).
- AGENTS.md:109 says offloading every tools/call to asyncio.to_thread keeps /health and /metrics responsive; for CPU-bound Starlark it does not, because the GIL is never released.
- Failed scripts return only {"type": "StarlarkError"}: no message or line. The docs tell the model to use the `calls` trace "instead of guessing why a script failed", but a failed script returns no trace at all.
- Concurrent executions leak print output into each other's responses through the shared StarlarkSandbox._logs (X1), although the tool description says each call runs in a "FRESH ISOLATED SCOPE".
- The per-call `timeout` argument from the model overrides the operator's MCP_GWAY_EXEC_TIMEOUT with no ceiling, so the operator cannot cap execution time.
- File, env and escape blocking (P4, P5, P12) is a regex on the source text, which also rejects harmless code such as a comment containing the word "os"; the real boundary is starlark-rust having no I/O builtins.
- An upstream tool's isError result is returned as a normal value with status "ok" in the trace (P10 code 4).
- Each executeTool spawns a fresh upstream stdio process. With the documented hardened settings in the prod container (0.5 CPU, 1 s timeout) even a single tool call cannot finish.

### mcp-run-python (Pyodide in Deno)

- Source: https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python (archived; PyPI mcp-run-python) at `mcp-run-python 0.0.22, commit 4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00 (archive notice, 2026-01-30); Deno 2.9.8 (Homebrew); Pyodide 0.28.2 (deno.jsonc)`
- Language and engine: Python, Pyodide (CPython compiled to wasm32) running in Deno (V8). Deno permission flags limit host access.
- How it was run: mcp_run_python.async_prepare_deno_env('stdio') (what code_sandbox uses) then the MCP stdio tool run_python_code; P5 and P12 also with the full host env forwarded to deno.
- Defaults: time none; the server has no timeout, and an infinite loop never returns (P6); memory no configured limit. Python heap hits MemoryError near 4 GiB (wasm32, inferred). V8 side not capped below 4 GiB (P7b).; output no cap observed (200000 chars intact in P2); tool_calls not applicable: no host tools
- Hardened config: allow_networking=False is the only public limit knob. When False, --allow-net is omitted from the deno run args (main.py:188-190 `_deno_run_args`: `if allow_networking: args += ['--allow-net']`; the hardened deno argv is ['run', '--allow-read=./node_modules', '--node-modules-dir=auto', 'src/main.ts', 'stdio', '--return-mode=json'], no --allow-net, confirmed in out/hardened-P1.txt). Set via code_sandbox(allow_networking=False) (code_sandbox.py:58), async_prepare_deno_env/prepare_deno_env/run_mcp_server(allow_networking=) (main.py:29, 84, 147), or CLI `--disable-networking` (_cli.py:27-28). No time, memory, output-size or tool-call knob exists: the CLI exposes only --port/--deps/--disable-networking (_cli.py:24-28) and grep of deno/src/main.ts and runCode.ts finds no timeout or memory limit. So every probe except P3 is run identically to defaults; only P3 changes. The server already runs without --allow-env, --allow-write or --allow-run and with --allow-read scoped to ./node_modules (main.py:191-195), which is the default, not a hardening step.

G3 holds: in every run a bystander sandbox (separate deno server, separate process group, opened before P7) ran print(1+1) -> 2 afterward, so the host and other sessions survive. The poisoned session's own next call returns run-error (that one Pyodide instance is dead), which is per-execution, not a host crash. Measured; see out/hardened-P7.txt and the mem-lock run. | research/probes/mcp-run-python/out/hardened-P7.txt |

In-sandbox asyncio.gather of five 200 ms sleeps took ~210 ms, so async scheduling works, but there is no host side to call. | research/probes/mcp-run-python/out/hardened-P9.txt |
| P12 Escape | escaped (JS realm; OS perms block) | Unchanged from default: the language boundary is still fully escaped; only Deno's permission layer limits blast radius. Pure-Python attempts stay inside Pyodide (subclass walk finds _wrap_close and Popen but subprocess.run -> OSError 'emscripten does not support processes'). The real escape is js.eval: this.constructor.constructor('return process')() yields the live host process (pid 30467 read), and the host Deno global is reached (version 2.9.8). Every OS action off that handle is then blocked by the run flags: readTextFileSync/writeTextFileSync/Deno.Command/dlopen/env.get all NotCapable, and Deno.permissions.requestSync('run') returns 'denied' (non-interactive). The server survived each of those attempts (print('alive') ran after). Two DoS footguns, same on default: os.system('echo PWNED') and the _wrap_close->system path trigger a spawnSync that needs --allow-env and crash the whole Pyodide/deno server with a fatal error (host crash of that one server; verified identical under default in out/hardened-P12-default-ossystem.txt). Cross-client note (out/hardened-P12x.txt): hardened allow_networking=False cannot run either HTTP mode at all (--allow-net is also what lets the HTTP server bind; it dies at listen with NotCapable, verified), and in stateful HTTP all client sessions share one Pyodide realm (one RunCode, main.ts:65,217; runCode.ts:21,35-37), so the P8 realm taint is also a cross-client taint. None of this moves the word: 'escaped' = the code reached the host runtime through the language, which it does. | research/probes/mcp-run-python/out/hardened-P12.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** One MCP tool, run_python_code(python_code, global_variables). global_variables go through pyodide.toPy, so they are JSON values only. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/main.ts#L94 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L59-L62)
- **Discovery.** The model sees one tool and its description. The description says code runs under Python 3.13. There is no discovery of host tools because there are none. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/main.ts#L94)
- **Bridge.** MCP JSON-RPC over stdio between the Python client and the deno process. The sandbox makes no callbacks to the host. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/code_sandbox.py#L75 (client side; this path is research/impls/mcp-run-python/src/mcp_run_python/code_sandbox.py:75))
- **Isolation boundary.** Deno flags are the boundary. The run step gets --allow-net (unrestricted when allow_networking is True) and --allow-read=./node_modules. No --allow-env, --allow-write, or --allow-run. The JS global is still reachable from Python. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/main.py#L190-L192 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/main.py#L168-L170 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/polyfill.ts#L4-L8)
- **Output channel.** stdout and stderr go to an output array. Return value is JSON from the last expression. No truncation in the server code. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L88-L97 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L134-L140)
- **Limits.** The server code sets no timeout and no memory limit. The only memory stop observed is the wasm32 MemoryError. (grep of mcp_run_python/deno/src/main.ts and runCode.ts for timeout, limit: no matches. Probes P6, P7, P7b.)
- **State.** Each run gets fresh Python globals (globals: pyodide.toPy({...})), but the Pyodide instance is reused, so sys and the JS realm persist. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L35-L37 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L59-L60)
- **Errors.** formatError strips Pyodide-internal frames and keeps user lines. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L197-L206)
- **Anything else.** allow_networking defaults to True (code_sandbox signature). Startup loads micropip and pydantic from the Pyodide CDN. The generated prepareEnvCode.ts is gitignored and must be produced by build/build.py before the server runs. (https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/code_sandbox.py#L58 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/mcp_run_python/deno/src/runCode.ts#L112 ; https://github.com/pydantic/mcp-run-python/blob/4f93a9261d5e9905cb3e93b4817bda7c3470ac00/.gitignore#L16 (gitignore at repo root))

Surprises:

- README claim that Pyodide runs arbitrary JavaScript is confirmed (P12: js.eval returns 3, Deno global reached).
- README claim that Deno has no good memory limit is confirmed for the JS side (P7b 3 of 3 runs past 4 GiB). Refuted for the Python side: MemoryError near 4 GiB in 4 of 5 P7 runs.
- README claim that code can taint the runtime is confirmed: Array.prototype and globalThis changes persist across runs in one server.
- README claim about files is partly confirmed: Deno host reads and writes are blocked by flags, but readDir inside node_modules and in-memory /tmp work.
- Fresh-globals design does not isolate state: sys attributes and JS globals survive across runs.
- Default config passes --allow-net with no host list, so js.fetch can reach any host. Only example.com was contacted by the probes.
- P1 and P9 cannot be expressed because there is no host-tool bridge. This is not a sandbox limit but a missing feature.

### mcp-use Python CodeModeConnector (MCPClient code_mode=True)

- Source: https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use (PyPI mcp-use 1.7.1) at `mcp-use 1.7.1 from PyPI (mcp 1.30.0). Repo read at 8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354; its code_executor.py differs from 1.7.1 only in using perf_counter instead of time.time for execution_time.`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython exec() of the code wrapped in an async function, inside the agent's own process and event loop, with a hand-picked __builtins__ dict. The asyncio module is handed to the guest. No process, interpreter or OS boundary.
- How it was run: MCPClient(config, code_mode=True); create_all_sessions(); then sessions['code_mode'].connector.call_tool('execute_code', {'code': ...}), the internal CodeModeConnector an agent's execute_code tool call reaches. lookup is served by a stdio MCP server (host_server.py) that counts calls.
- Defaults: time 30 s via asyncio.wait_for (code_executor.py:87), default from the execute_code tool schema (code_mode.py:76) which the model can override. It cannot interrupt synchronous code.; memory None; guest objects live in the agent process.; output None. logs list plus result, JSON-encoded into one TextContent (code_mode.py:132-134).; tool_calls None.
- Hardened config: execute_code timeout=10 (seconds), passed as the tool argument; it is the only knob (code_mode.py:76, client.py execute_code(code, timeout)). It is a model-controlled argument, and MCPClient(sandbox=True) sandboxes MCP servers via E2B, not code-mode code.

From the source:

- **API shape.** One namespace object per MCP server, built with type(server_name, (), {})(); each tool becomes an async wrapper `await server.tool(**kwargs)` that calls session.call_tool and JSON-decodes the first text content. Names are sanitized to identifiers. No types or stubs are generated. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L186-L229 and #L231-L273)
- **Discovery.** On demand: search_tools(query, detail_level) inside the code and as a second MCP tool, a substring match over name, description and server; detail_level='full' returns input schemas. Only two tools (execute_code, search_tools) are exposed to the model, so the prompt does not grow with the catalog. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L275-L352 ; https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/connectors/code_mode.py#L47-L106)
- **Bridge.** Direct in-process async calls: the wrapper closure holds the MCPClient and awaits the real MCP session. Because the guest shares the process, it can walk that closure to the client and read every server's config and env (out/closure-check.txt). (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L243-L266 ; research/probes/mcp-use-codemode/out/closure-check.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** Only a curated __builtins__ dict (no __import__, open, eval). It keeps getattr and type and hands over the asyncio module, and exec runs in-process, so __subclasses__ and asyncio subprocess/network APIs reach the host. The docstring calls it "a secure execution environment"; P3, P4, P5 and P12 show it is not. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L22-L27 (claim), #L136-L180 (builtins, asyncio), #L116-L127 (exec))
- **Output channel.** print is replaced with a capture into logs; stdout/stderr are also redirected and appended. The model gets JSON {result, logs, error, execution_time}. No truncation. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L67-L104)
- **Limits.** Only asyncio.wait_for(timeout) around the coroutine, which cannot preempt synchronous loops. No memory, output or call limits. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L84-L90)
- **State.** Fresh namespace per execution; host-side MCP sessions persist. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L72-L73)
- **Errors.** Any exception becomes error=str(e): message only, no type or line. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/client/code_executor.py#L92-L94)
- **Anything else.** Anonymized telemetry (PostHog and Scarf) is on by default and logs that on import; MCP_USE_ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false turns it off. The harness set it before each run; one early import in this session ran without it. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/python/mcp_use/telemetry/telemetry.py#L126-L164)

Surprises:

- The docstring calls CodeExecutor "a secure execution environment" (code_executor.py:25-27). It is exec() in the agent process with the asyncio module and getattr exposed; network, file, env and shell access all worked.
- The 30 s timeout cannot stop synchronous code because it is an asyncio timer on the same loop the guest blocks; one `while True: pass` hangs the whole agent.
- The timeout is a model-supplied tool argument in the execute_code schema, so the model, not the host, picks its own limit.
- Guest code can reach the MCPClient through the search_tools closure and read every configured server's env, where MCP API keys usually live.
- Telemetry to PostHog and Scarf is on by default for the library.

- Source: https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use (npm @mcp-use/client 2.4.6) at `@mcp-use/client 2.4.6 from npm (package.json at 8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354 also says 2.4.6); Node 24.22.1`

From the source:

- **API shape.** Per MCP server, a plain object whose properties are async wrappers calling session.connector.callTool and JSON-decoding the first text item. No types generated. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L319-L352)
- **Discovery.** search_tools inside the code and as a separate MCP tool; the model sees two tools (execute_code, search_tools), not every schema. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor.ts#L138 ; https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/connector.ts#L160-L230)
- **Bridge.** Direct in-process async calls from vm code to host closures; no serialization boundary. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L331-L347)
- **Isolation boundary.** node:vm with host intrinsics (Object, Array, Promise, setTimeout...) placed into the context; the class comment says it runs code "in an isolated V8 context". Node documents node:vm as not a security mechanism, and P12 escaped through the constructor chain. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L157-L161 (claim) and #L278-L317 (host globals))
- **Output channel.** console.* captured into logs; result is the async IIFE's return value; error is e.message. Returned as one JSON text item. No cap. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L206-L264 ; https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/connector.ts#L365-L384)
- **Limits.** Only the vm timeout, which bounds the synchronous part of runInNewContext. memoryLimitMb is documented as reserved and not enforced. The configured timeoutMs is overridden by the connector's default. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L162-L172 , #L233-L236 ; https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/connector.ts#L367 ; https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/core/node.ts#L85-L93)
- **State.** New context per execution. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L213 and #L356)
- **Errors.** error = e.message, or "Script execution timed out"; the stack is only logged at debug level. (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/code-mode/executor-vm.ts#L239-L254)
- **Anything else.** Asking for executor 'e2b' without an apiKey logs a warning and silently falls back to the in-process VM executor. Telemetry is on by default (MCP_USE_ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false disables it; the harness set it). (https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/core/node.ts#L557-L571 ; https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use/blob/8ff4b865e0e5712c66d5077e93392807daca9354/libraries/typescript/packages/client/src/telemetry/telemetry.ts#L159-L173)

Surprises:

- The configured executorOptions.timeoutMs is ignored on the agent path: the connector passes `args.timeout || 30000` (connector.ts:367), so the hardened 10 s run stopped at 30 s.
- memoryLimitMb is accepted and documented as reserved, but nothing enforces it.
- The vm timeout stops only synchronous code before the first await; `await null; while(true){}` freezes the host process indefinitely.
- Requesting the E2B executor without a key silently falls back to the in-process node:vm executor with only a log warning (node.ts:557-571).
- The executor is described as "an isolated V8 context" (executor-vm.ts:159); one constructor-chain expression returns the host process.

- Source: PyPI agent-framework-hyperlight 1.0.0b261112 (sdist sha256 a8895150f63773127fc9d95395b2f368330eab34257ed81f0af96ae294395c54); blog https://devblogs.microsoft.com/agent-framework/codeact-with-hyperlight/ ; the listed repo github.com/microsoft/agent-framework returned 404 on 2026-11-22 at `agent-framework-hyperlight 1.0.0b261112, agent-framework-core 1.26.0, run with hyperlight-sandbox / -python-guest / -backend-wasm 0.10.0 (OUT OF PIN: the package requires hyperlight-sandbox <0.10, and 0.9.0 has no macOS backend). From the source:

- **API shape.** A single built-in call_tool(name, **kwargs) inside the guest; each registered FunctionTool becomes a host callback registered with sandbox.register_tool(name, callback). The execute_code description lists every tool with its parameters (compact or JSON Schema). (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:1607-1612 ; research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_instructions.py:17-58 and :134-171)
- **Discovery.** All upfront: tool summaries are rendered into the execute_code tool description (or instructions via build_instructions). No search. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_instructions.py:134-171)
- **Bridge.** Synchronous host callback through the Hyperlight FFI. Each callback runs the async FunctionTool.invoke on a fresh thread with asyncio.run and returns raw Python primitives to the guest. Host exceptions become "Host tool execution failed." unless include_detailed_errors. Credentials stay in the host callback. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:1367-1401)
- **Isolation boundary.** Hyperlight micro-VM (hypervisor) plus a Wasm runtime with WASI CPython. No filesystem without mounts, no network without allowed_domains, empty environment. The blog says "every execute_code call gets its own freshly created micro-VM"; the code keeps one sandbox per tool configuration and restores a warm snapshot before each call, which gives fresh state but not a fresh VM. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:1580-1645 and :376-377 ; research/probes/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/out/blog-quotes.md)
- **Output channel.** stdout as text content, then output files from /output if mounts exist, then stderr on success. On failure an error Content "Execution error" whose details are None unless include_detailed_errors=True. Some failures (guest abort) raise instead of returning content. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:1311-1364 and :2082-2085)
- **Limits.** Time: 30 s budget, interruptible. Memory: whatever hyperlight-sandbox defaults to (heap_size not passed). Output files: 20 / 5 MB / 20 MB. stdout: no documented cap, but large prints abort the guest. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:52-61 , :1589-1603 ; research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/.venv-hl010/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hyperlight_sandbox/__init__.py:22-29)
- **State.** Snapshot taken after warm-up and restored before every execution, so no state carries over. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:1624-1643 and :376-377)
- **Errors.** Redacted by default: the model sees "Execution error" with no message. include_detailed_errors=True exposes stderr (message without line numbers here). (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/agent_framework_hyperlight/_execute_code_tool.py:1356-1364 ; research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/README.md:22-37)
- **Anything else.** Platform: the package pins hyperlight-sandbox <0.10 and installs the Wasm backend only on Linux x86_64 and Windows AMD64; 0.10.0 (released two days after this beta) ships macOS arm64 wheels that run it through Hypervisor.framework. The README warns FIDES policy enforcement does not apply to tool calls made from inside code. Approval mode is configurable per tool. (research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/pyproject.toml:27-29 ; research/impls/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/pkg/agent_framework_hyperlight-1.0.0b261112/README.md:5-20 and :80-86 ; research/probes/ms-agent-framework-hyperlight/out/attempt-macos-hyperlight-0.10-override.txt)

Surprises:

- It runs on Apple Silicon after all, but only outside the package's pin: hyperlight-sandbox 0.10.0 ships macOS arm64 wheels linked to Hypervisor.framework, while agent-framework-hyperlight requires <0.10 and its README lists only Linux x86_64 and Windows.
- The source repo named in the PyPI metadata (github.com/microsoft/agent-framework) returned HTTP 404 on 2026-11-22; source was read from the PyPI sdist.
- A print of about 50 KB or more crashes the guest ("G2H ... Backpressure") and the call raises RuntimeError("Code execution failed.") with no hint that output size was the cause.
- The default memory budget is tiny: about 8-10 MB of user data before "Out of physical memory".
- Errors are redacted by default, so the model cannot see its own exception message ("Execution error", details None).
- The blog says each execute_code call gets a "freshly created micro-VM"; the code reuses one sandbox per configuration and restores a snapshot each call (fresh state, measured 60 ms per call, not a new VM).
- The guest CPython has no asyncio, threading, socket, subprocess or urllib, so tool calls are strictly serial.
- PyO3 prints "WasmSandbox is unsendable, but is being dropped on another thread" when the tool is garbage-collected without the internal registry close.

### My Cool Proxy (Lua code-mode MCP gateway)

- Source: https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy (npm @karashiiro/my-cool-proxy) at `npm @karashiiro/my-cool-proxy 1.6.2 (ran); source read at 46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de (2026-04-09, package version 1.6.2); wasmoon 1.16.0`
- Language and engine: Lua 5.4, wasmoon 1.16.0: the reference Lua 5.4 interpreter compiled to WebAssembly, run in the gateway's Node.js process on the main thread, a new LuaEngine per execution. JS values cross with wasmoon's default proxying (enableProxy true).
- How it was run: npm install @karashiiro/my-cool-proxy@1.6.2 into research/impls/my-cool-proxy/npm; started bin/my-cool-proxy.mjs with CONFIG_PATH=config.json (transport http on 127.0.0.1:41420, one HTTP MCP client `probe` = lib lookup server on 41421) and HOME/XDG dirs pointed at a probe folder. Each driver session first calls list-servers and tool-details(probe, lookup), as the execute tool description requires, then calls execute {script}. A second run used transport stdio (stdio-inject.mjs).
- Defaults: time None. executeScript calls engine.doString(script) with no timeout; wasmoon's own functionTimeout and per-call timeout options are not used.; memory None set by the gateway. The only stop is the wasm32 heap ceiling of the wasmoon build (hit at about 2.2 GB RSS in P7). wasmoon's traceAllocations/setMemoryMax option is not used.; output print() is not returned (goes to process stdout). The result() value is returned inline up to resultSizeThreshold (default 50,000 bytes), above that offloaded with an execution ID and a schema summary.; tool_calls No cap.; hardened_null_reason The documented config (docs/configuration.md) has no execution timeout, memory, or call-count option; only resultSizeThreshold and tool filtering. wasmoon exposes functionTimeout, a doString timeout and setMemoryMax, but the gateway does not wire them to config, and RUBRIC forbids adding wrappers.

|---|---|---|---|

One script ran r.__proto__.probePolluted = "written-by-guest-lua"; after that every new MCP session, including a raw curl initialize, got "Parse error: Invalid JSON-RPC message" until the gateway was restarted. No process, env or fs access was reached in these attempts. | research/probes/my-cool-proxy/out/P12.txt, research/probes/my-cool-proxy/out/P12b-P12.txt, research/probes/my-cool-proxy/out/P12c-P12.txt, research/probes/my-cool-proxy/out/P12-pollution.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each connected MCP server becomes a Lua global table named by sanitizeLuaIdentifier(server), with one function per tool from client.listTools() (called on every execution). Each function returns a JS promise that the script unwraps with :await(). result(value) sets the return value. A _gateway table adds resource, prompt, completion, stats and offloaded-result builtins. (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L182-L390, https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/apps/gateway/src/tools/execute-lua-tool.ts#L45-L83)
- **Discovery.** On demand through MCP tools: list-servers, list-server-tools, tool-details and inspect-tool-response. A guard refuses any tool call from Lua until tool-details or inspect-tool-response has been called for that tool in the session, so the model must read the schema first. Server instructions preload brief excerpts of servers and tools. Scales past 100 tools without putting all schemas in the prompt. (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/apps/gateway/src/tools/gateway-builtins-builder.ts#L299-L316, https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L339-L388, https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/README.md#L88-L100)
- **Bridge.** wasmoon calls the JS wrapper directly in-process; the wrapper runs the guard synchronously, then calls the upstream through the MCP client's experimental tasks callToolStream. Results: structuredContent, else JSON-parsed single text, else the whole CallToolResult. An upstream isError result is thrown into Lua. (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L209-L330)
- **Isolation boundary.** Lua 5.4 in WebAssembly in the gateway's Node process. createEngine sets os, io, require, dofile, loadfile, package and debug to nil; load and string.dump remain. JS objects reach Lua as wasmoon proxies (enableProxy defaults to true), which exposes host-realm objects such as Object.prototype to reads and writes (P12). (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L154-L180; research/impls/my-cool-proxy/npm/node_modules/wasmoon/dist/index.js:1187 (LuaEngine options default enableProxy = true))
- **Output channel.** Only result() goes back. Objects become JSON text plus structuredContent; strings become "Script executed successfully.\n\nResult:\n..."; results above resultSizeThreshold (50,000) are offloaded with an ID. print() is wasmoon's stdout, which is the gateway's stdout; on the stdio transport that is the JSON-RPC channel, and out/stdio-inject.txt shows a guest print forging the response to the pending tools/call (client saw "FORGED by guest print for id 3" instead of "REAL-2"). (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/apps/gateway/src/tools/execute-lua-tool.ts#L189-L262, research/probes/my-cool-proxy/out/stdio-inject.txt)
- **Limits.** No time, memory or call-count limit in the gateway. wasmoon supports functionTimeout, a doString timeout and setMemoryMax with traceAllocations, none of which are passed. (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L26-L31 and #L157, research/impls/my-cool-proxy/npm/node_modules/wasmoon/dist/index.js:148, :522, :1187)
- **State.** New LuaEngine per execution, closed in finally. Host-realm state is shared across executions and sessions through the proxied JS objects (P12 pollution persisted until restart). (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L43-L45 and #L124-L126, research/probes/my-cool-proxy/out/P12-pollution.txt)
- **Errors.** Errors return isError true with "Script execution failed:" plus the Lua message, chunk line and traceback, and targeted hints for nil globals (unknown server) and nil fields (unknown tool). (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/packages/lua-runtime/src/runtime.ts#L67-L123, https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/apps/gateway/src/tools/execute-lua-tool.ts#L250-L262)
- **Credentials.** Upstream server credentials (headers, env for stdio servers) live in the gateway config; Lua sees only tool results. OAuth is not supported yet (README). (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/docs/configuration.md, https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/README.md#L189)
- **Maintenance.** MIT license; last commit on main 2026-04-09; npm 1.6.2. (https://github.com/karashiiro/my-cool-proxy/blob/46bfe3810988b202a6458868f77597b3874ae1de/LICENSE)

Surprises:

- Guest Lua can write to the gateway's own Object.prototype through a proxied tool result; one such write made every later MCP session fail with "Invalid JSON-RPC message" until restart (out/P12-pollution.txt).
- An infinite loop freezes the entire gateway, every session, and blocks graceful SIGTERM shutdown; only SIGKILL stops it.
- On the stdio transport, print() writes into the JSON-RPC stream and can forge responses (out/stdio-inject.txt).
- The memory stop is an accident of wasm32, at about 2.2 GB of gateway RSS, and the memory is not returned afterwards (RSS stayed about 1.2 GB).
- The first execute in a new session sees no servers until list-servers has run, and tool calls fail until tool-details has been called for that tool.
- wasmoon ships timeout and memory-cap options that the gateway does not use.

### Open-PTC (daly2211/open-ptc)

- Source: https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc at `2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de (last commit 2026-04-25); run on host Deno 2.9.8; dependencies resolved with --no-lock (see surprises)`
- Language and engine: TS, A fresh `deno run` subprocess per execution (V8, Deno's own permission system: --allow-net=localhost:<rpc port>, --allow-env=RPC_SERVER_URL, nothing else). There is only this one execution mode in the code; the README's 'Deno isolate' and 'restricted Deno subprocess' describe the same subprocess.
- How it was run: deno run --allow-all --no-lock src/server.ts --ws (the project's own server, ports 41302 RPC / 41303 WS); the harness registers `lookup` over the WebSocket register_tools message and sends each probe as execute_code, the local-tool path used by the project's AI SDK and LangGraph examples. Sandbox code calls it as main.lookup(...).
- Defaults: time 30,000 ms wall clock per execution (CODE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS, src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts:150-156), enforced by SIGTERM on the subprocess.; memory None set. The subprocess gets Deno's default V8 heap; P7 reached 4.3 GB before the harness stopped it.; output None. stdout + stderr are returned whole (sandbox-executor.ts:161-166); P2 returned 200,003 chars.; tool_calls No count cap. WebSocket tool calls time out after 60 s each (src/ws/ws-protocol.ts WS_CONFIG.TOOL_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS). Proxy mode caps LLM chain depth at 10 (src/proxy/sandbox-orchestrator.ts:18), not tool calls.
- Hardened config: CODE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 (documented in .env.example:25-27, read at src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts:150-152). This is the only per-execution limit the project exposes; there is no memory, CPU, output or network option. The value 5000 is the harness's choice: the option takes any number. Docker Compose is documented but sets no memory or CPU limits (docker-compose.no-proxy.yml) and runs the same subprocess sandbox, so it was not used.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools become plain objects of arrow functions generated as source text and prepended to the user code: `const <server> = { <tool>: (input) => callTool('<ref>', input) }`, with WebSocket and proxy runtime tools under `const main`. TypeScript signatures for the model come from JSON Schema via json-schema-to-typescript compile(). (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts#L22-L58 and https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/codegen/signature-generator.ts#L91)
- **Discovery.** Two styles. MCP and REST modes expose on-demand discovery: get_tools_tree (/tree, optional descriptions and charLimit) and get_tool_signatures (/signatures filtered by serverNames/toolNames). Proxy mode instead concatenates every runtime and MCP signature into the code_executor tool description, so all schemas go in the prompt. (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/server.ts#L103-L115 and https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/proxy/repl-tool-builder.ts#L55-L63)
- **Bridge.** Sandbox code calls callTool(), which POSTs JSON-RPC to the host's RPC server over HTTP (localhost, port allowed by --allow-net). The RPC server routes by a global toolRef string: api_* to proxy sessions, main_* to WebSocket connections, anything else to MCP tools. It never checks which execution or connection made the request. (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/bridge/jrpc-client.ts#L3-L24 and https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/bridge/tool-bridge.ts#L159-L181)
- **Isolation boundary.** Each execution writes the code to a temp .ts file and spawns `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net=localhost:<rpc> --allow-env=RPC_SERVER_URL <file>`. The boundary is Deno's permission system in a separate OS process, not an isolate inside the server. The parent env is inherited (no clearEnv), so secrets are in the child's memory and hidden only by --allow-env. The README says 'secure Deno isolate' and 'separate Deno isolate per execution', and also says it 'should not be treated as hardened multi-tenant isolation'. (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts#L128-L145; README https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/README.md#L273-L283)
- **Output channel.** The model gets `stdout + "\n\n" + stderr + timeoutText` as one string plus a success flag (exit code 0). No return value channel, no truncation, ANSI colour codes from Deno's error printer pass through. (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts#L158-L167)
- **Limits.** Only a wall-clock timeout (CODE_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_MS, default 30000). No memory flag (no --v8-flags=--max-old-space-size), no output cap, no tool-call cap. (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/execution/sandbox-executor.ts#L132-L156)
- **State.** Fresh process per execution; nothing persists. No snapshot support. (research/probes/open-ptc/out/P8.txt; sandbox-executor.ts#L128-L170)
- **Errors.** No formatting by Open-PTC: the model sees Deno's raw uncaught-error print on stderr, including ANSI codes and the temp file path, with line numbers offset by the prepended code. (research/probes/open-ptc/out/P10b.txt)
- **Credentials.** MCP server credentials are substituted from the host env into the MCP client config (${VAR}) and stay in the host process; the sandbox gets only RPC_SERVER_URL. Good separation, but the RPC server and all public servers bind 0.0.0.0 with no authentication, so anyone on the network can call tools or run code. (https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/server.ts#L47-L68 and #L92, #L133)
- **Cross-tenant tool access (extra probe X1).** A second WebSocket connection's sandbox called the first connection's local `lookup` with callTool("main_<connA>.lookup", {id:50}) and got {id:50,value:100}; connection A's handler ran. Connection ids are `ws_${Date.now()}_${counter}`, so they are guessable. The README's 'namespace-isolated per WebSocket connection' holds only for the generated proxy object, not at the RPC server. (research/probes/open-ptc/out/X1.txt; https://github.com/daly2211/open-ptc/blob/2f2ef0ce4087d338a2cd1646c8ef18cc3f57b1de/src/servers/ws-server.ts#L50)

Surprises:

- The documented start command `deno run --allow-all src/server.ts` fails at this commit: deno.json imports the unpinned `https://esm.sh/json-schema-to-typescript?target=esnext`, whose content no longer matches deno.lock (integrity check failed). The Dockerfile copies deno.json but not deno.lock, so the Docker path works. The harness ran with --no-lock to match the Docker build.
- README says 'secure Deno isolate' and 'separate Deno isolate per execution'; the code spawns a separate `deno run` OS process per execution. The isolation that holds (P3, P4, P5, P12) comes from Deno permission flags, and it held in every probe.
- README says local tools are 'namespace-isolated per WebSocket connection'. Sandbox code from one connection called another connection's tool by its reference name (X1), because the shared RPC server routes by name with no caller check.
- No memory limit at all: one execution reached 4.3 GB in 7.4 s. The README lists memory controls under Future Improvements, so this is acknowledged.
- Setting RPC_SERVER_PORT alone breaks tool calls: the executor reads RPC_SERVER_URL (default http://localhost:9732) independently, so both must be set together.
- Error output carries ANSI colour escape codes and the host's temp directory path into the model's context.

### OpenClaw Code Mode, Node executor (node:vm in a worker thread, the default)

- Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw (src/agents/code-mode*.ts); npm openclaw at `npm openclaw@2026.11.6 (published dist, installed with --ignore-scripts into research/impls/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/npm); source read at tag v2026.11.6 = 06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638 (2026-11-19), cloned to research/impls/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/src`
- Language and engine: JS, Node.js node:vm context (fresh per cell) inside a pooled worker_threads Worker of the Gateway process, env {}, V8 heap resourceLimits; Node v24.22.1 on the host
- How it was run: createCodeModeTools(ctx) + applyCodeModeCatalog({...ctx, tools: [exec, wait, lookup]}) from the published dist chunks (src/agents/code-mode.ts:220 and :313; not in the package's public exports, so imported from dist/prompt-tool-policy-XiWNJtPU.mjs), then execTool.execute(id, {code}) and waitTool.execute on status 'waiting': the same exec/wait control tools the embedded agent runtime gives the model. lookup is a plugin-tagged AgentTool (setPluginToolMeta) in the hidden catalog; guest code calls it as the async global lookup({id}). OpenClaw HOME/state/config are pointed at research/probes/<impl>/state. P11 is also measured with WARM_HOST=1, which runs cells inside a bound LegacyPluginSdkResourceHost + GatewayScheduler as the Gateway does (scripts/perf/code-mode-engine-measure.ts does the same). Executor: tools.codeMode = {enabled: true, executor: 'node'} (node is also the default executor).
- Defaults: time timeoutMs 10,000 ms wall clock per exec or wait call (clamp 100-60,000), shared by worker preparation, guest work and inline tool waits; approval waits pause it. Pending tool calls can instead return status 'waiting' for a later wait with a fresh budget (src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts:110; docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md).; output maxOutputBytes 64 KiB shared by output entries, value and error across waits (clamp 1 KiB-10 MiB); over the cap a {truncated, omittedBytes, guidance, prefix} marker replaces the item. Console: each string clipped to 512 UTF-16 units with '…[truncated]', 16,384 units per cell then '[console output truncated]' (code-mode-runtime.ts:112; code-mode-controller-source.ts:101-115; code-mode-json.ts:93). A trailing expression returns null; only `return` sets the value.; tool_calls maxPendingToolCalls 16 in flight (clamp 1-128); further calls queue in the guest, up to 128 queued ordinary calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:114; code-mode-controller-source.ts:12, :227-230; code-mode-worker-types.ts:10). No per-exec total call cap was found on the exec path: 40 calls ran. Headless scripts default to 5 calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:26).; memory memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB, applied as the Worker's V8 resourceLimits (maxOldGenerationSizeMb = 60, maxYoungGenerationSizeMb = 4) plus a GC-pressure watchdog that fails the cell with runtime_unavailable and retires the worker. Not an RSS limit: external buffers are excluded, and up to eight warm workers may be kept (code-mode-node.ts:234-238; docs/tools/code-mode/executors.md).
- Hardened config: tools.codeMode = {enabled: true, executor: 'node', timeoutMs: 5000, memoryLimitBytes: 16 MiB, maxOutputBytes: 8192, maxSnapshotBytes: 1 MiB, maxPendingToolCalls: 8, snapshotTtlSeconds: 60} (fields and clamps: docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L104-L117). Tight but usable values inside the documented clamps (timeoutMs floor 100 ms, memory floor 1 MiB). The project exposes no option that makes node:vm an isolation boundary; its documented hardening is executor: 'quickjs', which is the separate impl openclaw-codemode-quickjs-wasi.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Every catalog-eligible tool becomes an async global function (callableName) plus a callable handle; bindings come from createCodeModeCatalogBindings. The model sees a bounded quick index of `name input -> output` hints built from JSON Schema, capped at 8,000 chars, and TypeScript-style declarations through API.list/API.read. Executable cells are plain JavaScript; TypeScript syntax and require/import are rejected before execution. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode.ts#L64, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode.ts#L111-L149, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-catalog.ts#L73, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L660-L671)
- **Discovery.** Hidden catalog, searched on demand: only exec and wait (plus required direct-only tools) are model-visible (telemetry visibleTools [exec, wait] in every result). Tools past the 8,000-char index are reachable through catalog.search(query) (BM25 lexical index, default 8 results, max 50) and handle.describe(). Scales past 100 tools without putting every schema in the prompt. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode.ts#L95-L100, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L629-L638, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L104-L117; research/probes/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/out/P1.txt)
- **Bridge.** Guest calls go through the controller's request() into a host callback that carries only strings (method, JSON args, id, stack); the host runs the call through runtime.callExactValue, the same tool execution path as normal turns (policy, approvals, before_tool_call hooks). Replies are queued on the host and pulled by the guest (__openclawSettleBridge). Node: host function __openclawHostRequest installed on the vm context and deleted from globals after the controller captures it. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L20-L32, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L221-L231, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts#L386, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts#L272-L300)
- **Isolation boundary.** node:vm context (createContext(Object.create(null)), microtaskMode afterEvaluate, dynamic import rejected) in a worker_threads Worker with env {} and V8 heap resourceLimits. The docs say plainly that this is NOT a security boundary. The code adds one concrete hole: the host realm's TextEncoder/TextDecoder classes are injected into the context and wrapped by guest classes that hold the host instance in a #private field (comment: 'Keep native encoding prototypes private'). Errors thrown by the host decoder (bad label, fatal decode) reach guest code unwrapped, so e.constructor.constructor is the host Function: process, child_process, fs and network follow (P12 #9-#12, P3 #3). env {} hides process.env, but `ps -E` on the gateway pid returns PROBE_SECRET. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts#L155-L182, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts#L252-L271, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.ts#L228-L239, docs/tools/code-mode/executors.md ('Node's node:vm is not a security boundary'); research/probes/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/out/P12.txt)
- **Output channel.** The model gets one JSON document: status, telemetry, ordered output entries (text(), json(), console.*) and the returned value or error. Over-budget items become an explicit truncation marker with the original JSON prefix and omittedBytes, not a silent cut. Console strings are clipped to 512 units each. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L101-L115, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-json.ts#L93, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode.ts#L226-L245; research/probes/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/out/P2.txt)
- **Limits.** All limits come from tools.codeMode (global or per agent) and are clamped in resolveCodeModeConfig: timeoutMs 10 s (100 ms-60 s), memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB (1 MiB-1 GiB), maxOutputBytes 64 KiB, maxSnapshotBytes 10 MiB, maxPendingToolCalls 16, snapshotTtlSeconds 900. For Node, memoryLimitBytes becomes the Worker's maxOldGenerationSizeMb (limit-4 MB) plus 4 MB young; a GC watchdog retires near-limit workers; the deadline is enforced by terminating the worker. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L96-L119, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.ts#L234-L238)
- **State.** Each exec gets a fresh context (globals never carry over), confirmed by P8. Workers are pooled and reused only when cells run inside the Gateway's bound resource host; without it every Node cell starts a new worker (about 200 ms). There is opt-in persistence: store(key, value)/load(key) keep small JSON values per session across cells and restarts, but only for a session-bound run (P8 #3 fails in this harness). A suspended cell (status 'waiting') keeps its live worker and context for wait. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L430-L445, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-session-store.ts#L315, docs/tools/code-mode/executors.md 'Understand waits and limits'; research/probes/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/out/P8.txt, out/P11.txt, out/warm-P11.txt)
- **Errors.** Guest errors return status failed with code internal_error and `Name: message` plus stack frames rewritten to openclaw-code-mode:user.js:line:col (user line numbers, wrapper removed); error text is bounded to 16,384 units. Parse errors are reported before execution with line and column. A runtime `ReferenceError: process|require|module is not defined` is rewritten into the generic 'module access is disabled' invalid_input message. Tool errors are catchable in guest code and are redacted (input shown as [redacted]). (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-source.ts#L212-L231, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts#L360-L380, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts#L455-L470, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L62-L85)
- **Activation and credentials.** With tools.codeMode absent, activation is 'auto': Code Mode engages automatically for catalog-preferred models (for example claude-opus-5-5, gpt-5.6, gemini-3.5-flash) with the Node executor unless executor: 'quickjs' is set. Credentials stay host-side: tools run in the Gateway with their normal auth, and the guest only receives JSON results. The lexical module check (code-mode-source.ts:226) is a usability guard, not a security control: it blocks the literal require()/import() but not Function-constructor paths. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L75-L77, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L107-L108, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L128-L140, docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md 'Shipped preferred models')
- **Maintenance.** MIT license; tag v2026.11.6 committed 2026-11-19; npm openclaw 2026.11.6. Extensive tests under src/agents/code-mode*.test.ts, including an engine-parity suite. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/package.json, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-engine-parity.test.ts)

Surprises:

- The guest-API docs say TextEncoder/TextDecoder 'provide local byte conversion, not filesystem, module, or network access' (docs/tools/code-mode/guest-api.md:50-52). Under the Node executor they are the escape: errors thrown by the injected host-realm decoder carry the host Function constructor, so guest code gets process, child_process, fs and network. The wrapper hides the host prototypes (code-mode-node.worker.ts:155-182) but not the host errors.
- The docs are honest that node:vm is 'not a security boundary', but it is the default executor, and with tools.codeMode absent Code Mode engages automatically ('auto') for preferred models such as claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-5.6. A default install with a preferred model therefore runs model-written code in an escapable context inside the Gateway process.
- Worker env {} hides process.env from an escaped cell, but `ps -E` on the shared pid still returns the Gateway's environment, PROBE_SECRET included.
- A runtime 'process is not defined' is reported as invalid_input 'code mode module access is disabled' with failurePhase 'input', although the code had already run.
- Without the Gateway's bound resource host every Node cell spawns a new worker (median 253 ms); inside it, cells reuse warm workers (median 0.95 ms). Direct callers of the exec tool pay the cold path.
- At memoryLimitBytes 16 MiB, a trivial concurrent `return 42` cell failed once (1 of 3 runs) with 'worker exhausted its 16 MiB JavaScript heap' while another cell was spinning.
- A trailing expression yields null (documented in the exec schema), so the SPEC's P2 form returns no value; only `return` does.

### OpenClaw Code Mode, QuickJS executor (bundled code-mode-quickjs plugin, QuickJS-WASI)

- Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw (extensions/code-mode-quickjs, src/agents/code-mode*.ts); npm openclaw (dist/extensions/code-mode-quickjs) at `npm openclaw@2026.11.6 (published dist, installed with --ignore-scripts into research/impls/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/npm); source read at tag v2026.11.6 = 06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638 (2026-11-19), cloned to research/impls/openclaw-codemode-node-vm/src. Same install and clone as openclaw-codemode-node-vm (shared on purpose; research/impls/openclaw-codemode-quickjs-wasi/README.md points there). quickjs-wasi 3.6.3 bundled in the plugin.`
- Language and engine: JS, QuickJS compiled to WASM/WASI (quickjs-wasi 3.6.3) in a pooled Node worker thread, fresh VM per cell, serialized VM snapshot while suspended
- How it was run: createCodeModeTools(ctx) + applyCodeModeCatalog({...ctx, tools: [exec, wait, lookup]}) from the published dist chunks (src/agents/code-mode.ts:220 and :313; not in the package's public exports, so imported from dist/prompt-tool-policy-XiWNJtPU.mjs), then execTool.execute(id, {code}) and waitTool.execute on status 'waiting': the same exec/wait control tools the embedded agent runtime gives the model. lookup is a plugin-tagged AgentTool (setPluginToolMeta) in the hidden catalog; guest code calls it as the async global lookup({id}). OpenClaw HOME/state/config are pointed at research/probes/<impl>/state. P11 is also measured with WARM_HOST=1, which runs cells inside a bound LegacyPluginSdkResourceHost + GatewayScheduler as the Gateway does (scripts/perf/code-mode-engine-measure.ts does the same). Executor: tools.codeMode = {enabled: true, executor: 'quickjs'}; resolvePluginCodeModeExecutor loads the bundled plugin from the dist manifest with no extra plugin config.
- Defaults: time timeoutMs 10,000 ms wall clock per exec or wait call (clamp 100-60,000), shared by worker preparation, guest work and inline tool waits; approval waits pause it. Pending tool calls can instead return status 'waiting' for a later wait with a fresh budget (src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts:110; docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md).; output maxOutputBytes 64 KiB shared by output entries, value and error across waits (clamp 1 KiB-10 MiB); over the cap a {truncated, omittedBytes, guidance, prefix} marker replaces the item. Console: each string clipped to 512 UTF-16 units with '…[truncated]', 16,384 units per cell then '[console output truncated]' (code-mode-runtime.ts:112; code-mode-controller-source.ts:101-115; code-mode-json.ts:93). A trailing expression returns null; only `return` sets the value.; tool_calls maxPendingToolCalls 16 in flight (clamp 1-128); further calls queue in the guest, up to 128 queued ordinary calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:114; code-mode-controller-source.ts:12, :227-230; code-mode-worker-types.ts:10). No per-exec total call cap was found on the exec path: 40 calls ran. Headless scripts default to 5 calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:26).; memory memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB as the QuickJS engine memory limit (clamp 1 MiB-1 GiB), fixed maxStackSize; serialized suspended state capped by maxSnapshotBytes 10 MiB (code-mode.worker.ts:264-265; code-mode-runtime.ts:111-113). Not a Gateway RSS limit.
- Hardened config: tools.codeMode = {enabled: true, executor: 'quickjs', timeoutMs: 5000, memoryLimitBytes: 16 MiB, maxOutputBytes: 8192, maxSnapshotBytes: 1 MiB, maxPendingToolCalls: 8, snapshotTtlSeconds: 60} (docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L104-L117). Tight but usable values inside the documented clamps (floors: timeoutMs 100 ms, memoryLimitBytes 1 MiB, maxOutputBytes 1 KiB, maxPendingToolCalls 1). The docs' own hardening advice beyond this is OS-level (separate user, container or host).
