QuickJS: host functions installed with vm.newFunction in the worker; the guest keeps a serializable snapshot while suspended. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L20-L32, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L221-L231, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-bridge.ts#L386, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts#L176-L230, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts#L328)
- **Isolation boundary.** QuickJS compiled to WASM/WASI (quickjs-wasi 3.6.3, bundled; TextEncoder/TextDecoder come from the encoding.so extension inside the same WASM heap), in a worker thread from a shared WorkerTaskPool. No WASI preopens or env are given, so no ambient fs, network, subprocess or environment. memoryLimit = memoryLimitBytes, fixed maxStackSize, and an interruptHandler that checks the wall-clock deadline. The docs claim 'hardened guest isolation' with 'no ambient host access', which matches the probes: guest errors are guest-realm (e.constructor === RangeError), every Function-constructor path returns undefined for process. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts#L255-L275, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/executor.ts#L36-L62, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/package.json#L7-L9, docs/tools/code-mode/internals.md 'Security boundary'; research/probes/openclaw-codemode-quickjs-wasi/out/P12.txt)
- **Output channel.** The model gets one JSON document: status, telemetry, ordered output entries (text(), json(), console.*) and the returned value or error. Over-budget items become an explicit truncation marker with the original JSON prefix and omittedBytes, not a silent cut. Console strings are clipped to 512 units each. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L101-L115, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-json.ts#L93, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode.ts#L226-L245; research/probes/openclaw-codemode-quickjs-wasi/out/P2.txt)
- **Limits.** All limits come from tools.codeMode (global or per agent) and are clamped in resolveCodeModeConfig: timeoutMs 10 s (100 ms-60 s), memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB (1 MiB-1 GiB), maxOutputBytes 64 KiB, maxSnapshotBytes 10 MiB, maxPendingToolCalls 16, snapshotTtlSeconds 900. For QuickJS, memoryLimitBytes is the engine heap limit and timeoutMs drives the interrupt handler; snapshots are capped by maxSnapshotBytes. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L96-L119, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts#L264-L271)
- **State.** Each exec gets a fresh context (globals never carry over), confirmed by P8. Workers are pooled and reused only when cells run inside the Gateway's bound resource host; without it every Node cell starts a new worker (about 200 ms). There is opt-in persistence: store(key, value)/load(key) keep small JSON values per session across cells and restarts, but only for a session-bound run (P8 #3 fails in this harness). A suspended cell (status 'waiting') keeps a serialized VM snapshot for wait. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L430-L445, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-session-store.ts#L315, docs/tools/code-mode/executors.md 'Understand waits and limits'; research/probes/openclaw-codemode-quickjs-wasi/out/P8.txt, out/P11.txt, out/warm-P11.txt)
- **Errors.** Guest errors return status failed with code internal_error and `Name: message` plus stack frames rewritten to openclaw-code-mode:user.js:line:col (user line numbers, wrapper removed); error text is bounded to 16,384 units. Parse errors are reported before execution with line and column. A runtime `ReferenceError: process|require|module is not defined` is rewritten into the generic 'module access is disabled' invalid_input message. Tool errors are catchable in guest code and are redacted (input shown as [redacted]). (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-source.ts#L212-L231, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts#L360-L380, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/extensions/code-mode-quickjs/src/code-mode.worker.ts#L455-L470, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-controller-source.ts#L62-L85)
- **Activation and credentials.** With tools.codeMode absent, activation is 'auto': Code Mode engages automatically for catalog-preferred models (for example claude-opus-5-5, gpt-5.6, gemini-3.5-flash) with the Node executor unless executor: 'quickjs' is set. Credentials stay host-side: tools run in the Gateway with their normal auth, and the guest only receives JSON results. The lexical module check (code-mode-source.ts:226) is a usability guard, not a security control: it blocks the literal require()/import() but not Function-constructor paths. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L75-L77, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L107-L108, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts#L128-L140, docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md 'Shipped preferred models')
- **Maintenance.** MIT license; tag v2026.11.6 committed 2026-11-19; npm openclaw 2026.11.6. Extensive tests under src/agents/code-mode*.test.ts, including an engine-parity suite. (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/package.json, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/06afb10d3272cc9deaf38ca6a3b7b839d5935638/src/agents/code-mode-engine-parity.test.ts)

Surprises:

- QuickJS is opt-in: the default executor is Node (not a security boundary), and 'auto' activation engages Code Mode for preferred models without selecting QuickJS. Only an explicit executor: 'quickjs' gets this isolation.
- The plugin's register() is empty; selection works through the manifest's codeModeExecutors contract and a public-surface module load, and an explicit executor choice bypasses plugins.allow for this bundled plugin (src/plugins/code-mode-executor.ts:15-66).
- A runtime 'process is not defined' is reported as invalid_input 'code mode module access is disabled.' (shorter text than the Node executor's), which hides the real ReferenceError.
- A trailing expression yields null (documented in the exec schema), so the SPEC's P2 form returns no value; only `return` does.
- No docs-vs-code mismatch found on isolation: the docs' 'no ambient filesystem, networking, subprocess, environment, or module access' matched every probe.

### OpenCode 2.x Code Mode (execute tool, @opencode/codemode)

- Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode (packages/codemode, packages/core/src/codemode); npm @opencode/codemode 2.3.2, @opencode/cli 2.3.2 at `tag v2.3.2, commit c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1 (2026-11-18); @opencode/codemode 2.3.2 from npm (deps acorn 8.15.0, effect 4.1.0); run under Bun 1.4.4 (the repo's packageManager)`
- Language and engine: JS (a subset, interpreted), A hand-written JavaScript interpreter in TypeScript: Acorn parses, a custom compiler emits opcodes, a custom VM runs them in the host process, with a cooperative scheduler that yields to the host between step slices. No V8 isolate, no QuickJS, no node:vm, no new Function. Only the language features and globals the interpreter implements exist.
- How it was run: Default and deny runs call OpenCode's own execute tool, CodeModeTool.create(inventory, executeTool, permission) from packages/core at the pinned tag, as Tool.snapshot builds it (fetch extension on, no limits), with a Permission stub that evaluates the documented base policy through OpenCode's Permission.evaluate; the hardened run calls the public package API CodeMode.make({ tools, limits }).execute(code). No model. research/probes/opencode-codemode/run.sh <mode> <probe>.
- Defaults: time None in OpenCode's execute tool: runtime() builds CodeMode.make without limits (packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts:289-301) and execute passes none (tool.ts:129-132). The package default is also none: "Execution limits have no default values." (packages/codemode/README.md:459). Each fetch has its own 30 s timeout (packages/core/src/codemode/fetch.ts:9, 58). Hardened: timeoutMs, enforced between interpreter steps (packages/codemode/src/language/runtime/execute.ts:296-308).; memory None, and no option for one. Per-value guards only: MAX_STRING_LENGTH 2^24, MAX_ARRAY_LENGTH 10,000,000, MAX_PENDING_PROMISES 10,000, MAX_VALUE_DEPTH 32 (packages/codemode/src/language/runtime/limits.ts:7-13). Programs run in the host process.; output None in the execute tool (no maxOutputBytes). Every tool result, execute included, is then cut by the session at 50 KiB or 2,000 lines with a marker and the full text saved to a file (packages/core/src/tool-output.ts:13-14, 93-113; applied at packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts:152). Hardened maxOutputBytes cuts whole log lines: a single 200,000-char line came back as "[logs truncated: showing 0 of 1 lines]" with truncated: true (out/hardened-P2.txt).; tool_calls None in the execute tool; concurrency is unrestricted (README.md:464). Hardened maxToolCalls counts tools and search() calls; fetch and other extension calls are not counted (README "Extension.make").
- Hardened config: @opencode/codemode public API CodeMode.make({ tools, limits: { timeoutMs: 30000, maxToolCalls: 20, maxOutputBytes: 32768 } }) with no extensions, so no fetch. The values are the ones OpenCode itself uses for automations (packages/core/src/automation/code.ts:18-24). The limits option is documented at packages/codemode/README.md:451-464 and typed at packages/codemode/src/codemode/codemode.ts:33-50. OpenCode's interactive execute tool exposes none of these to users; the only user-side control is a permission rule {"action":"webfetch","resource":"*","effect":"deny"} (https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), shown in out/deny-P3.txt. No memory option exists anywhere.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each OpenCode tool (MCP, plugin, built-in with codemode not false) becomes a Code Mode Tool.make under a tools tree keyed by namespace, and the catalog renders a TypeScript-like signature per tool from its Effect Schema or JSON Schema. Signatures are rendered lazily, only for tools the catalog shows. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts#L326-L343 and #L239-L261)
- **Discovery.** The catalog is inlined into instructions up to a budget (INLINE_BUDGET 2,000 at 4 chars per token, descriptions cut at 500); beyond that the catalog is marked partial and the model must call the in-program search(...) global, which counts as a tool call. This scales past 100 tools without every schema in the prompt. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/catalog.ts#L50-L58 ; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/instructions.ts#L11-L15)
- **Bridge.** No process or isolate boundary. A tool call is a Host.fn the VM invokes in the same process; OpenCode runs the real tool through executeTool with permission.nested, so each nested call meets the same permission rules as a direct call. Tool calls start as Effect fibers, which is why P9 ran in parallel. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts#L133-L160)
- **Isolation boundary.** The boundary is the language, not the OS: "Rather than trying to sandbox arbitrary JavaScript, CodeMode only runs the language features we implement." The design issue locked "Keep the hand-rolled interpreter; do not embed QuickJS/V8 for v1". P4, P5 and P12 match the claim. But the project's own threat model says "OpenCode does not sandbox the agent", and the execute tool runs with no time, memory or output limit in the agent process, so P6 and P7 fail. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/codemode/README.md#L7-L9 ; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/34787 ; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/SECURITY.md#L15-L19)
- **Output channel.** formatResult sends the return value as compact JSON, then "Warnings:" and "Logs:" blocks, as one text part; a null value is dropped when there are logs. Files emitted by nested tools are collected on the host and attached as file parts, never inlined in the program value. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts#L434-L454 and #L170-L198)
- **Limits.** OpenCode's interactive execute passes no limits, while its own automations pass timeoutMs 30,000, maxToolCalls 20 and maxOutputBytes 32 KiB to the same runtime. The fetch extension has a 30 s per-request timeout, blocks file: URLs and credentials in URLs, re-checks webfetch rules on each redirect, and caps redirects at 20. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts#L289-L301 ; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/automation/code.ts#L18-L24 ; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/fetch.ts#L9-L82)
- **State.** Fresh per execution (P8). The package can suspend a run to a JSON snapshot and resume it later, even in another process of the same build, with idempotent and durable tool semantics; OpenCode uses this for background Code Mode jobs only under the full_codemode flag. (packages/codemode/README.md "Suspending and resuming a run" ; https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/job.ts#L45-L120)
- **Errors.** Diagnostics have kinds (ParseError, UnsupportedSyntax, UnknownTool, InvalidToolInput, ToolCallLimitExceeded, TimeoutExceeded, ToolFailure, ExecutionFailure) and a location for interpreter errors; a user throw loses its line (P10). The model gets the message plus suggestions not already in it. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/codemode/tool.ts#L434-L439)
- **Credentials and approvals.** Credentials stay on the host: MCP and plugin tools run in OpenCode's process, and OpenAPI tools resolve auth on the host ("Authentication is resolved by the host and never shown to the model"). Code Mode is on by default: execute is present unless a rule denies it with resource *. (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/c0ad18b402eb2827fc1ee71c171b1177b3fc02d1/packages/core/src/tool.ts#L272-L300 ; packages/codemode/README.md "OpenAPI tools")

Surprises:

- The tools docs say the runtime "has no direct filesystem access, imports, or timers" and "provides fetch" (https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/). Both hold (P3, P4). But import and require do exist as syntax: they load host-provided globals by Node module name and throw for anything else (README "Extension.make").
- The design issue #34787 locked "Keep ambient authority out: no fs, child processes, network/fetch, process/env, or timers for v1". v2.3.2 ships fetch on by default, gated only by the webfetch permission, whose documented default is allow. Model-written code can send data to any URL unless the user adds a webfetch rule.
- The early PR description's "in-process AsyncFunction with no isolation or timeout" no longer describes the engine: code now runs in a custom interpreter that blocks the Function constructor, eval and globalThis (P12). The "no timeout" half still holds for the interactive execute tool (P6), and there is still no memory limit in any configuration (P7).
- Execution limits exist and work (hardened P6 stopped at 30.0 s), but OpenCode only applies them to automations, not to the execute tool a model calls interactively.
- Because the interpreter yields between step slices, an infinite loop does not freeze the OpenCode process (119 timer ticks in 120 s, concurrent executions still answered in about 2 ms). A memory bomb does take the whole process down to the OS limit, since there is no heap cap.
- README shows runtime.catalog() as a call; at 2.3.2 it is an array property (codemode.ts:175, 280), so the README call throws "runtime.catalog is not a function".
- The language is not quite JavaScript: no globalThis, no this at top level, no Function constructor, ({}).__proto__ is undefined, and a bare final expression is returned like a REPL. The SPEC's P8 form fails as a ReferenceError.
- The wave-2 sweep subagent reported that Kilo Code includes a copy of this package; I did not verify that or probe Kilo Code.

### Pi coding agent codemode (@earendil-works/pi-codemode)

- Source: https://github.com/earendil-works/pi (packages/codemode); npm @earendil-works/pi-codemode at `fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1 (packages/codemode 1.6.0, CHANGELOG has no unreleased changes after 1.6.0); probed the npm build @earendil-works/pi-codemode 1.6.0 with quickjs-wasi 3.6.2`
- Language and engine: JS, QuickJS compiled to WASI wasm (quickjs-wasi 3.6.2), a fresh wasm instance in a fresh Node worker_thread per execute()
- How it was run: new CodemodeSandbox({ tools: [lookup], ...options }).execute(code), the same class and method Pi's coding agent calls (packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/execute.ts:584-605).
- Defaults: time 300,000 ms overall deadline including tool time (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, packages/codemode/src/runtime/execution.ts:49). Pi's coding agent overrides it to Infinity unless the script's own `// @options` line sets timeout_ms (coding-agent execute.ts:555, 592).; memory none beyond wasm32's 4 GiB (memoryLimitBytes undefined, execution.ts:471; types.d.ts doc). Pi's coding agent sets 256 MiB (coding-agent execute.ts:56, 593).; output 16 Mi chars and 100,000 items; past either the script fails with a RangeError (prelude-source.ts:42-43, 348-350). Pi's coding agent truncates to 10,000 tokens with a marker (execute.ts:306, 449-470).; tool_calls no per-execution cap in the package. Pi's coding agent limits workers process-wide to 2 (PI_CODEMODE_MAX_WORKERS, execute.ts:58-64) and model calls in flight to 4 (execute.ts:50).
- Hardened config: new CodemodeSandbox({ tools, timeoutMs: 30_000, memoryLimitBytes: 32 * 1024 * 1024 }). Both are public options (packages/codemode/README.md, types.d.ts CodemodeSandboxBaseOptions). 30,000 ms is the timeout_ms in the README's options-line example; 32 MiB is the per-VM memory default the README documents for the Cloudflare sandbox. The package exposes no network or filesystem option because the VM has neither. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/README.md

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each CodemodeTool becomes tools.<jsName> on a frozen null-prototype object built by the in-VM prelude; ALL_TOOLS lists {name, description}. renderDeclarations() turns JSON Schema inputSchema/outputSchema into TypeScript declarations for the model-facing description; schemas only shape the text, arguments are not validated. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L215-L227 and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/declarations.ts#L45)
- **Discovery.** Pi's coding agent inlines declarations up to an inline budget (3,000 estimated tokens by default) and exposes searchTools(query) (BM25), describeTool(name), describeNamespace(name) and ALL_TOOLS as in-VM globals for the rest, so it scales past 100 tools without every schema in the prompt. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/execute.ts#L664-L720, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/tool.ts#L133-L142 and #L252, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-defaults.ts#L59)
- **Bridge.** One `bridge` host function registered in the VM; the worker relays each tool call to the host thread with postMessage and the host posts the JSON result back. Calls are promises, so Promise.all overlaps them (P9 209 ms). (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L254 and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/host.ts#L33-L73)
- **Isolation boundary.** QuickJS in its own wasm instance and linear memory, inside a worker_thread. The wasm imports are a WASI shim (clock, random, discarded stdout/stderr) plus the bridge, so the only capability is the injected tools. The prelude freezes built-ins and makes built-in globals read-only. Code matches the README claim; P3, P4, P5 and P12 confirm. The worker has no Node resourceLimits; the memory cap is QuickJS's own memoryLimit. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L110-L180, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/worker.ts#L1-L39, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L30)
- **Output channel.** result.output holds text items from text() and console.* (marked console: true) plus image items; the return value is result.value. The package keeps everything up to 16 Mi chars. Pi's coding agent appends the return value as text, then truncates combined text to 10,000 tokens keeping head and tail, with 'Warning: truncated output (original token count: N)' and '[Full output: <path>]'. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L42-L43 and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/execute.ts#L449-L470)
- **Limits.** Time: host-owned deadline, default 300 s; on expiry the host sets a SharedArrayBuffer interrupt flag polled by QuickJS and between promise-job batches, then terminate()s the worker, so async spin loops are also stopped (hardened-P6b). Memory: QuickJS memoryLimit only when memoryLimitBytes is set. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/execution.ts#L49 and #L214-L217, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/host.ts#L59-L66, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/vm.ts#L172-L176 and #L238-L247)
- **Limits in Pi's own wiring.** The coding agent passes memoryLimitBytes 256 MiB with a comment that without it 'a runaway script can grow to wasm32's 4 GiB and take the session down', but its deadline is sourceOptions.timeoutMs ?? Infinity, i.e. no time limit unless the model writes `// @options: {"timeout_ms": ...}`. Only the user's abort stops a spinning script. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/execute.ts#L51-L56 and #L555-L593)
- **State.** Fresh worker and VM per execute(). store(key, value)/load(key) are explicit JSON persistence that the host passes in as options.store and receives back as result.storeWrites; the sandbox itself persists nothing. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/README.md (Store section) and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts#L306-L315)
- **Errors.** execute() never rejects for script failures; result.error has kind script/timeout/aborted/sandbox, name, message and stack with codemode.js:<line>. The wrapper shares line 1 with the script so line numbers are exact. (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/README.md (Results and Runtime notes) and research/probes/pi-codemode/out/P10.txt)
- **Credentials and other.** Tools run on the host thread; the VM sees only JSON results, so credentials stay host-side. A deterministic start() mode fixes time, randomness and result order for durable replay. Pi's coding agent routes nested calls through its tool hooks only when using runToolCall (README). (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/fb248c7fca2539318f18ceb6534258048cb579c1/packages/codemode/README.md (Deterministic runs, Using with pi-agent-core))

Surprises:

- Pi's coding agent, the main consumer, runs codemode with no time limit by default: deadline = sourceOptions.timeoutMs ?? Infinity (coding-agent execute.ts:555). P6 under that config ran until the 120 s harness kill. The standalone package default is 300 s.
- The package default has no memory cap. P7 grew to 1.9 to 3.5 GB RSS before QuickJS reported out of memory at the wasm32 boundary; the host survived. Pi's coding agent fixes this with 256 MiB and says why in a comment.
- The literal P2 form (bare last expression) returns nothing: code is an async function body, so only `return` yields a value. The README says so.
- Measured startup was 25 to 34 ms per execution under load average 39 to 42 on a shared machine, against the README's 'about 20 ms'.

### mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp (Pi extension: list_mcp_tools + call_mcp)

- Source: https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp at `0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d (package.json 0.1.0, last commit 2026-02-22); deps from its package-lock: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.26.0, @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent 0.54.0, @mariozechner/jiti 2.6.5`
- Language and engine: JS, node:vm (vm.createContext + vm.Script.runInContext) inside the Pi host process; not a sandbox. The context is seeded with host-realm objects (Buffer, URL, setTimeout, console, the MCP bindings).
- How it was run: Loaded src/index.ts with jiti as Pi's extension loader does, passed a minimal ExtensionAPI, fired session_start, then called the registered call_mcp tool's execute({code, timeoutMs?}); the lookup tool is a local stdio MCP server (lookup-server.mjs) registered with --mcp-config mcp.json, HOME pointed at a probe-local folder so no user config or tokens are read.
- Defaults: time 30,000 ms (normalizeTimeout, sandbox-runtime.ts:148-157), applied as vm timeout min(timeoutMs, 60,000) to the synchronous part (sandbox-runtime.ts:83-88) and as a promise race (withTimeout, :159-179) that cannot fire while the host event loop is blocked.; memory none; runs in the host process's V8 heap.; output none in the extension; the whole {result, logs} payload is JSON-stringified (formatSandboxValue, sandbox-runtime.ts:102-114). Only the TUI renderer truncates lines for display (index.ts:414).; tool_calls no cap. list_mcp_tools shows 20 tools inline (DEFAULT_INLINE_LIMIT, index.ts:33) and spills the rest to a temp .tsv.
- Hardened config: call_mcp parameter timeoutMs: 1000 (the only limit the extension exposes; schema allows 100 to 300000, default 30000). https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L324-L330 and https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L148-L157. 1000 ms rather than the 100 ms minimum so P9's 200 ms calls can finish. No memory, network or filesystem option exists.

From the source:

- **Negative result (README).** README.md line 15: "The actual findings are that with how MCP works today, such efficiency gains are not useful." Lines 12-13 frame it: "This was an experiment to see if there is an efficiency benefit of allowing a coding agent interface with MCP in a way that allows composition." Lines 15-19 add that "an MCP server that uses code internally can be very helpful" and that mitsuhiko's google-workspace-mcp "actually performs as well as a similar skill does." (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/README.md#L12-L19)
- **Isolation boundary.** The engine is node:vm. vm.createContext is given host objects Buffer, URL, URLSearchParams, TextEncoder, TextDecoder, setTimeout, clearTimeout, a host console and __api with host async functions. Any of their .constructor.constructor is the host Function, which returns the host process (P12: execSync PWNED; P4/P5 read /etc/hosts and the env). The README calls it 'runs JavaScript in a sandbox'; node:vm is documented by Node as not a security mechanism. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L1 and #L54-L67; https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/README.md#L6)
- **Limits.** The vm timeout covers only the synchronous run of the wrapping async IIFE. After the first await, user code runs as host microtasks; withTimeout's setTimeout cannot fire while a microtask spins, so `await null; while (true) {}` freezes the Pi process (P6b). No memory limit. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L69-L90 and #L159-L179)
- **API shape.** No generated per-tool functions. Code gets one generic call(server, tool, args), readResource(server, uri), listTools(query), plus servers, tools (server -> names) and resources maps. call() throws on MCP isError, adds schema hints, and retries once with snake_case -> camelCase args; it returns {content, structuredContent}. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L1972-L2066 and https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/README.md#L80-L94)
- **Discovery.** On demand: list_mcp_tools(query) does case-insensitive text or /regex/ matching, shows 20 inline with compact signatures, and writes the full list to a temp .tsv for grep. In code, listTools(query) returns matches with inputSchema. Scales past 100 tools without putting schemas in the prompt. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L33 and #L198-L240; https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L1994-L2006)
- **Bridge.** Direct in-process function calls: the bindings are host async closures placed on __api, so a tool call is an ordinary host promise that goes to the MCP SDK Client (stdio/HTTP/SSE). Promise.all overlaps calls (P9 218 ms). (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L63-L66 and https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L2028-L2063)
- **Output channel.** Returns JSON text {result, logs[]} where each log has level, message and ISO timestamp; errors return {ok: false, error: {name, message, stack}, logs}. No size cap. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L102-L127 and https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L362-L384)
- **State.** New vm context per call (globals fresh), plus a documented `state` object owned by the runtime that persists across calls until resetState: true. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L31-L48)
- **Credentials.** OAuth tokens are stored at ~/.pi/agent/mcp-oauth/<server>/tokens.json and bearer tokens in process env or memory, all host-side, but model code can reach them through the P12 escape (process.env, fs). (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/oauth-handler.ts#L7 and https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/README.md#L59-L69)
- **Other.** It is a Pi extension (package.json pi.extensions), not a standalone MCP server or proxy: it is an MCP client inside Pi. A regex rejects TypeScript-looking code before running it. The repo's own .mcp.json registers Sentry and GitHub Copilot MCP servers, so running Pi in the repo would contact them; the harness avoided that with --mcp-config and a probe cwd. (https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/package.json, https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L129-L146, https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/.mcp.json)

Surprises:

- The README says call_mcp 'runs JavaScript in a sandbox'. It is node:vm seeded with host objects; P12 ran a shell command (execSync echo PWNED), P4 read /etc/hosts, P5 read the env secret, P3b reached example.com with the host fetch.
- Even this.constructor.constructor("return process")(), the textbook first try, escapes, because the context global is a host-realm object.
- The 30 s timeout does not cover code after the first await: `await null; while (true) {}` hangs the whole host process (P6b, default and hardened).
- Error stacks leak absolute host paths of the extension and caller (P10).
- It is not an MCP server/proxy but a Pi extension that is an MCP client; the README is the author's own negative result on code-mode efficiency over MCP.
- The first call_mcp of a session pays a lazy MCP server spawn (about 400 ms), which made an unwarmed P9 look serial (954 ms) until the arrival timestamps showed all five calls reached the server within 1 ms.

### Pydantic AI Harness CodeMode (run_code over Monty)

- Source: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai (src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/); PyPI pydantic-ai-harness[code-mode] at `pydantic-ai-harness 0.71.0 from PyPI, which is pydantic/pydantic-ai tag v2.71.0 = 8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983 (clone at research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src; diff -r against the installed wheel is empty). Runtime: pydantic-ai-slim 2.71.0, pydantic-monty 1.6.0, CPython 3.12.11.`
- Language and engine: Python (Monty subset), Monty, a Rust bytecode interpreter, in a local `monty` worker subprocess from pydantic_monty.AsyncMonty (_monty_exec.py:212), driven through the feed_start/resume snapshot API. The first snippet of each REPL is type-checked with ty before it runs.
- How it was run: Agent(FunctionModel(scripted), capabilities=[CodeMode()]) with lookup registered via agent.tool_plain; the scripted model calls run_code(code=...) and the harness records the tool result the model would see. No LLM, no API key.
- Defaults: time 30 s of sandbox execution per run_code snippet; time awaiting tools and sleeping do not count (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:343-346 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L343-L346); default at research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:373 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L373)). From the source:

- **API shape.** Each sandboxed tool's ToolDefinition.function_signature (from its JSON Schema) is rendered as an `async def name(*, ...)` Python stub plus TypedDict blocks. With the CodeMode default dynamic_catalog=True the catalog goes into the agent instructions as <pyai:context id="toolset:code_mode:catalog">, and run_code's description keeps only static prose (module list, no fs/env/clock). Observed text in out/P1.txt. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:1682-1700 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L1682-L1700); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/_code_tools.py:289-297 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/_code_tools.py#L289-L297); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py:250-284 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py#L250-L284); research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P1.txt)
- **Discovery.** Every sandboxed tool is listed upfront in the catalog. Tools marked defer_loading stay off the wire until the local search_tools function (Tool Search) or a capability load reveals them; the catalog update is then appended to history, so the prompt cache survives. This is the path past 100 tools without every schema in the prompt. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:409-430 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L409-L430); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py:250-284 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py#L250-L284))
- **Bridge.** MontyExecutor drives the REPL with feed_start/resume: each external call pauses Monty as a FunctionSnapshot, CodeMode dispatches it through Pydantic AI's tool manager in the host process, and resumes with the result serialized to plain JSON. Async calls are kept pending so asyncio.gather resolves them together (P9 201 ms for five 200 ms calls). Tool functions, their credentials and os_access stay in the host process, also with a remote worker. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/_monty_exec.py:521-600 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/_monty_exec.py#L521-L600); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:770 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L770); README research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/README.md:652-661 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/README.md#L652-L661))
- **Isolation boundary.** Monty interpreter in a separate worker subprocess, no filesystem, env, clock or network unless os_access or mount is given. README claims Code Mode is safe in a webserver and IPython Code Mode is not. Probes agree for Code Mode: P3 not-defined, P4/P5 blocked, all 9 P12 attempts blocked at Monty's runtime even with the type checker skipped. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/README.md:84-94 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/README.md#L84-L94); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py:109-120 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py#L109-L120); research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P12.txt)
- **Output channel.** Printed text and the last expression both return, as {'output': ..., 'result': ...}; only one of them when the other is empty. The printed-output cap is 10 MiB and fires as a MemoryError, not a truncation marker. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:772-782 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L772-L782); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/_monty_exec.py:271-280 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/_monty_exec.py#L271-L280); research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P2.txt; research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/X-print-cap.txt)
- **Limits.** What the harness adds over raw Monty: raw pydantic-monty 1.6.0 has no time or memory default (results/pydantic-monty.json P6 no-limit-within-120s, P7 hit 4 GiB), while CodeMode applies 30 s and 256 MiB unless resource_limits='unlimited'. It also adds the 100-calls-per-snippet budget and keeps Monty's 1000-suspension session budget, which cannot be disabled. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:362-396 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L362-L396); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:745-752 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L745-L752))
- **State.** One REPL per agent run: variables persist across run_code calls in a run and start fresh in a new run unless repl_store is set. A time, memory or print-cap trip resets the session. `restart: true` lets the model reset it. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py:239-248 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py#L239-L248); research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** Runtime errors go back to the model as a retry: 'Runtime error:' + Monty traceback with file, line and message, plus a list of nested calls that already started (so the model does not replay side effects) and session-reset advice when a limit tripped. Type errors return 'Type error in code:' with the ty diagnostic before any code runs. Retries count against max_retries=3. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:849-880 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L849-L880); research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P10.txt; research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P3.txt)
- **Other.** Type checking runs only on the first snippet of a fresh REPL that has tools; later snippets skip it. Tools registered with requires_approval=True and external tools stay native under the default selector, so approvals still pause the run. speculate and eager can start read-only calls while arguments stream. IPythonCodeMode in the same package runs a real IPython kernel with no sandbox (README table), not probed here. (research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:1429-1432 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py#L1429-L1432); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py:130-143 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py#L130-L143); research/impls/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/src/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py:203-223 (https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/8e4f468aad21f87af6634885b44e2834d8b3b983/src/pydantic_ai_harness/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_capability.py#L203-L223))

Surprises:

- The 10 MiB print cap does not keep output away from the model. X-print-cap printed 11 MB: Monty raised MemoryError at 10,485,760 bytes and reset the session, and the retry text still carried all 10,485,760 printed chars between [stdout before error] markers (10,486,097 chars total). Below the cap nothing is truncated (P2). The README (code_mode/README.md:686) says the cap resets the session but not that the printed text is still forwarded. Evidence research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/X-print-cap.txt.
- The ty type check runs only on the first snippet (_toolset.py:1429-1431). The earlier run of this probe saw P12 stopped by ty and could not tell whether Monty itself blocks the escapes. Rerunning each attempt as a second snippet shows Monty's runtime blocks all 9. Evidence research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P12.txt.
- max_suspensions=1000 is per REPL session, so it caps a whole agent run, not one snippet. X-suspensions got 991 lookups through, then every later snippet in the run failed with 'suspension limit 1000 exceeded' until restart. An investigation agent that fans out to many lookups across run_code calls hits this ceiling. Evidence research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/X-suspensions.txt.
- One over the per-snippet budget fails the whole snippet: asking for 101 lookups in one gather ran 100 on the host and returned none of their results to the code.
- time.time() and datetime.now() raise inside run_code unless os_access or os_policy is set, so the SPEC's in-sandbox P9 timing code cannot run; P9 times the lookups on the host.
- The harness turns raw Monty's G2 and G3 failures into passes: raw pydantic-monty has no default time or memory limit, CodeMode applies 30 s and 256 MiB by default. results/fastmcp-codemode.json (also Monty-backed, MontySandboxProvider) did not exist when this was written, so no numeric comparison with it.

### Pydantic Monty

- Source: https://github.com/pydantic/monty (PyPI: pydantic-monty) at `pydantic-monty 1.6.0 (PyPI); monty tag v1.6.0 = 3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829 (repo main is 5f4a3dfc, v1.7.0-beta.1, not run)`
- Language and engine: Python, Monty, a Rust bytecode interpreter (Ruff parser). Each checkout runs in a `monty` worker subprocess started with an empty environment.
- How it was run: pydantic_monty.Monty() pool, pool.checkout(), session.feed_run(code, external_lookup={'lookup': fn}); AsyncMonty for P9.
- Defaults: time none (ResourceLimits.max_feed_duration None, resource.rs:219). CodeMode integration applies 30 s per snippet when resource_limits is None.; memory none (max_memory None, resource.rs:221). CodeMode integration applies 256 MiB when resource_limits is None.; output no cap observed in the Monty API (200000-char print arrives whole). CodeMode only bounds its list of started nested calls.; tool_calls max_suspensions 1000 per session (resource.rs:212, 224); recursion depth 1000 (resource.rs:203, 223)
- Hardened config: pool.checkout(limits={'max_memory': 10_000_000, 'max_feed_duration_secs': 1.0, 'max_recursion_depth': 100}), the example in docs/resource-limits.md:11-15 at v1.6.0 (https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/docs/resource-limits.md#L11-L15); keys defined in pydantic_monty/__init__.py ResourceLimits (max_feed_duration_secs, max_memory). No network option exists because the sandbox has no network module; file access already needs a host os handler. Harness: research/probes/pydantic-monty/hardened.py

From the source:

- **API shape.** Host functions are passed per feed as external_lookup (callables become host functions). Type-check stubs are separate (type_check_stubs, or ExternalModule stubs). No schema-driven generator at this layer; CodeMode builds stubs from each tool's JSON schema. (https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-python/python/pydantic_monty/_monty.pyi#L834-L840 ; research/impls/pydantic-monty/.venv-pai/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:1709)
- **Discovery.** Monty itself exposes nothing to a model. CodeMode puts every eligible tool behind one run_code tool, so the model sees one tool and writes stubs-typed Python calls to the rest. (research/impls/pydantic-monty/.venv-pai/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pydantic_ai_harness/.agents/skills/pydantic-ai-harness/references/CODE-MODE.md:1-30)
- **Bridge.** The sandbox runs in a subprocess reached over stdin and stdout pipes. A host call pauses the worker and returns a FunctionSnapshot. The host runs the function and calls resume. The snapshot can be dumped to about 2.2 KB and resumed in a new pool (snapshot_check.py). (https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-pool/src/worker.rs#L135-L141 ; https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-python/python/pydantic_monty/_monty.pyi#L1577)
- **Isolation boundary.** The worker is a separate process started with env_clear, so the in-process claim in the article does not hold for v1.6. Unmounted filesystem access returns Permission denied, and os.environ and os.getenv raise not-supported. Host-side reality matches the probes (P3 to P5). (https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-pool/src/worker.rs#L135-L138 ; https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-types/src/os.rs#L474 ; https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-types/src/os.rs#L479 ; research/probes/pydantic-monty/out/claims.txt (ARCH))
- **Output channel.** print() streams to print_callback. The return value is the last expression. Errors come back as MontyRuntimeError with frames. No truncation in the Monty API. (research/probes/pydantic-monty/out/P2.txt ; research/probes/pydantic-monty/out/P10.txt)
- **Limits.** Library defaults are no time and no memory limit, with recursion and suspension caps. When configured, limits fire: max_feed_duration_secs=0.5 raised TimeoutError after 0.54 s, max_memory=50 MB raised MemoryError. (https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-types/src/resource.rs#L216-L225 ; research/probes/pydantic-monty/out/claims.txt)
- **State.** Session state persists across feeds in one checkout (REPL). A new checkout is fresh. Sessions dump with session.dump(), and mid-run state with FunctionSnapshot.dump(). (https://github.com/pydantic/monty/blob/3f89dcbf82071896efb5e3ded507db4191e8d829/crates/monty-python/python/pydantic_monty/_monty.pyi#L1028 ; research/probes/pydantic-monty/out/P8.txt)
- **Pydantic AI wiring.** The article's CodeExecutionToolset is not in pydantic-ai-slim 2.71.0. The shipped integration is pydantic_ai_harness CodeMode (0.71.0). It drives Monty through checkout plus feed_start and resume, and sets a 30 s and 256 MiB default. (research/impls/pydantic-monty/.venv-pai/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pydantic_ai_harness/_monty_exec.py:195-226 ; research/impls/pydantic-monty/.venv-pai/lib/python3.14/site-packages/pydantic_ai_harness/code_mode/_toolset.py:373-374)

Surprises:

- Article hello-world (Monty(code, inputs=..., external_functions=...)) raises TypeError on 1.6.0: Monty.__new__() takes 0 positional arguments. The API is now a pool with checkout and feed_run (out/claims.txt).
- Article says Monty starts in microseconds because it is embedded in the parent process. v1.6 runs every checkout in a monty subprocess (verified with pgrep). Measured warm feed 33 to 59 us, fresh checkout 0.05 to 0.14 ms median, against the article's 0.004 ms.
- Article says the default is strict resource limits. The library default is none for time and memory (P6 never stops; P7 passes 4 GiB in 5 of 5 repeats). Limits only apply when configured or in the CodeMode integration.
- Access claims hold: no filesystem, network, or env by default (P3 to P5), and P12 reaches no host object.
- Snapshot dump is about 2.2 KB for a tiny state, which fits the article's single-digit-KB claim. Round trip across two pools works (out/snapshot.txt).
- The article's CodeExecutionToolset does not exist in the pinned pydantic-ai-slim 2.71.0; use pydantic-ai-harness CodeMode instead.
- Repo main (5f4a3dfc, v1.7.0-beta.1) is newer than the PyPI 1.6.0 the probes ran; pinned to the v1.6.0 tag. Source reading and the installed wheel match.

### Qwen Code Code Mode (tools.codeModeOnly, exec on QuickJS WASM)

- Source: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code (packages/core/src/code-mode, packages/core/src/tools/exec.ts, code-mode.ts); npm @qwen-code/qwen-code at `npm @qwen-code/qwen-code 0.28.4 (integrity sha512-KH4NHC3xZkjhg38kjmrMgSCE07Fiqm2IQE0gVDjobTarjgrhPL6/h4lEOB4EHAPrn0laPCq+9URtAO1EqG7cRQ==; bundled codeModeHost.js sha256 fd0d6029b936076beaf3bd4261f82bd22916f734fd383fbabe5966e9843da64f); source read at tag v0.28.4 = e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4 (2026-11-22). QuickJS via quickjs-emscripten-core 0.32.0 + @jitl/quickjs-singlefile-mjs-release-sync 0.32.0 (packages/core/package.json:113,164).`
- Language and engine: JS, QuickJS (2025-09-13) compiled to WASM via quickjs-emscripten, run in a fresh Node child process (codeModeHost.js) per exec call, with a new runtime and context; tool calls cross a framed JSON stdio protocol to the CLI, which runs them through its normal tool scheduler.
- How it was run: The released CLI headless (node cli.js -p ... --auth-type openai --output-format json) with tools.codeModeOnly true and lookup as a trusted stdio MCP server; a scripted local OpenAI-compatible mock (no model) returns one exec tool call per fixed probe source, so code reaches ExecTool through CoreToolScheduler exactly as a model's call would. P7 variants and P11's runtime-only timing also drive the bundled codeModeHost.js directly over its stdio protocol (host-direct.mjs).
- Defaults: time 30 s guest CPU budget via the QuickJS interrupt handler, plus a parent wall timer of 30 s + 30 s startup grace = 60 s; both pause while any nested tool call is in flight, so tool-bound programs have no per-exec time limit (host.ts:200-215, 230-243; host-client.ts:34, 156-198, 242, 274; protocol.ts:15). Not configurable. Run-level --max-wall-time exists for headless runs (off by default).; memory Nominal: QuickJS runtime.setMemoryLimit(64 MiB), stack 1 MiB (host.ts:31-32, 210-211). Observed: not enforced (malloc_usable_size unavailable in this build); a guest grows to about 1.5-1.9 GB RSS before "out of memory". One child process per exec; exec itself is Kind.Other, so model-issued exec calls run one at a time.; output Only text()/image()/audio()/generatedImage() output returns; return values are dropped. text() bounded to 100,000 chars in the host, then the whole exec result to 32,000 chars with a head/tail "… code mode output truncated …" marker (output.ts:7-16, protocol.ts:14, exec.ts:176-179). Source 131,072 chars; nested tool output sliced to 100,000 chars; control frames 1 MiB; media 16 items / 10 MiB; 1,024 live timers.; tool_calls No per-exec cap. Nested calls are not counted by --max-tool-calls (observed 286 nested calls under --max-tool-calls 32). Nested calls batch within a 5 ms window and run in parallel only when the scheduler deems them concurrency-safe (Kind.Read etc.).
- Hardened config: CLI flags --approval-mode default (instead of the headless AUTO classifier) --exclude-tools read_file,glob,grep_search,web_fetch,zoom_image,read_mcp_resource --max-wall-time 60s --max-tool-calls 32 (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/cli/src/config/top-level-options.ts#L257-L263, #L432-L454). The code-mode limits themselves have no option: executeCodeMode only clamps its optional timeoutMs/maxOutputChars down to the constants and ExecTool passes neither (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/exec.ts#L158-L163, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host-client.ts#L133-L141); memory and stack limits are constants (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L31-L32). tools.sandbox bwrap/landlock policy is Linux-only (docs/users/features/sandbox.md:23); the macOS seatbelt restrictive-closed/-proxied profiles deny outbound traffic to the localhost model endpoint (proxied allows only localhost:8877, outside this worker's ports) and the open profiles allow file-read* everywhere and all network, so they change nothing the guest can reach; not used. Files: research/probes/qwen-code-codemode/settings.hardened.json, args.hardened.json.

The SPEC's console.log form fails: "'console' is not defined" (console is deleted; text() is the print). From the source:

- **API shape.** Every registered tool whose exposure is code-mode-callable becomes tools.<jsName>(args) (names normalized, collisions resolved lexicographically). The exec description is generated per request from the registry: TypeScript-like signatures from each tool's JSON Schema (schemaToType), plus ALL_TOOLS metadata. In the guest, tools is a frozen Proxy whose entries call a host function __callTool that is deleted from globalThis before user code runs. (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode.ts#L89-L201, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode.ts#L203-L256, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L443-L494, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/tool-registry.ts#L1102-L1116)
- **Discovery.** Lazy: deferred tools (all MCP tools are shouldDefer) are omitted from the exec description when tool_search is in scope; the model calls top-level tool_search to get a tool's schema and jsName, then uses it in a later exec. ALL_TOOLS at runtime still lists every callable tool. Scales past 100 tools without putting every schema in the prompt. The captured declaration had 7 top-level tools (agent, autofix_pr, enter_worktree, exec, exit_worktree, send_message, tool_search). (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode.ts#L229, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts#L1262-L1267, docs/design/lazy-code-mode.md, research/probes/qwen-code-codemode/out/exec-declaration.default.json)
- **Bridge.** Guest __callTool posts a tool_call frame on stdout; the parent maps jsName to the registry name and calls ToolCallRuntimeContext.dispatch, which the scheduler binds with AsyncLocalStorage. Nested calls get ids <parent>:code:<n>, source 'code_mode', and go through a sibling scheduler: validation, permissions/approvals, hooks, telemetry and output truncation all apply (P3 web_fetch hit the approval classifier; P10 bad args hit schema validation). Credentials stay in the CLI; the child has no tools or config. (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L352-L371, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host-client.ts#L208-L276, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L2150-L2178, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L6610-L6627, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/tool-call-runtime.ts#L54-L80)
- **Isolation boundary.** QuickJS/WASM is the stated capability boundary; the child process is defense in depth. Matches the code for capabilities: no module loader, console, process, fetch, Atomics, SharedArrayBuffer, WebAssembly; child env reduced to PATH/TMPDIR (and Windows vars). It does not match for memory: the 64 MiB limit is set but not enforced. The boundary also does not cover what tools can do: read_file (unrestricted path), glob, grep_search and web_fetch are callable from exec by default. (docs/design/code-mode-only.md:100-118, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L208-L216, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L491-L493, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host-client.ts#L76-L90)
- **Output channel.** The model sees only helper output (text/image/audio/generatedImage), then "Script error:\n<message+stack>" on failure. host.ts computes and sends the program's return value (boundedValue) but ExecTool only reads result.output, so return values are silently dropped. Two truncation layers, each with a head/tail marker: 100,000 chars in the host, 32,000 for the exec result. (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L536-L545, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/exec.ts#L173-L179, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/output.ts#L7-L16)
- **Limits.** All constants: 30 s CPU, 60 s wall (30 s startup grace), 64 MiB/1 MiB memory/stack, 131,072-char source, 100,000/32,000-char output, frame caps, 1,024 timers. Both clocks pause during nested tool calls by design ("registered host tools, whose own scheduler/ACP timeouts remain authoritative"), so a loop of tool calls runs unbounded unless the headless --max-wall-time is set. (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/protocol.ts#L9-L15, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L31-L34, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L230-L249, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host-client.ts#L174-L198, docs/design/code-mode-only.md:110-116)
- **State.** Fresh child process, QuickJS runtime and context per exec; timers, pending calls, VM and runtime are disposed in finally. No snapshot or persistence. (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L553-L559, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host-client.ts#L142-L145)
- **Errors.** QuickJS error message plus stack (exec.js:line:col, offset by the 3-line async wrapper) bounded to 100,000 chars; prefixed "Script error:" by ExecTool and flagged EXECUTION_FAILED. Failed nested calls reject the guest promise with the scheduler's error text (sliced to 100,000 chars). (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L40-L62, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/code-mode/host.ts#L504-L516, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/tools/exec.ts#L173-L226)
- **Concurrency and budgets.** Nested calls queued within CODE_MODE_BATCH_WINDOW_MS (5 ms) form one batch; partitionByConcurrencySafety runs only concurrency-safe kinds in parallel. MCP tools are Kind.Read only with readOnlyHint, else serial. Shell calls from code mode are treated as concurrency-safe regardless of the read-only classifier. The headless --max-tool-calls budget ticks only for top-level calls. (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L471, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts#L1755-L1788, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/cli/src/nonInteractiveCli.ts#L2416, https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/cli/src/utils/runBudget.ts#L11-L19)
- **Maintenance.** Apache-2.0, released 0.28.4 on 2026-11-22 (tag commit date). Code mode is experimental and off by default (tools.codeModeOnly default false). (https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/e8424c88ddd463c56602063efde57c328b917cd4/packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts#L3102-L3111)

Surprises:

- Memory: host.ts sets a 64 MiB QuickJS limit and the design doc says "Runtime memory and stack limits are fixed", but the limit is not enforced in this QuickJS/WASM build: guests held 1.5 GB and the host child reached about 1.9 GB RSS before "out of memory" (P7, P7c-e).
- The design doc lists timers among things the guest does not have (code-mode-only.md:93, 108); the code installs setTimeout/clearTimeout (host.ts:405-441) and the model-facing description documents them.
- Time budgets pause during nested tool calls, so an exec that keeps calling tools never times out (564 calls in 120 s); the design doc states this deliberately, but --max-tool-calls (documented as cumulative tool calls in the run) does not count those nested calls; only --max-wall-time stopped it.
- The design doc says exec calls keep Qwen Code's output budgets; the runtime additionally drops program return values: host.ts serializes the value, ExecTool never reads it. The model-facing description does say bare return values produce no output.
- The SPEC's console.log fails ("'console' is not defined"); text() is the only print.
- P9 depends on MCP annotations: identical lookups run serially (1,065 ms) unless the server sets readOnlyHint (261 ms). The description tells the model "Safe calls run concurrently" without saying which are safe.
- Headless default approval mode is AUTO, an LLM classifier: web_fetch from exec sent a classifier request to the model endpoint (the mock's non-answer led to decline), while read_file of /etc/hosts needed no approval at all.

### imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark CodeExecutor (RestrictedPython)

- Source: https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark at `363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f (2025-10-09, last commit); RestrictedPython 9.0 (requirements.txt says >=7.0)`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython exec() in the host process (executor.py:209) of code compiled by RestrictedPython.compile_restricted. The restricted globals hand the guest the real __import__ and getattr, so the compile-time checks are the only guard.
- How it was run: sandbox.executor.CodeExecutor({'lookup': lookup}).execute(code), the call CodeModeAgent.run makes (agents/codemode_agent.py:187). The tool is reached as tools.lookup(id=...).
- Defaults: time None. CodeExecutor.execute(code) has no timeout and runs exec on the calling thread (executor.py:101, 209). P6 ran 120 s.; memory None. Guest allocations live in the host process (P7 reached 4.2 GB).; output print() output is discarded. Only the `result` variable is returned, plus JSON-serializable locals, uncapped (executor.py:211-227).; tool_calls No cap. Tools are plain host callables behind ToolsAPI.__getattr__ (executor.py:49-81).; hardened No stricter option exists. CodeExecutor.__init__ takes only the tools dict (executor.py:92-99), so hardened is null.

|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Tool call | works (42, 1 host call) | result variable = 42, 1 host-side call. print() output is discarded, so the probe also sets `result`, the only value the executor returns. | research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/P1.txt |
| P2 Output | print dropped; only `result` returns | Neither came back. print() goes to a SafePrinter whose buffer is never read (executor.py:179-199), and a bare last expression is not returned. Only the variable `result` returns: with result = "RETURNED" (out/PX.txt, P2-result-var) the value came back. 0 of 200000 printed chars reach the caller. | research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/P2.txt |
| P3 Network | works (example.com 200) | import urllib.request is allowed (the real __import__ is in the guest builtins, executor.py:145). urlopen("https://example.com") returned STATUS 200. | research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/P3.txt |
| P4 Files | works (via import io) | open() is not in the guest builtins (NameError, out/PX.txt P4-open-only), but import io; io.open("/etc/hosts").read() returned the host file (450 chars, identical to the host's). | research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/P4.txt |

Raising a ValueError subclass reached through import io gives "Execution error: probe-boom": message only, no type, no line number (out/PX.txt). | research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/P10.txt |
