But import os; os.system("echo PWNED-c >> <host file>") printed PWNED-c and wrote the host marker file. sys.modules and gc are also reachable (out/PX.txt). | research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/P12.txt |

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools are a dict of host callables wrapped in ToolsAPI, whose __getattr__ returns the raw host function, so guest code calls tools.<name>(...). The model learns the API from a hand-written string (TypedDicts, signatures, docstrings) returned by get_code_mode_api(); nothing is generated from a schema. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L49-L81 ; https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/tools/business_tools.py#L315)
- **Discovery.** Everything upfront: the whole tools_api string is pasted into the system prompt on every turn. No search. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/agents/codemode_agent.py#L48-L55)
- **Bridge.** No bridge. Guest and tools share one CPython process; a tool call is a direct Python call into the host function. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L198 and #L209)
- **Isolation boundary.** RestrictedPython compile-time checks only. The executor puts the real __import__ and the real getattr into the guest builtins, which disables RestrictedPython's import and attribute guards. Any module is importable, so os, socket and subprocess are one import away. The README claims "No filesystem access, No network access, No dangerous imports"; P3, P4, P5 and P12 show all three are false. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L145-L146 and #L200 ; README claim https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/README.md#L246-L252)
- **Builtins bug.** restricted_builtins = safe_globals.copy() copies {'__builtins__': safe_builtins}, not safe_builtins itself. So none of RestrictedPython's safe builtins (exceptions such as ValueError and NameError, isinstance, None-safe helpers) reach the guest; only the 25 names the executor adds by hand do. That is why raise ValueError and except NameError fail with NameError. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L141-L176)
- **Output channel.** Only the guest variable `result` and JSON-serializable non-underscore locals come back. print() is routed to a SafePrinter instance whose buffer is never read. No truncation anywhere. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L179-L227)
- **Limits.** No time, memory, output or call-count limits in the executor. The agent loop caps model turns at max_iterations=10, which does not bound one execution. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L101-L233 ; https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/agents/codemode_agent.py#L121)
- **State.** Fresh per execute(): new globals and locals dicts each call. Host-side tool state (the accounting state object) persists across calls. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L193-L206)
- **Errors.** Every exception becomes {'success': False, 'error': 'Execution error: ' + str(e)}: no type name, no traceback, no line number. Compile errors list RestrictedPython messages with line numbers. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L119-L124 and #L229-L233)
- **README numbers.** Reproducible as arithmetic from data still in git history, not from the repo tree. results/*.json is gitignored and commit 9053b68 deleted the root benchmark_results_*.json, but commit 917128b holds them. Summing input+output tokens over successful scenarios gives exactly 144,250 (regular, 6/8) and 45,741 (code mode, 7/8). The two totals cover different scenario sets: regular includes scenario 7 and lacks 8, code mode includes 8. On the 6 scenarios both passed, the totals are 144,250 vs 38,942 (73.0% fewer). The 6/8 vs 7/8 gap is rate limits, not capability: regular scenario 8 and code-mode scenario 6 both failed with HTTP 429; regular scenario 6 hit max iterations. One run per agent, Claude 3 Haiku. Verified without calling any model API. (research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/recompute_readme.py, research/probes/restrictedpython-codemode/out/readme-recompute.txt ; https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/917128b349645177f2aee74aeeac250b41c4cae6/benchmark_results_claude.json ; https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/docs/RESULTS_DATA.md#L9-L41)
- **Anything else.** No approvals, no credential separation (tools are host closures; guest code can read os.environ), no async support (tools are sync). Repo unlicensed in the tree and last touched 2025-10-09. (https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L57-L81)

Surprises:

- README says the sandbox has no filesystem, no network and no dangerous imports (README.md:246-252). The executor hands the guest the real __import__ (executor.py:145), so import os / io / urllib work: P3 got example.com 200, P4 read /etc/hosts, P5 read PROBE_SECRET, P12 ran os.system on the host.
- The SPEC escape forms are blocked, but only by RestrictedPython's compile-time rule against _-prefixed names. That rule is cosmetic once import is free.
- safe_globals.copy() is used where safe_builtins was meant (executor.py:141), so ValueError, NameError and the other RestrictedPython safe builtins are missing. The SPEC P10 code cannot even raise; error handling with except NameError fails.
- print() output never reaches the model. The agent prompt tells the model to store the answer in `result` (codemode_agent.py:60), which is the only channel.
- The README headline compares token totals over different scenario sets (regular has scenario 7 and not 8; code mode has 8). Matched on the 6 scenarios both finished, the saving is 73.0%, not 68.3%. The success-rate difference comes from HTTP 429 rate-limit failures, not from task failures.
- The result files behind the README are gitignored and were deleted from the tree in 9053b68; they survive only in commit 917128b.
- The executor runs exec in the agent's own process with no timeout: one `while True: pass` hangs the agent forever, and one big allocation kills it.

### Recursive Language Models (Zhang, Kraska, Khattab; arXiv 2512.24601): LocalREPL

- Source: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm (MIT), paper https://arxiv.org/html/2512.24601v3 at `commit e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb (default branch HEAD, pushed 2026-11-21); rlm 0.1.3`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython exec() in the host process, with a restricted builtins dict (LocalREPL is a NonIsolatedEnv). No isolation. (default local environment; container backends not probed)
- How it was run: LocalREPL(lm_handler_address=None, custom_tools={'lookup': fn}) with llm_query replaced by a stub, then env.execute_code(code) for each cell. This is the call rlm/core/rlm.py makes at rlm.py:757.
- Defaults: time None at the REPL level: P6 ran past the 120 s watchdog. RLM(max_timeout=None) is checked only between iterations (rlm.py:421-422, 551-553), not inside a cell.; memory None. P7 reached 4.03 GB peak RSS in 1.0 s with no error; the harness stopped it.; output execute_code returns all stdout, uncapped (P2: 200,001 chars). The model view is capped at 20,000 chars per block, head only, with a '... + [N chars...]' marker (parsing.py:26, 58-62).; tool_calls No cap on custom-tool calls. Sub-LLM concurrency is capped at max_concurrent_subcalls=4 (local_repl.py:170, 397).
- Hardened config: rlm.environments.get_environment('ipython', {'kernel_mode': 'subprocess', 'cell_timeout': 30, 'custom_tools': {'lookup': lookup}}), from the IPython environment docs (docs/src/app/environments/ipython/page.tsx:46-49 at e11f1a8, https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/docs/src/app/environments/ipython/page.tsx#L46-L49) and rlm/environments/ipython_repl.py:507-512 (cell_timeout is a hard limit via interrupt_kernel). Installed as rlms[ipython] (ipykernel 7.4.0, jupyter_client 8.10.0, dill 0.4.1) in research/impls/rlm/.venv-ipython. RLM has no memory or network option for local environments; the docker, modal, e2b, daytona and prime backends are the isolation path (rlm-docker probed separately). Harness: research/probes/rlm/hardened.py

From the source:

- **API shape.** custom_tools is a dict of name to callable. setup() copies each callable into self.globals, so the cell sees it as a plain name (P1). Names in RESERVED_TOOL_NAMES are refused. The reserved helpers are llm_query, llm_query_batched, rlm_query, rlm_query_batched, SHOW_VARS and answer. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L167, #L198, #L241-L243; https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/base_env.py#L13, #L130-L147)
- **Discovery.** The system prompt lists the built-in helpers and the context variable up front (context, llm_query, rlm_query, SHOW_VARS). I did not find where custom tool names reach the prompt, so I did not claim it. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/utils/prompts.py#L132-L140)
- **Bridge.** Custom tools: none. They are direct calls in the same process. llm_query is the only bridge, and it is a socket request to an LM handler: send_lm_request(lm_handler_address, LMRequest(...)). With no handler it returns the string 'Error: No LM handler configured', which is what the stub replaces. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L266-L289; https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/core/comms_utils.py)
- **Isolation boundary.** None for the default local REPL. The builtins dict keeps __import__, open and getattr, and drops only eval, exec, input, compile, globals and locals (set to None). The code runs through exec() in the host process (P3, P4, P5 and P12 all reached the host). The LocalREPL docstring says 'sandboxed namespace', and base_env.py's NonIsolatedEnv docstring says the default runs 'as a subprocess'. The code does neither. The README says 'generally safe' for local use. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L60, #L107, #L121-L122, #L145, #L156-L157, #L578 (exec); https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/base_env.py#L259-L263; https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/README.md (Local Environments, line 99))
- **Output channel.** execute_code returns REPLResult(stdout, stderr, locals, execution_time, llm_calls, final_answer). exec() returns None, so the last expression's value is not returned (P2). stdout is captured by swapping sys.stdout, a process-wide change for the duration of the cell. The model sees formatted output cut at 20,000 chars (head only), and the prompt tells the model about it. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L509-L518 (_capture_output), #L564-L604 (execute_code), #L578 (exec); https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/utils/parsing.py#L26, #L57-L62 (format_iteration); https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/utils/prompts.py#L141)
- **Limits.** The REPL has no time limit and no memory limit (P6, P7). The RLM-level max_timeout is checked between iterations only. The only numeric caps are the 20,000-char model view and max_concurrent_subcalls=4 for batched sub-calls. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/core/rlm.py#L66, #L421-L422, #L551-L553; https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L170, #L382-L397 (ThreadPoolExecutor for batched sub-calls))
- **State.** Persistent within one environment object. self.globals and self.locals survive between execute_code calls, and _restore_scaffold resets the reserved names after each cell (P8). The RLM persistent flag only controls whether a fresh environment is spawned per completion() call (default False: a new one each call). (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L215-L243 (setup), #L530-L562 (_restore_scaffold), #L578-L586 (namespace update); https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/core/rlm.py#L224, #L267-L272, #L303-L304)
- **Errors.** Exceptions are caught in execute_code and appended to stderr as '\n<Type>: <message>'. No traceback and no line number (P10). The harness saw only that string. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L589-L592)
- **Corpus exposure.** The corpus is the completion's prompt (rlm.py sets env_kwargs['context_payload'] = prompt). A str is written as plain text to <temp_dir>/context_0.txt and read back inside the REPL. A list or dict goes to context_0.json. 'context' is an alias of context_0. The corpus sits on disk in plaintext until cleanup (CTX). (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/core/rlm.py#L317; https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L415-L455 (load_context, add_context), #L438-L452)
- **Parallelism.** Batched sub-calls use a ThreadPoolExecutor. Custom tools get no such helper, but any cell can import concurrent.futures, since __import__ is available (P9b ran 5 lookups in 210 ms). The plain loop (P9) is serial at about 1 s. (https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/local_repl.py#L382-L397 (batched sub-calls))
- **Other environments.** The probed LocalREPL is the default (environment="local"), but the repo also ships docker, e2b, modal, daytona, prime and ipython environments, which were not probed. The escape result applies to the default only. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/core/rlm.py:60; research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/__init__.py:46)

Surprises:

- The 'sandboxed namespace' wording in the LocalREPL docstring and the 'as a subprocess' wording in base_env.py do not match the code, which runs exec() in the host process with open, __import__ and getattr available (local_repl.py#L156-L157, base_env.py#L259-L263, local_repl.py#L578).
- The default REPL has no time limit, so a cell that never ends never returns (P6). The RLM loop calls execute_code synchronously (rlm.py#L757), so the loop waits with it. max_timeout is checked only between iterations (rlm.py#L421-L422).
- The last expression of a cell is silently dropped, since exec returns None. The model's view of output is also cut to 20,000 chars with the tail gone (P2).
- P12 escaped twice: __import__('os').system and the os._wrap_close globals route both ran echo on the host (the PWNED lines are in out/P12.log).
- Corpus sits in plaintext in a temp directory during the run (CTX).
- The P3 network probe needed a CA bundle fix on this machine. Without it the failure was a certificate error, not a sandbox block.

### Recursive Language Models (RLM): DockerREPL

- Source: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm (MIT) at `commit e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb (rlm 0.1.3), same clone as rlm at research/impls/rlm/repo; image python:3.11-slim`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython 3.11 in a python:3.11-slim Docker container; each cell is `docker exec python /workspace/_exec.py`, which exec()s the code with dill-persisted locals
- How it was run: DockerREPL(custom_tools=...) then env.execute_code(code), the call RLM makes per cell; environment='docker' in get_environment. No LLM (lm_handler_address None). Harness pins the proxy port to 41920+n and names the container rlm-docker-<probe>.
- Defaults: time None. execute_code runs docker exec with no timeout (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:705-708); RLM max_timeout is checked only between iterations (rlm.py:421-422). P6 ran to the 120 s harness stop.; memory None. docker run has no --memory/--cpus/--pids-limit (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:530-545). P7 reached 4,808 MiB before the harness kill.; output execute_code returns all stdout uncapped (200,001 chars); the RLM loop caps the model view at 20,000 chars per block, head only, with a "... + [N chars...]" marker (rlm/utils/parsing.py).; tool_calls No custom-tool bridge (host callables skipped). llm_query/rlm_query go through a host ThreadingHTTPServer proxy; rlm_query_batched is capped at max_concurrent_subcalls=4.; hardened_null_reason DockerREPL exposes only `image` (plus shared env args); it has no timeout, memory, CPU, network or mount option (docker_repl.py:431-452, 530-545; docs/src/app/environments/docker/page.tsx:43-50), so there is no stricter configuration to run.

From the source:

- **Hardened config.** No stricter option exists. DockerREPL takes only `image` plus the shared env arguments (docker_repl.py:431-452); docs list image, setup_code, context_payload, lm_handler_address (docs/src/app/environments/docker/page.tsx:43-50). There is no timeout, memory, CPU, network or read-only flag to set, so hardened is null. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:431-452, https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm/blob/e11f1a8f8ee4490686e16dd6463233abe08a07eb/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py#L530-L545)
- **API shape.** custom_tools values that are code strings are pasted into the per-cell script; plain data is JSON-loaded; host callables are dropped with a warning comment. The model sees tool names and descriptions via format_tools_for_prompt. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:223-265)
- **Discovery.** All custom tools are listed upfront in the system prompt; no search. (rlm/environments/base_env.py format_tools_for_prompt)
- **Bridge.** Only llm_query/llm_query_batched/rlm_query/rlm_query_batched cross the boundary: container code POSTs to http://host.docker.internal:<port>, a ThreadingHTTPServer on the host bound to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces), which forwards to the LM handler socket. LM credentials stay on the host. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:291-320, 512-527)
- **Isolation boundary.** A Docker container, default bridge network, running as root (python:3.11-slim default user), with the host temp workspace bind-mounted read-write at /workspace. The module docstring says "fully isolated from the host LM process"; the README groups docker with non-isolated local environments. P4/P5/P12 stayed in the container; the sandbox can write the host workspace and call the proxy. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:1-18, 530-545; research/impls/rlm/repo/README.md:89; out/P12.txt)
- **Output channel.** stdout and stderr captured in the container script and returned in a JSON line; last expression dropped; RLM caps the model view at 20,000 chars. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:358-395; out/P2-model-view.txt)
- **Limits.** None in DockerREPL: no exec timeout, no container limits, no output cap at the env level. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:530-545, 705-708)
- **State.** Persists across cells through /workspace/state.dill; values that dill cannot pickle are silently dropped. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/docker_repl.py:333-347)
- **Errors.** traceback.print_exc into stderr, so the model sees the full traceback with line numbers (line 109 is the harness exec line, line 1 the user code). (out/P10.txt)
- **Other backends.** E2B, Modal, Daytona and Prime backends (e2b_repl.py, modal_repl.py, daytona_repl.py, prime_repl.py) need accounts and API keys: blocked-needs-credentials, not probed. (research/impls/rlm/repo/rlm/environments/{e2b,modal,daytona,prime}_repl.py; pyproject.toml optional-dependencies)

Surprises:

- Host callables passed as custom_tools are silently replaced by a comment in the container script; the first call fails with NameError. Tools must be source strings, so any credentials a tool needs must be inside the container.
- The LM proxy binds 0.0.0.0 on an OS-chosen port (docker_repl.py:512-520), so other machines on the network can reach llm_query while a session runs.
- Each setup runs pip install dill requests inside the container, so the default needs network, and setup took about 3.3 s.
- No execution timeout anywhere: an infinite loop holds the RLM iteration forever.

### Shift Labs codemode (@shiftlabs/codemode, formerly runline)

- Source: https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode at `88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3 (packages/codemode 0.46.0 in package.json; the npm 0.46.0 tarball is an older commit, 96683925, so the pinned source was compiled with tsc instead)`
- Language and engine: JS, Node.js worker_threads Worker (eval: true, env: {}, resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb) in the host process; bodies compiled with new Function and handed a real require and process. Run under Node 24.22.1.
- How it was run: Codemode.create({ plugins: [hostPlugin] }) then codemode.execute(code) from packages/codemode/src/sdk.ts, compiled with tsc from the pinned source; lookup is the action host.lookup with a TypeBox input schema.
- Defaults: time 30,000 ms per run (config/types.ts:50); worker.terminate() on expiry. timeoutMs 0 disables it.; memory 64 MiB V8 old generation per worker via resourceLimits (config/types.ts:51, engine.ts:413). Not reliable: 7 of 24 P7 runs aborted the whole host.; output 2,000 lines and 50 KB per result, error and logs, keeping the last lines and naming a full-output file (utils/output-limit.ts:17-18).; tool_calls No per-run cap found. Each action may hold 8 MiB of output (maxActionOutputBytes).
- Hardened config: Codemode.create({ timeoutMs: 5000, memoryLimitBytes: 16 MiB, maxRunsPerWorker: 1, outputLimit: { lines: 3, bytes: 1024 }, outputDir }) per docs/sdk.md 'Instance lifecycle' and 'Limit a run's result' (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/sdk.md). 8 MiB is the engine floor but no worker starts below 12 MiB (out/hardened-min-memory.txt). No option restricts require, process, files, network or child processes; docs/security.md tells users to add an OS sandbox themselves, which the project does not ship.

From the source:

- **Isolation boundary.** A worker_threads Worker inside the host process, created with eval: true, env: {} and resourceLimits. Bodies are compiled with new Function and receive require (a wrapper that only blanks worker_threads.parentPort) and the global process. The authors say plainly it is not a sandbox, and the code matches that. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L401-L414, #L1308-L1330, #L1343; https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/security.md#L5 and #L17)
- **Env secrets.** env: {} empties process.env inside the worker, and the comment explains why (host secrets one line away). docs/security.md:17 says the worker keeps the host's environment away from calling code. P5 shows ps eww on the shared PID still prints the host env, so that claim does not hold once child_process is available. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L402-L412; https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/security.md#L17; research/probes/shift-labs-codemode/out/P5.txt)
- **API shape.** Each plugin is a Proxy global; calling plugin.a.b(args) posts {t: 'invoke', path, args} to the host, which validates args against the action's TypeBox schema, resolves a connection, and runs execute(). Names are always plugin.action. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L962-L972 and #L600-L640)
- **Discovery.** On demand, inside the program: actions.find(query, limit = 5) searches with the ferrosearch native index, actions.describe(path) returns one signature, actions.check(path, input) validates without calling. No schema dump in the prompt, so it scales past 100 tools. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L1130; https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/how-codemode-works.md)
- **Bridge.** Async postMessage over the worker's parentPort with an unguessable runId per run (randomUUID) so a body cannot forge a done message for another run. Calls return promises, so Promise.all overlaps them (P9). (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L106-L128, #L736-L739, #L909-L919)
- **Output channel.** ExecuteResult {result, error, logs}. result is the JSON of the returned value; console.* is bridged into logs. Each is cut to 2,000 lines / 50 KB keeping the last lines, with a marker naming a full-output file the host writes to outputDir. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/utils/output-limit.ts#L17-L18; https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L444)
- **Limits.** Timeout via a host setTimeout that terminates the worker (#L453-L466). Memory via resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb on Node; an RSS watchdog arms only under Bun, which ignores resourceLimits (#L190-L198, #L469-L485). OOM surfaces as ERR_WORKER_OUT_OF_MEMORY when V8 terminates the worker cleanly (#L567), but V8 sometimes aborts the whole process instead (P7). (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L190-L198, #L453-L485, #L567)
- **State.** One pooled worker serves up to 500 runs (maxRunsPerWorker). After each run it deletes new globals and compares listed intrinsics; a leftover timer, undeletable global or touched intrinsic retires the worker. The process object is not checked, so state hung on it survives (P8). Concurrent execute() calls get throwaway workers. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L136-L152, #L1273-L1300; research/probes/shift-labs-codemode/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** Caught in the worker and formatted as message plus stack (__fmtErr); execute() never rejects. Line numbers are user line + 3. The output limit applies to the error too and keeps the last lines, so a tight limit drops the message and keeps the stack tail (hardened P3). (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts#L928-L937; research/probes/shift-labs-codemode/out/hardened-P3.txt)
- **Credentials.** Actions run on the host with connections the guest cannot read via the bridge; an optional credentialBroker signs requests outside the plugin process and declared credentials are only sent to declared HTTPS targets. But the guest can read ~/.codemode or project config.json directly with require('fs'), which docs/security.md admits. (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/sdk.md (Sign requests in the host); https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/docs/security.md (Protect credentials))
- **Maintenance.** MIT license; pinned commit dated 2026-11-22; npm @shiftlabs/codemode 0.46.0 published 2026-11-21 from an older commit. Large bundled plugin set (200+ services). (https://github.com/shift-labs-ai/codemode/blob/88de08941f62c52ecfde9f763ecb8bc8e8bad5b3/README.md)

Surprises:

- The default 64 MB memory limit is not containment: 7 of 24 runs of the literal P7 code aborted the whole host process with a V8 fatal OOM instead of terminating the worker (6 of 12 with an extra distinct-string variant). The engine's own doc comment promises the opposite: 'crash containment: a dead worker never takes the host process down' (packages/codemode/src/core/engine.ts:218).
- docs/security.md:17 says the worker keeps the host's environment variables away from calling code. process.env is empty, but ps eww on the shared PID printed the host's PROBE_SECRET in one line.
- fetch is 'disabled' only as a shadowed name: globalThis.fetch is Node's real fetch and reached example.com (200).
- The pooled worker's state scrub misses the process object: a property set on process in one run is visible to the next run, which may belong to another caller.
- The memory floor in code is 8 MB, but a worker cannot start below 12 MB; every run then fails with 'Memory limit exceeded'.
- The npm 0.46.0 tarball (gitHead 96683925) predates the pinned commit by 73 changed files in packages/codemode/src, including the whole output-limit feature that docs/sdk.md now documents.
- package.json keywords include "sandbox" and the fetch stub error says 'codemode sandbox', while the README and security doc say it is not a sandbox.

### smolagents DockerExecutor (executor_type="docker")

- Source: https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents (Apache-2.0), PyPI smolagents[docker] at `smolagents 1.26.0 (tag v1.26.0 = 12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845); image built from the default Dockerfile (python:3.12-bullseye + jupyter_kernel_gateway)`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython 3.12 IPython kernel inside a Jupyter Kernel Gateway Docker container; code sent over the kernel websocket
- How it was run: DockerExecutor(additional_imports=[], logger, port=41940+n, image_name='smolagents-docker-jupyter-kernel', build_new_image=False, container_run_kwargs={'name': 'smolagents-docker-<probe>'}), send_tools({'lookup': Lookup()}), then executor(code). This is what CodeAgent(executor_type='docker') builds (agents.py:1598-1619).
- Defaults: time None: _websocket_run_code_raise_errors blocks on ws.recv() until the kernel reports idle (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:481-530).; memory None unless container_run_kwargs sets one (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:634-652).; output No cap on logs for remote executors; CodeAgent truncates only the last-output value to 20,000 chars with a middle marker (agents.py:1752, utils.py:254-265).; tool_calls No cap. Tools run inside the kernel.
- Hardened config: DockerExecutor(..., container_run_kwargs={'name': ..., 'mem_limit': '512m', 'cpu_quota': 50000, 'pids_limit': 100, 'security_opt': ['no-new-privileges'], 'cap_drop': ['ALL']}). container_run_kwargs is public (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:567-568, 634-652); the values are the ones in the project's secure-execution tutorial (docs/source/en/tutorials/secure_code_execution.md:366-375, https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/docs/source/en/tutorials/secure_code_execution.md#L366-L375). The tutorial also says to disable network and add timeouts (lines 440-445), but DockerExecutor has no timeout option and network_mode='none' breaks it (out/extra-network-none.txt). Harness: research/probes/smolagents-docker/harness.py --hardened

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools become Python source: get_tools_definition_code runs instance_to_source on each Tool and the class is re-created in the kernel; the model sees tool signatures in the CodeAgent system prompt. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/tools.py:1335-1360; research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:94-113)
- **Discovery.** All tools are rendered upfront in the CodeAgent system prompt; no search. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/agents.py initialize_system_prompt)
- **Bridge.** None back to the host. Code goes in over the Jupyter websocket; tools execute inside the container, so credentials a tool needs must be inside the container too. Final answers come back by raising FinalAnswerException with a serialized value. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:94-113, 481-530)
- **Isolation boundary.** A Docker container from python:3.12-bullseye, running the kernel as root, default bridge network, published only on 127.0.0.1 with a random KG_AUTH_TOKEN. Docs call remote executors "truly robust security isolation"; the code adds no limits of its own. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:594-652; docs/source/en/tutorials/secure_code_execution.md:109)
- **Output channel.** stream messages become logs, execute_result becomes output; both returned whole. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:508-525)
- **Limits.** None by default; container_run_kwargs is the only knob. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:567-568)
- **State.** One kernel per executor, so state persists across calls. (out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** IPython traceback with ANSI colour codes, wrapped in AgentError. (out/P10.txt)
- **E2B, Modal, Blaxel.** E2BExecutor, ModalExecutor and BlaxelExecutor need accounts and API keys: blocked-needs-credentials, not probed. (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo/src/smolagents/remote_executors.py:335, 726, 859)

Surprises:

- No execution timeout: an infinite loop blocks CodeAgent forever. The tutorial lists "Implement execution timeouts" as a key practice (secure_code_execution.md:441), but DockerExecutor has no option for it.
- With the tutorial mem_limit, the cgroup OOM killer stops P7, but the caller hangs instead of getting a MemoryError.
- network_mode="none" cannot be used: the executor talks to the kernel through a published port, so the documented "disable unnecessary network access" breaks it.
- Remote-executor print logs reach the model uncapped (200,001 chars); the local executor caps them at 50,000.
- The kernel runs as root inside the container.

### Hugging Face smolagents CodeAgent, LocalPythonExecutor

- Source: PyPI smolagents; repo https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents at `smolagents 1.26.0 (git tag v1.26.0 = 12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845)`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython process running smolagents' own AST walker (evaluate_ast), not a separate runtime. Code runs in-process with the host, and a timeout runs it in a ThreadPoolExecutor worker thread.
- How it was run: LocalPythonExecutor(additional_authorized_imports=[]) with send_tools({'lookup': Tool}), then executor(code) for each probe. This is the class CodeAgent builds when executor_type='local' (agents.py:1598-1606).
- Defaults: time MAX_EXECUTION_TIME_SECONDS = 30 (local_python_executor.py:60). Not enforced as a wall clock: the caller gets the timeout only after the worker finishes (P6b, 35.01 s). The loop caps stop infinite loops first (P6, 1.9 s).; memory None found. 4.12 GB peak RSS reached with no error (P7), stopped by the harness.; output DEFAULT_MAX_LEN_OUTPUT = 50000 chars for print logs (local_python_executor.py:57). Head and tail kept with a marker in the middle (utils.py:257-265). Return value is not truncated.; tool_calls No cap in the executor or the CodeAgent path. MAX_OPERATIONS = 10,000,000 counts AST node evaluations, not tool calls (local_python_executor.py:58, 1444-1448).
- Hardened config: LocalPythonExecutor(additional_authorized_imports=[], timeout_seconds=5). timeout_seconds is the only stricter public option (src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py:1704-1713 at v1.26.0, https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1704-L1713). No memory or network option exists; imports are already the base allowlist. The project's own stricter path is a remote executor (docker, e2b, modal, blaxel), probed separately as smolagents-docker. With timeout_seconds=1 (out/extra-timeout1-P6.txt, extra-timeout1-P9.txt) P6 still returns only after 4.0 s because the timeout wrapper waits for the worker thread (local_python_executor.py:308-316), and P9's five serial 200 ms calls exceed the 1 s budget. From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools are smolagents Tool objects passed to send_tools(). They go into static_tools and are called in the sandbox as Python functions with keyword args. There is no generated stub. Calls go through evaluate_call, and a static tool cannot be overwritten by the code. (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1763-L1765 (send_tools); #L825 (evaluate_call); #L1708-L1723 (__init__))
- **Discovery.** All tools are rendered into the agent's system prompt up front through the 'tools' template variable, so the model sees every tool before writing code. The executor itself has no search or read step. (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/agents.py#L1269 (the template variable 'tools'); the executor itself has no discovery function)
- **Bridge.** No bridge. A tool call is a direct Python call in the same process. The Tool's forward() runs on the host, the sandbox and host share one interpreter, and there is no RPC, postMessage, or snapshot. Host calls are counted by the probe (P1, P9). (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L825-L865 (evaluate_call dispatches Python callables))
- **Isolation boundary.** The class docstring says it is not a security sandbox and points to remote executors for untrusted code. The guards are: an import allowlist (11 modules), dunder-attribute blocking, and a check that refuses module objects reached through attributes ('Forbidden access to module'). Those guards held in P3 to P5 and P12a to d. A custom AST walker is not a security boundary, so these guards are a filter, not a proof. (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1688-L1694 (docstring); #L68-L71 (nodunder_getattr); #L156-L175 (check_safer_result); #L372 (check_import_authorized))
- **Import allowlist.** BASE_BUILTIN_MODULES = collections, datetime, itertools, math, queue, random, re, stat, statistics, time, unicodedata. CodeAgent adds additional_authorized_imports on top, and the default is none. Only 'time' gives a clock, and there is no asyncio or threading. (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/utils.py#L49-L61; https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/agents.py#L1543-L1544)
- **Output channel.** __call__ returns CodeOutput(output, logs, is_final_answer). output is the last expression's value. logs is the print buffer. Both come back to the caller, and the print buffer is truncated, not the return value (P2). (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1747-L1758 (__call__); #L1583-L1676 (evaluate_python_code); https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/utils.py#L257-L265 (truncate_content))
- **Limits.** Time: MAX_EXECUTION_TIME_SECONDS = 30, applied by the timeout() wrapper, which runs the code in a ThreadPoolExecutor. The 'with' block waits for the worker in __exit__, so the caller is not cut off at 30 s (P6b). Operations: MAX_OPERATIONS = 10M, checked in evaluate_ast. While loops: MAX_WHILE_ITERATIONS = 1M, which stops P6 in 1.9 s. Memory: no limit in the source. (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L57-L60 (constants); #L285-L318 (timeout; 'with' at #L308, except at #L313); #L457-L458 (while cap); #L1444-L1448 (operations cap))
- **State.** Persistent. The executor keeps self.state across __call__, and send_variables() writes into it. evaluate_python_code resets only the print buffer and the operation counter each call. CodeAgent creates one executor per agent instance, so variables carry across steps of one run (P8). (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1716 (self.state); #L1627-L1628 (per-call reset of _print_outputs and _operations_count); #L1760-L1761 (send_variables); https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/agents.py#L1585 (one executor per agent))
- **Errors.** Any exception is re-raised as InterpreterError with the failing statement's source text, the exception type, and the message: "Code execution failed at line '<statement>' due to: <Type>: <msg>". The text has no numeric line number (P10). (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1653-L1663 (error wrap, message at #L1660))
- **Parallelism.** No parallel tool calls on the CodeAgent path. The executor has no await branch in evaluate_ast (grep for ast.Await returns 0), and asyncio is not authorized. max_tool_threads exists only on ToolCallingAgent (agents.py#L1215-L1258, #L1426). (https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/local_python_executor.py#L1547 (import dispatch); `grep -c ast.Await` on the file returns 0; https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents/blob/12c1bc820eca50ace6f80a21d90426d41d74f845/src/smolagents/agents.py#L1426 (ThreadPoolExecutor for max_tool_threads, ToolCallingAgent))

Surprises:

- The source sets a 30 s limit (MAX_EXECUTION_TIME_SECONDS) and the timeout error says so, but the caller only gets that error after the worker finishes. A 35 s sleep returned after 35.01 s with ExecutionTimeoutError (P6b).
- An infinite loop stops at 1.9 s from the 1M while-iteration cap, not from the 30 s limit (P6).
- No memory limit found: a 1 MB-per-append loop reached 4.12 GB peak RSS with no error (P7), and the harness stopped it there. Two earlier runs were stopped at 4.13 and 4.33 GB. A third run was SIGKILLed by the OS before the watchdog wrote anything, and I did not identify the cause.
- The class docstring says 'It is not a security sandbox'. The survey table lists the import allowlist and op-count cap as its controls, which is a weaker claim than the code makes.
- The escape attempts in P12 did not reach the host, including module-attribute routes (collections._sys.modules, queue.threading._os). Four shapes were tried, not all of them, so this does not prove there is no escape.
- The variable persistence question is settled: state persists across executions (P8). A print buffer does not persist.
- The 'concurrent' tool call is impossible in CodeAgent code: asyncio is blocked (P9b) and threading is not authorized. P9 ran 5 lookups in 1024 ms, which is serial.

### smolagents WasmExecutor (Pyodide in Deno, executor_type="wasm")

- Source: https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents (Apache-2.0); WasmExecutor added in v1.20.0 (PR #1261), removed in v1.26.0 (commit fd871374, PR #2321) at `smolagents 1.25.0 from PyPI (last release with WasmExecutor); Deno 2.9.8 on the host; npm:pyodide resolved at runtime to 314.0.8; deno.land/std unpinned, resolved to 0.224.0`
- Language and engine: Python, Pyodide (CPython compiled to wasm32) inside a Deno process started with --allow-net=<local server>,cdn.jsdelivr.net,pypi and --allow-read/--allow-write scoped to its cache dir
- How it was run: WasmExecutor(additional_imports=[], logger), send_tools({'lookup': Lookup()}), then executor(code); harness sets DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT to 41980+n and TMPDIR to a canonical scratch path (see surprises).
- Defaults: time timeout=60: the HTTP read timeout on the request to the Deno server (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1114, 1239). It returns control to the caller but does not stop the Deno event loop.; memory No option. The wasm32 heap ceiling raised MemoryError at about 2.4 GB host RSS.; output No cap on logs; CodeAgent truncates the last output to 20,000 chars.; tool_calls No cap; tools run inside Pyodide.
- Hardened config: WasmExecutor(additional_imports=[], timeout=5) (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1107-1115). deno_permissions is the other option, and its default is already the narrowest grant that loads Pyodide (local server, cdn.jsdelivr.net, PyPI; read/write only the per-instance cache, research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1138-1159). There is no memory option. Harness: research/probes/smolagents-wasm/harness.py --hardened

From the source:

- **Status.** Removed upstream: v1.26.0 deleted WasmExecutor and its docs (commit fd871374, "Remove remote WasmExecutor (#2321)", 2026-05-29). The current release cannot select executor_type="wasm". (research/impls/smolagents-docker/repo: git show fd87137 --stat)
- **API shape.** Same as other remote executors: tool classes are turned into source with instance_to_source and defined inside Pyodide. (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py RemotePythonExecutor.send_tools)
- **Bridge.** Python POSTs {code, packages} to a Deno HTTP server with a bearer token; no path back to host tools. (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1225-1275)
- **Isolation boundary.** Two layers: Pyodide has no processes and an in-memory FS; Deno permissions deny host files, env and subprocesses, and limit network to three hosts. The probes matched this. (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1138-1159; out/P12.raw.json)
- **Limits.** Only the 60 s client read timeout. The runner is single-threaded JS, so a stuck snippet blocks every later request until the server is restarted. (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1239; out/P6.txt, out/hardened-P6.txt)
- **Supply chain.** The runner imports https://deno.land/std/http/server.ts and npm:pyodide without versions, so each fresh cache resolves whatever is latest (here std 0.224.0 and Pyodide 314.0.8). (research/impls/smolagents-wasm/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/smolagents/remote_executors.py:1323-1324; out/startup-default-tmpdir.txt)

Surprises:

- On macOS the default WasmExecutor fails to start: tempfile returns /var/folders/..., Deno canonicalizes reads to /private/var/folders/..., and the --allow-read grant does not match (out/startup-default-tmpdir.txt). Setting TMPDIR to a non-symlinked path fixes it.
- Run from a temp dir inside a repo with package.json, Deno adopted that repo as its workspace, used its node_modules Pyodide (0.27.8) and wrote deno.lock at the repo root. The harness now uses a temp dir outside the repo; the stray deno.lock entries were removed.
- os.system inside Pyodide kills the whole Deno server (exit 1) rather than raising, so one snippet can take the executor down.
- The 60 s timeout frees the caller but not the server: after an infinite loop, every later call times out.
- The executor was removed in 1.26.0; the docs that called it a secure option went with it.

### Stainless-generated MCP server code tool (Mux example, @mux/mcp)

- Source: https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/tree/master/packages/mcp-server (npm: @mux/mcp) at `@mux/mcp 16.2.0 and @mux/ts 16.2.0 from npm (installed with --omit=optional --ignore-scripts, so the bundled deno package was not used); source read at mux-node-sdk 6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3 (packages/mcp-server version 16.2.0, compiled files match); Deno 2.9.8 via DENO_PATH`
- Language and engine: TS, A fresh Deno 2.9.8 subprocess per execution, started by @valtown/deno-http-worker and spoken to over HTTP on a unix socket; flags --allow-read=<install node_modules and package dir>, --allow-net=<SDK base URL host, api.mux.com, image.mux.com, stream.mux.com>, --allow-env (all variables). The code is type-checked with the TypeScript compiler, then imported as a data: URL module and run(client) is called with a proxied, pre-authenticated SDK client.
- How it was run: node node_modules/@mux/mcp/index.js (stdio transport, default --code-execution-mode=local) driven by an MCP client calling `execute` with `async function run(client) {...}`. No Mux key: MUX_BASE_URL pointed the SDK at a mock Mux API in the harness (127.0.0.1:41320), whose GET /video/v1/assets/:id plays `lookup` (200 ms, value = id * 2); MUX_TOKEN_ID/SECRET were dummy strings.
- Defaults: time None in local mode (runCode has no timer, code-tool-runner.ts:110-192). Remote mode caps the round trip at 300 s (code-tool.ts:185). The instructions claim about 5 minutes and a 30 s per-request SDK timeout.; memory None (no V8 flags on the worker). P7 reached 4.3 GB.; output None. Return value and all console.log lines are returned whole (code-tool.ts:270-281).; tool_calls No cap on SDK calls. Method policy via --code-allowed-methods / --code-blocked-methods / --code-allow-http-gets is substring matching on the code text (code-tool.ts:109-123).
- Hardened config: --code-allow-http-gets --no-client-header-overrides (packages/mcp-server/src/options.ts:37-59; README 'Request headers a caller may send'). These are the strictest documented options; they restrict which SDK methods the code may name (string/regex match) and stop HTTP callers overriding env or permissions. No time, memory, env or network option exists for local mode.

From the source:

- **API shape.** No tool stubs: the model writes `async function run(client)` against the generated TypeScript SDK (@mux/ts). The worker wraps the real Mux client in a Proxy (makeSdkProxy) that turns unknown paths into errors with fuzzy 'Did you mean' suggestions from a Fuse index of all method names. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool.ts#L21-L41 and https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-worker.ts#L396-L448)
- **Discovery.** A second tool, search_docs, queries a local MiniSearch index built from embedded SDK method docs, so method schemas are fetched on demand rather than placed in the prompt. The execute description itself is 1,149 chars. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/docs-search-tool.ts#L16 and https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/local-docs-search.ts#L12058-L12063; research/probes/stainless-mcp-codemode/out/TOOLS.txt)
- **Bridge.** There is no host bridge: the SDK client runs inside the sandbox and makes its own HTTP requests, which is why the network grant must include the API hosts and why credentials must be inside the sandbox. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-runner.ts#L43-L49 and #L146-L161)
- **Isolation boundary.** Deno permissions on a per-call subprocess: reads limited to the install, network limited to SDK hosts, no run/write/ffi, but --allow-env for everything and spawnOptions.env = the server's full process.env merged with caller-supplied client envs. The README's 'sandbox environment without web or filesystem access' holds for arbitrary hosts and host files; the environment is fully readable. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-runner.ts#L146-L161 and https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool.ts#L256-L264)
- **Output channel.** console.log and console.error are swapped for collectors inside the worker; the MCP result is up to three text blocks: the JSON return value, the log lines, and 'Error output:' lines. No truncation. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-worker.ts#L436-L446 and https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool.ts#L270-L281)
- **Limits.** Local mode has no time, memory, output or call limits. The only timeout in the code tool is remote mode's 300 s fetch timeout. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-runner.ts#L110-L192 and https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool.ts#L184-L185)
- **Robustness.** The HTTP request to the worker has a response 'error' handler but none on the request itself, so a worker that dies mid-request (killed, or a V8 OOM abort) raises an unhandled 'error' event and exits the MCP server process. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-runner.ts#L166-L191; research/probes/stainless-mcp-codemode/out/P6kill.txt)
- **Errors.** Uncaught errors become 'Name: message' plus a cause; the intended 'at line N' never appears because the stack frames are data: URLs, not '<anonymous>'. TypeScript diagnostics are returned with the offending line before any code runs. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool-worker.ts#L376-L393 and #L10-L12)
- **Credentials and method policy.** API credentials are passed into the sandbox twice: as client options and in the env. Method blocking is plain substring matching on the code text, and the source says so ('not secure against obfuscation'); H2 called the blocked assets.create through a computed property name and the POST reached the API. (https://github.com/muxinc/mux-node-sdk/blob/6037f04ae022ecac0bb6f986a35db66338b17ea3/packages/mcp-server/src/code-tool.ts#L109-L123 and #L243-L254; research/probes/stainless-mcp-codemode/out/X1.txt, hardened-H1.txt, hardened-H2.txt, hardened-mock-log.txt)

Surprises:

- The server instructions tell the model 'Code execution has a total timeout of approximately 5 minutes', but local mode (the default) has no timeout at all; P6 ran past 120 s.
- Killing a runaway worker, or a worker dying from OOM, crashes the whole MCP server (unhandled 'error' on the worker request), so one bad execution ends the session for the client.
- The worker inherits every server environment variable with --allow-env, so model code can read API secrets and anything else in the server's env (P5, X1, X2). The README says only 'without web or filesystem access', which is accurate but leaves env out.
- Network is open to api.mux.com, image.mux.com and stream.mux.com plus the base URL host, so data can leave the machine through those hosts (X3 showed a secret in a query string to the allowed host).
- The error formatter's line-number extraction cannot match because code runs from a data: URL (P10).
- --code-allow-http-gets blocked assets.create when named literally (H1) but a computed name went straight through (H2), as the source comment warns.
- Each call re-runs a full TypeScript type check, so plain-JS code with implicit types can be rejected before it runs, and an execution costs about 380 ms.

From the source:

- **API shape.** No stubs or generated declarations. Every other registered tool (minus any programmatic_tool_caller instance) becomes an async host function in Monty's external_lookup dict, keyword arguments only, with a `_` alias for names that are not identifiers. The run_code-style tool description is static prose that lists no tools; the model learns tool signatures from the agent's normal tool list, where every tool also stays callable directly. (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:205-257 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L205-L257); research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:191-202 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L191-L202); research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:102-118 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L102-L118))
- **Discovery.** All tools upfront: the model sees every tool's schema as an ordinary tool plus the static PTC description. No search or lazy loading inside the code; allowed_tools only narrows what the code may call. Does not scale past 100 tools without the full schemas in the prompt. (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:205-219 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L205-L219))
- **Bridge.** Monty pauses at an external call; pydantic_monty's feed_run awaits the host coroutine, which runs the tool through the agent's ToolExecutor._stream with a copy of the parent invocation_state (so Cedar or risk-policy interventions apply, and an approval interrupt becomes a RuntimeError). Results are unwrapped to dict/list/str. Tool code and credentials stay in the host process; only arguments and results cross to the worker. (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:161-188 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L161-L188); research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:125-148 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L125-L148))
- **Isolation boundary.** Language-level sandbox, stated as such: Monty's VM has no filesystem, env, network, FFI or process access and runs in a separate worker process; the docs warn it bounds the code, not the tools. Probes agree: P3 not-defined, P4 PermissionError, P5 os.environ unsupported, all three P12 attempts fail (no __class__, no __import__). (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:9-14 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L9-L14); research/impls/strands-codemode/src/site/src/content/docs/user-guide/harness/tools/programmatic-tool-calling.mdx:35-46 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/site/src/content/docs/user-guide/harness/tools/programmatic-tool-calling.mdx#L35-L46); research/probes/strands-codemode/out/P12.txt; research/probes/strands-codemode/out/worker_check.txt)
- **Output channel.** Only print() output reaches the model, as the ToolResult text; the last expression value is dropped. Capped at 200,000 chars with a visible truncation marker; on error, printed output and the error share the cap with at least half reserved for the error. (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:260-290 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L260-L290); research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:359 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L359); research/probes/strands-codemode/out/P2.txt; research/probes/strands-codemode/out/Pcap.txt)
- **Limits.** VM limits are hardcoded (60 s VM time, 256 MiB, 1000 suspensions); the only tunables are the wall-clock timeout (default 900 s, None disables it) and allowed_tools. The wall-clock timeout cancels the run and the worker stops with it (out/timeout_check.txt). (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:43-62 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L43-L62); research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:75-99 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L75-L99))
- **State.** Fresh per call: a new AsyncMonty pool and session per programmatic_tool_caller invocation, no persistence or snapshots. P8 fresh. (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:293-296 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L293-L296); research/probes/strands-codemode/out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** Errors return status 'error' with 'Execution error:' plus Monty's traceback display (file <python-input-0>, line, caret, message), prefixed by anything printed before the failure; syntax errors as 'Syntax error:'; wall-clock timeouts as 'timed out after N seconds.' (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:346-357 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L346-L357); research/probes/strands-codemode/out/P10.txt)
- **Other.** On by default in create_harness (default builtin_tools list). Inner calls share a 10-slot semaphore. A programmatic_tool_caller is never exposed to another's code, so no nested runs. The TypeScript harness (harness-ts) has its own implementation, not probed here. (research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/defaults.py:20; research/impls/strands-codemode/src/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py:49-54 (https://github.com/strands-agents/harness-sdk/blob/ad1ae00f35a560e492cb061b0103d10771f48cb6/harness-py/src/strands_harness/tools/programmatic_tool_caller.py#L49-L54))

Surprises:

- If the host process exits abruptly (os._exit) while guest code spins, the `monty subprocess` worker is orphaned to PID 1 and keeps burning a core until Monty's own 60 s VM limit ends it; a SIGKILL to the host's process group does take it down. Evidence research/probes/strands-codemode/out/orphan_check.txt. Two such orphans from a side check had to be killed by hand during this run.
- The docs say the worker has 'memory, time, and recursion limits', but none of them is configurable: _LIMITS is a module constant. The documented per-tool config (allowed_tools, timeout) only adds a wall clock, so the hardened run cannot lower the 256 MiB memory cap.
- Docs and the tool description say only print() output returns; confirmed. A last-expression value is silently dropped (P2), unlike Pydantic AI Harness CodeMode, which returns both.
- strands-harness pins pydantic-monty==0.0.23, a much older Monty line than the 1.6.0 used by pydantic-ai-harness 0.71.0 and fastmcp CodeMode in this repo. Same isolation results here, but fixes in later Monty releases do not reach Strands until the pin moves.
- `time` is not importable (Pclock: ModuleNotFoundError), so the SPEC's in-sandbox P9 timing cannot run; P9 is timed from host-side call spans. The tool description lists `datetime` as importable.

### Symbolica Agentica SDK (Warp RPC + sandboxed Python REPL)

- Source: https://docs.symbolica.ai/concepts/how-it-works ; https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server ; https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-python-sdk (PyPI symbolica-agentica 0.4.1) at `agentica-server 8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3, agentica-python-sdk 1e64ecda69b6456530c9aabff476923893f41fe8, agentica-internal e5c1774 (all last committed 2026-02-13); not built or run`
- Language and engine: Python, CPython 3.12 compiled to WASI (componentize-py), run by a Rust wasmtime host (PyO3) inside the agentica-server process
- How it was run: agentica-server's wasm Sandbox (CPython 3.12 for WASI under a Rust wasmtime host), built from the pinned clones in a rust:1-bookworm Docker image (research/probes/symbolica-agentica/docker/Dockerfile) and driven directly by probe.py with fixed code, one fresh container per probe; no model and no Symbolica key. Built and probed by a wave-3 worker; P7 and the results file finished by the coordinator.
- Defaults: time none; memory none; output Value reprs truncated to 80 lines x 1000 chars with a "[truncated, N ...]" marker (guest/common.py:64-92).; tool_calls Not determined from source.; hardened null: not run, and no stricter sandbox option was found beyond the default Wasm mode.; hardened_reason no limit options exist; only forcing wasm mode
- Hardened config: mode='wasm' forced explicitly (probe.py --mode wasm), which ignores AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX; no time, fuel, epoch or memory option exists to set (wasmtime host sets none)

From the source:

- **API shape.** Functions and objects passed in scope appear in the sandbox as stubs/proxies ("Warp"); return values are proxies by reference, not serialized. Async host functions appear as functions returning Future[T]. (research/probes/symbolica-agentica/out/docs-how-it-works.md lines 19-24 and 137)
- **Discovery.** All upfront: the request to the model includes signatures and docstrings of every function and type in scope. (research/probes/symbolica-agentica/out/docs-how-it-works.md ("What Happens Behind the Scenes", step 1))
- **Bridge.** RPC over two host imports into the Wasm component, send-bytes and recv-bytes (plus recv-ready, write-log); messages are msgspec-encoded Warp frames relayed to the SDK process, where the real functions run. (https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/src/lib.rs#L193-L203 ; https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/sandbox.py#L170-L200)
- **Isolation boundary.** wasmtime component with a default WasiCtxBuilder: no preopened dirs, no env, no inherited network; stdio inherited only in debug mode. The server can instead run guest code in-process when AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX=1 (choose_mode). (https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/src/lib.rs#L210-L218 ; https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/sandbox.py#L145-L151 and #L765-L773)
- **Output channel.** REPL summary: output text, stdout, stderr/traceback, and the eval value; reprs truncated to 80 lines and 1000 chars per line with a visible marker. (https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/sandbox.py#L681-L693 ; https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/guest/common.py#L64-L92)
- **Limits.** No fuel, no epoch interruption, no memory limiter in the wasmtime setup. A loop in guest code would run until the session is closed. (https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/src/lib.rs#L189-L227)
- **State.** Persistent REPL for the life of an agent; docs show multi-step sessions. (research/probes/symbolica-agentica/out/docs-how-it-works.md ("sandboxed REPL environment"))
- **Errors.** Traceback string returned as stderr of the REPL summary. (https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/src/sandbox/host/sandbox.py#L681-L693)
- **Anything else.** Hosted use needs AGENTICA_API_KEY; local use points the SDK at a self-run server via S_M_BASE_URL=http://localhost:2345 and needs an inference key (OpenRouter by default) for the server, not for the sandbox. Credentials of in-scope functions stay in the SDK process because calls are proxied. (https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-python-sdk/blob/1e64ecda69b6456530c9aabff476923893f41fe8/src/agentica/__main__.py#L496-L538 ; https://github.com/symbolica-ai/agentica-server/blob/8db268f44ef8d09bd706b49e72e329348bb4b8b3/README.md)

Surprises:

- The sandbox is fully open source and runs without a Symbolica key, but no prebuilt server exists: running it means building CPython for WASI, wasi-sdk, msgspec and a Rust wasmtime extension from source.
- An environment variable, AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX=1, silently switches the server to running agent code in-process with no Wasm sandbox (sandbox.py:765-773).
- The wasmtime host sets no fuel, epoch deadline or memory limiter, so time and memory are unbounded inside the sandbox by design of the shown code (not measured).
- With AGENTICA_NO_SANDBOX=1 the same probes read /etc/hosts, read the secret and ran os.system twice (out/nosandbox-*.txt): the switch silently turns the sandbox off.
- Closing a sandbox does not stop a guest busy loop: it keeps spinning on a host thread (P6).

### TanStack AI Code Mode, Cloudflare Workers driver (@tanstack/ai-isolate-cloudflare), local wrangler dev

- Source: https://github.com/TanStack/ai (packages/ai-code-mode, packages/ai-isolate-cloudflare); npm @tanstack/ai-code-mode 1.1.2, @tanstack/ai-isolate-cloudflare 1.1.0 at `TanStack/ai c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0 (npm src folders identical); wrangler 4.166.0 with its bundled workerd; Node v24.22.1`
- Language and engine: TS (stripped with sucrase), The package's ready-made Worker under local `wrangler dev` (workerd). For each round it loads the wrapped program into a fresh V8 isolate with the Worker Loader binding (env.LOADER.load, globalOutbound null, env {}). Probed locally only; deployed Cloudflare (Workers Paid plan) would add Cloudflare's own CPU and memory limits, which were not tested.
- How it was run: wrangler dev serves `export { default } from '@tanstack/ai-isolate-cloudflare/worker'` on 127.0.0.1:41010 with the package's wrangler.toml settings; the host runs createCodeModeTool({ driver: createCloudflareIsolateDriver({ workerUrl }), tools: [lookup, failing] }).execute({ typescriptCode }). No account or login.
- Defaults: time 30,000 ms requested per round, enforced only by a setTimeout inside the Worker (ai-isolate-cloudflare/src/worker/index.ts:116-123), which a synchronous loop starves locally; memory None set by TanStack; local workerd crashed at V8's heap limit. Deployed Workers limits were not tested.; output No cap on logs or result; tool_calls maxToolRounds 10 per execution (isolate-driver.ts:119, :324); no per-call cap
- Hardened config: createCodeModeTool({ driver, tools, timeout: 5000 }) (create-code-mode-tool.ts:96; the driver passes it to the Worker as request.timeout). memoryLimit is not used by this driver (docs/code-mode/code-mode-isolates.md:57). The driver's own options are workerUrl, authorization, timeout and maxToolRounds (default 10, already strict).

From the source:

- **Bridge.** No live bridge. Each tool wrapper records the call and throws __ToolCallNeeded; the Worker returns need_tools; the host runs the calls and re-sends the whole program with all results so far, which replays from the start. Tool calls are keyed by sequence index (tc_0, tc_1, ...). (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-cloudflare/src/worker/wrap-code.ts#L86-L120 and #L126-L196; isolate-driver.ts#L119-L222)
- **Parallelism.** The host executes one round's tool calls in a for loop with await, so calls the guest issued together still run one after another. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-cloudflare/src/isolate-driver.ts#L199-L222)
- **Isolation boundary.** Worker Loader isolate with globalOutbound null and env {}: no network, no bindings. The ready-made Worker answers CORS with Access-Control-Allow-Origin * and does not check the Authorization header; the docs warn about this. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-cloudflare/src/worker/index.ts#L126-L132 and #L218; docs/code-mode/code-mode-isolates.md (WARNING under Cloudflare Workers driver))
- **Limits.** Timeout is a setTimeout race inside the Worker; there is no host-side timeout on the driver's fetch, so a starved Worker hangs the caller. (worker/index.ts#L116-L156; isolate-driver.ts#L138-L141 (fetch carries only the caller abort signal))
- **State.** Fresh isolate per round. Replay means guest code before a tool call runs once per round, and its console output is collected once per round (duplicated logs). (out/P1b.txt; isolate-driver.ts#L168 and #L190 (allLogs accumulation))

Surprises:

- Locally, the Worker's own timeout never fired for a busy loop, at 30 s or 5 s; the call hung until the harness killed it at 120 s, and it held up a second program too.
- A memory-hungry program crashed the whole local workerd (V8 fatal heap OOM), failing a concurrent program and every later one.
- Programs are replayed from the start after each tool round, so pre-call side effects inside the sandbox and console output repeat (P1b logged "before" twice).
- Tool calls are serial on the host even when issued with Promise.all, and the default maxToolRounds of 10 caps dependent tool calls at 10 per execution; going over fails after the side effects already ran (P9c).
- Not measured: deployed Cloudflare Workers enforce their own CPU and memory limits, so P6 and P7 may behave better in production. That needs a Workers Paid account.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each TanStack tool becomes a guest function external_<name>; the model gets TypeScript stubs generated from the tools' JSON Schema in the system prompt (createCodeModeSystemPrompt) and the function names in the tool description. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-code-mode/src/create-code-mode-tool.ts#L133 and #L432-L447; create-system-prompt.ts#L28-L37)
- **Discovery.** Eager tools get full stubs up front. Tools marked lazy: true appear by name only, and a separate discover_tools tool returns their stubs on demand, so large catalogs need not put every schema in the prompt. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-code-mode/src/create-discovery-tool.ts#L55-L108; docs/code-mode/lazy-tools.md)
- **Bridge.** Each tool is an ivm.Reference to an async host function stored on the guest global as __<name>_ref; the guest wrapper calls applySyncPromise with JSON, which blocks the isolate until the host settles. That makes calls serial. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-node/src/isolate-driver.ts#L194-L229)
- **Isolation boundary.** isolated-vm V8 isolate in the host process. Docs claim no access to host file system, network or process; P3 to P5 and P12 agree. The raw References being reachable from guest code is wider than needed, though no escape through them was found. (docs/code-mode/code-mode.md:126; isolate-driver.ts#L156-L161 and #L212)
- **Output channel.** execute returns { success, result, logs, error }; result is JSON.stringify'd inside the isolate and parsed on the host. No truncation anywhere in this driver. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-code-mode/src/create-code-mode-tool.ts#L369-L404; ai-code-mode/src/code-wrapper.ts#L9-L23)
- **Limits.** Only timeout and memoryLimit, both set per createCodeModeTool. No output, call-count or concurrency limit. (create-code-mode-tool.ts#L93-L103)
- **State.** A new isolate per execution, disposed in finally. The cleanup disposes again after isolated-vm already disposed on OOM, which throws out of execute (P7). (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-node/src/isolate-context.ts#L94-L101; ai-code-mode/src/create-code-mode-tool.ts#L418-L424)
- **Errors.** Errors are normalized to { name, message, stack }; tool errors are passed to the guest as plain messages and reach the model verbatim. Line numbers are not mapped back past the wrapper. (ai-isolate-node/src/error-normalizer.ts#L6-L15; isolate-driver.ts#L203-L207)
- **Anything else.** Rejects tools with needsApproval at construction; warns (or throws, by option) when a tool input schema has parameter names like password, token or apiKey, to stop the model passing secrets through code; input and output schemas are validated on the host per call. MIT, last commit 2026-11-21. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-code-mode/src/create-code-mode-tool.ts#L112-L143; validate-bindings.ts; bindings/tool-to-binding.ts#L75-L100)

Surprises:

- The docs say the three Promise.all weather calls "run in parallel inside the sandbox" (code-mode.md:116), but with the Node driver they run one after another (P9, 1,030 ms for 5 calls).
- At the memory limit, execute() throws "Isolate is already disposed" from its own cleanup instead of returning the memory error it had already built, so callers that rely on execute never throwing get an exception.
- Raw isolated-vm Reference objects (__external_lookup_ref, __captureLog) are guest globals; guest code can call the tool host function directly, skipping the wrapper. No escape was found through them in P12g to P12j.
- Host tool error messages reach the model verbatim (P10c printed the fake DSN), unlike the Vercel layers, which replace them with a generic message.
- Driver creation spawns a Node subprocess once to check isolated-vm compatibility (213 ms setup).
