From the source:

- **API shape.** Same Code Mode layer as the other TanStack drivers: external_<name> functions and TypeScript stubs from JSON Schema; lazy tools through discover_tools. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-code-mode/src/create-code-mode-tool.ts#L133; create-discovery-tool.ts#L55-L108)
- **Bridge.** Each binding is a QuickJS host function that returns a QuickJS promise immediately and resolves it when the host promise settles, then pumps executePendingJobs. Calls overlap, so Promise.all is parallel. The authors chose the sync build plus promises to avoid asyncify bugs. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-quickjs/src/isolate-driver.ts#L87-L133 and #L220-L224)
- **Isolation boundary.** QuickJS WASM on the host's main thread, not a worker. Guest has no host APIs (P3 to P5, P12), but CPU-bound guest code freezes the whole host event loop until the interrupt fires (P6), and memory growth is bounded only by the WASM 2 GB ceiling (P7). (isolate-driver.ts#L223-L229; out/P6.txt siblingStartMs 30019; out/P7b.txt)
- **Limits.** setMemoryLimit is called per runtime, but QuickJS under quickjs-emscripten still allocated 2,141 MB before failing. The same happens calling quickjs-emscripten directly with both setMemoryLimit and newRuntime({memoryLimit}), on 0.31.0 and 0.32.0, so the gap is in quickjs-emscripten, not TanStack's call. (research/probes/tanstack-ai-codemode-quickjs/qjs-memlimit-check.mjs; out/qjs-memlimit-check.txt; out/qjs-memlimit-check-0.32.txt)
- **Output channel.** { success, result, logs, error }; console methods push every line, no caps. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-quickjs/src/isolate-driver.ts#L231-L265)
- **Errors.** The error normalizer passes error.stack through; quickjs-emscripten's unwrap error appends the host stack after "Host:", so absolute host paths reach the model. (ai-isolate-quickjs/src/error-normalizer.ts#L34; out/P10b.txt)
- **Anything else.** Same approval rejection, secret-parameter warning and host-side schema validation as the other drivers. Docs call this driver "Slower (interpreted)", but its per-execution cost was the lowest measured here. (docs/code-mode/code-mode-isolates.md:52-60)

Surprises:

- The documented memoryLimit (default 128 MB, hardened 32 MB) did not stop P7; the program grew the host process to about 2.1 GB before QuickJS ran out of WASM memory. Verified outside TanStack on quickjs-emscripten 0.31.0 and 0.32.0. This repo's own asb-quickjs uses quickjs-emscripten 0.32.0, and its wave-1 P7 (6.8 s to out of memory, RSS not recorded) matches this 2 GB pattern rather than its 512 MB cap. That is an inference, not a measurement of asb-quickjs.
- Guest CPU loops block the host's main thread: during P6 no other request could run for 30 s.
- Error stacks include the host's stack and absolute file paths (P10b).
- Docs rate this driver slower than Node; measured startup was 0.71 ms median against 3.14 ms for the Node driver.

From the source:

- **API shape and discovery.** Same Code Mode layer as the other TanStack drivers: external_<name> functions, TypeScript stubs from JSON Schema in the system prompt, and lazy tools behind discover_tools. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-code-mode/src/create-system-prompt.ts#L28-L83; create-discovery-tool.ts#L55-L108)
- **Bridge.** Each tool call creates a guest promise (vm.newPromise), runs the host binding asynchronously, and resolves the promise when it settles; the execution loop pumps pending jobs until the program settles or the deadline passes. Calls overlap, so P9 is parallel. (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-quickjs-bun/src/isolate-context.ts#L480-L535)
- **Isolation boundary.** Native QuickJS in the Bun process via FFI, on the main thread. A QuickJS memory-safety bug would be a native bug in the host process, with no WASM boundary in between. The engine is compiled at runtime with TinyCC from C sources shipped in the npm package. (quickjs-bun 0.1.2 src/ffi.ts:438-454 (npm, cc({ source: quickJSSources })))
- **Limits.** The only driver here with output and call-count caps, and the memory limit holds (P7 at 200 MB RSS, 104 MB hardened). (https://github.com/TanStack/ai/blob/c695ada5091e7022bf13b235220645ceb65d43b0/packages/ai-isolate-quickjs-bun/src/isolate-context.ts#L51-L58)
- **Errors.** Guest stacks use the <code-mode> file name; no host stack is appended, unlike the QuickJS WASM driver. (out/P10b.txt)

Surprises:

- Guest CPU loops block the whole Bun process for the full timeout (P6: 30 s), although docs call it the fastest sandbox for Bun.
- Native QuickJS is compiled at first use with TinyCC from C source shipped in node_modules, which adds about 1.1 to 1.5 s to the first execution in each process.
- This driver caps logs and tool calls, while the Node and QuickJS WASM drivers in the same project cap neither.

### ToolHive Virtual MCP (vMCP) code mode (Starlark execute_tool_script)

- Source: https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive (pkg/script, pkg/vmcp/codemode); release binary toolhive_0.67.1_darwin_arm64.tar.gz at `v0.67.1 = 2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f (commit 2026-11-21; release published 2026-11-21T20:08Z). Binary sha256 c1a09a5e6bf965780d9fb75ddc31b93fe1d4fde2150acde151acdbe46e67ca13 matches toolhive_0.67.1_checksums.txt. Engine go.starlark.net v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d (go.mod:90).`
- Language and engine: Python subset (Starlark), google/starlark-go (go.starlark.net), run in-process in the vMCP Go server on a fresh starlark.Thread per execution with only SetMaxExecutionSteps; parallel() runs child threads on goroutines
- How it was run: thv vmcp serve --config vmcp-default.yaml (release binary, local, no Kubernetes, isolated HOME, update checks and usage metrics off) with one static streamable-http backend (the SPEC lookup MCP server on 127.0.0.1:42141, aggregated as probe_lookup) and anonymous incoming auth; the driver connects an MCP client to vMCP's /mcp on 127.0.0.1:42140 and calls the execute_tool_script virtual tool with {script}.
- Defaults: time stepLimit 100,000 Starlark steps (codemode/config.go via script.DefaultStepLimit, script.go:16), counted only in the bytecode loop: builtin work is not charged and cancellation is not checked inside builtins. defaultScriptTimeout 1 minute (decorator.go:34) is a context deadline that reaches tool calls and parallel() only, never the Starlark thread (core.Execute takes no context), so it does not bound computation (P6c ran 72.9 s). toolCallTimeout 30 s per inner tool call.; memory None. google/starlark-go has no allocation budget, and vMCP sets none; only the engine's 1 GiB per-operation cap (eval.go:1143). Memory is bounded indirectly by the step budget times per-step allocation, which allowed 2.9 GB (default) and 4.4 GB+ in 35 steps (variant).; output None. Return value as JSON text plus a 'Script logs:' item with every print line; neither is capped or truncated (P2: 200,000 + 2,000,000 chars).; tool_calls No total call cap. parallel() concurrency 10 (defaultParallelMax, codemode/config.go:30), each child thread gets stepLimit/n steps; per-call timeout 30 s.
- Hardened config: vmcp-hardened.yaml codeMode = {enabled: true, stepLimit: 10000, parallelMaxConcurrency: 5, toolCallTimeout: 5s}. These three knobs are the only code-mode options (pkg/vmcp/config/config.go:1212-1238; docs/operator/crd-api.md:348-350; https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/config/config.go#L1212-L1238). stepLimit's documented minimum is 1, which rejects any useful script, so 10,000 (10x below the default, still enough for P1/P9) is used as the tight-but-usable setting. No memory, wall-clock, output or call-count option exists. File: research/probes/toolhive-vmcp-codemode/vmcp-hardened.yaml

From the source:

- **API shape.** Every tool the caller may use (admission-filtered ListTools) becomes a predeclared Starlark builtin under its sanitized advertised name (prefix-aggregated, e.g. probe_lookup), plus call_tool(name, ...) and parallel(). Keyword args become the argument map; positional args become arg0, arg1, ... No schema, stub or type information is generated for the script. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/builtins/builtins.go#L33-L62, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/builtins/tools.go#L24-L64, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L290-L324)
- **Discovery.** No on-demand discovery in code mode. execute_tool_script's description lists every callable tool name with its description cut to 80 characters, and all backend tools stay in tools/list with full schemas next to it (tools-list.json), so the prompt grows with the catalog. Scaling past 100 tools relies on the separate optimizer (find_tool/call_tool), which can index execute_tool_script (example yaml comment). (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/description.go#L18-L38, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L166-L176, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/examples/operator/virtual-mcps/vmcp_codemode.yaml#L16-L18, research/probes/toolhive-vmcp-codemode/out/tools-list.json)
- **Bridge.** In-process Go call: the builtin calls the bound closure, which wraps ctx with toolCallTimeout and re-enters inner.CallTool with the caller's identity, so Cedar admission runs per inner call by its real name; denied calls return a generic message. parallel() fans out through foreach.Concurrent with maxConcurrency. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L290-L324, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/builtins/parallel.go#L24-L92)
- **Tool result shape.** The backend client always synthesizes StructuredContent {"text": ...} from text content when the backend sends none, and pkg/script's ParseToolResult prefers StructuredContent, so its JSON-text parsing fallback never runs under vMCP. A text-returning tool arrives in the script as {"text": "<json string>"}, and with no json module the script cannot parse it. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/client/client.go#L2025-L2041, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/types.go#L549-L557, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/conversions/result.go#L35-L71, research/probes/toolhive-vmcp-codemode/out/P1.txt)
- **Isolation boundary.** Starlark with only tool builtins, call_tool and parallel predeclared; load() refused by the thread's Load hook; default FileOptions disable while loops and recursion is rejected by the interpreter. This holds (P3-P5, P12). Resource isolation is only SetMaxExecutionSteps: steps are charged per bytecode instruction (checkSteps), so one builtin call of any size costs one step, and there is no memory budget in google/starlark-go. It runs in the gateway process, so a memory blow-up takes down every session. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/core/execute.go#L28-L71, https://github.com/google/starlark-go/blob/4f4267fb140d1e8b91c9bce55cee2f809e8840dd/starlark/interp.go#L700-L720, https://github.com/google/starlark-go/blob/4f4267fb140d1e8b91c9bce55cee2f809e8840dd/starlark/eval.go#L78-L106, https://github.com/google/starlark-go/blob/4f4267fb140d1e8b91c9bce55cee2f809e8840dd/starlark/eval.go#L1143-L1158)
- **Limits / timeout plumbing.** The decorator creates execCtx with a 1-minute deadline and passes it to Execute, but executor.Execute hands only the script, globals and stepLimit to core.Execute; no thread.Cancel is wired to ctx.Done(). The deadline reaches tool calls and parallel() only. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L28-L34, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L233-L240, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/executor.go#L27-L48, research/probes/toolhive-vmcp-codemode/out/P6c.txt)
- **Output channel.** Result is the script's top-level return value marshalled as JSON text, plus a second text item 'Script logs:\n' joined from print() lines (parallel children's logs merged in order). No size cap. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/executor.go#L69-L87, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/core/execute.go#L73-L90)
- **State.** Stateless: a fresh script.Executor and globals per execute_tool_script call; data arguments are injected as top-level variables and may not shadow tools or builtins. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L110-L112, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/executor.go#L27-L40)
- **Errors.** Engine errors are wrapped as 'script execution failed: <err>' and returned as an IsError result. Runtime EvalErrors keep only the message (no backtrace, no line); compile errors keep a position shifted by the def __main__() wrapper (+1 line, +4 columns). Backend tool errors pass through verbatim. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/core/execute.go#L58-L60, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L241-L246, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/script/internal/conversions/result.go#L25-L33)
- **Credentials and approvals.** Backend credentials (outgoingAuth header injection, token exchange) are applied by the gateway's backend client; scripts only see tool results. Each inner call is admission-checked per identity, but execute_tool_script itself bypasses Cedar admission (the config flag is the grant). No approval or human-in-the-loop step. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/codemode/decorator.go#L250-L266, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/vmcp/config/config.go#L395-L425)
- **Maintenance.** Apache-2.0, Stacklok; v0.67.1 released 2026-11-21, code mode added in 2025 (SPDX headers) and actively changed (#5845 reserved-name guard). Local mode needs no account; update checks and anonymous usage metrics are on by default and were disabled with TOOLHIVE_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK / TOOLHIVE_USAGE_METRICS_ENABLED=false. (https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/updates/client.go#L62, https://github.com/stacklok/toolhive/blob/2d33d6bea91715c3421ddac2e94a3fae015f174f/pkg/usagemetrics/collector.go#L22)

Surprises:

- The SPEC P6 and P7 code fails to compile: this Starlark dialect has no while loops, and the tool description does not tell the model so.
- decorator.go says defaultScriptTimeout 'bounds the total wall-clock time of a single script execution', but the context never reaches the Starlark thread: a builtin-heavy script returned success after 72.9 s, and another was still running past 120 s and kept burning CPU after the client disconnected.
- The CRD docs say stepLimit 'bounds runaway loops and computation', but steps are charged per bytecode instruction, so work and allocation inside builtins (string repeat, count, list comprehensions of huge strings) is nearly free: 35 steps allocated 4.4 GB and the gateway process was killed.
- No memory limit and no output limit exist in any configuration, and scripts run inside the shared gateway process.
- The example script (vmcp_codemode.yaml, and the exampleScript in the tool schema) uses r.get("vulns") as if tool results were parsed objects. A backend that returns JSON text arrives as {"text": "<json string>"}, because client.go synthesizes StructuredContent before pkg/script's JSON fallback can run, and there is no json module to decode it.
- The tool description says 'Use call_tool("name", ...) to call any tool by its original name', but call_tool accepts only the aggregated (prefixed) name: call_tool("lookup") -> unknown tool.
- Runtime errors lose their line number, and compile errors report positions shifted by the hidden wrapper (+1 line, +4 columns).
- thv vmcp serve in local static mode logs 'dynamic backend registry enabled for Kubernetes environment'. Harmless, but misleading.

### UTCP Code Mode (@utcp/code-mode)

- Source: https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode (npm: @utcp/code-mode 1.2.13, gitHead e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51) at `e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51 (@utcp/code-mode 1.2.13); @utcp/sdk 1.1.0; @utcp/direct-call 1.1.0; isolated-vm 6.0.2`
- Language and engine: TS, isolated-vm 6.0.2: a separate V8 isolate per callToolChain call, with a 128 MB memoryLimit. Guest code is plain JavaScript with no Node APIs. The README says "Node.js VM sandboxing", but the code does not use node:vm.
- How it was run: CodeModeUtcpClient.create(), then registerManual({name: "host", call_template_type: "direct-call", callable_name: "hostManual"}) for the lookup tool, then client.callToolChain(code, timeout, memoryLimit) once per execution.
- Defaults: time 30000 ms per callToolChain (default timeout arg). Enforced by the isolated-vm script timeout and a host-side timer. src line 182, 292-296, 312.; memory 128 MB isolate heap (default memoryLimit arg). src line 183, 189.; output No cap found in the source. The logs array and the JSON return value are unbounded (src 186, 280, 319, 400). 200000 printed chars came back whole in P2.; tool_calls No per-execution call cap found in the source (grep for limit/max finds only the memory limit). Only the 30 s timeout bounds the count. Not measured beyond 5 calls in P9.
- Hardened config: client.callToolChain(code, 10000, 64): timeout 10000 ms and memoryLimit 64 MB, the only two public limit arguments, positional (typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts:181-184; memoryLimit goes to new ivm.Isolate at :189, timeout to script.run at :312 and a host timer at :291-296). Defaults are 30000 ms and 128 MB; 10 s and 64 MB were chosen by this run, as no floor is documented. No network, filesystem, env, output or tool-call option exists. The typescript-library README documents an options object, callToolChain(code, { timeout, memoryLimit }) (typescript-library/README.md:79-82). Passed that way, every execution fails at once with "Script execution timeout after [object Object]ms", even P1 (out/hardened-README-options-form.txt), so this run uses the positional form.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Each registered tool becomes a global function under its manual namespace: global.<manual>.<tool> = function(args) { applySyncPromise(...) }. Names with no dot would be flat globals, but registerManual always prefixes the manual name, so only the namespaced form occurs. TypeScript interfaces are generated from JSON Schema by toolToTypeScriptInterface and getAllToolsTypeScriptInterfaces. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L106-L168 and #L464-L496 (generator loop); manual prefix at @utcp/sdk dist/index.js:1396-1397 (npm, not in repo))
- **Discovery.** Everything is pushed in up front on every execution. callToolChain calls getTools() and then setupUtilities injects __interfaces, which is the TypeScript text for all tools. searchTools is a host-side UtcpClient method (sdk dist/index.js:1536-1538), not available inside the sandbox. The prompt template tells the agent to search first, then read __interfaces. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L185 and #L506-L521; agent prompt #L15-L58)
- **Bridge.** Tool calls go from the isolate to the host through an ivm.Reference that wraps an async host function (toolCallerRef). The in-isolate stub blocks its thread in applySyncPromise until the host promise settles. This makes calls look synchronous, and it is why Promise.all over tool calls ran serially in P9. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L440-L456 and #L475-L482 (applySyncPromise at #L478))
- **Isolation boundary.** The engine is an isolated-vm Isolate (a separate V8 isolate), not node:vm. The authors claim "Node.js VM sandboxing" in the README, and the code does not match that wording. It does match the claim that the guest has no network and no filesystem, which P3 and P4 confirm. P12 also confirms the guest cannot reach process, so the isolate, not the wrapper, is the boundary. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L2 and #L189; README claim https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/README.md#L435)
- **Output channel.** console.* is bridged to a host array (logs) with no cap, and the return value goes back as JSON. Errors are caught and written into logs as "[ERROR] ..." with result null, so callToolChain never throws for guest errors. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L186, #L280, #L321-L327, #L390-L421)
- **Limits.** Time: timeout default 30000 (#L182), enforced by script.run({timeout}) (#L312) and a host timer (#L291-L296). Memory: memoryLimit default 128 (#L183), applied at isolate creation (#L189). Count: none found. Output: none found. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L180-L336)
- **State.** A new isolate and context are created for every callToolChain call, so no state persists between executions. P8 confirms this. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L189 and #L239)
- **Errors.** The wrapper runs user code inside an async IIFE and reports String(e.stack) through __rejectResult. The stack carries isolate line numbers, offset by 4 wrapper lines from user code (P10 multi-line case). (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L274-L285 and #L321-L327)
- **Other: teardown and leak handling.** Every bridged call races a chainDone promise so no call can pin an isolate thread past the chain, and disposal is retried. The authors describe a thread leak they fixed, so the design treats thread health as a real risk. (https://github.com/universal-tool-calling-protocol/code-mode/blob/e5fdc319bfae1ceec57e7bce37048337635ffb51/typescript-library/src/code_mode_utcp_client.ts#L192-L221 and #L357-L384)
- **Host tool argument convention.** @utcp/direct-call spreads the args object into positional parameters (Object.values(toolArgs)), so lookup({id:21}) calls the host function as lookup(21). Host code that expects an object gets the raw value. (@utcp/direct-call dist/index.js:4184 (npm, not in repo))

Surprises:

- README.md (lines 101 and 435) says "Node.js VM sandboxing" and "Node.js isolates". The engine is isolated-vm, a V8 isolate, not node:vm. The naming is loose, but the security property the README claims (no fs, no network, no process) holds in P3, P4, P5, and P12.
- The sandbox does not return the last expression. The literal spec form (bare "RETURNED") gives result null, and only "return" gives the value. The README examples and the agent prompt both use return, so the docs are consistent but the spec form is not valid here.
- Guest errors do not throw to the caller. callToolChain resolves with result null, and the error is only in logs as "[ERROR] ...". A caller that checks only result sees a silent null.
- Tools are always namespaced as manual.tool, so the bare lookup({id}) form in the spec cannot be expressed. The probe uses host.lookup.
- Each direct-call host function receives its arguments spread positionally. lookup({id:21}) calls the host with 21, so a host implemented against an object argument silently gets the wrong value.
- Promise.all over tool calls runs serially (P9: 1013 ms for five 200 ms calls). Nothing in the README claims parallel execution, but "Batching advantage" could be read that way.
- The README cites imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark for "$9,536/year" and "validates the performance claims", and lists "16 realistic scenarios" (README line 483). That repo measures a different thing: a Python RestrictedPython code mode against native tool calling, with Claude 3 Haiku, 8 scenarios, and end-to-end wall time including LLM calls. It does not test @utcp/code-mode and does not test any sandbox boundary. The benchmark repo does not mention UTCP. The UTCP table figures "67% / 75% / 88% faster" with "3 / 8 / 16 iterations" (README lines 25-35) do not appear in the benchmark. Its nearest figures are 80.5% speedup for the 16-iteration Scenario 7 (docs/RESULTS_DATA.md line 23) and 87.5% fewer iterations on average.
- Benchmark source evidence: sandbox/executor.py line 209 runs exec(byte_code, restricted_globals, restricted_locals) in the same CPython process. https://github.com/imran31415/codemode_python_benchmark/blob/363507ee639f63532c70ed81aa5ef44ac28c619f/sandbox/executor.py#L209. The repo has no results/ JSON at this commit, even though its README tree lists results/ with benchmark_results_claude.json (README lines 112-118).

From the source:

- **Layering.** @ai-sdk/code-mode depends only on `run` (package.json dependencies: run ^2.1.8). runCodeMode builds a Run runner with createRunner, wraps the user's source, exposes every AI SDK tool as one Run host group `__codeMode` (tool0, tool1, ..., missing), and returns result.value. Limits, continuations and approvals are Run features re-exported under code-mode names. (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/run-code-mode.ts#L104-L135 and #L219-L254)
- **API shape.** The guest sees a `tools` Proxy; property access maps a tool name to its __codeMode.toolN binding or to __codeMode.missing. The model sees a TypeScript `declare const tools: {...}` block plus example calls generated from each tool's JSON Schema (input and output types, descriptions as JSDoc). (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/run-code-mode.ts#L209-L217 and tool-prompt.ts#L15-L47; generated text saved in research/probes/vercel-ai-sdk-codemode/out/P1.json (toolDescriptionSeenByModel))
- **Discovery.** Default toolDiscovery 'description' puts every tool's signature in the code_mode tool description. toolDiscovery 'conversation' keeps the description fixed and sends a catalog as a user message; combined with the AI SDK's toolSearch() and deferLoading tools, only discovered tools enter the catalog, so it can scale past 100 tools. (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/code-mode-tool.ts#L64-L89, tool-prompt.ts#L49-L67, tool-search.test.ts#L7-L30)
- **Bridge.** Run's async host-function bridge (worker postMessage to the main thread); each tool call runs invokeHostTool on the host, which validates input with the tool's schema (only if the schema has a validator), checks needsApproval, and calls the tool's execute with the outer abort signal. (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/run-code-mode.ts#L256-L348 and tool-invocation.ts#L73-L120, #L183-L194)
- **Isolation boundary.** Same as vercel-run: QuickJS WASM in a worker thread, fresh context, Function and eval blocked. The docs call the sandbox "defense in depth" and say tools run on the host with full authority; the code matches. (content/docs/03-ai-sdk-core/18-code-mode.mdx:289-305)
- **Output channel.** runCodeMode returns only the JSON round-tripped return value. Nothing in packages/code-mode/src captures console output (grep finds no console handling outside tests), so the model never sees logs. (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/run-code-mode.ts#L131-L135)
- **Errors.** Run errors are translated to CodeMode* error classes (timeout, CPU timeout, bridge limit, source too large); the stack is rewritten from run.js to code-mode.js with the wrapper line removed. Any non-CodeModeError thrown by a tool becomes "Host tool failed." (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/run-code-mode.ts#L335-L347 and #L638-L751)
- **Anything else.** Approval: callback mode or interrupt mode with HMAC-signed continuations (default signing key is random per process). The docs say code mode does not integrate with AI SDK approval flows and nested tools needing approval are rejected, while the code ships an interrupt-based approval path. Apache-2.0, part of vercel/ai, last commit 2026-11-20. (https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/d55f3cfc456d1b7bc7db3a4b70fbf602ddc8647d/packages/code-mode/src/continuation-capability.ts#L13-L29, types.ts#L201-L213; docs 18-code-mode.mdx:233-242)

Surprises:

- The docs list console.log, console.info, console.debug and console.error as supported in programs (18-code-mode.mdx:196), and the tool's own guidance never says logs are invisible, but console output goes to the server's stdout and never into the tool result. A model that debugs with console.log sees nothing.
- The docs say code mode "does not currently integrate with AI SDK tool approval flows" and nested approval tools are rejected, yet the package exports an interrupt-based approval API (experimental_continueCodeModeApproval, approval.mode 'interrupt').
- Input validation depends on the tool's schema object: a jsonSchema() without a validate function passed {id: "not-a-number"} straight to execute (P10d). With zod schemas it validates.
- Going over 32 concurrent tool calls fails the whole execution after the first 32 calls already ran, which can leave side effects behind.

### Vercel just-bash

- Source: https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash (npm: just-bash) at `source ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26; ran npm just-bash@3.6.1 (same version as packages/just-bash/package.json at that commit)`
- Language and engine: Bash (shell script); JS only when javascript is enabled (js-exec, QuickJS); Python off by default, Shell: a TypeScript AST interpreter running in the Node.js host realm, with no VM, worker, or process boundary. JS (js-exec): QuickJS compiled to WASM through the run package, with a 64 MiB guest memory cap. Python: CPython on WASM, disabled by default.
- How it was run: new Bash(options) from the package root import { Bash } from "just-bash" (the same import bash-tool uses), then await bash.exec(script); host functions registered via customCommands (shell) and javascript.invokeTool (JS).
- Defaults: time normal profile maxExecutionTimeMs 3,600,000 ms (60 min) (limits.ts#L201); hardened 30 s. Loops stop sooner on maxCommandCount and maxLoopIterations (100,000 each). js-exec deadline maxJsTimeoutMs 30 s (limits.ts#L205).; memory maxStringLength 64 MiB (limits.ts#L208); maxLiveBytes 512 MiB (limits.ts#L189); in-memory filesystem maxFileSystemBytes 1 GiB (limits.ts#L191); js-exec guest 64 MiB (run-runtime.ts#L74). Host heap is not capped by just-bash.; output maxOutputSize 256 MiB, aggregate stdout plus stderr (limits.ts#L213). Over the limit the result keeps partial stdout, exit 126, and an error line. No truncation marker.; tool_calls maxCommandCount 100,000 per exec, shared across nested exec, charged per pipeline command (execution-scope.ts#L95-L96, pipeline-execution.ts#L97). No separate host tool counter for shell commands. js-exec bridge cap maxJsBridgeRequests 1,000,000 (limits.ts#L206).
- Hardened config: new Bash({ executionLimitProfile: "hardened" }), the project's own preset (packages/just-bash/src/limits.ts:218-261, selected via BashOptions.executionLimitProfile at src/Bash.ts:155, documented in README.md:661-682): maxCommandCount 10,000 (:221), maxLoopIterations 10,000 (:222), maxJsTimeoutMs 10 s (:228), maxStringLength 10 MiB (:232), maxOutputSize 10 MiB (:236), maxLiveBytes 64 MiB (:250), maxFileSystemBytes 128 MiB (:252), maxExecutionTimeMs 30 s (:260). No network or fetch option, so network is off and curl/wget are not registered (src/Bash.ts:175-179, README.md:342). python off (default), default InMemoryFs, defenseInDepth on (default). No other public knob tightens these probes. The js-exec rows add javascript: { invokeTool } (src/Bash.ts:115-142). Its 64 MiB guest heap is a fixed constant (src/commands/js-exec/run-runtime.ts:74), not an option. Each cell uses the shell form, the language bash-tool exposes and the form of the default row. Each detail also gives the js-exec run of the literal SPEC JS code under the same profile (out/hardened-P<n>js.json).

From the source:

- **API shape.** Shell host functions are plain commands. defineCommand(name, execute(args, ctx)) returns {name, trusted, execute} (no schema, no codegen; the host parses args itself), and the constructor registers each customCommands entry. JS side: a Proxy named tools turns tools.a.b(args) into invokeTool("a.b", JSON), also without codegen. just-bash-executor createExecutor generates commands and invokeTool from inline or SDK tools (read, not run). (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/custom-commands.ts#L100-L106; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L549-L557; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/commands/js-exec/run-runtime.ts#L590-L603; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash-executor/src/create-executor.ts#L76-L118)
- **Discovery.** Everything is eager. Shell custom commands are registered at construction, so every name is known up front and nothing is searched or read on demand. The js-exec tools Proxy accepts any property path, so the guest cannot list tools at all. just-bash-executor lists every tool with sdk.tools.list() and exposes all of them as commands. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L549-L557; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/commands/js-exec/run-runtime.ts#L590-L603; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash-executor/src/create-executor.ts#L127-L131)
- **Bridge.** A shell host command is a direct async call in the same Node realm (custom-commands.ts#L199) and, when trusted, runs under runTrustedAsync (builtin-dispatch.ts#L1020-L1022). For JS, the guest calls host.invokeTool synchronously (run-runtime.ts#L601) and the host binding awaits the callback (run-runtime.ts#L1013-L1020). Guest code runs in QuickJS from the run package (run-runtime.ts#L3-L11). The child_process shim in js-exec calls back into the sandboxed shell (run-runtime.ts#L543-L558, #L974-L1005), not into Node. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/custom-commands.ts#L199; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/interpreter/builtin-dispatch.ts#L1020-L1022; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/commands/js-exec/run-runtime.ts#L601; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/commands/js-exec/run-runtime.ts#L1013-L1020)
- **Isolation boundary.** Shell: no separate engine. Bash.exec (Bash.ts#L631) runs a TypeScript AST interpreter in the host realm, with no VM, worker, or process boundary. JS: QuickJS-in-WASM via run. The README Security Model says "All execution happens without VM isolation" (README.md#L697), and the code matches that. THREAT_MODEL.md#L5 calls it "a secure, sandboxed bash environment", which the code does not back up as an OS-level boundary. Defense-in-depth is on by default (Bash.ts#L412) and patches globals on each execution (defense-in-depth-box.ts#L597). THREAT_MODEL.md#L164 says child_process is "Not imported anywhere", but cli/exec.ts#L25 imports spawnSync from node:child_process. That file is the host CLI, not the sandbox path, so the sandbox claim holds. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L631; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/README.md#L697; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/THREAT_MODEL.md#L5; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/THREAT_MODEL.md#L164; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L412; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/security/defense-in-depth-box.ts#L597; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/cli/exec.ts#L25)
- **Output channel.** The result is {stdout, stderr, exitCode, env}. Shell scripts have no return value, so the only output channel is stdout and stderr. Bash.ts, execution-scope.ts, control-flow.ts, and pipeline-execution.ts contain no truncation marker. Output above maxOutputSize throws ExecutionLimitError, and the caller gets the partial stdout with exit 126 (observed: 240 MB kept, no END line, P2b). (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/execution-scope.ts#L250-L253; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L963-L969; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L1023-L1029)
- **Limits.** Normal profile (the default): maxCallDepth 100 (limits.ts#L166), maxCommandCount 100,000 (#L167), maxLoopIterations 100,000 (#L168), maxLiveBytes 512 MiB (#L189), maxExecutionTimeMs 3,600,000 (#L201), maxJsTimeoutMs 30 s (#L205), maxJsBridgeRequests 1e6 (#L206), maxStringLength 64 MiB (#L208), maxOutputSize 256 MiB (#L213). Hardened profile at limits.ts#L218-L262 (commands 10,000 at #L221, time 30 s at #L260). The profile defaults to normal in resolveLimits (limits.ts#L266-L268), and the Bash constructor passes executionLimitProfile through (Bash.ts#L354-L371). (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/limits.ts#L163-L215; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/limits.ts#L218-L262; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/limits.ts#L266-L275; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L354-L371)
- **State.** Fresh per exec. Each exec copies the instance env into a new Map (Bash.ts#L745-L747) and nothing writes that copy back; the instance state is assigned only in the constructor (Bash.ts#L418). The InMemoryFs is created once per instance (Bash.ts#L374) and shared across calls, as README.md#L25 says. Observed: variables and cwd reset, files persist (P8). No snapshot or serialization API was found in Bash.ts or sandbox/. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L745-L747; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L418; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L374; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/README.md#L25)
- **Errors.** ExecutionLimitError becomes exit 126 with sanitized stderr and the partial stdout (Bash.ts#L963-L969, errors.ts#L201-L205). Other command errors become stderr text prefixed with the command name, and the script continues (builtin-dispatch.ts#L1030-L1041; observed "boom: probe-boom", P10b). Parse errors exit 2 with "Parse error at 1:1" (observed, P10). A host command throw does not reject exec. A JS uncaught throw gives "at <eval> (-c:L:C): message" and exit 1 (observed, P10js). (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L963-L969; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/interpreter/errors.ts#L201-L205; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/interpreter/builtin-dispatch.ts#L1030-L1041)
- **Anything else.** (a) '&' is parsed (parser.ts#L531-L535), but the interpreter never reads the background flag, and wait is a stub (builtin-dispatch.ts#L643-L645), so concurrent-looking code runs serially (P9). (b) The JS invokeTool bridge is synchronous, so Promise.all over tools is serial (run-runtime.ts#L601, P9js). (c) Network is off by default and allow-listed by URL prefix (network/types.ts#L56-L82). Header transforms inject credentials at the fetch boundary so the secret never enters the sandbox (README.md#L392). (d) Python is off by default (Bash.ts#L521-L525). (e) The executor onToolApproval gate applies only to SDK tools; inline tools skip it (create-executor.ts#L189-L190). (f) The package requires Node >=20.19 (packages/just-bash/package.json#L15). (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/parser/parser.ts#L531-L535; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/interpreter/builtin-dispatch.ts#L643-L645; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/network/types.ts#L56-L82; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash-executor/src/create-executor.ts#L189-L190; https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/package.json#L15)

Surprises:

- The default time limit is 60 minutes (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/limits.ts#L201), not 30 seconds. The README Execution Protection example uses 30 s under the hardened profile, and a reader would expect a time limit by default. In practice an infinite shell loop stops in about 0.4 s on the 100,000 command cap (P6). With both counters raised, the loop ran past 120 s (P6b).
- '&' is parsed but never runs concurrently, and wait is a no-op (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/parser/parser.ts#L531-L535, https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/interpreter/builtin-dispatch.ts#L643-L645). Five 200 ms lookups took about 1 s with max in flight 1 (P9). Nothing in the output says the background jobs ran in the foreground.
- The JS tool bridge is synchronous (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/commands/js-exec/run-runtime.ts#L601), so Promise.all over tools.lookup runs one call at a time (P9js, max in flight 1). In-guest Date.now() printed 1 ms while the host measured 1176 ms, so guest timers mislead about elapsed time.
- A failing host command does not fail the script. 'boom; echo after-boom' resolves with exit 0 and the error only on stderr. 'boom' alone exits 1 (P10b).
- The README calls defense-in-depth 'Secondary', but it is on by default (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L412) and costs most of the per-exec time: 0.160 ms per exec with it on and 0.033 ms off, 5 alternating rounds (out/ablate-defense.json). applyPatches, applyPatch, restorePatches, and protectReversibleIntrinsics take about 21% of self time in the CPU profile (out/profile/top-self-time.txt).
- The output limit does not truncate. 240 MB of stdout came back with exit 126 and the final END line missing, and the only signal is the stderr error (P2b, https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/Bash.ts#L963-L969).
- https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/THREAT_MODEL.md#L5 says 'secure, sandboxed bash environment', while https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/README.md#L697 says 'All execution happens without VM isolation'. The code matches the README. The threat model also says child_process is 'Not imported anywhere' (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/THREAT_MODEL.md#L164), but https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/cli/exec.ts#L25 imports it in the host CLI.
- The just-bash-executor README calls onToolApproval a 'pre-invocation gate' (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash-executor/README.md#L224), but inline tools bypass it (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash-executor/src/create-executor.ts#L189-L190). Source only; the executor was not run.
- python3 with python disabled on Node says 'command not available in browser environments' and tells the user to use the Node.js bundle (https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/interpreter/builtin-dispatch.ts#L818-L824, https://github.com/vercel-labs/just-bash/blob/ec5ab766551d479f2782b078b373d49ddc78bd26/packages/just-bash/src/commands/browser-excluded.ts#L17). That message is wrong for a Node host.
- Inside js-exec, process.env is the virtual environment (HOME, PATH, ...), and require('child_process').execSync runs in the sandboxed shell (P12js). Both are the designed behavior, but a reader may expect them to reach Node.

### Vercel Run (npm `run`, vercel-labs/run)

- Source: https://github.com/vercel-labs/run (npm: run 2.1.13) at `6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce (tag run@2.1.13); embedded quickjs-wasi 3.6.3 and devalue 5.8.2 per THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`
- Language and engine: JS (type-stripped TS), QuickJS compiled to WASM (quickjs-wasi 3.6.3, embedded in the package), a fresh QuickJS context per run inside a pooled Node worker thread
- How it was run: run({ source, hostFunctions: { host: { lookup } } }) for the default configuration and createRunner({ limits }).run(...) for the hardened one, both from the package entry point; guest code calls host.lookup({id}).
- Defaults: time timeoutMs 30,000 wall for the whole invocation; cpuTimeoutMs 10,000 of guest execution, enforced by a QuickJS interrupt handler (packages/run/src/types.ts:64-88, runtime/worker.ts:207-235). The CPU limit fires first for a busy loop.; memory memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB QuickJS heap, maxStackSizeBytes 2 MiB (types.ts:89-92, runtime/worker.ts:514-534); output maxResultBytes 1 MiB for the return value (fails, not truncates); maxConsoleOutputBytes 64 KiB, but console output goes to host stdout and never to the caller (types.ts:93-96, runtime/worker.ts:662-690); tool_calls maxBridgeRequests 256 total and maxInFlightBridgeRequests 32 concurrent; exceeding either fails the run with RUN_BRIDGE_LIMIT (types.ts:103-106, runtime/manager.ts:995-1003)
- Hardened config: createRunner({ limits: { timeoutMs: 15000, cpuTimeoutMs: 5000, memoryLimitBytes: 32 MiB, maxStackSizeBytes: 1 MiB, maxSourceBytes: 128 KiB, maxResultBytes: 512 KiB, maxConsoleOutputBytes: 32 KiB, maxHostFunctionArgumentsBytes: 256 KiB, maxHostFunctionOutputBytes: 1 MiB, maxBridgeRequests: 100, maxInFlightBridgeRequests: 8, maxContinuationBytes: 8 MiB } }), the createRunner example in content/docs/advanced/limits.mdx (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/content/docs/advanced/limits.mdx). Run has no network or filesystem option because the sandbox has neither.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Host functions are passed as named groups; each group becomes a guest global object whose members are callable (`host.lookup(...)`). There are no top-level functions and no generated declarations: Run is an execution layer and leaves prompts and types to the caller. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/packages/run/src/types.ts#L37-L46; content/docs/foundations/sandbox.mdx (Globals))
- **Discovery.** None in Run itself. No type generation or search code exists in packages/run/src (grep for declaration or JSON Schema generation finds nothing). The AI SDK code mode layer adds it. (packages/run/src (grep))
- **Bridge.** Each host call goes from the QuickJS context to __runInvokeHostFunction in the worker, which posts a request to the manager on the main thread and returns a guest promise; the manager runs the host function and posts the result back. Async calls overlap, which is why P9 is parallel. An optional synchronous bridge (syncHostFunctions) uses a separate shared-memory protocol. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/packages/run/src/runtime/worker.ts#L733-L755 and runtime/manager.ts#L949, #L995-L1003)
- **Isolation boundary.** QuickJS WASM in a Node worker thread, fresh context per run, worker reused. Guest hardening deletes Node-style globals and replaces Function and eval with throwing stubs. The docs say plainly that this is not a container, VM or separate OS process. The worker is created with a copy of process.env, but nothing in the guest can read it (P5). (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/packages/run/src/runtime/guest-sources.ts#L200-L216, runtime/manager.ts#L1819-L1826, content/docs/foundations/sandbox.mdx (Isolation))
- **Output channel.** Only the return value comes back (RunCompletedResult has status and value). console.* writes with writeSync to the host process's fd 1 or 2 under a 64 KiB budget; a line larger than the remaining budget is silently dropped and zeroes the budget. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/packages/run/src/types.ts#L163-L167 and runtime/worker.ts#L662-L690)
- **Limits.** Twelve per-run limits with defaults, overridable per runner or per run. CPU and wall time are separate; the interrupt handler checks both. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/packages/run/src/types.ts#L64-L109, content/docs/advanced/limits.mdx)
- **State.** Fresh QuickJS context per run. Continuations: a host function can interrupt (for approval or auth), and the run resumes later by replaying the source with a ledger of recorded host results, so completed host calls are not repeated. Date and Math.random are deterministic in the guest to make replay consistent. (content/docs/foundations/interruptions.mdx; packages/run/src/types.ts#L227-L249)
- **Errors.** Guest errors keep name, message and a guest stack with run.js line:column. Host function errors are replaced by "Host function failed." unless the host throws a RunError, so host secrets in error text stay on the host side. (https://github.com/vercel-labs/run/blob/6c146567b19d96b4164550314875ed55eb2366ce/packages/run/src/errors.ts#L215-L240; content/docs/foundations/host-functions.mdx (Failures))
- **Anything else.** Process-wide worker cap (setMaxWorkers, default from available memory up to 32). Signed or stored continuation codecs. A fail-closed banned-pattern security scan runs in CI. Labs experiment status, Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-11-12. (packages/run/src/runtime/max-workers.ts#L3, README.md)

Surprises:

- console.log output never reaches the caller. It goes to the host server's stdout, so in an agent it lands in server logs and the model never sees it.
- A console.log line bigger than the remaining 64 KiB budget is dropped whole, with no marker, and later lines in the same run are dropped too.
- Going over maxInFlightBridgeRequests fails the whole run instead of queueing; in P9b, 32 host calls had already executed when the run failed.
- Guest Date.now() is deterministic for replay, but it still advanced across host awaits in P9 (259 ms), so in-guest timing is usable.

### VoidMCP (Go MCP proxy with QuickJS-in-WASM code mode)

- Source: https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp at `22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c (main). Ran the v0.0.10 darwin-arm64 release binary (tarball sha256 f8b54b632400cdea53926e9eef6c55be7b6df8680034d13312376569cdd64b75); v0.0.10 tags 3a4d33b, and `git diff 3a4d33b 22e37f1` is empty (the two later commits are a fix and its revert). Embedded deps: github.com/fastschema/qjs v0.0.6 (commit 461716f), tetratelabs/wazero v1.9.0 (go.mod).`
- Language and engine: JS, quickjs-ng compiled to WASM (fastschema/qjs v0.0.6) on the wazero pure-Go WASM runtime, WASI preview 1, with an empty host temp directory mounted read-write as '/'. A fresh runtime per execution from a pre-warmed pool.
- How it was run: voidmcp serve --stdio --db <probe-local db> on macOS arm64 (host, not Docker), with HOME pointed at the probe folder and PROBE_SECRET=s3cr3t in its env; the lookup server (research/probes/voidmcp/lookup-server.mjs) registered with `voidmcp add --db ... lookup "node lookup-server.mjs calls.log"`; probes sent as MCP tools/call execute_code by run-probes.mjs, no LLM.
- Defaults: time Documented --timeout 30s (cmd/voidmcp/main.go:63) is passed to qjs.Option.MaxExecutionTime (internal/executor/pool.go:72), which fastschema/qjs v0.0.6 forwards to New_QJS but never uses (qjswasm/qjs.c:15-41 has no interrupt handler). No context deadline is set either. Effective: none (P6).; memory Documented --memory 16 MB (main.go:62) becomes JS_SetMemoryLimit (qjs.c:33-34). Observed: only single allocations above the limit fail; total heap grows to the 4 GB wasm32 ceiling (P7). Cause guessed, not verified: quickjs-ng's malloc accounting does not track usable size in this WASI build.; output No cap. 200,000 logged chars came back whole (P2). Code input is capped at 256 KB (executor.go:22) and HTTP bodies at 512 KB (server.go:148).; tool_calls 50 per execution (--max-tool-calls, main.go:64), enforced in the bridge (executor.go:177-182); verified at 10 in the hardened run.
- Hardened config: voidmcp serve --stdio --timeout 5s --memory 8 --max-tool-calls 10 --pool-size 1. All four are documented serve flags (README.md Configuration section lines 160-171; cmd/voidmcp/main.go:59-64). --timeout 5s and --memory 8 are stricter than the 30 s / 16 MB defaults; --max-tool-calls 10 is stricter than 50.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools are reached as tools.<server>.<tool>(args) through two nested ES Proxies that call one randomized async Go bridge with (server, tool, JSON args). TypeScript declarations (`declare namespace tools.<server> { function x(args: {...}): Promise<T> }`) are generated from each tool's JSON Schema, and return types are inferred from the first real response and stored in SQLite. (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/executor.go#L344-L381 ; https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/types.go#L34 ; README.md#L131-L141)
- **Discovery.** On demand. The execute_code description lists each server with at most 5 tool names; full signatures come from the search tool, which does case-insensitive substring scoring over server, name and description and returns at most 50 matches ("*" browses all). Scales past 100 tools without putting every schema in the prompt. (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/types.go#L95-L120 ; https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/server/server.go#L509 ; https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/registry/registry.go#L258-L300)
- **Bridge.** qctx.SetAsyncFunc registers an async host function, but its callback calls the upstream MCP tool synchronously (entry.call) before resolving the promise, so Promise.all over tool calls runs serially (P9) even though the tool description tells the model to fan out with Promise.allSettled. (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/executor.go#L176-L248 (synchronous call at L213); prompt at https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/server/server.go#L262)
- **Isolation boundary.** Engine is quickjs-ng in WASM on wazero with WASI, which is a real boundary for network, env and host files (P3-P5, P12). The preamble deletes the std/os/bjson globals, but qjs registers them as 'qjs:std'/'qjs:os' modules that dynamic import() still loads. The WASI root is an empty host temp dir mounted read-write, shared by every execution in a serve process and left behind when the process is killed, so the README's "no access to the host filesystem" is not quite true: guest code can write host files there without a quota (writes measured, quota absence inferred from source). (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/executor.go#L28-L43 ; https://github.com/fastschema/qjs/blob/461716f4f380f81ffd09378751f1812919cddbca/qjswasm/qjs.c#L7-L9 ; https://github.com/fastschema/qjs/blob/461716f4f380f81ffd09378751f1812919cddbca/qjswasm/helpers.c#L163-L170 ; https://github.com/fastschema/qjs/blob/461716f4f380f81ffd09378751f1812919cddbca/runtime.go#L135-L148 ; https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/pool.go#L37-L41 ; out/P4.txt, out/P8.txt, out/sandbox-dir-leftovers.txt)
- **Output channel.** One JSON text with result, error, logs[], tool_calls[] (server, tool, ms, status) and duration_ms. Error results set isError. No truncation anywhere. (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/server/server.go#L593-L615)
- **Limits.** Time and memory flags exist and are wired to qjs options, but the time option is a no-op in the pinned qjs and the memory limit only bounds single allocations in practice. Tool-call cap works. Concurrency is bounded by --pool-size (4). (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/cmd/voidmcp/main.go#L59-L64 ; https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/pool.go#L66-L80 ; https://github.com/fastschema/qjs/blob/461716f4f380f81ffd09378751f1812919cddbca/qjswasm/qjs.c#L15-L41 ; out/P6.txt, out/P7.txt)
- **State.** Fresh runtime per execution (Acquire closes the pre-warmed placeholder and builds a new runtime bound to the request ctx; Release discards it). JS globals do not persist; files in the shared WASI root do. (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/pool.go#L85-L130 ; out/P8.txt)
- **Errors.** The wrapper catches and stores only e.name + ': ' + e.message, dropping the stack and line. A tool-call-limit rejection surfaced as "[uninitialized]". (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/executor/executor.go#L262-L270 ; out/P10.txt ; out/hardened-P9cap.txt)
- **Credentials.** Kept on the host side of the bridge: auth tokens are stored AES-256-GCM encrypted in SQLite, attached by the Go transport, and can only be registered from the CLI, not by the model's add_mcp tool. stdio upstreams get only PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG. The sandbox never sees tokens or env. (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/store/store.go#L139 ; https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/transport/stdio.go#L52-L59 ; README.md Security section)
- **Concurrency of the stdio server.** ServeStdio reads a line and calls Handle inline, so one long execute_code blocks every other request on that connection, including ping (P6). (https://github.com/voidmind-io/voidmcp/blob/22e37f12b5e720f253faab854256e681292d635c/internal/server/server.go#L176-L200)

Surprises:

- --timeout is documented (README line 168, default 30s) but never enforced: fastschema/qjs v0.0.6 accepts max_execution_time and ignores it, and voidmcp sets no context deadline. while(true){} ran past 120 s in default and hardened (--timeout 5s) runs and wedged the stdio server.
- --memory is documented as a per-execution limit (README line 167, default 16 MB) but in practice only refuses single allocations above it; a loop of 1 MB strings reached 4.2 GB process RSS (harness kill) with both 16 MB and 8 MB settings.
- The README says the sandbox has no access to the host filesystem (lines 129, 176). Reads of host files are blocked, but guest code can write files into a real host temp directory ($TMPDIR/voidmcp-sandbox-*), those files persist across executions in the same process, and the directory is left behind when the process dies.
- The preamble deletes globalThis.std/os, but `await import('qjs:std')` and `import('qjs:os')` still load. The WASI build makes their dangerous functions (exec, popen, urlGet) unavailable, so this did not lead to an escape.
- The tool description recommends Promise.allSettled fan-out for parallel calls (server.go:262), but the bridge is synchronous and five calls took 1,018 ms.
- The randomized bridge name is meant to stop user code calling the bridge directly (executor.go:170-172), but it is an enumerable global; P12 found and called it. It only reaches registered tools, so no new capability.
- Thrown errors lose stack and line number; only `Error: probe-boom` reaches the model.
- `voidmcp add <name> <target> --db X` ignores the trailing flag (Go flag parsing stops at the first positional) and silently wrote to ~/.voidmcp instead. The README's `voidmcp add github https://mcp.github.com --token ghp_...` has the same shape, so the token would be silently dropped (inferred, not run with a token). out/flag-order.txt.
- With --max-tool-calls the limit holds, but the caller sees error "[uninitialized]" instead of the limit message, and an in-script try/catch did not catch it.
- initialize reports serverInfo version "dev" while `voidmcp version` prints 0.0.10.

From the source:

- **Availability.** The OSS agentgateway repo has no code mode: no run_code, no QuickJS or other JS engine dependency, no entMcp/toolMode config (the only grep hits are the substring "codemode" inside encode_model_path_segment). Code mode is an enterprise feature configured as entMcp.toolMode: Code | CodeSearch on an EnterpriseAgentgatewayBackend. The blog is tagged Agentgateway Enterprise. (research/probes/agentgateway-codemode/out/oss-search.txt; https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/kubernetes/latest/documentation/mcp/tool-mode/; https://www.solo.io/blog/agentgateway-code-mode-for-openapi-to-mcp)
- **Engine (isolation boundary).** QuickJS via rquickjs, compiled into the gateway binary, module mcp::ent_code_mode. Solo's own docs say: "Code mode currently runs in an in-process JavaScript runtime. It is not yet a fully sandboxed runtime that gives each session its own credentials, filesystem, and network." The blog instead says "Host, filesystem, and network access are restricted." (research/probes/agentgateway-codemode/out/engine-strings.txt; https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/kubernetes/latest/documentation/mcp/tool-mode/)
- **API shape.** One MCP tool run_code {code}. Its description holds a typed JS API rendered from the descriptions, input and output schemas of the tools the caller is authorized to use (symbols render_run_code_description, render_tool_api_definition, schema_to_js_hint). Each tool is an async function; top-level await is available; the final expression is the return value and top-level return is not allowed. (research/probes/agentgateway-codemode/out/engine-strings.txt; https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/kubernetes/latest/documentation/mcp/tool-mode/)
- **Discovery.** Code mode puts every authorized tool's signature in the run_code description upfront. A separate CodeSearch mode pairs get_tool search with run_code (symbol list_tools_with_search), which is the variant that scales past 100 tools. (https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/kubernetes/latest/documentation/mcp/tool-mode/; research/probes/agentgateway-codemode/out/engine-strings.txt)
- **Bridge and authorization.** Host functions are installed into the QuickJS context (install_host_functions, invoke_bound_tool, call_bound_tool_value). Docs and blog: denied tools are omitted from the generated API and also rejected at runtime by the same authorization check as direct tools/call. Upstream API credentials stay in the gateway (blog: the model never sees API keys or OAuth tokens). (research/probes/agentgateway-codemode/out/engine-strings.txt; https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/kubernetes/latest/documentation/mcp/tool-mode/; https://www.solo.io/blog/agentgateway-code-mode-for-openapi-to-mcp)
- **Limits.** Memory 4 MiB and 20 tool calls and 256 KiB stack fixed; wall-clock and CPU time configurable. Exceeding a limit returns an error result, not a failed session (docs). Wall-clock default is 60 s in the docs and 5 s in Solo's workshop lab. (https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/kubernetes/latest/documentation/mcp/tool-mode/; https://github.com/solo-io/fe-enterprise-agentgateway-workshop/blob/main/labs/mcp/mcp-tool-mode-code.md)
- **Licensing.** The image is public, but the proxy refuses to start without a valid key and there is no grace period for an installation that never held one. (research/probes/agentgateway-codemode/out/no-license-start.txt; https://docs.solo.io/agentgateway/standalone/latest/documentation/setup/install/docker/)

Surprises:

- The parent brief and missed-implementations.md point at the OSS repo, but code mode is enterprise-only and absent from github.com/agentgateway/agentgateway.
- Solo's docs say the runtime is in-process and "not yet a fully sandboxed runtime", while the blog says host, filesystem and network access are restricted.
- Two different wall-clock defaults are published: 60 s (docs) and 5 s (Solo workshop lab).
- The engine is QuickJS (rquickjs), the same family as the most common engine in this survey, which the blog does not name.

From the source:

- **API shape.** One generated TypeScript file per MCP tool under ./servers/<server>/, each wrapping callMCPTool. (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)
- **Discovery.** Progressive disclosure by filesystem browsing, or a search_tools tool with a detail level (name only; name and description; full definition with schemas). Headline: "This reduces the token usage from 150,000 tokens to 2,000 tokens—a time and cost saving of 98.7%." (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)
- **Bridge.** callMCPTool from inside the execution environment to the MCP client; transport not specified. (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)
- **Notable (privacy).** "The MCP client intercepts the data and tokenizes PII before it reaches the model"; values are untokenized when passed to another MCP call, so real values flow between tools "but never through the model". (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)
- **Notable (cost).** "Running agent-generated code requires a secure execution environment with appropriate sandboxing, resource limits, and monitoring. These infrastructure requirements add operational overhead and security considerations that direct tool calls avoid." (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)

Surprises:

- The pattern needs a writable filesystem (tool discovery by directory listing, state in ./workspace, skills in ./skills), which is in tension with the no-filesystem sandboxes (OpenAI PTC, Cloudflare isolates) usually cited as the safe reference.
- Anthropic's own hosted PTC does not implement this pattern: it is Python, presents opted-in tools upfront rather than as files, and forbids MCP connector tools from programmatic calls.

From the source:

- **API shape.** Client tools opt in with allowed_callers; the API turns them into async Python functions taking one dict and returning a string. SDK types accept direct, code_execution_20250825, code_execution_20260120, code_execution_20260521. (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/types/tool_param.py#L45-L47 ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#the-allowed_callers-field)
- **Discovery.** All opted-in tools are presented upfront; deferred loading via defer_loading + Tool Search Tool is a separate feature (tool_param.py defer_loading field). (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/types/tool_param.py#L52-L56)
- **Bridge.** Pause/resume over the Messages API. Code pauses at each call; the response has stop_reason tool_use and a tool_use block whose caller is {type: code_execution_20260120, tool_id: <server_tool_use id>}. The client replies with a user message of only tool_result blocks and must pass the container ID, or the API rejects it. (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#step-3-provide-tool-result ; https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/types/tool_use_block.py#L19)
- **Bridge (SDK).** The SDK thread state copies the container ID from each reply into the next request automatically: "container-bound server tools reject a follow-up request that omits the container the previous turn ran in." A tool that raises becomes a tool_result with is_error: True. (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/lib/threads/_thread_state.py#L332-L341 ; https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/lib/tools/_beta_runner.py#L853-L874)
- **Bridge (SDK, MCP).** mcp_tool() wraps an MCP ClientSession tool as a client-side runnable tool and accepts allowed_callers. Docs forbid programmatic calls to MCP connector tools, but MCP tools run client-side through this helper can be offered to code (inference from source; not run). (https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/8baaef1c4d23b2e4861d05da0dca65252e879eb8/src/anthropic/lib/tools/mcp.py#L316-L351 ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#tool-restrictions)
- **Isolation boundary.** Container, not a language sandbox. Docs claim full host isolation, workspace-only file access, no internet. (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool#networking-and-security)
- **Output channel.** Only the final code output enters context: "Tool results from programmatic calls are not added to Claude's context: Only the final code output is." Programmatic tool results also do not count toward token usage. (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#token-efficiency)
- **Errors.** Tool errors are returned to the running code as tool_result text; code-level exceptions go to stderr. (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#tool-execution-errors)
- **Notable.** Not ZDR or HIPAA eligible; container data retained up to 30 days. Tool results must be strings or text blocks (images rejected). strict: true tools, tool_choice forcing, and MCP connector tools are excluded. Not available in Managed Agents. Haiku 4.5 lacks PTC. (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#data-handling ; https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling#constraints-and-limitations)
- **Numbers.** Docs report: agentic search benchmarks (BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA) +11% average with 24% fewer input tokens; a 75-tool benchmark -38% billed input tokens with no accuracy change; tau2-bench unchanged score at about 8% more cost. (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/programmatic-tool-calling (intro and #token-efficiency))

Surprises:

- The survey's opt-in value allowed_callers: ["code_execution_20250825"] is outdated. PTC now requires code_execution_20260120 or later, yet the SDK Literal still lists code_execution_20250825 as a caller value (tool_param.py:45-47).
- allowed_callers is guidance, not enforcement: "it is not a hard API-level block on direct calls ... Do not rely on allowed_callers as a security boundary."
- The documented TimeoutError result has return_code 0 with the error only in stderr.
- Network inside the container is now documented as completely disabled (survey listed it as unverified).
- Not ZDR eligible and data is retained up to 30 days, which matters for an investigations customer. OpenAI PTC supports ZDR.
- On tau2-bench, PTC cost about 8% more with no score change; Anthropic says sequential single-call workflows do not benefit.
