From the source:

- **Not implemented.** The e2b adapter is a TODO stub: execute() throws 'E2B runtime not yet implemented'. Its constructor also throws without e2b.apiKey, and the MCP server never passes one, so via MCP it fails before that. Credentials were not needed to establish this. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/runtime/e2b-runtime.ts#L17-L35; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/package.json)
- **Bridge.** Not a live bridge but a two-pass replay. Pass 1 runs the whole program with every mcp.* call returning a placeholder string and logging '__MCP_CALL__' JSON; the server then runs all logged calls with Promise.all, bakes the results into the source as literals, and runs the whole program a second time. Arguments that depend on an earlier tool result are computed from the placeholder, and every side effect happens twice (P13). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L903-L918; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L946-L1021; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L1111-L1134; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P13_twoPass.txt)
- **API shape.** A generated `const mcp = { <server>: { <tool>: async (args) => __mcpCall('<server>.<tool>', args) } }` proxy is prepended to the program. Results come back wrapped as {content, text, parsed, isError, helpers}, so `r.value` is undefined and the value sits at r.parsed.value (P1). (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L403-L466; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L974-L1007)
- **Discovery.** On-demand mode (the default) tells the model to read the resource mcp://types/declarations, but reading it always fails: loadTypeScriptDeclarations calls require() inside an ES module. The model gets no tool names. auto-include mode (CODEMODE_TYPE_EXPOSURE) lists every tool in the description instead. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L35; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L327-L340; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L513-L529; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/P15_discovery.txt)
- **Setup.** Tool access is off unless CODEMODE_ENABLE_MCP_INTEGRATION=true, which the README does not mention. execute_code defaults to runtime 'quickjs', although the README recommends Bun. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L1359; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879)
- **Credentials.** Tools run in the MCP server process, but on startup it prints the first 20 characters of every downstream MCP server env value with console.log, which goes to stdout, the MCP protocol channel. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L281; research/probes/codemode-unified-bun/out/envlog-stdout.txt)
- **Limits.** execute_code takes a timeout (default 30 s) and nothing else; getRuntime builds every runtime with only {type}, so the memoryLimit, Deno permission and E2B apiKey fields in RuntimeConfig cannot be set through the MCP server. No output cap, no tool-call cap. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L502-L508; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L879; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/mcp-server.ts#L945)
- **HTTP mode.** The HTTP backend's /execute ignores the `runtime` field shown in the README curl example; its sandbox manager only wraps QuickJS. (https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/server.ts#L109-L128; https://github.com/danieliser/codemode-unified/blob/6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93/src/sandbox/index.ts#L9-L19)
- **Maintenance.** 27 commits, last on 2025-10-01, single author; package.json says MIT but the repo has no LICENSE file; not published to npm. The README badge says 'Production Ready'. (git log at 6e4daa3e7ae17bf0764adeb5c72ba922c58b4d93; npm view @danieliser/codemode-unified -> 404)

Surprises:

- README lists e2b among the supported runtimes with startup figures, but the adapter is a stub.

- **API shape.** Helper functions pre-initialized in the notebook: run_composio_tool (any Composio tool by slug), invoke_llm, upload_local_file, proxy_execute, web_search, smart_file_extract. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#built-in-helpers ; research/probes/composio-remote-sandbox/out/docs-quotes.md)
- **Discovery.** Meta tools: SEARCH_TOOLS finds tools, MULTI_EXECUTE runs simple calls, COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH runs code for bulk or multi-step work. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#where-it-fits ; research/probes/composio-remote-sandbox/out/docs-quotes.md)
- **Bridge.** run_composio_tool calls back to Composio's Tool Router, which holds the user's connected-account auth. In the local variant every call routes back through the Tool Router. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/local#the-helper-contract ; research/probes/composio-remote-sandbox/out/docs-quotes.md)
- **Isolation boundary.** Not stated for the remote sandbox. For the local sandbox the docs say "The sandbox is your security boundary" and that the project COMPOSIO_API_KEY is injected into the sandbox env, readable by any code and acting across every connection on the project. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/local#security-the-sandbox-is-your-boundary ; research/probes/composio-remote-sandbox/out/docs-quotes.md)
- **Output channel.** Not documented beyond notebook execution results and files on the /mnt/files mount. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#files-and-mounts)
- **Limits.** Compute tiers only (1 vCPU / 1 GB default). No time or output limits documented. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#compute-tier)
- **State.** Persistent Jupyter notebook per session; /mnt/files survives sandbox restarts. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#persistent-state)
- **Errors.** The sandbox "corrects common mistakes in the code your agent generates", for example mapping result["apiKey"] to api_key instead of failing. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#error-correction ; research/probes/composio-remote-sandbox/out/docs-quotes.md)
- **Anything else.** Packages not preinstalled are installed automatically on use. invoke_llm inside the sandbox is the only Composio-side LLM usage. Sandboxes are not billed today. (https://docs.composio.dev/docs/sandbox/remote#libraries ; research/probes/composio-remote-sandbox/out/docs-quotes.md)

Surprises:

- The sandbox silently rewrites failing code ("resolves the mismatch instead of failing"), so the model can get results from code that would have errored.
- The local sandbox puts the project-wide COMPOSIO_API_KEY inside the sandbox environment, where any model-written code can read it.
- Missing packages are installed automatically, which implies outbound package-index access from the sandbox (inferred, not tested).

### Cursor agent (Instant Grep, formerly semantic search; terminal sandbox)

- Source: https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/search ; https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes ; https://cursor.com/blog/semsearch ; https://cursor.com/blog/fast-regex-search ; https://cursor.com/blog/agent-sandboxing at `docs fetched 2026-11-22; blog posts dated 2025-11-06 (semsearch), 2026-02-18 (agent-sandboxing), 2026-03-23 (fast-regex-search)`
- Language and engine: Tool calls and shell commands (no documented code mode), Shell on the user's machine; optional sandbox: Seatbelt via sandbox-exec (macOS), Landlock + seccomp (Linux). Search: Instant Grep, a local index.
- How it was run: Not run: Cursor is not installed and scriptable here. All entries from docs and Cursor blog posts.
- Defaults: time not documented; memory not documented; output not documented; tool_calls not documented

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |

| P3 Network | blocked | Sandboxed commands: "Network: Blocked by default, then opened by your network mode and sandbox.json." The default network mode is "sandbox.json + Defaults" ("Cursor's built-in defaults for common package managers and language tools"). Whether example.com is in that default list was not checked. | https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes#network-access |

Workspace mode restricts sandboxed commands to the workspace, a read allowlist and system paths. | https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes#read-access |
| P5 Env secret | blocked-needs-credentials | Docs list variables Cursor injects (CURSOR_SANDBOX, CURSOR_ORIG_UID, ...) but do not say whether host secrets are stripped. | https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes#environment-variables |

From the source:

- **Discovery / search.** Current docs: "Cursor ships with Instant Grep, a custom search engine that outperforms ripgrep on large codebases"; "Instant Grep builds and queries its index on your machine. Cursor does not upload file paths or code to build a search index, and it does not store embeddings of your codebase for search." (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/search)
- **Semantic search retired.** Forum posts from accounts that speak for Cursor (staff status not verified) say semantic indexing was turned down in 2026: "Semantic/embeddings indexing is being turned down in favor of grep-based retrieval." and "Search runs against the files on your machine, so Cursor no longer builds a semantic index of the repo." (v3.12 onwards). Read only as search excerpts. (https://forum.cursor.com/t/what-do-you-think-about-cursor-removing-the-codebase-indexing-settings/165899 ; https://forum.cursor.com/t/codebase-indexing-not-working-in-v-3-12-onwards/167527)
- **Earlier evidence.** The Nov 6, 2025 post measured +12.5% average accuracy (6.5% to 23.5%) with semantic search added to grep and concluded "Semantic search is currently necessary to achieve the best results, especially in large codebases." (https://cursor.com/blog/semsearch)
- **Isolation boundary.** macOS: Seatbelt via sandbox-exec with a generated profile for the whole subprocess tree. Linux: Landlock + seccomp; ignored files overwritten in an overlay. Kernel too old -> falls back to asking approval. (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes#how-sandboxing-works-on-your-platform ; https://cursor.com/blog/agent-sandboxing)
- **Approvals.** Run modes Auto-review (classifier), Allowlist, Run Everything. Auto-review "is not a security boundary". (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/security/run-modes#pick-a-mode)

Surprises:

- Cursor's current docs say it no longer stores embeddings for search, and forum posts say semantic indexing was turned down in favor of Instant Grep in 2026. The survey's key finding 4 (+12.5% with semantic search) describes a path Cursor has since retired.
- Default read access is System: sandboxed commands can read outside the workspace unless Workspace mode is chosen.
- Default network mode allows Cursor's built-in package-manager domains, not zero domains.

From the source:

- **Setup failure 1 (default).** CodeModeExecutor.setup() passes env_vars=dict(os.environ) and DockerSandbox puts env_vars into the container environment. With the host's HOME=/Users/<user> inside the container, jupyter server crashes creating its runtime directory (PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/Users'), and setup ends with 'Timed out waiting for Jupyter Server'. Reproduced directly with docker run -e HOME=... on the same image. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L243-L252; https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/docker/docker.py#L140-L175; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-docker/out/P1.txt; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-docker/out/home-env-repro.txt)
- **Setup failure 2 (hardened, env_vars={}).** The container starts, then register_tool_caller(self.call_tool) asks the kernel client to set_variable('__call_tool__', bound_method), which pickles it and fails: 'Cannot serialize variable __call_tool__ ... Can't get local object _make_handshake_stamp.<locals>.stamp'. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L374; https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/docker/docker.py#L348-L351; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-docker/out/hardened-P1.txt)
- **Credentials.** By design the default path ships the full host environment, secrets included, into the container (failure 1 shows it arrives). That would make P5 'works' even inside Docker if setup succeeded. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L243-L252; https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/docker/docker.py#L140-L141)
- **Network.** DockerSandbox starts the container on the default bridge network with a published Jupyter port and never reads network_policy, so outbound network would be on. The host port is chosen by Docker (ports={'8888/tcp': ('127.0.0.1', None)}), with no option to pin it. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/docker/docker.py#L148-L163)
- **Bridge (as written).** For non-eval variants, tools are regenerated inside the kernel and called either through an HTTP proxy (mcp_proxy_url, served by the separate agent-runtimes project) or by MCP clients created inside the kernel from the host's server configs. The second needs agent_codemode installed in the image and the MCP server command runnable inside the container; neither is true for this image. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L394-L605)

Surprises:

- The documented docker variant cannot start through CodeModeExecutor on this Mac: forwarding the host environment into the container breaks Jupyter, and even with an empty environment the tool caller cannot be pickled into the kernel.
- network_policy is a SandboxConfig field but DockerSandbox ignores it; the container gets normal outbound networking.
- The container's host port is assigned by Docker and cannot be configured, so this probe could not keep to the 41500-41599 range (ports were ephemeral on 127.0.0.1).

From the source:

- **Credentials.** For every variant CodeModeExecutor.setup() copies the whole host environment into the sandbox config (env_vars = dict(os.environ)). On a hosted variant that would ship the host's environment, including any API keys, to the provider's kernel. Inferred from the code; not run. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L239-L252)
- **Bridge.** Remote variants call tools either through an HTTP proxy (mcp_proxy_url, served by the separate agent-runtimes project) or by constructing MCP clients inside the kernel from the host's server configs, including their env dicts. Without mcp_proxy_url the kernel needs agent_codemode installed and must be able to start the MCP servers itself. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L394-L599)

Surprises:

- The README lists colab, kaggle, modal and datalayer as sandbox_variant values; the docstring in types.py spells two of them 'google-colab' and 'jupyter-server'.

### Datalayer Agent Codemode, monty sandbox variant

- Source: https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode; sandbox from PyPI code-sandboxes[monty] (repo https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes) at `agent-codemode 566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea (1.1.1), code-sandboxes 1.12.4 (tag v1.12.4 = d7030b0b), pydantic-monty 0.0.18 (the last release that has MontyRepl; a fresh install resolves 1.6.0, which fails earlier)`
- Language and engine: Python (Monty subset), Would be pydantic-monty's in-process MontyRepl. Never reached user code: CodeModeExecutor.setup() raises before the first execution.
- How it was run: Same harness as datalayer-codemode-eval with CodeModeConfig(sandbox_variant='monty'); executor.setup() raises in every configuration, so no probe code ran.
- Defaults: time Not observable: setup fails. MontySandbox only takes a limits dict at construction and MontyRepl.feed_run takes no timeout (monty.py:129-146).; memory Not observable: setup fails.; output Not observable: setup fails.; tool_calls CodeModeConfig.max_tool_calls defaults to None (types.py:233).
- Hardened config: sandbox_client=CodeSandboxClient.create(variant='monty', config=SandboxConfig(timeout=30, network_policy='none', env_vars={}), limits={'max_duration_secs': 10, 'max_memory': 50_000_000}) and CodeModeConfig(max_tool_calls=50). Setup raises the same MontySyntaxError, so the hardened run has the same outcome.

From the source:

- **Setup failure 1 (current pydantic-monty).** code-sandboxes[monty] depends on an unpinned pydantic-monty. The current release (1.6.0) has no MontyRepl, so MontySandbox.start() raises AttributeError: module 'pydantic_monty' has no attribute 'MontyRepl'. MontyRepl last exists in 0.0.18 (checked 0.0.16 to 1.6.0). (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/monty/monty.py#L95-L127; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-monty/out/setup-crash-monty-1.6.0-P11.txt)
- **Setup failure 2 (any pydantic-monty).** With 0.0.18 the sandbox starts, but CodeModeExecutor registers its tool caller with register_tool_caller(self.call_tool), and MontySandbox._set_internal_variable implements that as feed_run(f'{name} = {value!r}'). The repr of a bound method is not Python, so setup raises MontySyntaxError: Expected an expression. The bridge cannot be installed in this variant at all. (https://github.com/datalayer/agent-codemode/blob/566e324a42e86074d29fd5e6bb5da2f282d459ea/agent_codemode/composition/executor.py#L374; https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/base.py#L1131-L1160; https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/monty/monty.py#L252-L255; research/probes/datalayer-codemode-monty/out/P1.txt)
- **Isolation boundary (as written).** MontySandbox runs pydantic-monty's MontyRepl in-process, with external_functions given at construction. The module docstring claims no access to filesystem, environment or network unless granted. Not observable here; wave 1's pydantic-monty row covers the interpreter itself. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/monty/monty.py#L5-L19; research/probes/results/pydantic-monty.json)
- **Limits (as written).** Its own docstring says MontyRepl.feed_run 'takes no limits (only Monty.run does)', and _do_interrupt returns False because the REPL cannot be interrupted, so a per-call timeout is not possible in this variant. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/monty/monty.py#L129-L146)
- **State (as written).** MontyRepl keeps heap and namespace across feed_run calls, so state would persist. (https://github.com/datalayer/code-sandboxes/blob/d7030b0bb37609195cc3048d1145622dd81170a5/code_sandboxes/sandboxes/monty/monty.py#L17-L18; #L113-L114)

Surprises:

- The README and docs list 'monty' as a supported sandbox_variant ('Secure in-process interpreter'), but CodeModeExecutor cannot finish setup with it under any pydantic-monty release: the current one lacks MontyRepl, and the old one cannot parse the tool caller assignment.
- No test in the agent-codemode repo exercises the monty variant (grep finds 'monty' only in the README, the docs page and the types.py docstring).

From the source:

- **Availability.** "Context Mesh is in active development." MCP servers "can only be linked to and proxied with Kong Gateway control planes that were provisioned with Kong Operator", and "MCP server code managed by Konnect" is listed for both deployment modes. Advanced mode is Tech Preview. (https://developer.konghq.com/context-mesh.md)
- **API shape and discovery.** Generates one Code Mode MCP server per configuration from OpenAPI 3.0 specs (uploaded or from Catalog) plus existing MCP servers added by upstream URL, exposing them "as a single SDK-like interface rather than one tool per operation". The docs link Cloudflare's Code Mode post but do not name the tools, the language, or the sandbox. (https://developer.konghq.com/context-mesh.md)
- **Isolation, bridge, limits, errors, state.** Not documented. The generated server runs as a Kubernetes workload managed by Kong Operator behind a Kong Gateway Service (mcpserver-<id>), so gateway plugins can govern it, but nothing says what runs the agent's code or what it can reach. (https://developer.konghq.com/context-mesh.md)
- **Claims.** "reduces token consumption by ~99% (from ~120,000 tokens to ~1,200 tokens)" with no method, workload or source given. (https://developer.konghq.com/context-mesh.md)

Surprises:

- The ~99% token-reduction figure has no benchmark, workload or method behind it on the page.
- The docs never say what language the agent writes or what runs it, so even a docs-only security comparison is not possible.

From the source:

- **Bridge.** Same stdio frame protocol as the default transport, but the runner and program are written into the VM with the E2B files API and run with plain `node`; TypeScript is stripped on the host with esbuild. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/workspaces/e2b/src/code-mode/transport.ts#L1-L19; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/workspaces/e2b/src/code-mode/transport.ts#L76; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/workspaces/e2b/src/code-mode/transport.ts#L115-L116)
- **Credentials.** Tools still execute on the host (same dispatcher as other transports), so tool credentials never enter the VM; the E2B API key is read from the constructor or E2B_API_KEY. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L102-L119; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/workspaces/e2b/src/sandbox/index.ts#L159-L160)
- **API shape.** Each Mastra tool's input and output schema goes zod -> JSON Schema -> a TypeScript string, and becomes one `declare function external_<id>(input): Promise<output>` line with the tool description as a doc comment. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L164-L186)
- **Discovery.** Everything upfront: createCodeModeInstructions joins a fixed usage contract and every stub into one instructions string for the system prompt. No search or lazy loading; the docs scope tools by making several createCodeMode instances instead. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/stub-generator.ts#L189-L213)
- **Credentials.** Tools run on the host: each external_* call re-enters the real Mastra tool's execute with the outer tool's requestContext, mastra instance and workspace, and an allow-list rejects tool ids that were not exposed. Credentials the tool uses stay on the host side of the bridge. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L102-L119)
- **Defaults.** Timeout defaults to 30 s for every backend (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT). The tool id defaults to execute_typescript. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/code-mode.ts#L20-L21)
- **Errors.** The result type declares error.line, but no transport ever sets it: the stdio runner, the isolated-vm envelope and the QuickJS envelope all copy only message and name. The model never sees a line number or stack. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/types.ts#L50-L54; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L153-L157; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/isolated-vm/src/transport.ts#L266-L270; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/code-mode/quickjs/src/transport.ts#L425-L429)
- **Output channel.** Both console output (logs[], one entry per call, in order) and the program's `return` value come back. Nothing truncates either; a bare final expression is not returned because the program is wrapped in an async function body. (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/transport.ts#L76-L80; https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/blob/aa82a4a7858c637f654be24391ff306dcb568c00/packages/core/src/tools/code-mode/runner.ts#L38-L40)

From the source:

- **API shape.** Single hosted python tool; the model knows it as "python". No client tools bridged in. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-code-interpreter)
- **Isolation boundary.** Container VM; network off by default for hosted containers, opt-in allowlist governed by an org-level admin allow list; request policy can only narrow it. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-shell#network-policy-precedence)
- **State.** Container lives until 20 minutes idle; memory tier fixed for the container's life. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-code-interpreter#expiration)
- **Notable.** Allowlisting "introduces security risks such as prompt injection-driven data exfiltration" (shell guide). (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-shell#network-access)

Surprises:

- The Code Interpreter page never states the network default; the answer is on the hosted Shell page, which says hosted containers have no outbound network by default and that Shell and Code Interpreter share the container lifecycle.
- Network can be opened per container with an allowlist and per-domain secrets, so "no network" is a default, not a property.

### OpenAI Programmatic Tool Calling (Responses API and Agents API)

- Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling ; https://github.com/openai/openai-python at `docs fetched 2026-11-22 (markdown at https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling.md); openai-python@f63f14b34754fa77fc839ac2cf95da3ef42e1f6a`
- Language and engine: JavaScript (top-level await), OpenAI-hosted fresh isolated V8 runtime per program
- How it was run: Not run: no API key on this machine. Documented entry point is a Responses API request with {type: programmatic_tool_calling} plus allowed_callers: ["programmatic"] on each eligible tool.
- Defaults: time not documented; memory not documented; output text(...)/image(...) only, as program_output.result (string); tool_calls not documented

| Probe | Outcome | Detail | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Tool call | works | Docs only, not run. Tools appear as tools.* inside the program; a client-owned call surfaces as a function_call item whose caller.caller_id matches the program's call_id, and the client returns function_call_output with the same caller. Example: "const [stock, demand] = await Promise.all([tools.get_inventory({ sku: 'sku_123' }), tools.get_demand({ sku: 'sku_123' })]);" | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-program-response-items |
| P2 Output | limited | No console: output only via text(...) or image(...). Docs: "Programs ... can emit output with text(...) or image(...)." The result arrives as a program_output item with a result string and status completed or incomplete. console.log would be not-defined per the runtime description. Truncation of a 200,000-char text() is not documented. SDK type ProgramOutput has only result and status, no stderr field. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment ; https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/f63f14b34754fa77fc839ac2cf95da3ef42e1f6a/src/openai/types/responses/response_output_item.py#L66-L80 |
| P3 Network | blocked | Docs: "OpenAI runs each generated program in a fresh, isolated V8 runtime. The runtime supports JavaScript with top-level await, but it does not provide Node.js, package installation, direct network access, a general-purpose filesystem, subprocess execution, a console, or persistent JavaScript state between program executions." Not run. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment |
| P4 Files | blocked | Docs: no "general-purpose filesystem" (same sentence). The client's host files are also unreachable by construction. Not run. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment |
| P5 Env secret | not-applicable | The program runs on OpenAI's servers, so the client's PROBE_SECRET is never sent (inference). Docs say the runtime has no Node.js, so process.env does not exist. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment |
| P6 Infinite loop | blocked-needs-credentials | Docs are silent on a time limit. program_output.status can be incomplete; the cause list is not documented. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling |
| P7 Memory | blocked-needs-credentials | Docs are silent on a memory limit. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling |
| P8 State | fresh (docs) | Docs: no "persistent JavaScript state between program executions." | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment |

Both function_call items arrive in one response. Elapsed time depends on the client. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-program-response-items |
| P10 Errors | blocked-needs-credentials | Docs do not show how a thrown exception is reported. ProgramOutput has no error field in the SDK, only result and status. | https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/f63f14b34754fa77fc839ac2cf95da3ef42e1f6a/src/openai/types/responses/response_output_item.py#L66-L80 |
| P11 Startup | blocked-needs-credentials | No startup figure in the docs. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling |
| P12 Escape | not-defined | Docs claim no Node.js and no subprocess execution, so process and child_process should not exist. Not tested. | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment |

From the source:

- **API shape.** Tools are exposed as tools.<name>(args). Function tools may declare output_schema so generated code can rely on returned fields. allowed_callers values: direct, programmatic, or both. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#configure-programmatic-tool-calling)
- **Discovery.** All allowed tools upfront. Tool search runs only as a top-level tool, not from inside a program; deferred tools become callable from a later program once loaded. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#combine-with-tool-search)
- **Bridge.** Pause/resume across Responses API calls. The program item carries an opaque fingerprint "used to resume or replay the program"; the client must copy caller into each function_call_output. Stateless mode replays every program, reasoning, function-call, output and program_output item. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#continue-after-client-owned-function-calls ; https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/f63f14b34754fa77fc839ac2cf95da3ef42e1f6a/src/openai/types/responses/response_output_item.py#L49-L64)
- **Isolation boundary.** Fresh V8 runtime; no Node.js, network, filesystem, subprocess, console, or persistent state. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment)
- **Notable (hosted tools from code).** allowed_callers: ["programmatic"] is supported on function, custom, mcp, apply_patch, local and hosted shell, and code_interpreter. MCP require_approval "can pause the program until you approve the call." (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#supported-tools)
- **Notable (data).** "Programmatic Tool Calling supports Zero Data Retention (ZDR) workflows without requiring a persistent code-execution container." (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#understand-the-runtime-environment)
- **Notable (routing).** "Adaptive search or semantic evaluation" -> direct tool calling; "Final citation or native artifact validation" -> direct unless the program preserves native output and validates every item. (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#choose-when-to-use-programmatic-tool-calling)
- **Agents API.** PTC is on by default; the harness gives the agent an exec tool. "Orchestrating a tool in JavaScript doesn't change where the tool runs." (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-programmatic-tool-calling#agents-api)

Surprises:

- OpenAI documents no time, memory, output-size or call-count limits for the program runtime.
- Hosted tools (code_interpreter, hosted shell, MCP) can be called from inside a program, so a PTC program can drive a networked or file-holding container even though the V8 runtime itself has neither.
- PTC supports ZDR; Anthropic PTC is not ZDR eligible.
